question: Will Iran close the Strait of Hormuz before 2027?
description:
If Iran halts or severely restricts international maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official governmental information, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Iran's Supreme National Security Council officially order the closure or blockade of the Strait of Hormuz between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06?
subquestions.background_information:
In June 2025, Iran's parliament voted to approve a measure to close the Strait of Hormuz following US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites. However, the final decision on whether to actually implement a closure rests with Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), which is the ultimate decision-making body on national security matters in Iran. As of the articles available through late June 2025, the SNSC had not yet made a final decision. Iranian lawmaker Esmail Kosari stated, 'The closure of the strait is on the agenda and will be done whenever necessary,' but the Supreme National Security Council had not formally ordered it. Meanwhile, tanker traffic through the strait had begun to reduce due to rising tensions, with some operators halting transits. Commodore Alireza Tangsiri, head of Iran's IRGC naval forces, stated that Iran has the option of disrupting traffic but chooses not to. The strait handles approximately 20 million barrels of oil per day, about 20% of global oil consumption, making any closure decision enormously consequential for both global markets and Iran's own economy (as it would also prevent Iran from exporting its petroleum and antagonize China, its biggest oil buyer).

Sources:
- India Today: Iran approves closure of oil corridor, Strait of Hormuz, after US strikes: https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/iran-approves-closure-of-oil-corridor-strait-of-hormuz-after-us-strikes-report-2741123-2025-06-22
- Times of India: US strikes on Iran: Tehran's top security council to decide on Strait of Hormuz closure: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/us-strikes-on-iran-tehrans-top-security-council-to-decide-on-strait-of-hormuz-closure-after-parliamentary-nod/articleshow/122051671.cms
- The Straits Times: What if Iran tries to close the Strait of Hormuz?: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/what-if-iran-tries-to-close-the-strait-of-hormuz
- Ship & Bunker: Crude Futures Jump After Iranian Threats: https://shipandbunker.com/news/world/471380-crude-futures-jump-after-iranian-threats-to-strait-of-hormuz-ship-traffic
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 (inclusive), Iran's Supreme National Security Council (or an equivalent top-level Iranian governmental authority such as the Supreme Leader) officially orders or publicly announces a decision to close, blockade, or severely restrict international maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz. Evidence must come from at least two credible international news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, Al Jazeera, or official Iranian state media such as IRNA or Press TV). A parliamentary vote alone does not count; the decision must come from the executive/security authority empowered to implement such an order. If no such announcement or order is confirmed by credible reporting by 2025-12-06 23:59 UTC, the question resolves No. If reports are ambiguous or contradictory, a consensus of at least three major international news outlets will be required for Yes resolution.

Sources for resolution:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- IRNA (Islamic Republic News Agency): https://en.irna.ir/
- Press TV: https://www.presstv.ir/
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Iran will close the Strait of Hormuz before 2027 (with the market end date in March 2026). A formal order from Iran's Supreme National Security Council is the critical prerequisite step before any actual closure could occur. Iran's parliament already voted to approve closure in June 2025, but the SNSC has the final say. Monitoring whether the SNSC makes this decision in the near term is the most direct leading indicator of whether an actual closure will follow. If the SNSC orders closure, the probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes increases dramatically. If no such order materializes despite ongoing tensions, it suggests Iran is maintaining its historical pattern of threatening but not following through, which would significantly decrease the probability of a closure before March 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Iran's Supreme National Security Council (or equivalent such as the Supreme Leader) officially orders or publicly announces a decision to close, blockade, or severely restrict international maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 (inclusive), confirmed by at least two credible international news sources. A parliamentary vote alone does not count; must come from executive/security authority.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Iran Supreme National Security Council Strait of Hormuz closure blockade 2025' — to find direct evidence of an official order; 2) 'Iran Hormuz Strait close blockade order November December 2025' — to find any closure-related announcements; 3) 'Iran officially close Strait Hormuz order announcement November 2025' — to find formal announcements; 4) 'Iran Khamenei Pezeshkian Strait Hormuz blockade decision 2025' — to find decisions from top leadership; 5) 'Iran Supreme National Security Council Hormuz order blockade maritime restriction' — to find institutional decisions; 6) 'Iran naval drill Hormuz December 2025 threat closure' — to find if drills included closure orders.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Events found in window: (1) Iran seized tanker Talara in Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 14, 2025 (AP, Reuters, BBC, IRNA) — individual vessel seizure under judicial order, not a Strait closure. Rejected as not meeting criteria. (2) IRGC conducted naval drills 'Shahid Mohammad Nazeri' Dec. 4-5, 2025 near Strait of Hormuz (AP, AFP, Times of Israel, Newsweek) — military exercises demonstrating capability, not a closure order. Rejected. (3) IRGC Deputy Commander Fadavi declared the Strait a 'red line' and warned US vessels during drills on Dec. 4, 2025 — rhetorical warnings during military exercises, not an official blockade/closure order. Rejected. (4) Multiple articles reference Iran's historical threats to close the Strait — background context, not a qualifying event. All candidates rejected.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of any official order from Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Supreme Leader (Khamenei), or equivalent executive/security authority to close, blockade, or severely restrict international maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz during the window. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/iran-tanker-mideast-tensions-1762f491e9eb1912cb8b8bd9a1a634d8) reports a tanker seizure, not a blockade order. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/iran-ejercicio-naval-misiles-e317fecc7f9e364206d0da049c6cda47) and [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/iran-warns-us-stay-away-naval-war-drills-11160946) report naval drills and warnings, not a closure order. IRGC statements about the Strait being a 'red line' are warnings/posturing, not formal closure orders. The resolution criteria explicitly require an official order from executive/security authority, which was not found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event occurred; therefore no timestamp to extract for a Yes resolution. The resolution window closed at 2025-12-06T23:59:59Z without a qualifying event.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove a No conclusion by searching specifically for any closure orders, blockade announcements, or security council decisions related to the Strait. Found only: tanker seizures (individual vessel actions under judicial order), military exercises, rhetorical warnings, and historical context about threats. All articles about Iran's drills and Hormuz activity consistently describe exercises and warnings rather than closure orders. No contradictory evidence was found suggesting a blockade order was issued. The Seatrade Maritime article from Nov. 19, 2025 specifically notes container shipping continues to transit the Strait, which would be inconsistent with a closure order having been made. The tanker Talara was released on Nov. 20, 2025, demonstrating the Strait remained open to transit.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying event occurred within the window (2025-11-06 to 2025-12-06). Iran's Supreme National Security Council or equivalent authority did not officially order or publicly announce a decision to close, blockade, or severely restrict international maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz. Activities observed (tanker seizure, naval drills, rhetorical warnings) do not meet the resolution criteria of an official blockade/closure order. The question resolves No as of the window closing date of 2025-12-06T23:59:59Z.

question: Will Wicked: For Good be the top grossing movie of 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the "Gross" column on https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses shows 'Wicked: For Good' (2025) as the film with the highest 2025 gross once data for December 31 is made available. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: This market is about the movie's domestic calendar gross in 2025 - dates outside of 2025 will not count toward this movie's gross.

In the event of an exact tie the film that comes first alphabetically will be considered the winner.

If there is no final data available by January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

subquestions.question: Will any single movie's 2025 domestic cumulative gross exceed $500 million on Box Office Mojo by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
For Wicked: For Good to be the top-grossing domestic film of 2025, it would need to outperform all other 2025 releases. As of late August 2025, the top domestic grossers of the year include several major releases from the first eight months. Key competitors include sequels and franchise films released in the summer season. If any film has already crossed $500 million domestically before Wicked: For Good even opens on November 21, 2025, that would represent a very high bar for the musical sequel to clear in roughly five and a half weeks of release (November 21 – December 31). For context, the original Wicked earned approximately $468 million domestically during its full theatrical run spanning late 2024 into early 2025. Only a handful of films in history have earned over $500 million domestically in a single calendar year. If a competitor has already reached this level by the end of September, it would significantly reduce the probability that Wicked: For Good finishes as the #1 domestic grosser for the 2025 calendar year. Current 2025 domestic box office standings can be tracked at Box Office Mojo.

Sources:
- Box Office Mojo 2025 yearly domestic grosses: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses
- Wicked worldwide gross data: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt1262426/
- Wicked: For Good release info: https://www.imdb.com/title/tt15360024/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, as of September 30, 2025, any single movie's 2025 calendar-year domestic gross listed on Box Office Mojo's 2025 yearly domestic chart (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses) equals or exceeds $500,000,000. Only domestic (U.S.) gross accumulated between January 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025, counts. The data must be checked on or after October 1, 2025, when September 30 figures are available. If Box Office Mojo is unavailable, The Numbers (https://www.the-numbers.com/market/2025/top-grossing-movies) may be used as a fallback source. This question covers the period from 2025-09-01 (the question's start date) to 2025-09-30 (the end date), but the gross figures considered are cumulative 2025 calendar-year totals as of September 30, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a meaningful early indicator because it measures how dominant the competition already is before Wicked: For Good even releases on November 21. If a film has already crossed $500 million domestically by the end of September, Wicked: For Good would face an extremely difficult task to overtake it in just ~5.5 weeks of 2025 calendar-year release. Conversely, if no film has reached that threshold, the race remains more open and Wicked: For Good's chances improve. This is a genuine crux for disagreement: forecasters who believe a summer blockbuster will dominate would expect 'Yes,' while those who think the field is weak enough for a late-year musical sequel to win would expect 'No.'

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Any single movie's 2025 domestic (U.S.) cumulative gross listed on Box Office Mojo's 2025 yearly domestic chart must equal or exceed $500,000,000 as of September 30, 2025. Observable evidence: Box Office Mojo/fallback source showing a domestic gross ≥ $500M for any 2025 release. Key threshold: $500,000,000 domestic U.S. gross.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'box office 2025 domestic gross $500 million movie' (general search); 2. 'highest grossing movies 2025 domestic box office United States' (top performers); 3. 'Lilo Stitch domestic box office total 2025 United States cumulative gross' (specific candidate); 4. 'Demon Slayer Infinity Castle domestic box office United States gross September 2025' (September release); 5. 'Superman 2025 domestic box office total cumulative gross United States'; 6. 'Minecraft Movie domestic box office total United States 2025 cumulative'; 7. '2025 yearly domestic box office chart highest grossing films September'; 8. 'top grossing movies 2025 domestic chart box office mojo $500 million'; 9. 'box office mojo 2025 calendar year domestic chart top grossing September October'; 10. 'highest grossing movie 2025 US domestic final box office total year-to-date'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate films: A Minecraft Movie ($423.9M domestic as of Sept 17, per Businessday NG citing Box Office Mojo), Lilo & Stitch ($423.7M domestic as of Sept 17), Superman (~$353.9M domestic), Jurassic World Rebirth (~$339.4M domestic), Sinners (~$278.6M domestic), Demon Slayer Infinity Castle ($104.7M domestic by second weekend Sept 21-22). All rejected as candidates because none reached $500M domestic.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Per [Businessday NG article](https://businessday.ng/life-arts/article/2025-hollywood-box-office-leaders-reflect-franchise-dominance/) published Sept 20, 2025: 'By September 17, 2025, Hollywood's domestic box-office had accumulated $2.9 billion across the top ten releases...The leading film is the Minecraft Movie, which earned $423.9 million domestically.' Per [TheWrap Sept 1](https://www.thewrap.com/summer-box-office-2025-flat/): Lilo & Stitch described as 'the only film that crossed $400 million domestically.' Per [ComingSoon.net Sept 22](https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/2030385-demon-slayer-infinity-castle-box-office-beat-fantastic-four-superman): Demon Slayer domestic total was $104.7 million by second weekend. No film is confirmed to have crossed $500M domestic by September 30, 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Businessday NG article published September 20, 2025 cites data 'by September 17, 2025' — showing top domestic film at $423.9M. The Wrap article from September 1, 2025 explicitly states no film crossed $500M domestically during summer 2025. SlashFilm article from August 26, 2025 confirms Lilo & Stitch at 'just shy of $422 million domestically' — still far from $500M.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence found. Multiple sources corroborate that no domestic film reached $500M in 2025 through September 30.
evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence. evidence.step8_final_decision: Based on multiple independent, explicitly sourced articles citing Box Office Mojo data, no single 2025 movie reached $500 million domestic cumulative gross by September 30, 2025. The highest domestic grossers as of mid-to-late September 2025 were A Minecraft Movie and Lilo & Stitch at approximately $423-424 million each, well below the $500M threshold. Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle opened September 12 to only $70.6M domestically and accumulated only $104.7M by its second weekend. Resolution: No.

question: Israel and Saudi Arabia normalize relations in 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will Israel publicly commit to a pathway toward Palestinian statehood (e.g., endorsing a two-state framework or presenting a plan for an independent Palestinian state) between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Saudi Arabia has repeatedly and explicitly stated that normalization with Israel is contingent on the establishment of a Palestinian state and the end of the war in Gaza. On July 28, 2025, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan stated: 'For the kingdom, recognition is very much tied to the establishment of the Palestinian state' and that 'there's no reason, even, or no credibility, to have a conversation about normalization with constant death and suffering and destruction in Gaza' (Anadolu Agency, July 28, 2025). On August 17, 2025, former Saudi intelligence chief Prince Turki al-Faisal called Netanyahu a 'genocidal maniac' and stated Saudi Arabia would not normalize under his leadership (The Siasat Daily, August 17, 2025). Meanwhile, Israel's current coalition government under PM Netanyahu has consistently opposed the creation of a Palestinian state. Experts cited by The Wall Street Journal and TASS (July 7, 2025) assessed that Israel's unwillingness to meet Saudi conditions makes normalization unlikely. A June 2025 UN conference co-chaired by Saudi Arabia and France produced a roadmap focused on Palestinian statehood, international recognition, and normalization with Israel (Asharq Al-Awsat, May 24, 2025). Whether Israel shifts its position on Palestinian statehood is the single most critical precondition for Saudi normalization.

Sources:
- Anadolu Agency, July 28, 2025: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/saudi-arabia-says-no-normalization-with-israel-without-establishing-palestinian-state/3350123
- The Siasat Daily, August 17, 2025: https://www.siasat.com/saudi-arabia-will-not-normalise-relations-with-a-genocidal-maniac-says-prince-turki-al-faisal-3166892/
- TASS, July 7, 2025: https://tass.com/world/1945789
- Asharq Al-Awsat, May 24, 2025: https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5268351
- The Jerusalem Post, April 16, 2025: https://www.jpost.com/opinion/article-852133
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), the Israeli government—through the Prime Minister, Foreign Minister, or an official government statement—publicly endorses, commits to, or presents a concrete plan or framework for the establishment of an independent Palestinian state as part of a two-state solution. A vague reference to 'future negotiations' or 'discussing options' does not qualify; there must be an explicit acknowledgment that the goal is Palestinian statehood. Resolution will be based on official Israeli government communications (e.g., statements from the Prime Minister's Office at https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office), as well as credible international news sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), The Times of Israel (https://www.timesofisrael.com), and Haaretz (https://www.haaretz.com). If no such commitment is made by September 30, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Saudi Arabia has made Palestinian statehood the non-negotiable precondition for normalization with Israel. Israel's current government under Netanyahu has firmly opposed this condition. If Israel were to shift its stance and publicly commit to a pathway toward Palestinian statehood in September 2025, it would dramatically increase the likelihood of normalization by year-end. Conversely, continued Israeli opposition to Palestinian statehood would strongly signal that normalization in 2025 is essentially impossible. This is the core crux on which forecasters disagreeing about normalization are most likely to disagree: whether Israel will budge on the Palestinian state issue in time.

evidence.step3_event_detection: No qualifying events found. evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is definitively No. Israel's government, through PM Netanyahu and FM Sa'ar, repeatedly and explicitly rejected Palestinian statehood throughout the entire resolution window (Sep 1-30, 2025). subquestions.question: Will Israel formally respond to or engage in active negotiations on the Hamas-accepted 60-day ceasefire proposal (or any new ceasefire proposal) between September 1 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 18, 2025, Hamas approved a 60-day ceasefire proposal mediated by Egypt and Qatar, based on a framework put forth by US envoy Steve Witkoff. The proposal includes Hamas releasing ten Israeli hostages and the remains of 18 others in exchange for Palestinian prisoners, with Israeli forces redeploying closer to the Gaza border to facilitate humanitarian aid. As of August 31, 2025, Israel has not formally responded to Hamas's acceptance. Netanyahu's office insists any agreement must involve the simultaneous release of all hostages, and senior Israeli officials have indicated that Netanyahu does not intend to prioritize ceasefire negotiations. Instead, Israel's security cabinet is focused on plans for a Gaza City offensive. CNN reported on August 31 that 'the fact that the deal isn't formally on the agenda indicates how low the proposal is on Netanyahu's priority list.' However, IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and parts of the Israeli security establishment have urged the cabinet to discuss negotiations before escalating military operations. The US and Israel shifted in late July 2025 toward seeking a comprehensive deal that ends the war entirely rather than partial ceasefires. Hundreds of thousands of Israelis have protested demanding an end to the war and the safe return of hostages.

Sources:
- "Hamas Approves 60-Day Ceasefire Proposal, Awaiting Israel's Response" (Egyptian Streets, August 19, 2025): https://egyptianstreets.com
- "Ceasefire deal not on agenda with Israel's security cabinet set to discuss looming Gaza City offensive" (ABC17NEWS/CNN, August 31, 2025): https://abc17news.com/news/national-world/cnn-world/2025/08/31/ceasefire-deal-not-on-agenda-with-israels-security-cabinet-set-to-discuss-looming-gaza-city-offensive/
- "'No more partial deals': Official says Israel, US now back comprehensive plan to end war" (Times of Israel, July 31, 2025): https://www.timesofisrael.com/no-more-partial-deals-official-says-israel-us-now-back-comprehensive-plan-to-end-war/
- "Top Israeli officials meeting to discuss ceasefire after Hamas's 'positive' response" (Washington Examiner, July 5, 2025): https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/defense/3100000/top-israeli-officials-meeting-ceasefire-hamas-positive-response/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), Israel's government (Prime Minister's Office, security cabinet, or authorized negotiating team) formally responds to the existing Hamas-accepted 60-day ceasefire proposal OR enters into active, acknowledged negotiations on any ceasefire proposal with Hamas through mediators (Egypt, Qatar, US, or others). 'Formally responds' means an official Israeli government statement accepting, rejecting with a counter-proposal, or presenting modified terms in response to the Hamas-accepted proposal. 'Active negotiations' means at least one round of talks (direct or through mediators) in which Israeli representatives participate with the stated purpose of reaching a ceasefire agreement, as reported by at least two credible international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, Times of Israel, Al Jazeera). Mere informal comments by unnamed officials, background briefings without concrete engagement, or unilateral Israeli statements about preconditions without direct engagement with mediators do not count. If no credible media reports confirm such formal engagement by September 30, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Israel engages with the existing ceasefire proposal or enters negotiations in September is a strong leading indicator of whether a ceasefire deal can be reached before the ultimate question's October 9, 2025 deadline. As of late August, Israel has not responded to Hamas's August 18 acceptance, and negotiations are not on the cabinet's agenda. A shift toward active engagement would dramatically increase the probability of a deal, while continued refusal to negotiate would make a ceasefire before the deadline very unlikely. This is a genuine crux: forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question likely disagree on whether Netanyahu will pivot toward negotiations under domestic, military, and international pressure, or continue prioritizing the Gaza City offensive.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: (A) formal Israeli response to Hamas-accepted 60-day ceasefire proposal (accept/reject with counter/modified terms), OR (B) active acknowledged negotiations via mediators with ≥1 round of Israeli-participated talks with stated purpose of ceasefire agreement, confirmed by ≥2 credible outlets. Key entities: Israel PM's office/security cabinet/authorized team; mediators: Egypt, Qatar, US; Hamas. Window: Sept 1–30, 2025.

The Sept 4 Paris talks are acknowledged in multiple credible outlets, involve Israeli authorized representatives (Dermer), through mediators (US/Qatar), for ceasefire purposes. This resolves Yes.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution = Yes. The earliest qualifying event within the window is September 4-5, 2025, when Israeli authorized negotiator Ron Dermer met with US envoy Witkoff and Qatari officials in Paris/Miami for the stated purpose of reaching a ceasefire/hostage agreement, confirmed by Times of Israel, Al Bawaba, and Channel 12 (Israeli broadcaster). Resolution datetime = 2025-09-04T17:32:00Z (time of Times of Israel report on Dermer-Witkoff Paris meeting) — this is the first confirmed occurrence.

subquestions.question: Will U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett file to run in the 2026 Texas Democratic Senate primary by December 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2026 Texas Democratic Senate primary currently features two major candidates: former U.S. Rep. Colin Allred and State Rep. James Talarico. However, U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett of Dallas has publicly stated she is considering entering the race, with her decision reportedly hinging on polling results. As of early November 2025, Crockett's supporters have been conducting text polls to gauge her viability. The Texas candidate filing period for the 2026 primary runs from November 8 to December 8, 2025, meaning any candidate must file by that deadline to appear on the ballot.

Crockett is a high-profile Democratic congresswoman representing Dallas, and her entry could significantly reshape the primary. She would draw from a similar base of Black and urban voters as Allred, potentially splitting the Dallas-area vote and benefiting Talarico. Conversely, if she does not enter, the race remains a two-person contest between Allred and Talarico, where Allred's higher name recognition and 2024 Senate campaign experience may give him an advantage.

A CBS News report from November 2, 2025, noted that Crockett was actively considering the race and that her decision would be based on polling data. Talarico welcomed potential competition, while Allred expressed respect for Crockett.

Sources:
- CBS News, "Democrats Colin Allred, James Talarico tout endorsements as Jasmine Crockett eyes Texas Senate race" (Nov 2, 2025): https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/democrats-colin-allred-james-talarico-tout-endorsements-as-jasmine-crockett-eyes-texas-senate-race/
- The Dallas Morning News, "James Talarico targets rival Colin Allred's home turf in Senate primary fight" (Oct 28, 2025): https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/2025/10/28/james-talarico-targets-rival-colin-allreds-home-turf-in-senate-primary-fight/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett files as a candidate in the 2026 Texas Democratic Senate primary between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-08 (the filing deadline). It resolves No if, by December 8, 2025, Crockett has not filed to run in the Democratic Senate primary. Resolution will be based on the Texas Secretary of State's candidate filing records (https://www.sos.state.tx.us/elections/index.shtml) or credible news reporting from outlets such as the Texas Tribune (https://www.texastribune.org/), Dallas Morning News, or CBS News confirming or denying her filing. If the filing deadline is extended beyond December 8, 2025, this question resolves based on whether Crockett has filed by the original December 8 deadline. The resolution window is 2025-11-13 to 2025-12-13, with the key event (filing) needing to occur by December 8, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: Jasmine Crockett's entry into the Democratic primary would be one of the most consequential developments affecting whether Talarico wins the nomination. As a sitting congresswoman from Dallas—Allred's home base—Crockett would likely split the moderate and Black voter base that Allred relies on, potentially creating a path for Talarico to win a plurality in a three-way race. Conversely, if she stays out, Talarico faces a more straightforward one-on-one contest against Allred, who has higher statewide name recognition and fundraising infrastructure from his 2024 campaign. The filing deadline falls within our resolution window, making this a concrete, observable indicator that would meaningfully update forecasts on the ultimate question.

question: Will Gemini 3.0 be released by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve according to the date (ET) Google's Gemini 3.0 model is made available to the general public. 

For this market to resolve to "Yes," Gemini 3.0 must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by Google as being accessible to the general public.

Gemini 3.0 refers to a product explicitly named Gemini 3.0 (e.g. Gemini 3.0 pro would count), or one that is recognized as a successor to Gemini 2.0, similar to the progression from Gemini 1.0 to Gemini 2.0. Products labeled as Gemini 2.5 or similar will not count for this market's resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Google, with additional verification from a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Google officially announce or preview a model explicitly named 'Gemini 3.0' (or widely recognized as the direct successor to Gemini 2.x) at a public event or blog post between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Google's Gemini model family has progressed from Gemini 1.0 (launched December 2023) through Gemini 1.5 and then to Gemini 2.0 (launched in late 2024/early 2025). As of September 2025, the latest publicly available models are in the Gemini 2.5 series, including Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 2.5 Flash (with its recent image generation variant). There has been no public mention or leak from Google regarding a 'Gemini 3.0' model as of September 1, 2025.

Google typically announces major model releases at its annual developer conference (Google I/O, usually in May) or at dedicated Made by Google hardware events (often in August-October). The August 2025 Made by Google event focused on Pixel 10 hardware and Gemini for Home integration, with no mention of Gemini 3.0. Google's recent focus has been on iterating within the 2.x line (2.0, 2.5 Pro, 2.5 Flash).

For Gemini 3.0 to be publicly released by October 31, 2025, it would almost certainly need to be announced or previewed before October 1. Major AI model releases from Google are typically preceded by blog posts, research papers, or event announcements weeks before general availability.

Sources:
- Digital Trends, 'Google Gemini: everything you need to know' (2025-08-22): https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-gemini-everything-you-need-to-know/
- Telangana Today, 'Google unveils Gemini 2.5 Flash Image' (2025-08-28): https://telanganatoday.com/google-unveils-gemini-2-5-flash-image-with-advanced-ai-powered-editing-and-generation
- Google AI Blog: https://blog.google/technology/ai/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), Google publicly announces, previews, or reveals a model explicitly named 'Gemini 3.0' (including variants such as 'Gemini 3.0 Pro', 'Gemini 3.0 Flash', etc.) or a model that is officially described by Google as the successor to the Gemini 2.x family (not merely an incremental update like 2.5 or 2.7). The announcement must appear on an official Google channel such as the Google AI Blog (https://blog.google/technology/ai/), the Google DeepMind blog (https://deepmind.google/), a keynote presentation at a Google event, or an official Google social media account. Alternatively, if a credible consensus of major tech outlets (e.g., The Verge, TechCrunch, Ars Technica) reports such an announcement based on official Google communications, that also suffices. A leak or rumor without official confirmation does not count. If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM UTC on October 1, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For Gemini 3.0 to be publicly released by October 31, 2025, Google would almost certainly need to announce or preview the model before October 1. Google's pattern with major model releases involves public announcements (blog posts, event keynotes, developer previews) weeks before general availability. The absence of any mention of Gemini 3.0 in recent events (including the August 2025 Made by Google event) and the continued focus on the 2.5 line suggest a 3.0 release by October 31 is unlikely — but tracking whether an announcement materializes in September is the strongest leading indicator. If no announcement appears by October 1, forecasters should significantly lower their probability for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Google must officially announce/preview a model explicitly named 'Gemini 3.0' (or variants like 'Gemini 3.0 Pro', 'Gemini 3.0 Flash') OR a model officially described by Google as the direct successor to the Gemini 2.x family (not just a 2.5/2.7 incremental update). subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Congress vote on or pass a War Powers Resolution to restrict U.S. military operations against Venezuela-linked targets by November 6, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 3, 2025, the Trump administration sent a memo to Congress declaring a 'non-international armed conflict' with Latin American 'terrorist organisations' linked to Venezuelan drug cartels, granting wartime powers to strike, kill, and detain cartel fighters without trial. Democrats in Congress, including Senator Jack Reed, criticized the move as lacking legal justification and began drafting a War Powers Resolution to block further unilateral military action. Senator Adam Schiff also warned that 'lawless killings may lead to war.' The War Powers Resolution process is a key congressional check on presidential military authority. If Congress moves to block or restrict operations, it would signal strong domestic political resistance to escalation, making a full invasion far less likely. Conversely, if no such resolution advances, it may indicate tacit acceptance of the administration's military posture, leaving the door open for further escalation. As of early October 2025, the Pentagon has deployed the 22nd Marine Expeditionary Unit (2,200 Marines), ten F-35 stealth jets, Navy warships, a nuclear submarine, and special operations forces to the Caribbean near Venezuela. Three lethal strikes on suspected narcotrafficking boats in September 2025 killed at least 17 people.

- The US Sun, 'US prepares to seize ports in Venezuela as Trump declares war on cartels' (Oct 3, 2025): https://www.the-sun.com/news/13671234/us-prepares-seize-ports-venezuela-trump-declares-war-cartels/
- TASS, 'Trump declares war on drug cartels — media' (Oct 3, 2025): https://tass.com/world/1879451
- Vanguard, 'Venezuela wants peace, but will fight US if invaded' (Sep 19, 2025): https://www.vanguardngr.com/2025/09/venezuela-wants-peace-but-will-fight-us-if-invaded-ambassador-padilla/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06 (inclusive), either chamber of the U.S. Congress (House or Senate) holds a floor vote on a War Powers Resolution or similar joint resolution specifically aimed at restricting, limiting, or terminating U.S. military operations related to Venezuela or Venezuela-linked cartel targets. The resolution does not need to pass; a floor vote in either chamber is sufficient. Resolution will be determined by official congressional records available at https://www.congress.gov/ or credible news reporting from sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), or The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com). If no such vote occurs by November 6, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Congressional action on a War Powers Resolution is a critical leading indicator of whether the U.S. will escalate to a full military invasion of Venezuela. If Congress actively moves to restrain the President's military authority, it significantly reduces the probability of an invasion by December 31, 2025, as it would create legal and political barriers. If Congress does not act, it signals acquiescence to the administration's escalating military posture, which could enable further steps toward invasion. This subquestion captures a concrete, observable institutional action that is distinct from the invasion itself but highly informative about its likelihood.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06, either chamber of Congress holds a floor vote on a War Powers Resolution or similar joint resolution specifically aimed at restricting/limiting/terminating U.S. military operations related to Venezuela or Venezuela-linked cartel targets. question: Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”  if, Ukraine signs any written instrument (e.g., treaty, ceasefire/armistice, framework/“roadmap,” exchange of letters, or mediated agreement text) that: (i) includes both Ukraine and the Russian Federation as parties, and (ii) either ends hostilities/establishes a ceasefire or commits both sides to a defined process toward ending the war (i.e., stated objective of peace/normalization plus principles, steps, and/or a timetable) by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

Only Ukraine’s signature is required; Russia’s signature or ratification is not.

Localized, temporary, or issue-specific arrangements—such as airstrike-limitation or deconfliction protocols, humanitarian pauses, evacuation corridors, prisoner-exchange or trade/export arrangements, border/DMZ adjustments, or ceasefires limited to a particular sector/front/municipality—will not qualify.

The document must bear a wet-ink or officially issued electronic signature of an authorized Ukrainian representative. Unsigned agreements (e.g., the 2023 Ohrid arrangement) will not qualify regardless of if they are otherwise officially enacted. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine and Russia hold direct, officially acknowledged bilateral or multilateral negotiations (with both delegations physically present) between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late September 2025, Ukraine and Russia have not held direct face-to-face peace negotiations since the early rounds of talks in Istanbul in spring 2022. Although diplomatic activity has increased—with the U.S. hosting a Trump-Putin summit in Alaska in August 2025 and Trump publicly proposing a meeting between Putin and Zelensky—no direct Ukraine-Russia negotiating session has been confirmed. Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov stated on August 21, 2025 that Putin is 'ready to meet' Zelensky but only after issues are 'well worked out' at expert and ministerial levels, and he raised questions about Zelensky's legitimacy since his term expired in May 2024 (https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PUTIN-PREPARED-TO-MEET-ZEL-148234567/). Ukraine has insisted on a ceasefire as a first step and has rejected territorial concessions as preconditions (https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/18/). The G7 foreign ministers on September 24, 2025 reaffirmed support for Ukraine and pledged to work with the U.S. on 'robust and credible security guarantees' (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/). European allies have outlined five requirements for a peace deal, including a ceasefire as the starting point (various sources from August 2025). The significant gap between the two sides' preconditions—Russia demanding recognition of territorial changes and Ukrainian neutrality, Ukraine demanding a full ceasefire first—means that the initiation of direct talks would be a major leading indicator that a signed peace deal before year-end 2025 is plausible.

Sources:
- Market Screener, 'Putin prepared to meet Zelenskiy but legitimacy an issue, Lavrov says' (Aug 21, 2025): https://www.marketscreener.com
- Ukrainska Pravda, 'Ukraine Rejects Territorial Concessions in Deal with Russia' (Aug 18, 2025): https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/
- Anadolu Agency, 'G7 vows continued support for Ukraine' (Sep 24, 2025): https://www.aa.com.tr/en/
- WION, 'Russia says Putin ready to meet Zelensky' (Aug 21, 2025): https://www.wionews.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), credible international news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, or official government statements from Ukraine or Russia) report that official representatives of both Ukraine and the Russian Federation participated in the same direct negotiation session—whether bilateral or multilateral (e.g., mediated by a third party such as the U.S., Turkey, or the UN). The session must involve both Ukrainian and Russian delegations physically or virtually co-present at the same meeting (not merely parallel or shuttle diplomacy conducted through intermediaries). The meeting must be officially acknowledged by at least one of the two governments (Ukraine or Russia) as a negotiation or peace talk. Informal backchannel contacts, prisoner exchange discussions, or meetings solely between one party and a mediator do not count. If no such meeting is reported by credible sources by November 2, 2025 (allowing two days for reporting lag), this question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- Official Ukrainian presidential website: https://www.president.gov.ua/en
- Official Russian government statements via TASS: https://tass.com/politics
subquestions.rationale: A signed peace deal by December 31, 2025 is virtually impossible without direct negotiations between Ukraine and Russia taking place first. As of October 2025, no such talks have occurred since early 2022, and both sides have significant preconditions. If direct negotiations begin in October, it would dramatically increase the probability of a signed agreement by year-end. Conversely, if October passes without any direct talks, the window for negotiating, drafting, and signing a peace deal by December 31 becomes extremely narrow. This subquestion thus serves as a strong leading indicator: forecasters who believe a 2025 peace deal is likely should assign higher probability to October talks, while skeptics would assign low probability to both.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: Between October 1-31, 2025, official representatives of BOTH Ukraine AND Russia must have participated in the SAME direct negotiation session (bilateral or multilateral), physically or virtually co-present at the same meeting (not shuttle diplomacy), officially acknowledged by at least one government as a negotiation or peace talk. Excluded: informal contacts, prisoner exchange discussions only, or meetings between one party and a mediator only.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Ukraine Russia direct negotiations talks October 2025' - to find any direct talks; 2) 'Ukraine Russia peace talks bilateral meeting 2025' - to find bilateral meetings; 3) 'Ukraine Russia joint negotiation session same room October 2025' - to find co-present sessions; 4) 'Istanbul talks fourth round Ukraine Russia delegates 2025' - to find Istanbul process fourth round; 5) 'fourth round Ukraine Russia talks Istanbul ceasefire negotiations October November 2025' - to find scheduled fourth round.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events reviewed: (1) Istanbul process - three rounds occurred in May, June, and July 2025, with the last round on July 23, 2025. No fourth round held during October. (2) TASS (Oct 9): Kremlin notes Istanbul process 'considerably stalled'; fourth round to be decided only after prior agreements implemented. (3) Kremlin (Oct 1): Expert-level talks needed before any Putin-Zelensky meeting; process paused. (4) Kremlin (Oct 10): Istanbul negotiation process 'on hold.' (5) Turkish FM Fidan (Nov 1): Ready to host FOURTH round - implying no fourth round had been held yet. (6) Russia's Galuzin (Oct 31): Russia 'ready for direct talks' - implying none had yet occurred. (7) Ukraine's Foreign Ministry (Oct 31): Ukraine rebuffs Russia's claims, confirms only three Istanbul rounds occurred. (8) All October activity was shuttle diplomacy: Trump-Putin phone calls, Trump-Zelensky meeting in Washington, US-EU sanctions, Coalition of the Willing. No co-present Ukraine-Russia session found. REJECTED: Body/prisoner exchange handovers (solely humanitarian, not negotiations as defined); MEP-Russian Duma video call (neither Ukrainian nor Russian government representatives in official talks).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of Ukraine and Russia delegations being physically or virtually co-present at the same negotiation session during October 2025. Multiple sources confirm the Istanbul process was 'on hold'/'stalled' as of October 2025: [TASS Oct 9](https://tass.com/politics/2027221), [TASS Oct 9](https://tass.com/politics/2027475), [Yahoo/Kremlin Oct 10](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/kremlin-says-istanbul-negotiation-process-114522204.html). Turkey announced readiness to host FOURTH round on November 1, implying none had occurred yet: [Anadolu Ajansı Nov 1](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/turkiye-ready-to-host-next-round-of-ukraine-russia-peace-talks-possible-leaders-summit-in-istanbul-foreign-minister/3732664). Ukraine itself confirmed (Oct 31) that their Istanbul talks were the only direct sessions, and challenged Russia to agree to a leaders' meeting: [Anadolu Ajansı Oct 31](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/ukraine-rebuffs-russias-claims-over-talks-claiming-putin-does-not-seek-peace-/3732127). The planned Budapest Trump-Putin summit was postponed/cancelled, and Zelensky was excluded from that format anyway.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event (direct Ukraine-Russia co-present negotiation session) occurred within the window. Therefore no timestamp for Yes resolution. Evidence of 'on hold' status is dated October 9-10, 2025, and confirmed through October 31, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the October 1-31, 2025 window. The question is about No resolution - the window closed without any meeting occurring.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification attempts: (1) Checked for any fourth Istanbul round - not scheduled or held in October. (2) Checked Trump-Putin-Zelensky summit in Budapest - planned but then postponed/cancelled; this would not have been a Ukraine-Russia session anyway (it was US-Russia). (3) Checked for any working group sessions or virtual sessions - Russia proposed these but Ukraine had not responded. (4) Russian FM Galuzin (Oct 31) stated Russia is 'ready' for talks - implying they hadn't happened. (5) Ukrainian FM spokesperson (Oct 31) challenged Russia to agree to a leaders' meeting - implying none had happened. (6) Turkish FM (Nov 1) said ready to host 'next' (fourth) round - implying the third (July 23) was still the last. No contradictory evidence found suggesting a meeting occurred.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence consistently confirms that no direct Ukraine-Russia co-present negotiation session occurred during October 1-31, 2025. The Istanbul process was explicitly 'on hold'/'stalled.' All diplomatic activity in October involved shuttle diplomacy (US mediating separately with each side), not direct Ukraine-Russia sessions. The question resolves No. The window closed at October 31, 2025 with no qualifying event having occurred.

subquestions.question: Will Andrew Cuomo officially withdraw from the 2025 New York City mayoral race by September 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2025 NYC mayoral race features a crowded field of non-Democratic candidates competing against Democratic nominee Zohran Mamdani. The key non-Democratic candidates include incumbent Mayor Eric Adams (running as an independent), former Governor Andrew Cuomo (also running as an independent), Republican Curtis Sliwa, and attorney Jim Walden. Both Cuomo and Walden pledged in late July 2025 to drop out if they were not leading in polls by early September, in order to avoid splitting the anti-Mamdani vote (https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/andrew-cuomo-jim-walden-pledge-to-drop-independent-bids-in-nyc-mayoral-race-if-not-leading-come-fall). As of early August, Adams and Cuomo were calling on each other to drop out, with Cuomo's camp calling Adams 'unelectable' and Adams insisting Cuomo should rally behind him as the sitting mayor (https://nystateofpolitics.com/state-of-politics/new-york/2025/07/18/adams-cuomo-call-on-each-other-to-drop-out). Recent polling has generally shown Mamdani with a significant lead, with Adams and Cuomo splitting the moderate/independent vote. If Cuomo drops out and consolidates support behind Adams (or vice versa), it dramatically changes Adams' calculus about whether to remain in the race. Conversely, if Cuomo stays in, the continued vote-splitting may increase pressure on Adams to drop out — or may embolden Adams to stay in, hoping Cuomo eventually exits.

Sources:
- Donald J. Trump site: https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/andrew-cuomo-jim-walden-pledge-to-drop-independent-bids-in-nyc-mayoral-race-if-not-leading-come-fall
- NY State of Politics: https://nystateofpolitics.com/state-of-politics/new-york/2025/07/18/adams-cuomo-call-on-each-other-to-drop-out
- WBAP 820 AM: https://www.wbap.com/2025/08/06/adams-cuomo-refuse-to-drop-out-of-nyc-mayoral-race/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Andrew Cuomo officially withdraws from, suspends, or announces his withdrawal/suspension from the 2025 New York City mayoral race between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-20 (inclusive). Resolution will be based on an official statement from Cuomo or his campaign, or a consensus of credible reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., New York Times, Politico, NY1, New York Post, Daily News). If Cuomo merely signals he might drop out without making a definitive announcement, or if he endorses another candidate but does not formally withdraw, this resolves No. If no credible reports of a withdrawal emerge by end of day September 20, 2025 (ET), this resolves No.

Sources for resolution:
- New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com
- Politico New York: https://www.politico.com/states/new-york
- NY1: https://www.ny1.com
- New York Post: https://www.nypost.com
- New York Daily News: https://www.nydailynews.com
subquestions.rationale: Cuomo's decision to stay in or drop out is one of the most important factors affecting Adams' own calculus. Both Cuomo and Walden pledged to exit by early September if not leading in polls. If Cuomo drops out and endorses Adams, Adams gains a much more viable path to victory and is far less likely to drop out himself. If Cuomo drops out and does NOT endorse Adams (or endorses someone else), this could also shift the race dynamics. If Cuomo stays in despite his earlier pledge, the continued vote-splitting makes both candidates less competitive against Mamdani, potentially increasing pressure on Adams to exit. This is a genuine crux: two forecasters who disagree on whether Adams will drop out likely disagree in part based on what they expect Cuomo to do.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: Andrew Cuomo must officially withdraw from, suspend, or announce his withdrawal/suspension from the 2025 NYC mayoral race between September 1-20, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: Official statement from Cuomo or his campaign, or consensus of credible reporting from at least two major news outlets. Key entities: Andrew Cuomo, 2025 NYC mayoral race. Timing: 2025-09-01T00:00:00Z to 2025-09-20T23:59:59Z.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Andrew Cuomo withdraw drop out NYC mayoral race 2025' (Sept 1-20) — to find any withdrawal announcement. Query 2: 'Cuomo suspends campaign New York City mayor September 2025' (Sept 1-20) — to find suspension of campaign. Query 3: 'Andrew Cuomo drops out withdraws suspends NYC mayor race' (Sept 10-20) — later in window. Query 4: 'Cuomo exits ends campaign New York City mayor September 2025' (Sept 10-20) — later in window. Query 5: 'Cuomo drops out NYC mayor race September 16 17 18 19 20 2025' (Sept 15-20) — final days of window. Query 6: 'NYC mayoral race September 18 19 20 2025 candidates status' (Sept 15-21) — status of all candidates.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Jim Walden (independent) withdrew from the race on September 2, 2025 — but Walden is NOT Cuomo, so this does not satisfy criteria. (2) Andrew Cuomo was actively campaigning throughout the window: praised Walden's exit (Sept 2), urged Adams to drop out (multiple dates), held 9/11 press conference at Ground Zero (Sept 11), walked NYC Fashion Week runway (Sept 12), hired new pollster (Sept 15), attended charter school event (Sept 18), still being described as a candidate through Sept 19. (3) Eric Adams was the candidate being urged to drop out — not Cuomo. No events found where Cuomo withdrew, suspended, or exited the race during the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article from any source (NYT, Politico, NY1, NY Post, Daily News, NBC NY, ABC7, CBS News, AP, Newsday, Marist, Quinnipiac, etc.) reports Andrew Cuomo withdrawing, suspending, or exiting the 2025 NYC mayoral race during the September 1-20, 2025 window. To the contrary, Cuomo is consistently described as an active candidate: [New York Post (Sept 17)](https://nypost.com/2025/09/17/us-news/mayor-eric-adams-andrew-cuomo-buried-below-zohran-mamdani-curtis-sliwa-on-cluttered-nyc-mayoral-election-ballot/) shows Cuomo appearing on the official certified ballot under 'Fight and Deliver' line; [New York Post (Sept 18)](https://nypost.com/2025/09/18/us-news/woody-allen-fawns-over-andrew-cuomo-backs-him-over-zohran-mamdani-for-nyc-mayor/) reports Woody Allen endorsing Cuomo; [TribLIVE (Sept 19)](https://triblive.com/opinion/s-e-cupp-in-nyc-zohran-mamdani-makes-politics-fun/) refers to Cuomo as still a candidate in the race. The ballot was officially certified with Cuomo on it (Board of Elections certified the ballot the week of Sept 11-17, with absentee ballots starting to be mailed on Friday Sept 19).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a Cuomo withdrawal can be extracted because no such event occurred within the window. The most recent articles in the window (Sept 17-19, 2025) all confirm Cuomo was still actively running.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (Cuomo withdrawal/suspension) was found at any point in the September 1-20, 2025 window. The question of 'first occurrence' is moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple sources across the entire window confirm Cuomo remained in the race. The NYC Board of Elections certified the ballot with Cuomo listed under the 'Fight and Deliver' independent line (NY Post, Sept 17). Absentee ballots were being mailed as of September 19, 2025, with Cuomo's name on them. Woody Allen endorsed Cuomo on September 18. Articles from September 19 refer to Cuomo as an active candidate. There is zero report from any credible source of Cuomo withdrawing. The withdrawal speculation throughout this period was focused entirely on Eric Adams and Curtis Sliwa — not Cuomo.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence conclusively shows Andrew Cuomo did NOT withdraw from the NYC mayoral race between September 1-20, 2025. He was actively campaigning, appeared on the certified ballot, received endorsements, and was reported as a candidate through at least September 19, 2025. The condition for Yes resolution was never met. Resolution is No, with the window closing at 2025-09-20T23:59:59Z.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House Oversight Committee issue a subpoena to the Walz administration or Minnesota state agencies in connection with the Minnesota fraud probe between December 29, 2025, and January 21, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:

As of late December 2025, Comer warned that 'the walls are caving in on Tim Walz' and indicated the probe was incorporating whistleblower testimony, subpoenas, and federal agency coordination (Fox News, Dec 23, 2025). Comer had previously threatened subpoenas for withheld information (Redstate, Dec 12, 2025). Multiple Trump cabinet officials, including Education Secretary Linda McMahon and SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler, have publicly called for Walz to resign or accused him of obstructing investigations. Governor Walz has acknowledged responsibility but questioned the scope of claimed fraud figures, calling them politically motivated. Whether the congressional investigation escalates through formal subpoena power could significantly increase political pressure on Walz and signal whether the scandal reaches a level that could force a resignation.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between December 29, 2025, and January 21, 2026 (inclusive), the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Accountability issues at least one formal subpoena directed at the Walz administration, any Minnesota state agency (e.g., Minnesota Department of Human Services, Minnesota Department of Education), or any current or former official of these entities in connection with the Minnesota fraud investigations. subquestions.rationale: The escalation of the congressional investigation is a key leading indicator of whether political pressure on Walz intensifies to the point where resignation becomes more likely. A formal subpoena would signal that the probe is producing actionable findings and that Congress is willing to use compulsory process against Walz's administration—substantially increasing the political and legal pressure on him. Forecasters who believe Walz is likely to resign would probably also expect the investigation to escalate rapidly, while those who think he will ride out the storm would expect the probe to stall or remain at the rhetorical level. This makes it a meaningful crux for disagreements about the ultimate question.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The House Oversight Committee did not issue a formal subpoena to the Walz administration or any Minnesota state agency in connection with the Minnesota fraud probe between December 29, 2025 and January 21, 2026. question: Ukraine recognizes Russian sovereignty over its territory by December 31, 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to formally recognize Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement. 

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory for any amount of time will count.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995, “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia, which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement, is an example of a qualifying agreement.

An official unilateral pledge by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution even if not part of an agreement with Russia.

The April 19, 2013, Brussels Agreement between Serbia and Kosovo, in which Serbia recognized Kosovo’s de facto administration but did not formally grant de jure recognition, would not be considered a qualifying agreement under this market, as this market requires formal recognition of sovereignty rather than acknowledgment of administrative control.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine and Russia hold direct, officially acknowledged bilateral negotiations (in person or via videoconference) between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, Ukraine and Russia have not engaged in direct bilateral peace negotiations. Most diplomatic activity has been mediated through third parties, primarily the United States and various European actors. In April–May 2025, the Trump administration presented proposals that included US recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea and de facto acceptance of Russian control over other occupied territories, but Ukraine firmly rejected formal cession of any territory. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has stated that formally surrendering land is a constitutional red line, and Ukrainian lawmakers have been nearly unanimous in opposing de jure recognition of Russian sovereignty over any Ukrainian territory (https://kyivindependent.com/dangerous-and-cruel-trumps-reported-crimea-proposal-sparks-horror-among-ukraines-lawmakers/). Russia, for its part, has demanded preconditions such as Ukraine halting mobilization and ceasing acceptance of foreign military aid before agreeing to a full ceasefire (https://www.rt.com/news/616089-ukraine-cede-land-russia-trump-envoy/). The European Union has also rejected US proposals to recognize Crimea as Russian (https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/04/23/brussels-rejects-russian-recognition-of-crimea-and-sanctions-relief). Without direct talks between Kyiv and Moscow, any agreement — let alone one involving territorial recognition — remains extremely unlikely. The initiation of direct negotiations would therefore be a critical early indicator of whether a deal recognizing Russian sovereignty over Ukrainian territory could materialize by end of 2025.

Sources:
- Kyiv Independent: https://kyivindependent.com/dangerous-and-cruel-trumps-reported-crimea-proposal-sparks-horror-among-ukraines-lawmakers/
- RT (Trump envoy report): https://www.rt.com/news/616089-ukraine-cede-land-russia-trump-envoy/
- Euronews (Brussels rejects Crimea recognition): https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/04/23/brussels-rejects-russian-recognition-of-crimea-and-sanctions-relief
- Yahoo News (Ukrainians reject Crimea surrender): https://www.yahoo.com/news/shocked-us-peace-proposal-ukrainians-090028498.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), Ukraine and Russia hold or publicly announce they have scheduled direct bilateral negotiations (whether in person, via videoconference, or through formally designated bilateral negotiating teams meeting face to face). The negotiations must be officially acknowledged by both the Ukrainian government and the Russian government (e.g., through statements from the respective presidents, foreign ministries, or official spokespeople). Talks mediated solely through a third party (e.g., US shuttle diplomacy, or UN-mediated discussions where Ukrainian and Russian delegations do not directly engage with each other) do not count. The primary resolution sources will be official statements from the Ukrainian President's Office (https://www.president.gov.ua/en) and the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.mid.ru/en/). If official statements are unavailable, resolution may rely on an overwhelming consensus of credible international media reporting (e.g., Reuters https://www.reuters.com/, Associated Press https://apnews.com/, BBC https://www.bbc.com/news) confirming that direct bilateral negotiations took place or were formally scheduled. If the event is announced but postponed beyond October 1, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For Ukraine to formally recognize Russian sovereignty over any of its territory by December 31, 2025, a necessary precondition is that Ukraine and Russia are actually engaged in direct negotiations. As of September 2025, no such direct talks have occurred; all diplomatic channels have been indirect. The commencement of direct bilateral negotiations within the next month would be a strong early signal that a deal — including potentially one involving territorial recognition — could be reached within the ultimate question's timeframe. Conversely, the absence of any direct talks would strongly suggest that the ultimate question will resolve No, since there would be insufficient diplomatic runway to negotiate and announce such a monumental agreement by year's end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Ukraine and Russia must hold or formally schedule direct bilateral negotiations (in person or videoconference) between Sept 1–Oct 1, 2025, officially acknowledged by BOTH governments. Key entities: Ukrainian President's Office / Zelensky government; Russian government / MFA. Must be direct (no third-party-only mediation). Observable evidence: official statements from both sides confirming a meeting took or will take place within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Ukraine Russia direct bilateral negotiations talks September 2025' - to find any direct meetings in the window; 2) 'Ukraine Russia peace talks direct meeting September October 2025' - broader search for any format; 3) 'Ukraine Russia Istanbul talks negotiations September 2025 fourth round' - checking if Istanbul process continued; 4) 'Medinsky Ukraine delegation direct talks meeting September 2025' - checking if delegation-level talks occurred; 5) 'Ukraine Russia new round direct talks September October 2025 scheduled' - checking for scheduled meetings; 6) 'Zelensky Putin direct meeting bilateral summit September 2025' - checking for high-level direct talks
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Three prior rounds in Istanbul (May, June, July 23) - all BEFORE the Sept 1 window, rejected. (B) Kremlin announcement on Sept 12 that talks are 'on pause' - this is a negative indicator, not a qualifying event. (C) Putin's invitation to Zelensky to come to Moscow (Sept 3-5) - no accepted meeting, rejected. (D) Zelensky's UNGA appearance (Sept 23-24) - met Trump, not Putin/Russia delegation directly, rejected. (E) Lavrov-Rubio meeting at UNGA (Sept 30) - US-Russia, not Ukraine-Russia, rejected. (F) Peskov's Sept 24 statement that Ukraine hadn't responded to working group proposals - negative indicator. No qualifying direct Ukraine-Russia bilateral event found within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that satisfies the criteria. Multiple sources confirm talks were explicitly 'on pause' as of September 12, 2025 [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2016099), [Ukrinform](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/4035865-kremlin-says-russiaukraine-talks-are-on-pause.html), [RT](https://www.rt.com/russia/624568-kremlin-peace-talks-pause/). Ukraine's NSDC head Umerov stated on Sept 19 that 'no cease-fire negotiations are currently underway' [Charter97](https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/9/19/656324/). Zelensky at UNGA on Sept 24 criticized Putin for refusing direct talks [Meduza](https://meduza.io/en/news/2025/09/24/without-china-putin-s-russia-is-nothing-zelensky-tells-u-n-security-council). Peskov on Sept 24 confirmed Ukraine had not responded to Russia's proposals for working groups [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2020681). Vance on ~Sept 28 confirmed Russia was 'unwilling to negotiate bilaterally or trilaterally' [Unz Review](https://www.unz.com/article/when-tomahawk-meets-bear-the-hazel-tree-oreshnik-wins/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event to timestamp. The 'pause' announcement was made on September 12, 2025, and remained in effect through at least September 30, 2025 (end of window). The last qualifying direct talks were on July 23, 2025, before the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable - no qualifying event occurred within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Putin stated on Sept 3 that Moscow is 'open to bringing direct negotiations with Ukraine to a truly high political level' [RT Sept 3] - but this is an expression of willingness, not an actual meeting. Zelensky stated willingness to meet bilaterally or trilaterally on Sept 16-17 [TASS, RT] - but no meeting materialized. Turkey's Erdogan at UNGA (Sept 23) said he would 'continue efforts for a ceasefire' and praised the Istanbul process, but noted no new round had taken place [Interfax-Ukraine]. All evidence consistently points to talks being paused with no new meetings during the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution = No. The Kremlin explicitly confirmed on September 12, 2025 that Russia-Ukraine negotiations were 'on pause.' Multiple independent, high-quality sources (TASS, Ukrinform, RT, Macau Business, Anadolu Agency, Taipei Times) corroborate this. No direct bilateral talks occurred or were formally scheduled during September 1–October 1, 2025. The last talks were in Istanbul on July 23 (before the window). Both sides expressed willingness to negotiate in principle but could not agree on format/venue or agenda. The window closed without any qualifying event. Resolution datetime = end of window: 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z.

If this resolves Yes, it would significantly increase the probability of a pregnancy announcement before year-end; if No, it modestly decreases the probability since it suggests business-as-usual.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: (1) Taylor Swift cancels/postpones/skips a previously scheduled professional commitment in Oct 2025, AND (2) at least two major entertainment outlets (People, TMZ, E! The deployment of a carrier strike group or additional missile-defense assets to the region is often a precursor to or concurrent with major Israeli military operations, as it provides both defensive cover and a signal of U.S. political backing. As of late September 2025, the USS Harry S. Truman Carrier Strike Group is operating in the Mediterranean, and the U.S. maintains CENTCOM assets in the Gulf region. subquestions.question: Will the United States and Iran reach a nuclear deal or formal diplomatic agreement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?

subquestions.question: Will a woman appear on TIME Magazine's November 2025 shortlist or 'Person of the Year' speculation coverage as a leading candidate?
subquestions.background_information:
Each year, TIME Magazine announces its Person of the Year in early-to-mid December. In the weeks leading up to the announcement, TIME and other media outlets publish shortlists, reader polls, and speculative coverage about likely candidates. In 2024, TIME's shortlist included figures such as Donald Trump (who won), Kamala Harris, Kate Middleton, and others. In 2023, Taylor Swift won the award. Recent reporting from Showbiz411 (October 10, 2025) suggested TIME may be distancing itself from awarding Donald Trump again, with an editorial criticizing his Nobel Peace Prize campaign. Meanwhile, a Just Jared article from September 30, 2025, cited reports that Trump was 'reportedly set to be named' Person of the Year for a second time. The mixed signals make the identity of the 2025 honoree uncertain. Historically, women have won the individual Person of the Year award relatively rarely — notable recent winners include Taylor Swift (2023), Greta Thunberg (2019), and Angela Merkel (2015). Whether a woman features prominently in the pre-announcement speculation and shortlist coverage can serve as an early indicator of the final selection.

Sources:
- Showbiz411: TIME Magazine Seems To Shut the Door on Trump Getting Person of the Year (October 10, 2025): https://www.showbiz411.com/2025/10/10/time-magazine-seems-to-shut-the-door-on-trump-getting-person-of-the-year-with-damning-nobel-peace-prize-editorial

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), TIME Magazine publishes an official shortlist, reader poll, or equivalent 'Person of the Year' candidates feature for 2025 that includes at least one woman as a named candidate, OR if at least three major English-language news outlets (e.g., CNN, BBC, The New York Times, The Washington Post, Reuters, AP, The Guardian) publish articles between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 identifying a specific woman as a leading or frontrunner candidate for TIME's 2025 Person of the Year. The woman must be identified by name, and the coverage must specifically discuss her as a serious contender (not merely listed among dozens of possibilities). If TIME does not publish a shortlist or poll by November 30, 2025, resolution relies solely on the three-major-outlet criterion. If neither condition is met by November 30, 2025, the question resolves No.

Primary sources for resolution:

subquestions.rationale: TIME's Person of the Year announcement in December is typically preceded by weeks of shortlist speculation and official reader polls in November. If a woman features prominently as a leading candidate in this pre-announcement coverage, it significantly raises the probability that a woman will ultimately be selected. Conversely, if November speculation is dominated entirely by male candidates (e.g., Trump, Zelensky, or other male world leaders), it would be a strong indicator that the final pick is unlikely to be a woman. This subquestion captures an observable early signal — the composition of the speculative shortlist — that is distinct from the final announcement itself but highly correlated with the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: (1) TIME publishes official shortlist/poll Oct 31–Nov 30 with named woman, OR (2) at least 3 major outlets (CNN, BBC, NYT, WaPo, Reuters, AP, Guardian) publish articles Oct 31–Nov 30 identifying a specific named woman as a leading/frontrunner TIME 2025 Person of the Year candidate. evidence.step8_final_decision: Neither condition for Yes resolution was met within the Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025 window. TIME did not publish an official shortlist with a named woman, and no evidence exists of three major specified outlets identifying a named woman as a leading or frontrunner candidate for TIME's 2025 POTY.
