Resolution: No. The window closed without a qualifying event, so resolution_datetime = 2025-11-30T23:59:59Z.

question: Will Eric Adams endorse Cuomo?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Eric Adams announces that he will vote for Andrew Cuomo or endorses Cuomo for the 2025 NYC Mayor election between June 25, and November 4, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

If  Eric Adams announces that he will vote for another candidate or endorses another candidate for NYC Mayor this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Eric Adams or one of his representatives, or a consensus of credible reporting of Adams' endorsement.

subquestions.question: Will Eric Adams publicly call on Andrew Cuomo to drop out of the NYC mayoral race (or vice versa, Cuomo call on Adams to drop out) between September 1 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2025 NYC mayoral general election features Democratic nominee Zohran Mamdani leading in polls with ~44% support, followed by Andrew Cuomo running as an independent (~25%), Republican Curtis Sliwa (~12%), and incumbent Mayor Eric Adams (~7%). There has been widespread discussion among business leaders and political figures about the need for either Adams or Cuomo to drop out to consolidate the anti-Mamdani vote. Former Gov. David Paterson, who previously supported Cuomo in the primary, switched to endorsing Adams in August 2025, and has suggested one of the two should step aside. Attorney Jim Walden has proposed a ranked-choice poll pledge to determine which non-Democratic candidate should face Mamdani one-on-one, with Cuomo signing on but Adams not yet agreeing. Cuomo has previously urged other candidates to coalesce behind the strongest opponent, but Adams has refused to drop out. As of late August 2025, there is no indication that Adams plans to endorse Cuomo or vice versa; instead, both camps appear to be competing for the same lane of moderate/centrist voters opposed to Mamdani.

Sources:
- NewsMax, "Fmr N.Y. Gov. Paterson to Endorse Adams in Mayoral Race" (2025-08-13): https://www.newsmax.com
- The Hill, "Former NY governor endorsing Eric Adams for NYC mayor" (2025-08-13): https://thehill.com
- CBS News, "Former Gov. David Paterson endorsing Eric Adams for reelection" (2025-08-13): https://www.cbsnews.com
- NewsMax, "Mamdani Leaves NY Business Leaders Divided on Opposition Strategy" (2025-07-22): https://www.newsmax.com
- The Wave, "Editorial: Jim Walden To The Rescue?" (2025-07-18): https://rockawave.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), Eric Adams publicly calls on Andrew Cuomo to withdraw from the mayoral race, OR Andrew Cuomo publicly calls on Eric Adams to withdraw from the mayoral race. A 'public call' must be a direct, on-the-record statement (e.g., in a press conference, interview, official social media post, or campaign statement) explicitly urging the other candidate to drop out or step aside. Vague suggestions that 'someone' should consolidate do not count — the statement must specifically name the other candidate. Resolution will be based on credible reporting from major news outlets such as the New York Times, New York Post, Politico New York, or NY1, or official statements from the Adams or Cuomo campaigns. If no such public call occurs by September 30, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Adams and Cuomo are publicly pressuring each other to drop out is a key indicator of whether an endorsement could follow. If Adams publicly calls on Cuomo to drop out, it signals he views the race as competitive and himself as the stronger candidate — making an Adams-endorses-Cuomo outcome very unlikely. Conversely, if Cuomo publicly calls on Adams to drop out (and Adams's poll numbers remain very low), this increases pressure on Adams to exit the race and potentially endorse Cuomo. The absence of any such public calls would suggest the status quo continues — both running independently with no endorsement forthcoming. This is a different observable event from the endorsement itself, but it directly tracks the political dynamics that would precede or preclude an endorsement.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Eric Adams publicly calls on Andrew Cuomo to withdraw from the mayoral race, OR Andrew Cuomo publicly calls on Eric Adams to withdraw, between September 1-30, 2025. The statement must be direct, on-the-record, explicitly naming the other candidate, and reported by credible outlets.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: 'Eric Adams Andrew Cuomo drop out NYC mayoral race 2025', 'Adams Cuomo withdraw step aside NYC mayor race September 2025', 'Andrew Cuomo calls on Eric Adams drop out withdraw mayoral race 2025', 'Cuomo urges Adams step aside NYC mayor race September 2025', 'Adams Cuomo drop out called on NYC mayor race mutual challenge 2025', 'Eric Adams tells Andrew Cuomo drop out OR step aside NYC mayor 2025', 'Cuomo asked Adams drop out arrogance mayor race July 2025', 'Adams Cuomo drop-out challenge NYC mayor race August September 2025', 'Cuomo calls on Adams drop out NYC mayor September 2025 direct', 'Adams blames Cuomo drop out rumors September 2025 NYC mayor'
evidence.step3_event_detection: 1. July 7, 2025 (BEFORE window): Cuomo privately asked Adams to drop out; Adams publicly revealed this and rejected it. Multiple sources confirm this is a July event. 2. September 2, 2025: NBC New York/AP News article states 'both Adams and Cuomo have called on the other to drop out' — ambiguous timing, appears to reference July history. 3. September 12, 2025: Adams blamed Cuomo for spreading rumors he was dropping out, but no direct call for Cuomo to drop out. 4. September 28-29, 2025: Chosun.com states Cuomo 'has reportedly urged Adams to step down' — vague, unspecified timing, no direct quote within September window. 5. The Western Journal (September 29): 'Former Gov. Andrew Cuomo has urged other candidates to drop out' — general statement, not specifically naming Adams within September window. REJECTED: Most evidence of direct mutual calls is from July 2025, outside the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution requires a direct, on-the-record statement explicitly urging the other candidate specifically to drop out, within September 1-30, 2025. The NBC New York article [https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/politics/jim-walden-drops-out-nyc-mayoral-race-unite-against-zohran-mamdani/6382232/] states 'both Adams and Cuomo have called on the other to drop out' in a September 2 article, but this appears to reference prior (July) history. The Chosun.com article [https://www.chosun.com/english/world-en/2025/09/29/FX2EQCWJJJA6VG33UEVTR2SEXI/] says Cuomo 'has reportedly urged Adams to step down' with no specific date or direct quote. The WCIV article from September 4 [https://abcnews4.com/news/nation-world/new-york-city-mayor-eric-adams-denies-being-offered-trump-administration-job-in-exchange-for-quitting-mayoral-race-independent-democratic-nominee-mamdani-cuomo] references 'In July, Adams said Cuomo asked him to drop out' — confirming the key Cuomo-to-Adams call was in July. No direct, on-the-record statement from within September 1-30 specifically naming the other and explicitly calling on them to drop out was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The clearest timestamp for a qualifying event is July 7, 2025 — outside the window. Within the September 1-30 window, the NBC New York article of September 2 mentions mutual calls but references prior events. No exact timestamp for a new, qualifying September-window statement was found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first occurrence of the mutual calls appears to be in July 2025 (July 7, 2025 specifically), before the September 1, 2025 window start date. No clear first occurrence of a new, qualifying call within the September window was established.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Multiple September 2025 articles show Adams refusing to call on Cuomo to drop out and instead insisting he himself would stay in the race. Cuomo's September statements after Adams dropped out (September 28-29) were praising Adams' decision, not calling on him to drop out. The key prior mutual call evidence is from July 2025. The NBC New York September 2 article references this history without establishing a new September call.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The key Cuomo-to-Adams call to drop out occurred in July 2025, before the September 1 window. The Adams-to-Cuomo calls appear to also be from July 2025 or referenced as historical background by the September 2 NBC New York article. No direct, on-the-record, explicitly named call within September 1-30, 2025 was confirmed with a reliable timestamp. The evidence is insufficient to conclude Yes with the required precision, but the NBC New York September 2, 2025 article states 'both Adams and Cuomo have called on the other to drop out' — this is within the window but appears to describe prior history, making resolution ambiguous. Given the strict criteria requiring explicit evidence within the window, and that the primary evidence (July 7 events) predates the window, this resolves No.

question: Will tariffs generate >$250b in 2025?
description:
The U.S. government collected $82.2b in customs duties in FY 2025 (See: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/files/reports-statements/financial-report/2024/notes-to-the-financial-statements19.pdf).

This market will resolve to "Yes"  if the value of costumes duties collected in FY 2025 according to the Financial Report of the United States Government published by the Treasury Department for FY 2025 (See: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/financial-report/) is greater than $250b. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No". 

If the Treasury Department does not publish relevant data  for FY 2025 by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No". 

The resolution source will be the Treasury Department.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury report cumulative gross customs duties of at least $200 billion for FY 2025 through August 2025 in the Monthly Treasury Statement?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. fiscal year 2025 runs from October 1, 2024, to September 30, 2025. For the ultimate question of whether tariffs generate more than $250 billion in FY 2025, the trajectory of customs duty collections through the penultimate month (August) is a critical leading indicator. As of the end of July 2025, cumulative customs duties reached approximately $150 billion on a gross basis, with monthly collections hitting records of $27.2 billion in June and $28 billion in July. Higher 'reciprocal' tariffs on U.S. trading partners took effect on August 1, 2025, which President Trump and Treasury Secretary Bessent indicated would significantly increase collections further. Bessent has predicted tariffs may generate more than $300 billion in revenue for the full fiscal year. If cumulative collections through August reach $200 billion, that would mean September would need to generate approximately $50 billion to cross the $250 billion threshold — a plausible amount given recent monthly trends. If collections fall well short of $200 billion through August, reaching $250 billion for the full year becomes much harder. The Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) for August is typically published in mid-September and reports customs duties as a line item under government receipts.

Sources:
- Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement: https://fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mts/
- July tariff revenues break monthly record: https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/articles/july-tariff-revenues-break-monthly-record/
- US customs duties top $100B for first time: https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/us-customs-duties-top-100-billion-first-time-fiscal-year-2025-07-11/
- Benzinga report on customs duties exceeding $100B: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/07/45709858/amid-trump-tariffs-us-customs-duty-collection-exceeds-100-billion-in-a-fiscal-year-for-the-first-time
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) for August 2025, published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, reports cumulative gross customs duties collected during FY 2025 (October 2024 through August 2025) of at least $200 billion. The relevant data can be found in the MTS 'Receipts' table under 'Customs duties' (gross basis, before refunds). The MTS is available at https://fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mts/. If the August 2025 MTS is not published by 2025-10-01, or if it does not contain customs duty data, this question resolves No. For avoidance of doubt, the $200 billion threshold refers to the 'fiscal year-to-date' gross customs duties figure reported in the August 2025 MTS.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion tracks the cumulative customs duty trajectory through August 2025 — the second-to-last month of FY 2025. If cumulative collections reach $200 billion through August, then September would need only ~$50 billion to hit $250 billion for the full year, which is very plausible given June ($27B) and July ($28B) collections, especially with reciprocal tariffs in effect since August 1. If collections are well below $200 billion, reaching $250 billion becomes much harder. This makes the $200 billion threshold a meaningful crux: forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question are likely to find that the August cumulative figure substantially updates their beliefs about whether $250 billion will be reached for the full fiscal year.

subquestions.question: Will French Prime Minister François Bayrou lose a confidence vote in the National Assembly between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A confidence vote on Prime Minister François Bayrou's budget plan is scheduled for September 8, 2025. Bayrou has proposed approximately €44 billion in spending cuts and tax increases, including scrapping two public holidays and freezing spending increases. Opposition from both the far-right National Rally (led by Marine Le Pen) and the far-left France Unbowed (led by Jean-Luc Mélenchon) makes his survival uncertain. Bayrou's predecessor, Michel Barnier, was ousted after only three months via a similar no-confidence motion in late 2024. If Bayrou loses, he must resign along with his government, leaving Macron to either reappoint him, choose a seventh prime minister since 2017, or call new elections. The hard-left has explicitly called on Macron to resign if the government falls, with Mélenchon stating 'Macron is chaos... He must go.' However, Macron has repeatedly and firmly stated he will serve out his term until 2027, saying on August 29, 2025: 'The mandate which has been given to me by the French people, and by no-one else, is a mandate that will be carried out through to the end of its term.' The Paris stock exchange fell roughly 2% amid the political uncertainty, and French sovereign bond yields have risen.

Sources:
- France 24: https://www.france24.com
- The Straits Times, 'France's Macron vows to serve out term despite budget crisis' (Aug 29, 2025): https://www.straitstimes.com
- Hurriyet Daily News, 'Fears of new political crisis grip France' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com

The question resolves No if no such vote occurs or if Bayrou survives all confidence/no-confidence votes held during this period. Resolution will be based on official records of the French National Assembly (https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/) or a consensus of credible reporting from sources such as France 24 (https://www.france24.com), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), and Le Monde (https://www.lemonde.fr). If Bayrou survives, the political pressure on Macron eases substantially, making his departure in 2025 extremely unlikely. If Bayrou falls, it creates the chaotic political environment in which opposition calls for Macron's resignation intensify, parliament could be dissolved again, and the scenario for Macron's departure — while still unlikely given his stated intentions — becomes more plausible. subquestions.question: Will Israel withdraw from all five of its military positions in southern Lebanon by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Since the November 2024 ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, Israel has maintained troops at five strategic positions inside southern Lebanon. A key reason Hezbollah has given for refusing to disarm is Israel's continued occupation of Lebanese territory and ongoing military strikes. Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem has repeatedly stated that 'the resistance will not hand over its weapons as long as aggression and occupation continue' (Middle East Eye, 2025-09-09). Israel has conditioned its withdrawal on Lebanese efforts to disarm Hezbollah, with PM Netanyahu offering a 'phased' pullout only if Lebanon follows through on disarmament plans (BSS, 2025-08-25). Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has stated that 'the IDF isn't withdrawing — and with God's help, won't withdraw — from the five positions' (The Duran, 2025-08-03). Lebanese officials have insisted that Israel must first commit to a full cessation of hostilities and withdrawal before disarmament can proceed. This creates a deadlock: Hezbollah won't disarm while Israel occupies Lebanese territory, and Israel won't withdraw until Hezbollah disarms. An Israeli withdrawal would remove one of Hezbollah's primary justifications for retaining its weapons, potentially shifting internal Lebanese political dynamics toward disarmament.

Sources:
- Middle East Eye, 'Lebanon: What will it take to disarm Hezbollah?', 2025-09-09: https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/lebanon-what-will-it-take-disarm-hezbollah
- BSS, 'Israel PM offers phased withdrawal if Lebanon disarms Hezbollah', 2025-08-25: https://www.bssnews.net/news/international/189273
- The Duran, 'Beirut walks a political tightrope without a safety net', 2025-08-03: https://theduran.com/beirut-walks-a-political-tightrope-without-a-safety-net/
- The Express Tribune, 'Hezbollah refuses to be disarmed', 2025-09-27: https://tribune.com.pk/story/2506789/hezbollah-refuses-to-be-disarmed
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, credible reporting from at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, Al Jazeera) confirms that Israel has fully withdrawn its military forces from all five positions it has maintained inside southern Lebanon since the November 2024 ceasefire. 'Fully withdrawn' means no Israeli military personnel remain stationed at any of the five positions. Temporary cross-border incursions or patrols that do not constitute permanent or semi-permanent stationing do not prevent resolution as Yes, provided the five fixed positions are vacated. If Israel withdraws from some but not all five positions, or if withdrawal is announced but not completed by 2025-10-31, the question resolves No. If reporting is ambiguous or contradictory, the question resolves based on UNIFIL situation reports (https://unifil.unmissions.org/) and official Israeli Defense Forces statements (https://www.idf.il/en/).
subquestions.rationale: Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon is a critical precondition that Hezbollah has explicitly cited for any discussion of disarmament. If Israel withdraws, it removes Hezbollah's primary stated justification for retaining weapons, which could shift the political calculus in Lebanon and make a formal disarmament announcement more plausible before year-end. Conversely, continued Israeli occupation makes Hezbollah disarmament in 2025 virtually impossible, as it gives the group both political cover and genuine security rationale for maintaining its arsenal. This is a genuine crux: forecasters who believe Hezbollah might disarm likely expect some movement on the Israeli withdrawal front, while those who see disarmament as near-impossible likely expect the occupation to persist.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, credible reporting from at least two major international news outlets confirms Israel has FULLY withdrawn from ALL FIVE military positions it has maintained inside southern Lebanon since the November 2024 ceasefire — meaning no Israeli military personnel remain stationed at any of the five positions. Key entities: Israel Defense Forces (IDF), five border outposts in southern Lebanon, UNIFIL. Threshold: Complete withdrawal from all five positions. Timing: Must occur and be confirmed within October 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Israel withdraw military positions southern Lebanon 2025' (Sept–Oct 2025) — to find any withdrawal announcements or completions. Query 2: 'Israel five positions Lebanon ceasefire withdrawal deadline' (Jan–Oct 2025) — to track the history of withdrawal deadlines and status. Query 3: 'Israel complete withdrawal Lebanon five outposts October 2025' — to check for any October 2025 completion of withdrawal. Query 4: 'Israel Lebanon border positions vacated completed withdrawal' (Oct 2025) — to search for any vacating of all five positions.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: Multiple reports from October 1–30, 2025 consistently state Israel 'continues to maintain military presence at five border outposts' (AP, AFP, Anadolu Agency, Qatar News Agency, Daily Sabah, Yahoo News, Al-Manar TV, American Spectator). No articles found reporting any withdrawal from any of the five positions. On October 30, Israeli troops actively raided Blida, a town inside Lebanon. Israel conducted large-scale military drills near Lebanon border (Oct 24). As of August 25, 2025, Netanyahu stated withdrawal would only happen conditionally if Hezbollah is disarmed — a condition not met. No withdrawal events detected.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All evidence found is directly contrary to resolution as Yes. Multiple sources from throughout October 2025 — including [AP (August 25)](https://apnews.com/93215f1301904961f2dabf82f47fc380), [AFP (October 24)](http://doc.afp.com/79WV4WF), [Yahoo/Reuters (October 30)](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/israeli-troops-kill-municipal-worker-110926872.html), [Anadolu Agency (October 29)](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-praises-lebanese-army-for-efforts-to-molopolize-weapons/3729836) — all confirm Israel still maintains military presence at all five border outposts as of the end of October 2025. The criteria require full withdrawal from all five positions, which explicitly did not happen.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The question resolves No. No qualifying withdrawal event exists. The evidence definitively shows Israel maintained all five positions throughout the entire October 2025 window. The window closed at 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z with no withdrawal completed. Since Israel was still actively occupying the positions as late as October 30, 2025 (with troops raiding Blida and conducting exercises near the Lebanon border), the condition for Yes was never met during the resolution window.

evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: None found. No source in any search reported Israel completing withdrawal from any of the five positions during October 2025. The American Spectator (Oct 19) noted Israel was conditioning withdrawal on Hezbollah disarmament. Netanyahu's August 25 statement confirmed withdrawal would only be staged/conditional. Hezbollah itself cited Israel's continued occupation of all five outposts as justification for retaining its own arms. The October 30 raid into Blida confirms Israel was actively moving INTO Lebanon, not withdrawing. IDF completed five-day military exercises near Lebanon border October 24, indicating a posture of presence, not withdrawal.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is definitively No. Multiple credible major international sources (AP, AFP, Anadolu Agency, Yahoo News, Qatar News Agency, TASS) from throughout October 2025 consistently confirm that Israel maintained military presence at all five border outposts in southern Lebanon during the entire October 2025 window. subquestions.question: Will Israel's Prime Minister publicly announce or confirm plans for a new military strike on Iran during his visit to Washington, D.C. before February 5, 2026?

Reports indicate that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu plans to present proposals for a new attack on Iran to President Trump during an upcoming visit to Washington. Israel is particularly concerned about Iran rebuilding and expanding its ballistic missile production capacity, with estimates of up to 3,000 missiles per year if unchecked. Meanwhile, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi claimed on December 21, 2025, that all damaged strategic facilities have been 'fully reconstructed,' asserting Iran's readiness for renewed conflict. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei stated on January 5, 2026, that Iran is 'intensifying efforts to safeguard its territorial integrity' and does not trust external statements. A public Israeli commitment to new strikes on Iran would be a strong leading indicator that the ceasefire could break before March 31, 2026.

Vague warnings, general deterrence rhetoric (e.g., 'we will defend ourselves'), or unnamed source reporting alone do not qualify. subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if any movie that had its wide theatrical release in the United States between January 1, 2025, and November 20, 2025 (inclusive) achieved a 3-day domestic opening weekend gross of $150 million or more, as reported on The Numbers (https://www.the-numbers.com/). The relevant figure is the movie's first 3-day weekend (Friday–Sunday) domestic gross as listed in its 'Weekend Box Office Performance' table on The Numbers. This question covers the period from 2025-10-31 (start_date) to 2025-11-22 (end_date), meaning resolution will be assessed based on data available by November 22, 2025. If The Numbers data is unavailable, Box Office Mojo (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/) will be used as a fallback. If no finalized data is available by November 22, 2025, the question resolves based on the best available estimates from these sources.
subquestions.rationale: Whether any 2025 film already crossed $150M in its domestic opening weekend is a key crux for the ultimate question. If the bar is already set at or above $150M, Wicked: For Good would need to hit the high end of its tracking range to claim #1, making a 'No' resolution to the ultimate question more likely. If no film has reached $150M, then Wicked: For Good's projected $112M-$155M range makes it highly likely to be the top opener (with only Avatar: Fire and Ash in December as a remaining threat). This subquestion is observable before Wicked opens and directly informs the competitive landscape.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Any movie with a wide theatrical release in the US between January 1, 2025, and November 20, 2025 (inclusive) must have achieved a 3-day domestic opening weekend gross of $150 million or more, as reported by The Numbers (or Box Office Mojo as fallback). Observable evidence: box office reports from The Numbers or major entertainment news citing official box office figures for the first Friday-Sunday weekend. Key threshold: $150M domestic 3-day gross. Timing: release date must be on or before November 20, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. '2025 movie opening weekend box office $150 million' - to find general candidates; 2. 'highest grossing opening weekend 2025 domestic box office record' - to find top openers; 3. 'A Minecraft Movie opening weekend box office domestic gross' - to check specific candidate; 4. 'Lilo Stitch 2025 opening weekend domestic box office gross million' - to check specific candidate; 5. 'Jurassic World Rebirth opening weekend domestic box office 2025' - to check specific candidate; 6. '2025 top opening weekends list domestic box office rankings' - to confirm year rankings; 7. 'Wicked For Good opening weekend box office results November 2025' - to check November candidate; 8. 'November 2025 box office opening weekend domestic results' - for recent data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) A Minecraft Movie (April 4-6, 2025): Multiple sources confirm $157 million domestic 3-day opening (revised to $162.8-163 million in some reports). One article mentions '$162.8 million debut' for Minecraft. This clearly exceeds $150M. (2) Lilo & Stitch (May 23-25, 2025): Multiple sources confirm ~$183 million domestic 3-day opening weekend. Clearly exceeds $150M. (3) Jurassic World: Rebirth (July 2-6, 2025): 3-day opening was ~$91.5 million (CinemaBlend confirmed); the 5-day holiday extended weekend was ~$147-148 million domestic. The 3-day figure does NOT meet $150M threshold. (4) Superman (July 10-13, 2025): $122 million 3-day domestic — below $150M. (5) Fantastic Four: First Steps (July 25-27, 2025): $118 million 3-day domestic — below $150M. (6) Wicked: For Good (November 21, 2025): This is being reported as '$150 million projected' for its opening weekend - released on November 21, 2025, which is technically outside the coverage period (releases before November 21, i.e., through November 20). However, this is moot since A Minecraft Movie already qualifies.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: A Minecraft Movie: Released April 4, 2025 in the US. Multiple high-quality sources confirm its 3-day domestic opening weekend (Friday-Sunday, April 4-6, 2025) was $157 million ([CNN](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/04/06/business/minecraft-movie-box-office/index.html), [Entertainment Weekly](https://ew.com/a-minecraft-movie-first-weekend-at-box-office-157-million-11709990), [PINKVILLA](https://www.pinkvilla.com/entertainment/box-office/box-office-a-minecraft-movie-scores-biggest-domestic-opening-weekend-for-a-video-game-adaptation-grossing-usd-157-million-1381154), [Screen Daily](https://www.screendaily.com/news/a-minecraft-movie-rescues-box-office-on-record-157m-launch-for-video-game-adaptation/5203727.article)). One source (We Got This Covered) mentions $163 million as a revised figure. All agree the figure far exceeds $150 million. The release date (April 4, 2025) is within the January 1–November 20, 2025 window. The figures cited are specifically the 3-day domestic opening weekend gross. This exactly satisfies the resolution criteria. Lilo & Stitch ($183M) also qualifies but is the second occurrence.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: A Minecraft Movie had its wide theatrical release on April 4, 2025 (Friday). Its 3-day opening weekend (April 4-6, 2025) was confirmed on April 6-7, 2025. Multiple articles published April 6-7, 2025 report the $157 million figure explicitly. The event occurred at 2025-04-06T00:00:00Z (end of its opening Sunday, when results were tallied).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: A Minecraft Movie (April 4-6, 2025) is the first movie of 2025 to have a $150M+ domestic 3-day opening weekend. No earlier 2025 releases achieved this threshold. Earlier 2025 releases (Captain America: Brave New World with $88.8M, Snow White flopping) did not meet the threshold. A Minecraft Movie was explicitly called 'the biggest opening weekend of the year' and the first $100M+ weekend of 2025, confirming it was the first to cross $150M.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Some sources cite slightly different final figures ($157M vs $162-163M revised), but all agree the figure exceeds $150M. CinemaBlend's article on Jurassic World's opening correctly identifies 'Lilo & Stitch' and 'A Minecraft Movie' as having bigger openings than Jurassic World's 3-day gross of $91.5 million, confirming both those films exceeded $150M. Multiple independent sources (CNN, EW, Variety, Screen Daily, ScreenRant, Forbes, Vulture, PINKVILLA, IGN) all explicitly confirm A Minecraft Movie's domestic opening weekend was at minimum $157 million. The IndieWire article from November 2025 also references 'A Minecraft Movie's $162.8 million debut' in context. No contradictory evidence was found. The resolution criteria specify The Numbers as the primary source; the $157M figure reported across all outlets is consistent with what would be reported on The Numbers.
evidence.step8_final_decision: A Minecraft Movie, released on April 4, 2025, achieved a confirmed 3-day domestic opening weekend gross of $157 million (with some sources reporting a revised $162.8 million), which exceeds the $150 million threshold. This occurred within the question's coverage period (January 1–November 20, 2025) and was the first occurrence of a 2025 film exceeding $150M in a domestic 3-day opening weekend. The question therefore resolves YES. The first occurrence was confirmed over the weekend of April 4-6, 2025.

question: Starmer out in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Keir Starmer ceases to be the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom for any period of time between February 2 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement of Keir Starmer's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/removal goes into effect.

The resolution source for this market will be the government of the UK, however a consensus of credible reporting will also suffice.

subquestions.question: Will a formal Labour leadership challenge or a no-confidence motion against Keir Starmer as Labour leader be publicly initiated between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Keir Starmer has faced growing discontent within the Labour Party throughout 2025. His personal approval ratings have cratered, with an Ipsos survey showing 73% of UK adults unsatisfied with his performance — the lowest score the polling company has ever recorded for a prime minister's first-year performance. Reform UK has overtaken Labour in some polls, and senior Labour MPs have openly discussed the possibility of Starmer being forced out. Sky News deputy political editor Sam Coates reported in July 2025 that 'I am hearing from ministers in government that Starmer might have to go in months.' A LabourList poll of party members found that former leader Ed Miliband topped favourability rankings among potential replacements, with a net favourability of +68.6.

Under Labour Party rules, a leadership challenge can be triggered if a challenger secures nominations from 20% of Labour MPs and MEPs, or if the leader loses a confidence vote at the party's annual conference. Labour's annual conference is scheduled for late September 2025, which could provide a natural focal point for any organised challenge. The July 2025 bond market sell-off, prompted by Starmer's perceived failure to back Chancellor Rachel Reeves, further damaged confidence in his leadership.

Sources:
- Sky News report on Starmer's position: https://www.rt.com/news/601234-starmer-could-be-on-way-out/
- Economic Times on Labour leadership speculation: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/uk/keir-starmer-on-the-way-out-this-surprise-contender-could-be-the-uks-next-prime-minister/articleshow/111510234.cms
- Labour Party rulebook on leadership challenges: https://labour.org.uk/rulebook/
- Starmer bond market crisis: https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2025/07/03/starmer-crisis-shows-uk-still-lives-at-mercy-of-the-bond-market
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), any of the following occur: (1) A Labour MP or group of Labour MPs publicly announces they are formally challenging Keir Starmer for the Labour leadership, including by declaring candidacy and/or submitting nomination papers; OR (2) A formal no-confidence motion in Starmer as Labour leader is tabled or voted upon at Labour's annual conference or through any other official Labour Party mechanism; OR (3) Starmer himself announces he will face a leadership contest. This does not include informal media speculation, anonymous briefings, or opinion polls about leadership preferences. The event must be confirmed by official Labour Party communications (https://labour.org.uk/) or reported by at least two of the following: BBC News (https://www.bbc.co.uk/news), Sky News (https://news.sky.com/), The Guardian (https://www.theguardian.com/), or Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/). If no such formal challenge or no-confidence motion is publicly initiated within this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The most plausible mechanism for Starmer to leave office in 2025 is through internal Labour Party pressure — either a formal leadership challenge or a no-confidence motion that forces his resignation. Labour's annual conference in late September 2025 is a natural flashpoint where such a challenge could crystallize. If a formal challenge is initiated in September, it dramatically increases the probability that Starmer ceases to be PM before year-end. Conversely, if Starmer survives the conference period without a formal challenge, it suggests the party establishment is not yet ready to move against him, making his departure by December 2025 less likely. This subquestion captures an observable, near-term event that is a strong leading indicator of the ultimate outcome without merely restating it.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: (1) Labour MP formally challenges Starmer — declares candidacy AND/OR submits nomination papers; OR (2) formal no-confidence motion tabled/voted on at Labour conference or official party mechanism; OR (3) Starmer himself announces he'll face a leadership contest. Must be confirmed by official Labour comms or ≥2 of BBC News, Sky News, The Guardian, Reuters. Window: 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Labour leadership challenge Keir Starmer 2025' (Sept 1 – Oct 1) — to find any formal challenge; 2. 'no-confidence motion Keir Starmer Labour leader 2025' (Sept 1 – Oct 1) — to find any formal no-confidence motion; 3. 'Andy Burnham formal leadership challenge Labour nomination papers 2025' (Sept 1 – Oct 1) — to find nomination papers or formal declaration; 4. 'Labour annual conference Liverpool 2025 no confidence vote Starmer' — to check conference proceedings; 5. 'Burnham Starmer leadership challenge backed down conference September 2025' — to confirm no formal move occurred.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Andy Burnham's 'Mainstream' group launched Sept 12 — described as speculation/groundwork, not a formal challenge. Burnham is not an MP and cannot formally stand. (B) Burnham's Telegraph interview (Sept 24-25) confirming MPs approached him — described as informal briefings, not a formal challenge. (C) Labour conference (Sept 28 – Oct 1) in Liverpool — all coverage confirms speculation but no formal no-confidence motion or leadership nomination. (D) Burnham at conference downplayed bid (LabourList, Sept 30): 'he had only launched a debate about the party's future, not a leadership campaign.' (E) Starmer's conference speech Sept 30 described as stabilizing his leadership and defusing the challenge from Burnham. ALL candidate events REJECTED as not meeting formal criteria — they constitute informal speculation, media briefings, and non-MP statements.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event explicitly matches the resolution criteria. [LabourList](https://labourlist.org/2025/09/andy-burnham-labour-conference/) reports Burnham 'stated that he had only launched a debate about the party's future, not a leadership campaign' and he 'cannot formally launch a leadership bid' as a non-MP. [Sky News](https://news.sky.com/story/labour-mps-gather-in-liverpool-as-starmer-mounts-fightback-against-reform-13439788) confirms 'Burnham would need to win a Westminster seat and secure 80 backbench votes to mount a credible bid' — he did neither. [The Spectator](https://www.spectator.co.uk/article/keir-starmer-gave-the-speech-of-his-life-at-labour-conference/) states Starmer's speech 'successfully defused leadership challenges from Andy Burnham.' No no-confidence motion was tabled or voted upon. No MP formally declared candidacy or submitted nomination papers against Starmer's leadership.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp exists because no qualifying event occurred within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event found at all within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: multiple credible sources (LabourList, Sky News, Politico, The Spectator) all confirm the speculation did not materialize into a formal challenge. Burnham explicitly said he was not launching a leadership campaign. The conference ended with Starmer's position temporarily stabilized. No official Labour Party communications (labour.org.uk) or qualifying media sources reported any formal challenge. The deputy leadership contest (Phillipson vs Powell) is explicitly about the deputy role, not Starmer's own leadership.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence confirms that throughout Sept 1 – Oct 1, 2025, while there was significant informal speculation and public maneuvering (particularly by Andy Burnham), no formal Labour leadership challenge meeting the resolution criteria was publicly initiated. The resolution criteria explicitly exclude 'informal media speculation, anonymous briefings, or opinion polls about leadership preferences.' The window closed (Oct 1) with no formal challenge materialized. Resolution: No.

question: Bank of Japan decreases interest rates after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The Statement on Monetary Policy for the Bank of Japan's Monetary Policy meeting for January is scheduled to be released on January 23, 2026 (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm).

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the short-term policy interest rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Bank of Japan's January 2026 meeting.

If the short-term policy interest rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Bank of Japan (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market may resolve as soon as the Bank of Japan's statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will Japan's core consumer price index (CPI, excluding fresh food) year-over-year increase exceed 3.0% for the October 2025 reading (released in November 2025)?
subquestions.background_information:
Japan's core CPI (excluding fresh food) has remained at or above the BOJ's 2% target for over three years. In September 2025, core CPI year-over-year growth was reported at around 2.4-2.8%, with some measures of underlying inflation running above 3%. The persistence and trajectory of inflation is a key factor in whether the BOJ will raise rates at its January 2026 meeting. If inflation accelerates further above 3%, it increases pressure on the BOJ to hike rather than cut rates, making a rate decrease even less likely. Conversely, a sharp deceleration in inflation could open the door to a more dovish stance. The October 2025 CPI data is scheduled for release by the Statistics Bureau of Japan on November 21, 2025.

At the BOJ's October 2025 meeting, the board voted 7-2 to hold rates at 0.5%, with two members dissenting in favor of a hike to 0.75% due to ongoing inflationary pressures (bne IntelliNews, 2025-10-30: https://www.intellinews.com/bank-of-japan-keeps-key-rate-unchanged-as-takaichi-takes-office-348841/). ING analysts noted core inflation remaining above 3% as a reason a December 2025 hike was possible (Investing.com, 2025-10-29: https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/boj-preview-oct-rates-to-remain-on-hold-outlook-in-focus-amid-sticky-inflation-93CH-3942567). The IMF urged the BOJ to proceed 'very gradually' with hikes given trade uncertainties (Yahoo Finance, 2025-10-15: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/imf-urges-bank-japan-move-040124407.html).

Sources:
- Statistics Bureau of Japan CPI release: https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/index.html
- bne IntelliNews, BOJ holds rate (2025-10-30): https://www.intellinews.com/bank-of-japan-keeps-key-rate-unchanged-as-takaichi-takes-office-348841/
- Investing.com, BOJ preview Oct (2025-10-29): https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/boj-preview-oct-rates-to-remain-on-hold-outlook-in-focus-amid-sticky-inflation-93CH-3942567
- Yahoo Finance, IMF urges gradual hikes (2025-10-15): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/imf-urges-bank-japan-move-040124407.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Japan's core consumer price index (CPI, excluding fresh food, as reported by the Statistics Bureau of Japan at https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/index.html) for October 2025 shows a year-over-year increase exceeding 3.0% (i.e., strictly greater than 3.0%). The relevant data release is expected on or around November 21, 2025. If the October 2025 CPI data is not released by December 8, 2025, this question resolves No. The resolution window is between 2025-11-08 and 2025-12-08. The primary resolution source is the Statistics Bureau of Japan's CPI release page: https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/index.html. If this source is unavailable, a consensus of credible financial news sources (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, NHK) reporting the official figure may be used.
subquestions.rationale: The trajectory of Japan's core inflation is one of the most critical inputs to the BOJ's rate decision. If core CPI exceeds 3.0% year-over-year, it strongly signals persistent inflationary pressure, which makes a rate cut at the January 2026 meeting extremely unlikely and instead increases the probability of a rate hike. Conversely, if inflation decelerates meaningfully, it could shift expectations toward a more dovish BOJ stance. This inflation reading will be available well before the January meeting and is a key data point the BOJ will consider, making it a highly informative early indicator of whether the BOJ would decrease rates.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Japan's core CPI (excluding fresh food, as reported by Statistics Bureau of Japan) for October 2025 must show year-over-year increase STRICTLY GREATER THAN 3.0%. Observable evidence: official government data release showing >3.0% figure. Key entities: Statistics Bureau of Japan; threshold: >3.0% (strictly); timing: data release expected ~November 21, 2025, within window 2025-11-08 to 2025-12-08.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Japan core CPI October 2025 year-over-year inflation' (to find the reported figure); Query 2: 'Japan consumer price index October 2025 statistics bureau' (to find official source); Query 3: 'Japan CPI October 2025 exactly 3.0 percent fresh food excluded' (to confirm the exact figure and rule out rounding).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events identified from November 20-21, 2025 data releases. All consistently report Japan's core CPI (excluding fresh food) rose 3.0% year-over-year in October 2025. The core-core measure (excluding fresh food AND energy) rose 3.1%, but that is a different metric than specified in the resolution criteria. The standard core CPI (excluding fresh food) = exactly 3.0%.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires strictly greater than 3.0%. All sources explicitly report exactly 3.0%: [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/japan-oct-core-cpi-rises-30-yryr-5481406), [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/84NU263), [Reuters/Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japans-core-inflation-accelerates-in-october-stays-above-boj-target-4371887), [Mainichi Shimbun](https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20251121/p2g/00m/0bu/021000c), [ActionForex](https://www.actionforex.com/live-comments/619979-japan-cpi-core-accelerates-again-to-3-in-october/). The figure does NOT strictly exceed 3.0%, it equals 3.0%. This does not satisfy the resolution criteria of 'strictly greater than 3.0%'.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Data released on November 20-21, 2025. CNA published at 23:38 on November 20, 2025 (JST). Official government release was November 21, 2025 (JST). Both are within the resolution window (2025-11-08 to 2025-12-08). Exact timestamp: 2025-11-20T23:38:00+09:00 (CNA) / 2025-11-21T00:00:00+09:00 (official release).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence exists — the first release of October 2025 data was on November 20-21, 2025, and the figure was exactly 3.0%, not above it.
evidence.step7_verification: All major financial news sources (Reuters, AFP, CNA, Mainichi Shimbun, Investing.com, ActionForex) consistently report 3.0% — no source reports a figure above 3.0% for the standard core CPI (excluding fresh food). The core-core metric (excluding fresh food and energy) did rise to 3.1%, but the resolution criteria specifies the standard core CPI metric. No contradictory evidence found regarding the 3.0% figure for the specified metric.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Japan's core CPI (excluding fresh food) for October 2025 rose exactly 3.0% year-over-year. The resolution criteria requires strictly greater than 3.0% (i.e., >3.0%). Since 3.0% does not exceed 3.0%, the condition is not satisfied. This resolves No. The condition became definitively clear when the data was officially published on November 21, 2025 (JST), which is November 20, 2025 in UTC.

question: Will Trump's approval rating hit 40% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump’s approval rating according to Silver Bulletin is equal to or below the listed value for any date between April 14 and December 31 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Note that the approval ratings for this date must be finalized before it is considered for this market (namely once the next data point is available, the previous one is finalized).

This market's resolution source will be Silver Bulletin' approval rating poll aggregator, https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin, specifically the approval rating indicated by the green trend line for the resolution date. subquestions.question: Will Trump's Silver Bulletin approval rating trend line fall below 44% at any point between September 1 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-August 2025, Nate Silver described Trump's approval rating numbers as 'very boring,' with his net approval fluctuating between -8.5 and -8.9 percentage points since August 1 (https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-numbers-very-boring-nate-silver-1939558). This implies an approval rating of roughly 45-46% and disapproval of roughly 54-55%. Earlier in 2025, Trump's approval dipped as low as roughly 44.5-45% on the Silver Bulletin trend line during the tariff-driven decline in late April (net approval hit -9.7). To reach 40% approval — the threshold in the ultimate question — Trump would need a significant further decline from his current ~45-46% level. Whether his approval drops below 44% in September would be a meaningful intermediate signal, as it would indicate the kind of accelerating decline needed to eventually reach 40%. Silver Bulletin publishes daily approval trend line data at https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin. The approval rating has been relatively stable since mid-July at around 45-46% approve / 54-55% disapprove, so a drop below 44% would represent a notable shift.

Sources:
- Newsweek, "Donald Trump approval rating numbers have become 'very boring' -- Nate Silver" (Aug 11, 2025): https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-numbers-very-boring-nate-silver-1939558
- Silver Bulletin approval rating tracker: https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin
- Newsweek, "Trump's approval rating has 'started to drop more quickly' -- Nate Silver" (Jul 21, 2025): https://www.newsweek.com/trump-approval-rating-drop-nate-silver-2025-1936821
- NYMag, "At 100 Days, Trump Approval Rating Is As Low As First Term" (Apr 28, 2025): https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/at-100-days-trump-approval-rating-is-as-low-as-first-term.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between September 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), the green trend line on Silver Bulletin's approval rating tracker (https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin) shows Trump's approval rating at or below 44.0%. The relevant data point is the 'approve' percentage on the green trend line (not individual polls). A data point is considered finalized once the next day's data point is published. If Silver Bulletin's tracker becomes permanently unavailable during this period, RealClearPolitics' approval average (https://www.realclearpolling.com/polls/approval/donald-trump/approve) will be used as a fallback. If neither source is available, the question resolves as ambiguous. The question resolves No if, for every finalized data point between September 1 and September 30, 2025, the approval trend line remains above 44.0%.
subquestions.rationale: For Trump's approval to reach 40% by the end of 2025 (the ultimate question), it would need to decline roughly 5-6 percentage points from its current ~45-46% level. A drop below 44% in September would represent a meaningful downward break from the stable range observed since mid-July, signaling the kind of erosion trajectory that could plausibly continue to 40% by year-end. Conversely, if approval stays above 44% through September — maintaining the 'very boring' stability Silver noted — it becomes significantly less likely that approval will plunge all the way to 40% in the remaining three months of 2025. This subquestion thus serves as an early warning indicator: forecasters who disagree on whether 40% will be reached should update substantially based on whether a sub-44% reading materializes in September.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Silver Bulletin's green trend line 'approve' percentage must reach AT OR BELOW 44.0% at any point between September 1-30, 2025. Observable evidence: explicit citations of Silver Bulletin approval percentage ≤44.0% from news articles reporting on the tracker during this period. Key threshold: 44.0% (inclusive). Key entity: Silver Bulletin / natesilver.net tracker.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Silver Bulletin Trump approval rating September 2025' (to find general data points); 2. 'Nate Silver Trump approval rating tracker 2025' (to find tracker-specific readings); 3. 'Silver Bulletin Trump approval 44% trend line September 2025' (to find specific threshold mentions); 4. 'Trump approval rating 44 percent Silver Bulletin late September 2025' (to find late-month readings); 5. 'Silver Bulletin Trump approval 43.9 43.7 percent weekly tracker' (to find specific low readings); 6. 'Trump net approval -10 Silver Bulletin September 25-28 2025' (to find the lowest points).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified from news articles: (a) ~Sept 9-10: Silver Bulletin shows 44.1% approval — above threshold, rejected. (b) Sept 14: ~44.2% approval (Newsweek) — above threshold, rejected. (c) Sept 19: 44.2% approval (Twin Cities) — above threshold, rejected. question: Will Hamas agree to disarm by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Hamas officially announces it will disarm in the Gaza Strip by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only credible announcements, for example by the widely acknowledged leadership of Hamas, will qualify.

For the purposes of this market, "disarm" refers to a public commitment to relinquish or dismantle its military, whether partially or completely, in the Gaza Strip.

Announcements of partial disarmament (e.g., surrendering a class of weapons or agreeing to disarm in stages or a certain region) will qualify as long as it is part of an acknowledged disarmament process.

Only official announcements will qualify. Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

Primary resolution sources will include official statements from Hamas leadership; however, a wide consensus of credible reporting confirming a policy of disarmament has been instituted will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Hamas publicly reject disarmament as a precondition for advancing to the second phase of the Trump peace plan between November 30 and December 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Hamas has consistently resisted demands to disarm as part of the US-backed 20-point Trump peace plan, which took effect with a ceasefire on October 10, 2025. The plan's second phase requires Hamas to relinquish its military capabilities and governance role in Gaza under international supervision. However, Hamas has only agreed to the first phase (ceasefire and hostage exchange) and has publicly stated that the remaining phases are 'up for negotiation.' On November 26, 2025, Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem reiterated that the organization will not disarm unless the issue is resolved through 'internal Palestinian dialogue' and linked to a broader political process culminating in an independent Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital. Senior Hamas official Osama Hamdan has stated that Hamas rejects disarmament, international forces inside Gaza, and non-Palestinian governance, and that weapons would only be handed over to a future Palestinian state. Meanwhile, Qatar's Prime Minister has indicated that Qatar is pressuring Hamas to accept disarmament, and Arab mediators have suggested Hamas might be open to partial disarmament. Despite this, Hamas has been reasserting power in Gaza, carrying out retribution executions and rebuilding infrastructure, signaling it intends to maintain its military and political position. A fresh formal rejection of disarmament by Hamas leadership in December would be a strong signal that the ultimate question (agreement to disarm by December 31) will resolve No.

Sources:
- Arutz Sheva: "Hamas continues steadfast refusal to disarm" (Nov 26, 2025) https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/404567
- Gatestone Institute: "How Hamas Is Planning to Deceive the Trump Administration" (Nov 13, 2025) https://www.gatestoneinstitute.org/21529/hamas-deceive-trump-administration
- The Hill: "Hamas reasserts power in Gaza with retribution campaign" (Oct 14, 2025) https://thehill.com/policy/international/5043210-hamas-reasserts-power-gaza-retribution/
- The Boston Globe: "Arab mediators believe Hamas could be open to partially disarming" (Oct 8, 2025) https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/10/08/world/arab-mediators-believe-hamas-could-be-open-partially-disarming/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between November 30, 2025 and December 25, 2025 (inclusive), a senior Hamas official (e.g., a member of the politburo, a recognized spokesman such as Hazem Qassem or Osama Hamdan, or a leader such as Khalil al-Hayya) makes a public statement—reported by at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera, BBC, CNN)—explicitly rejecting disarmament as a precondition for proceeding to the second phase of the Trump peace plan or explicitly stating that Hamas will not agree to disarm. Statements that condition disarmament solely on future Palestinian statehood or 'internal Palestinian dialogue' without agreeing to a concrete disarmament process count as rejections. The question resolves No if no such public rejection is reported during this period, or if Hamas makes statements indicating openness to disarmament without preconditions. Resolution sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com), BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news).
subquestions.rationale: Hamas's public stance on disarmament in the weeks leading up to December 31 is the most direct observable indicator of whether they will formally agree to disarm by the deadline. As of late November 2025, Hamas has been consistently rejecting disarmament demands, but the situation is fluid with ongoing mediation. If Hamas issues another explicit rejection in December, it would strongly suggest the ultimate question resolves No. Conversely, a notable absence of rejection statements—or signals of openness—could indicate movement toward agreement. This subquestion captures a concrete, observable indicator (public statements by Hamas leadership) that directly informs the probability of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A senior Hamas official (politburo member, recognized spokesman, or leader like Khalil al-Hayya) publicly rejects disarmament as a precondition for proceeding to the second phase of the Trump peace plan between Nov 30–Dec 25, 2025, reported by at least two major international outlets. Conditioning disarmament on Palestinian statehood without agreeing to a concrete disarmament process also counts as rejection.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Hamas reject disarmament precondition Trump peace plan second phase' (Nov 30–Dec 25, 2025); 2) 'Hamas disarmament statement December 2025' (Nov 30–Dec 25, 2025); 3) 'Khalil al-Hayya Hamas weapons legitimate right disarmament rejection December 2025'; 4) 'Khaled Meshaal Hamas disarmament Al Jazeera interview December 2025'; 5) 'Hamas Husam Badran Osama Hamdan disarmament precondition second phase reject'; 6) 'Hamas senior official second phase disarmament precondition reject November December 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple qualifying events identified: (A) Dec 6, 2025: Khalil al-Hayya (Hamas Gaza chief/negotiator) stated Hamas weapons conditioned on end of occupation/Palestinian statehood, rejected international force with disarmament mandate — France 24, Arab News, AFP, Malay Mail. (B) Dec 10, 2025: Khaled Meshaal (Hamas political bureau head) explicitly rejected full disarmament as 'unacceptable' ('stripping away the soul'), proposed weapons freeze instead — Al Jazeera, AFP, France 24, NDTV. (C) Dec 14, 2025: Khalil al-Hayya declared weapons are 'legitimate right' under international law, rejected ISF disarmament mandate — AFP, Asharq Al-Awsat, Times of Israel, Dawn. (D) Dec 19, 2025: Khalil al-Hayya again asserted 'legitimate right' to weapons — AFP. No events found outside the window that would disqualify these.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: FIRST QUALIFYING EVENT: December 6, 2025 — Khalil al-Hayya (Hamas Gaza chief/chief negotiator, senior official), stated weapons conditioned on end of occupation and establishment of Palestinian sovereign state, and 'rejected the deployment of an international force with a disarmament mandate' [France 24](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20251206-hamas-says-it-will-hand-over-weapons-to-a-palestinian-authority-if-the-occupation-ends), [Arab News](https://www.arabnews.com/node/2625307/middle-east), [AFP via Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/world/2025/12/07/hamas-signals-readiness-to-disarm-under-sovereign-palestinian-authority-if-israeli-occupation-ends/201050). Under the resolution criteria, conditioning disarmament on Palestinian statehood without agreeing to a concrete disarmament process counts as rejection. Hamas also rejected the disarmament mandate for the ISF. SECOND QUALIFYING EVENT (clearest): December 10, 2025 — Khaled Meshaal (Hamas political bureau head) explicitly called disarmament 'unacceptable' [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/10/hamas-leader-vows-to-curb-gaza-attacks-on-israel-but-rejects-disarmament), [AFP/France 24](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20251211-hamas-signals-openness-to-weapons-freeze-but-rejects-full-disarmament), [NDTV](https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/hamas-proposes-weapons-freeze-in-return-for-long-term-truce-report-9788625). Both events are within the window, involve senior Hamas officials, reported by multiple major international outlets, and explicitly reject disarmament as a precondition for advancing to the second phase of the Trump peace plan.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First qualifying event: December 6, 2025 (al-Hayya statement on weapons conditional on Palestinian statehood, rejection of international disarmament force). Published by France 24 on 2025-12-06. Second qualifying event: December 10, 2025 (Meshaal rejection of disarmament as 'unacceptable'), published by Al Jazeera on 2025-12-10. Both are explicitly timestamped.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event was found within the window (Nov 30–Dec 5, 2025). The first qualifying event in the window is December 6, 2025 with al-Hayya's statement. A search for November 30 – December 5 yielded no matching reports of senior Hamas officials explicitly rejecting disarmament as a precondition for the second phase.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Hamas also offered a 'weapons freeze' as an alternative, which might suggest some openness to arms limitation measures. However, this is explicitly NOT full disarmament, and Hamas leaders consistently rejected the disarmament precondition demanded in Trump's second phase. The resolution criteria specify that conditioning disarmament solely on Palestinian statehood without agreeing to a concrete disarmament process counts as a rejection, which is exactly what Hamas did. Osama Hamdan's Dec 15 statement also confirmed Hamas would only accept a monitoring force at borders, not an internal disarmament force. No evidence suggests Hamas openly accepted unconditional disarmament during this period. The evidence is consistent and corroborated by multiple major outlets.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria are clearly met: Multiple senior Hamas officials (Khalil al-Hayya, Khaled Meshaal, Osama Hamdan) made public statements during the Nov 30–Dec 25, 2025 window explicitly rejecting disarmament as demanded in Trump's peace plan for proceeding to the second phase. These statements were reported by multiple major international outlets including Al Jazeera, AFP (as distributed by France 24, Arab News), and others. The first qualifying event occurred on December 6, 2025 (al-Hayya). The criteria also note that conditioning disarmament on Palestinian statehood without concrete disarmament process counts as a rejection — which precisely describes Hamas's position. Resolution: YES.

subquestions.background_information:
Elon Musk's net worth is heavily tied to Tesla stock. As of late August 2025, Musk's net worth was approximately $407-410 billion according to Forbes' real-time tracker, with a substantial lead over the second-richest person, Larry Ellison (~$278-280 billion). However, Musk's wealth has been highly volatile in 2025 — he lost over $71 billion earlier in the year due to Tesla stock declines triggered by trade war fears and political controversies (Benzinga, July 5, 2025: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/07/45678-elon-musks-71-billion-wealth-wipeout). Tesla stock is the primary driver of Musk's wealth; a sharp decline in Tesla shares could significantly narrow or eliminate his lead. Musk holds approximately 506 million Tesla shares after his recent pay package approval (Morningstar, August 4, 2025: https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/2025080411148/elon-musk-to-get-29-billion-richer-as-his-pay-package-is-approved-teslas-stock-jumps). A 15% decline in Tesla stock would wipe roughly $23 billion from his stake, though this alone might not close the gap. However, a significant Tesla decline often coincides with market conditions that could boost competitors' wealth (e.g., Oracle stock rising for Ellison). Tesla's stock has been volatile throughout 2025 due to EV market competition, Musk's political activities, and trade policy uncertainty.

A Yes resolution here would meaningfully increase the probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes before year-end, while a No resolution (Tesla staying relatively stable) would suggest Musk's lead remains robust.

question: Will USA win the 2025 Ryder Cup?
description:
In the 2025 Ryder Cup, scheduled for September 25-28, 2025.

If Team USA wins the 2025 Ryder Cup by finishing with more total points than Team Europe, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If the Ryder Cup is postponed, this market will remain open until the tournament has been completed.

If the Ryder Cup is canceled entirely, with no make-up tournament, this market will resolve “Tie”.

subquestions.question: Will the USA be favored (odds of 50% or higher implied probability) to win the 2025 Ryder Cup in the betting markets as of September 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2025 Ryder Cup is scheduled for September 26-28 at Bethpage Black in Farmingdale, New York. Team USA, captained by Keegan Bradley, features Scottie Scheffler (World No. 1), Xander Schauffele, Bryson DeChambeau, Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Patrick Cantlay, Sam Burns, Cameron Young, Ben Griffin, Russell Henley, Harris English, and J.J. Spaun. Team Europe, captained by Luke Donald, includes Rory McIlroy, Tommy Fleetwood, Tyrrell Hatton, Robert MacIntyre, Justin Rose, Rasmus Højgaard, and six captain's picks to be finalized.

Historically, the home team has a significant advantage in the Ryder Cup. The USA has won their last two home Ryder Cups (2016 at Hazeltine, 2021 at Whistling Straits — where they won 19-9). However, Europe won the 2023 edition in Rome 16.5-11.5 and are the defending champions. Europe holds a 12-9-1 record against the USA since 1979 overall.

As of late August 2025, betting markets and fan sentiment are divided, with some expecting a strong USA performance at home and others backing Europe's veteran match-play expertise. The final betting odds on the eve of the tournament (September 25) will incorporate the most up-to-date information about player form, captain's picks, practice round observations, course conditions, and any injury news — making them a strong composite indicator of which team is likely to prevail.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, on September 25, 2025, the consensus of major sportsbook odds (such as those aggregated on OddsChecker, BetMGM, DraftKings, or FanDuel) implies that Team USA has a 50% or higher probability of winning the 2025 Ryder Cup outright (excluding the tie/draw outcome). The implied probability is calculated from the decimal odds as: implied probability = 1 / decimal odds. If multiple major sportsbooks are available, the average implied probability across at least two major books will be used. If odds are only available in American or fractional format, they should be converted to decimal for the calculation.

The resolution window is between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26. Specifically, the odds snapshot should be taken from the latest available odds on September 25, 2025 (the day before play begins). If September 25 odds are not available due to a market closure, the most recent odds available before September 26, 2025 will be used.

If the Ryder Cup is postponed or canceled before September 26, 2025, such that no pre-tournament odds are posted, the question resolves N/A.

If the USA is favored at 50%+ implied probability on the eve of the event, this is a strong (though not conclusive) signal that they will win. Conversely, if Europe is favored, that updates significantly toward a European win. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question of whether USA wins the Ryder Cup are likely to partly ground their disagreement in whether they believe the USA will be the market favorite heading into the competition. This subquestion resolves before the event begins, making it a true leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

subquestions.question: Will any sitting Conservative Party of Canada MP publicly call for Pierre Poilievre to resign as party leader between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Pierre Poilievre lost his seat in the 2025 federal election but has vowed to stay on as Conservative leader, citing the party's historic gains in votes and seats. A mandatory leadership review is scheduled for January 2026 at the party's national convention in Calgary. MP Damien Kurek resigned his seat to allow Poilievre to run in a byelection in Battle River-Crowfoot, Alberta. As of mid-2025, Poilievre expressed confidence in his position, stating the party gained 2.4 million more votes and 25 more seats. However, some commentators have noted that Poilievre's loss of his own riding and the 'Mark Carney factor' could make his position less secure. The period leading up to the January 2026 leadership review is critical — public dissent from caucus members would be a strong signal that Poilievre's leadership is under serious threat and could precipitate an early departure.

Sources:
- CBC News, "Poilievre to undergo Conservative Party leadership review in January" (2025-06-16): https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/poilievre-leadership-review-january-1.7538000
- Global News, "Poilievre says he's confident he'll get to stay as Conservative leader" (2025-05-30): https://globalnews.ca/news/11198000/poilievre-conservative-leader-confidence/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), at least one sitting Conservative Party of Canada Member of Parliament publicly calls for Pierre Poilievre to resign or step down as leader of the Conservative Party of Canada. 'Publicly' means in a statement reported by at least one major Canadian news outlet (e.g., CBC, CTV, Global News, The Globe and Mail, National Post, Toronto Star) or posted on the MP's own official social media or website. A call for resignation includes explicit statements such as 'Poilievre should resign,' 'Poilievre should step aside,' 'we need new leadership,' or equivalent phrasing clearly indicating the MP believes Poilievre should leave the leadership role before or instead of facing the scheduled January 2026 review. Merely stating an intent to vote against Poilievre in the January leadership review, without calling for his immediate resignation, does not count. If no such public statement is identified by November 30, 2025, the question resolves No. Resolution sources: CBC News (https://www.cbc.ca/news), CTV News (https://www.ctvnews.ca), Global News (https://globalnews.ca), The Globe and Mail (https://www.theglobeandmail.com), National Post (https://nationalpost.com).
subquestions.rationale: Public calls from caucus members for Poilievre's resignation would be a strong leading indicator that he is at serious risk of being ousted — either voluntarily or through the January 2026 leadership review. If no MPs are publicly breaking ranks in the month before the review, it suggests Poilievre's grip on the caucus remains strong and he is very unlikely to leave before or at the review. Conversely, visible caucus dissent in November would significantly raise the probability that Poilievre departs as leader before December 31, 2025, either through mounting pressure leading to a resignation or through an emergency process. This subquestion captures an observable, near-term signal that is distinct from the ultimate question but highly informative about its outcome.

The key distinction is 'resignation/step down' vs. merely expressing dissatisfaction or planning to vote against him in the January review.

(D) Multiple named Conservative MPs (Vien, Kronis, Jivani, etc.) publicly reaffirmed loyalty to Poilievre throughout November. subquestions.question: Will the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) close above 35 on any trading day between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), often called the 'fear gauge,' measures expected 30-day volatility of the S&P 500 based on options prices. Historically, NYSE marketwide circuit breakers (triggered at a 7% single-day S&P 500 decline) have only been activated during periods of extreme volatility. Every instance of a circuit breaker being triggered—October 1997, March 2020—was accompanied by VIX readings well above 35, typically exceeding 40-50. In early April 2025, the VIX spiked to around 45-52 amid the tariff-induced sell-off that brought the S&P 500 close to circuit breaker territory (the S&P 500 fell as much as 6% intraday on April 4, 2025, just short of the 7% Level 1 threshold). As of late August 2025, the VIX has settled back to the low-to-mid 20s range after markets partially recovered from the April tariff shock. A VIX reading sustainably above 35 would indicate the kind of extreme fear environment in which a circuit breaker trigger becomes plausible. During the March 2020 circuit breaker events, the VIX peaked above 80. The April 2025 near-miss saw VIX readings in the 45-52 range. Thus, a VIX close above 35 in September 2025 would be a meaningful leading indicator that market conditions are deteriorating toward circuit breaker territory.

- CBOE VIX Index historical data: https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/

subquestions.rationale: A VIX close above 35 serves as a strong leading indicator for potential circuit breaker events. Circuit breakers require a 7%+ single-day S&P 500 decline, which historically only occurs during periods of extreme market fear reflected in elevated VIX readings. The April 2025 tariff-induced sell-off demonstrated this relationship: the S&P 500 came within 1% of triggering a Level 1 circuit breaker while the VIX was in the 45-52 range. Monitoring whether the VIX breaches 35 in September provides an early warning signal about whether market conditions are moving toward the kind of extreme stress that could produce a circuit breaker trigger in the remaining months of 2025. If the VIX stays calm (below 35), it substantially reduces the probability of a circuit breaker in the near term. If it spikes above 35, the probability of an eventual circuit breaker trigger increases meaningfully.
