question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.0% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 10-year yield reaches or is higher than the listed value for any date between April 9 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield close above 4.60% on any trading day between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 10-year Treasury yield is a key benchmark for US borrowing costs and reflects market expectations about inflation, growth, and fiscal policy. As of late July 2025, the 10-year yield was around 4.36%, having risen from a 2025 low of 3.992% on April 4 but remaining well below its 52-week high of 4.802% hit on January 13, 2025. Throughout 2025, the yield has fluctuated significantly due to tariff uncertainty, fiscal concerns over the US deficit and tax-cut legislation, and shifting expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts. In May 2025, some traders began positioning for a move toward 5% on the 10-year yield, driven by concerns about US government debt sustainability and structural shifts in bond demand (Yahoo Finance, May 21, 2025). However, the yield has not revisited its January highs. A sustained move above 4.60% in September would represent a meaningful shift upward from the ~4.36% level at end of July and would bring the yield closer to the 4.80%+ range that is a necessary waypoint toward 5.0%. Key drivers in September include the September FOMC meeting (September 16-17), updated economic projections, and any new developments on tariffs or fiscal policy.

Sources:
- Morningstar, "10-Year Treasury Yield Rises to 4.360% This Month," July 31, 2025: https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/2025073112294/10-year-treasury-yield-rises-to-4360-this-month-data-talk
- Yahoo Finance, "Traders Brace for Treasury 10-Year Yield at 5% as Mood Sours," May 21, 2025: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/traders-brace-treasury-10-year-110000371.html
- US Treasury, Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rate for the '10 Yr' column, as published by the U.S. Department of the Treasury at https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025, shows a value of 4.600% or higher for any trading day between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive). If no trading day in this window shows a 10-year yield at or above 4.600%, the question resolves No. If the Treasury data source is temporarily unavailable, resolution will be delayed until the data is published. If the data source is permanently discontinued, the Federal Reserve's H.15 statistical release (https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h15/) for the 'Treasury constant maturities, Nominal, 10-year' series will be used as a fallback.
subquestions.rationale: For the 10-year Treasury yield to reach 5.0% by end of 2025, it would need to rise roughly 60-65 basis points from its late-July level of ~4.36%. A breach of 4.60% in September would represent a meaningful step in that direction, indicating that the upward momentum and macro conditions (fiscal concerns, sticky inflation, reduced Fed cut expectations) necessary for a move to 5.0% are materializing. Conversely, if the yield remains well below 4.60% in September, it would suggest the market lacks the bearish bond dynamics needed to push to 5.0% in the remaining months of 2025. This threshold is chosen to be informative — it is above recent trading ranges but below the January 2025 high, making the probability neither trivially low nor trivially high.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The U.S. Treasury Par Yield Curve Rate for the '10 Yr' column must show a value of 4.600% or higher on any trading day between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive). evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found across the entire September 2025 period: The highest yield recorded was approximately 4.276% on September 2, 2025 (first trading day of September after Labor Day). The yield trend was clearly downward for most of September, falling from the 4.2% range to near 4.0% by mid-month, then partially recovering to ~4.14-4.18% by end of month. No event or report mentioned a yield at or above 4.60% during this window. No event was rejected — all reported values were well below 4.60%.

The highest confirmed closing value found in the evidence was 4.276% on September 2, 2025 [MarketWatch](https://www.marketwatch.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-s-p500-nasdaq-struggle-to-make-headway-after-labor-day-gold-hits-record/card/stocks-end-lower-as-bond-market-jitters-lift-treasury-yields-15qUcezu7rg3xUwfUaqs). The yield was generally declining throughout the month, hitting a five-month low of around 4.00% on September 17 and only partially recovering to ~4.18% by late September. The question resolves No.

question: Gaza mass population relocation in 2025?
description:
On February 4, Donald Trump floated a plan for the reconstruction of Gaza including the relocation of Gaza’s population (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/)

This market will resolve to “Yes” if at least 500,000 Gazans leave the Gaza strip between February 6, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This includes the transfer of Gazans to Israel, the West Bank or other countries, as well as the departure of Gazans from the Gaza Strip through visa or refugee programs.

This market refers to the total number of Gazans who leave, regardless of method.  

Announcements of relocation plans will not count, only actual relocation will qualify.

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will any country officially accept and begin receiving a batch of at least 1,000 Palestinian relocatees from Gaza between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Since President Trump first proposed relocating Gaza's population in February 2025, Israel and the U.S. have been actively seeking countries willing to accept Palestinians from Gaza. As of late August 2025, several countries have been approached but most have declined. Israel reportedly sent around 100 Gazans to Indonesia for construction work (https://worldisraelnews.com/netanyahu-asks-mossad-for-assistance-relocating-gazans-to-other-countries/), and talks have been reported with South Sudan (https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/israel-in-talks-with-south-sudan-over-plans-to-relocate-palestinians-from-gaza-report-13821046.html), though South Sudan's foreign ministry denied any such discussions. A leaked 38-page plan called the 'GREAT Trust' envisions temporary relocation of Gaza's 2 million residents, offering $5,000 in cash and subsidies to each person who leaves (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Post-war-Gaza-plan-sees-relocation-of-population-digital-token-for-Palestinian-land-Washington-P-49749866/). Despite these plans and diplomatic outreach, actual large-scale relocations have not materialized. Most Palestinians reject permanent resettlement, and international organizations have condemned the proposals as violations of international law. The total number of Gazans who have actually left the strip since February 2025 appears to be in the low hundreds at most, far short of the 500,000 threshold in the ultimate question.

Sources:
- Reuters on Trump-Netanyahu talks: https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/
- World Israel News on Mossad relocation efforts: https://worldisraelnews.com/netanyahu-asks-mossad-for-assistance-relocating-gazans-to-other-countries/
- Firstpost on South Sudan talks: https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/israel-in-talks-with-south-sudan-over-plans-to-relocate-palestinians-from-gaza-report-13821046.html
- Market Screener on GREAT Trust plan: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Post-war-Gaza-plan-sees-relocation-of-population-digital-token-for-Palestinian-land-Washington-P-49749866/
- Devdiscourse on relocation proposal: https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/politics/3302057-controversial-relocation-israels-proposal-for-gazas-future
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), at least one country (other than Israel) officially begins receiving a cumulative total of at least 1,000 Palestinian residents of Gaza as part of any relocation, resettlement, refugee, visa, or migration program originating from the Gaza Strip. The receiving country must have formally agreed to accept the relocatees (through a public government statement, signed agreement, or official program), and at least 1,000 individuals must have physically arrived in that country within this window. Resolution is based on a consensus of credible international reporting from sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), BBC (https://www.bbc.com), or official UN agency reports (https://www.unrwa.org). If no credible source reports that any single country has received at least 1,000 Gazan relocatees during this period, the question resolves No. Announcements of future plans or agreements without actual physical arrivals do not count.
subquestions.rationale: Reaching 500,000 relocations by end of 2025 would require a massive acceleration in actual departures from Gaza. A key near-term indicator is whether any country transitions from diplomatic talks to actually receiving Gazans at meaningful scale (1,000+). As of September 2025, actual relocations remain in the low hundreds total. If no country begins receiving even 1,000 Gazans in September, it would be an extremely strong signal that the 500,000 threshold is unreachable by year-end. Conversely, if a pipeline opens at this scale, it signals that the infrastructure and political will exist for larger flows. This is a genuinely different observable from the ultimate question — it measures whether the diplomatic efforts have produced any operational receiving capacity — and it is a crux that would substantially update forecasters' estimates of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: At least one country (other than Israel) must have (a) formally agreed to accept at least 1,000 Palestinian residents of Gaza, AND (b) physically received at least 1,000 such individuals within September 1–October 1, 2025. Observable evidence would be credible reporting (Reuters, AP, BBC, UNRWA) confirming formal government agreement AND physical arrivals of ≥1,000 Gazans in the same country within that calendar window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Palestinian Gaza relocation resettlement country 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 1) — to find any country accepting Palestinians. Query 2: 'Gaza Palestinians relocated country 1000 September 2025' — to find 1,000-threshold crossings. Query 3: 'Palestinians Gaza refugees arrived Egypt Turkey UAE Qatar September 2025' — to check top recipient countries. Query 4: 'Gaza medical evacuation patients 1000 country received September 2025' — to check medical evacuations. Query 5: 'Canada Gaza refugees 860 1000 arrived September 2025' — to check Canada specifically. Query 6: 'Gaza voluntary emigration third country accepted arrived October 2025' — to check voluntary emigration plans. Query 7: 'Gaza Smotrich voluntary emigration directorate country agreement relocation' — to check any new agreements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Canada's Gaza refugee program: As of August 1, 2025, only 860–886 Palestinians had arrived cumulatively since January 2024 — well below 1,000 total arrivals, and far from 1,000 within the September window. (2) UK medical evacuations (September 17, 2025): Only 10 critically ill children + 50 companions arrived — far less than 1,000. (3) Israel's 'voluntary emigration' plan: Netanyahu discussed it on September 11–12, 2025, but Finance Minister Smotrich explicitly stated 'no countries are interested.' Preliminary talks with African nations (South Sudan, Libya, Uganda, Somaliland) — no agreements finalized. (4) Libya: UN envoy confirmed (September 27, 2025) that Libyans would not support Palestinian resettlement and no formal position existed. (5) Regional countries (Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, UAE): All actively condemned and opposed receiving Palestinians. (6) Total medical evacuations Oct 2023–July 2025: 7,642 patients total over ~21 months — not 1,000 in September. (7) Trump 'GREAT Trust' plan: A proposal rejected by most countries. All candidate events REJECTED as not meeting criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event matches the resolution criteria. The criteria require (a) formal agreement AND (b) physical arrivals of ≥1,000 Gazan Palestinians within September 1–October 1, 2025. Evidence shows: [Times of Israel, Sep 11-12](https://www.timesofisrael.com/netanyahu-discusses-plan-for-voluntary-emigration-of-gazans-starting-next-month/) — no agreements finalized with any country for voluntary emigration; [Times of Israel Sep 11](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/smotrich-pushes-back-on-funding-gaza-emigration-program-given-that-no-countries-are-interested/) — Smotrich said 'no foreign country would accept Palestinians'; [The Star Sep 22](https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/ndp-calls-on-ottawa-to-do-more-to-get-approved-refugees-out-of-gaza/) — Canada had only 860 arrivals as of August 1; [TASS Sep 27](https://tass.com/world/2022211) — Libya would not support Palestinian resettlement; [ReliefWeb Sep 17](https://reliefweb.int/report/occupied-palestinian-territory/msf-uk-statement-medical-evacuations-gaza) — only 2 children arrived in UK initially, scheme for up to 300 children; [Yahoo Sep 17](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/first-critically-ill-children-gaza-085555124.html) — UK received 10 children + 50 companions total in first batch.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp could be extracted because no qualifying event occurred. The window closed at 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z with no country having formally agreed to and physically received ≥1,000 Palestinian relocatees from Gaza.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: No report from Reuters, AP, BBC, UNRWA, or any other credible source reported that any country received 1,000+ Palestinian relocatees from Gaza in September 2025. All evidence points in the opposite direction — governments were actively resisting accepting Palestinians, plans were in early stages with no agreements, and the small-scale evacuations (medical, family) numbered in the dozens to low hundreds. The Trump/Netanyahu 'voluntary emigration' plan was still being discussed as of September 30, 2025, with no agreements. The Trump peace plan released September 29–30 explicitly stated it 'prohibits forced relocation' and was still being negotiated. No contradictory evidence found suggesting 1,000+ arrivals occurred.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. All evidence indicates that no country officially accepted and began receiving a batch of at least 1,000 Palestinian relocatees from Gaza between September 1 and October 1, 2025. Key evidence: (1) Israel's voluntary emigration plan had no finalized agreements with any country as of end-September 2025; (2) Canada's entire Gaza refugee program (started January 2024) had only ~886 total arrivals as of late September 2025; (3) UK received only ~10 children + 50 companions for medical treatment; (4) Regional countries (Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia) actively refused to accept Palestinians; (5) Libya rejected resettlement; (6) Total medical evacuations from Gaza over 21 months were ~7,642 — not concentrated in September 2025. The window closed (October 1, 2025) without any qualifying event occurring.

question: Zelenskyy wears a suit and tie during next Trump meeting?
description:

question: Fed rate cut by October 2025 meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is decreased at any point between September 18 and the completion of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for October 2025, currently scheduled for October 28–29. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If no relevant statement is released for this meeting by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, and no qualifying rate cut is announced, this market will resolve to "No". Emergency rate cuts will qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch Tool show a probability of 80% or higher for a 25-basis-point rate cut at the October 28–29, 2025 FOMC meeting as of October 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve cut the federal funds rate by 25 basis points on September 17, 2025, lowering the target range from 4.25%–4.50% to 4.00%–4.25%. According to Coingape's reporting on the September FOMC decision, CME FedWatch data immediately after the cut indicated a 93.2% probability of a further 25-bps cut at the October meeting (https://coingape.com/fomc-meeting-fed-makes-first-rate-cut-of-the-year-lowers-rates-by-25-bps/). The FOMC's median economic projections suggest another 50 bps of cuts could occur in 2025, potentially bringing the target rate to 3.50%–3.75% by year-end. However, market expectations can shift rapidly based on incoming economic data. Key data releases between now and the October meeting include: the September jobs report (expected early October), the September CPI report (expected mid-October), and various Fed official speeches. If the labor market stabilizes or inflation picks up, the probability of an October cut could decline significantly. The CME FedWatch Tool (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) uses fed funds futures prices to calculate implied probabilities for upcoming FOMC decisions and is widely referenced by financial media and analysts.

Sources:
- Coingape, FOMC Meeting: Fed Makes First Rate Cut of the Year: https://coingape.com/fomc-meeting-fed-makes-first-rate-cut-of-the-year-lowers-rates-by-25-bps/
- CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
- Forbes, What To Look From The Fed's September Meeting: https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonmoore/2025/09/13/what-to-look-from-the-feds-september-meeting/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, on October 17, 2025, the CME FedWatch Tool (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) shows a probability of 80% or higher for a 25-basis-point rate cut (i.e., a target range of 3.75%–4.00%) at the October 28–29, 2025 FOMC meeting. The probability reading should be taken at market close (4:00 PM ET) on October 17, 2025. If the CME FedWatch Tool is unavailable on that date, a consensus of at least two credible financial news sources (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC) reporting equivalent fed funds futures-implied probabilities may be used instead. If the Fed conducts an emergency rate cut between September 18 and October 17, 2025 (i.e., before the scheduled October meeting), this question resolves Yes regardless of FedWatch readings, since the ultimate question would already be satisfied. The resolution window is between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-17.
subquestions.rationale: Market-implied probabilities from the CME FedWatch Tool are the most widely used forward-looking indicator for FOMC rate decisions. As of September 17, 2025, markets priced in a ~93% chance of an October cut. However, this probability could shift meaningfully based on the September jobs report and CPI data released before October 17. If the probability remains above 80% after absorbing this key economic data, it would be a strong indicator that the Fed will indeed cut at the October meeting. Conversely, if the probability drops below 80%, it would suggest that economic conditions have shifted enough to make a hold more plausible, which would be informative for the ultimate question. This subquestion measures a distinct observable (market expectations after key data releases) rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: On October 17, 2025, the CME FedWatch Tool must show ≥80% probability for a 25-bps rate cut (target range 3.75%-4.00%) at the October 28-29, 2025 FOMC meeting, measured at market close (4:00 PM ET). Observable evidence would be news reports or financial sources citing CME FedWatch data from October 17, 2025. Key entities: CME FedWatch Tool, 25 bps cut, October 28-29 FOMC meeting, 80% threshold.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'CME FedWatch probability October 2025 FOMC rate cut' (Oct 15-17) — to find FedWatch readings near resolution date; 2) 'Fed funds futures October 2025 FOMC meeting rate cut probability' (Oct 15-17) — to find market-implied probabilities; 3) 'CME FedWatch October 17 2025 rate cut probability percentage' (Oct 17 only) — to find specific resolution-date reading; 4) 'Fed rate cut October 29 FOMC 2025 probability market October 17' (Oct 17-18) — to find day-specific readings; 5) 'emergency Fed rate cut September October 2025' — to check for emergency cut condition.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events from October 17, 2025 found: (1) Benzinga: '96.8% probability of a 25-basis-point rate cut at the October 29, 2025, FOMC meeting' per CME FedWatch; (2) TalkMarkets: '94.7% probability of a 25-basis-point cut' per CME FedWatch; (3) FXStreet: 'fully priced for a 25-bps rate cut, with only a 1% chance of a 50-bps cut' per CME FedWatch; (4) CBS News: '99% likelihood' per CME FedWatch as of October 17; (5) Yahoo Finance: '98% probability' per CME FedWatch. All readings are well above the 80% threshold. No emergency rate cut between September 18 and October 17 was found (the scheduled September cut brought rate to 4.00%-4.25%).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All sources explicitly report CME FedWatch probabilities for a 25-bps rate cut at the October 28-29 FOMC meeting on October 17, 2025, all substantially exceeding the 80% threshold. [Benzinga Oct 17](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/economic-data/25/10/48267203/feds-christopher-waller-floats-5-more-rate-cuts-to-reach-neutral-125-basis-points-to-go-sees-disinflation-labor-softness-ahead): 96.8%; [TalkMarkets Oct 17](https://talkmarkets.com/content/flying-nearly-blind-fed-almost-guaranteed-to-cut-interest-rate-this-month?post=529092): 94.7%; [CBS News Oct 17](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/could-mortgage-interest-rates-fall-before-fed-october-2025-meeting/): 99%; [Yahoo Finance Oct 17](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/dollar-declines-gold-soars-expectations-193843915.html): 98%; [FXStreet Oct 17](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/gbp-usd-pulls-back-towards-134-as-trump-softens-china-rhetoric-us-dollar-recovers-202510171551): implied ~99% for 25 bps cut specifically. All readings clearly satisfy the ≥80% criterion.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple articles published on October 17, 2025 explicitly cite CME FedWatch data from that date. CBS News explicitly states 'as of October 17, 2025, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.' The resolution date is 2025-10-17, and the reading is confirmed as of that date.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question asks about the state as of October 17, 2025 (not the first time it crossed 80%). Evidence from October 15-16 also shows probabilities above 80% (94-97.8%), confirming the threshold was met at least by October 15. By October 17, readings were 94.7-99%. The condition was clearly satisfied on the resolution date.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: TalkMarkets reports 94.7% for 25 bps and 5.3% for 50 bps — both scenarios involve a rate cut, and 94.7% for 25 bps alone is above 80%. CBS News reports 99%, Yahoo Finance reports 98%, Benzinga reports 96.8%. The slight variation in reported numbers across sources is due to different timestamps during the trading day, but all are well above 80%. No source on October 17 reports a probability below 80% for a 25-bps cut. No emergency cut occurred in the window. The current fed funds rate was 4.00%-4.25% after the September cut, so a 25-bps cut would bring it to 3.75%-4.00% as specified.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition is definitively met. Multiple credible financial sources (CBS News, Yahoo Finance, Benzinga, TalkMarkets, FXStreet) explicitly cite CME FedWatch Tool data from October 17, 2025 showing probabilities ranging from 94.7% to 99% for a 25-bps rate cut at the October 28-29 FOMC meeting — all well above the 80% threshold. The resolution is Yes, with the resolution datetime being 2025-10-17T21:00:00Z (approximate market close at 4:00 PM ET = 21:00 UTC).

question: Will Trump deport 750,000 or more people in 2025?
description:
During the 2024 FY ICE removed 271,484 non citizens (see: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) removes 750,000 or more non citizens in the 2025 fiscal year. Otherwise, this market ill resolve to "No".

The resolution source will be the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report. If the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report is not published by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report be published by February 26, 2026, showing ICE removal numbers for FY 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question about whether Trump deported 750,000 or more people in 2025 hinges on the official FY 2025 ICE Annual Report. The FY 2024 report showed 271,484 removals (https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf). Multiple news reports throughout 2025 provided unofficial figures: by August 2025, ICE had deported nearly 200,000 people since Trump took office in January (https://www.foxnews.com/politics/ice-deported-nearly-200000-so-far-during-trumps-second-term-setting-pace-highest-level-decade), and by late September 2025, DHS announced 400,000 deportations since January (https://www.bellinghamherald.com/news/politics-government/national-politics/article294084929.html). By October 2025, border czar Tom Homan claimed 548,000 removals by October 19 and projected 600,000 by year-end (https://www.newsweek.com/trump-administration-aiming-600000-deportations-2025-1978055). An Express article from December 2025 cited approximately 622,000 removals in 2025 (https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/2003818/ice-santa-illegal-immigrants-christmas). However, public ICE data has not been regularly published since January 2025, and the official FY 2025 Annual Report—which covers October 2024 through September 2025—has not yet been confirmed as released. The availability of this report is critical because the ultimate question's resolution depends on it. The FY 2025 ICE Annual Report would include both the pre-Trump period (Oct–Dec 2024) and the Trump period (Jan–Sep 2025). Without the official report, resolution may require alternative credible sources.

Sources:
- ICE FY 2024 Annual Report: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf
- Fox News (Aug 2025): https://www.foxnews.com/politics/ice-deported-nearly-200000-so-far-during-trumps-second-term-setting-pace-highest-level-decade
- Newsweek (Oct 2025): https://www.newsweek.com/trump-administration-aiming-600000-deportations-2025-1978055
- Express (Dec 2025): https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/2003818/ice-santa-illegal-immigrants-christmas
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive), the official FY 2025 ICE Annual Report is published on the ICE website (https://www.ice.gov/) or a direct link to the report is made available through the Department of Homeland Security (https://www.dhs.gov/), and the report contains a specific total number of ICE removals for FY 2025 (October 1, 2024 – September 30, 2025). The report must be a publicly accessible document, not merely a press release or spokesperson statement. If the report is published but does not contain a clear total removal figure, this question resolves No. If no such report is published by 11:59 PM ET on February 26, 2026, this question resolves No.

Primary resolution source: https://www.ice.gov/ (specifically the annual report section, historically at URLs like https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2025.pdf or similar).
Fallback: https://www.dhs.gov/ official publications page.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question resolves based on the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report. Whether or not this report is published before the ultimate question's deadline (February 28, 2026) is a critical logistical crux. If the report is published, we will know definitively whether ICE removals reached 750,000. Based on unofficial figures throughout 2025—with Homan projecting around 600,000 removals by calendar year-end and the Express citing ~622,000—the FY 2025 total (which includes Oct–Dec 2024, adding roughly 71,400 ICE removals) could plausibly reach around 390,000–420,000 in ICE-only removals for the full fiscal year. The 750,000 threshold appears to refer to ICE removals specifically, which based on all available reporting seems very unlikely to be met. However, the publication of the official report is the necessary precondition for definitive resolution, and knowing whether it will be available in time is itself informative—if it's not published, the ultimate question falls to alternative sources that may present different figures or counting methodologies.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The official FY 2025 ICE Annual Report (covering October 1, 2024 – September 30, 2025) must be published between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26 on ice.gov or dhs.gov as a publicly accessible document (not a press release or spokesperson statement), and must contain a specific total number of ICE removals for FY 2025. Observable evidence: A PDF or formal report document published on ice.gov/dhs.gov with FY 2025 removal totals. Key timing: The window is January 29 to February 26, 2026.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'ICE Annual Report FY 2025 removals published' (Jan 29 – Feb 26, 2026) — to find direct report publication evidence. 2. 'ICE fiscal year 2025 annual report immigration enforcement' (Jan 1 – Feb 26, 2026) — broader search. 3. 'ICE FY2025 annual report publication ice.gov removals statistics' (Jan 1 – Feb 26, 2026) — site-specific search. 4. 'ICE end of year report 2025 total deportations removal numbers official' (Oct 1, 2025 – Feb 26, 2026) — to find any formal report. 5. 'DHS ICE transparency deportation data removed public website 2025 2026' — to check data availability. 6. 'ICE end of year OR year end report removal statistics FY2025' — to find formal publications.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events were found that match the criteria of a formal FY 2025 ICE Annual Report published on ice.gov or dhs.gov within the resolution window. The only data found includes: (a) Informal figures from spokesperson statements and press releases (not formal reports); (b) Congressional testimony by Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons citing calendar-year figures (Jan 20, 2025 – Jan 20, 2026), not FY 2025 figures; (c) Reports from third parties like the American Immigration Council, Brookings Institution, and UC Berkeley; (d) The wow.dhs.gov database (individual case records, not an annual report with totals); (e) Multiple explicit statements that ICE's public data trackers have not been updated since January 2025. All rejected as not satisfying the criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No match found. The resolution criteria require: (1) an official FY 2025 ICE Annual Report as a formal document, (2) published on ice.gov or dhs.gov, (3) between Jan 29 and Feb 26, 2026, (4) containing a specific total removal figure for FY 2025 (Oct 1, 2024 – Sep 30, 2025). Multiple sources explicitly confirm ICE has not published formal removal data or updated its trackers since January 2025. DHS has removed deportation data from its public website per [Newsweek Feb 25, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/3-million-undocumented-immigrants-have-left-us-trump-administration-11581214). The Mass Deportation Coalition as of Feb 18, 2026 stated ICE trackers 'have not been updated since January 2025' per [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-pressured-by-conservative-orgs-to-ramp-up-deportations-11545352). No formal annual report document was identified in any source.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp could be extracted because no qualifying publication event was found within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at all, let alone a first occurrence within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: While some ICE removal figures are mentioned in news articles (e.g., Lyons' congressional testimony, DHS press releases), these are not formal ICE Annual Report documents. The Brookings Institution explicitly noted 'a lack of data transparency from the Trump administration' affecting estimates. Newsweek Feb 25, 2026 reports that 'DHS has removed deportation data from its public website, making the composition of the numbers unverifiable.' The Mass Deportation Coalition on Feb 18, 2026 demanded 'full data transparency, noting that ICE's arrest, detention, and removal trackers have not been updated since January 2025.' These sources collectively confirm no formal annual report with FY 2025 removal totals was published on ice.gov or dhs.gov during the resolution window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. The condition required a formal FY 2025 ICE Annual Report published on ice.gov or dhs.gov between January 29 and February 26, 2026, containing a specific total removal figure for FY 2025. No such report was published. Multiple independent sources confirm that ICE has not updated its public data trackers since January 2025, DHS removed deportation data from its public website, and no formal annual report document was found in any news article within the resolution window. The window closed on February 26, 2026 without the qualifying event occurring.

question: Will RFK Jr. find the cause of Autism before November?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly announces that he or an affiliated team has identified a definitive cause of autism between April 18 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If RFK Jr. identifies multiple causes, this will qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source will be announcements from RFK Jr., however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will RFK Jr. or HHS publicly release a report or formal announcement in September 2025 claiming to have identified specific causes or contributing factors of autism?
subquestions.background_information:
In April 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. pledged to identify the cause of autism by September 2025, attributing rising autism rates to 'environmental toxins.' In May 2025, Kennedy walked back this timeline, saying definitive results would take an additional six months (until approximately March 2026), and that September would only yield replication studies of existing research. However, at an August 26, 2025 Cabinet meeting, Kennedy reversed course again, announcing that his department had found 'certain interventions' that are 'clearly almost certainly causing autism' and that a full public announcement would come in September. President Trump pressed for an update at the meeting, calling autism a 'tremendous horror show.' Kennedy cited CDC data showing autism prevalence rising from 1 in 36 children (2020) to 1 in 31 (2022), with California figures as high as 1 in 19 children overall and 1 in 12.5 boys. Major scientific organizations and multiple large-scale studies (including a 2024 Danish study of 1.2 million people) have found no link between vaccines and autism. Experts, including the Autism Science Foundation and CDC researchers, attribute the rise in diagnoses primarily to improved screening, broader diagnostic criteria, and reduced stigma. Kennedy's plan involves using federal and private health data—including medical records, insurance claims, and wearable-device data—to investigate links between medical interventions and autism.

Sources:
- The Independent, 'RFK Jr is already walking back his pledge to find the cause of autism by September' (May 23, 2025): https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/rfk-jr-autism-cause-september-b2758123.html
- Yahoo News, 'RFK Jr. has made big promises on autism. Here's the latest' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.yahoo.com/news/rfk-jr-made-big-promises-215842498.html
- Gizmodo, 'RFK Jr. Promises to Reveal the Cause of Autism Next Month' (Aug 27, 2025): https://gizmodo.com/rfk-jr-promises-to-reveal-the-cause-of-autism-next-month-2000596889
- UPI, 'RFK Jr: Report on autism's root causes to be released in September' (Aug 27, 2025): https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/08/27/rfk-autism-report-september/3771724787241/
- The Hill, 'RFK Jr. softens pledge to find autism cause by September' (May 23, 2025): https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5314220-rfk-jr-autism-cause-september/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Robert F. Kennedy Jr. or the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) publicly releases a report, white paper, press conference statement, or formal announcement that explicitly claims to identify one or more specific causes or contributing factors of rising autism rates. The announcement must go beyond vague promises or previews — it must name specific interventions, substances, or factors claimed to cause or contribute to autism. Qualifying sources include official HHS or NIH press releases (https://www.hhs.gov/about/news/index.html), statements at press conferences or Cabinet meetings reported by major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, UPI, The Hill, CNN), or posts on RFK Jr.'s verified official social media accounts. If the announcement is postponed beyond October 1, 2025, or if only vague statements are made without naming specific claimed causes, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a direct leading indicator of the ultimate question. Kennedy has repeatedly promised a September reveal, and at the August 26 Cabinet meeting he strongly signaled that an announcement is imminent. However, he also walked back a similar promise in May. Whether he actually releases a formal announcement claiming to identify autism causes in September is the key near-term observable event. If he does release such an announcement, the ultimate question almost certainly resolves Yes. If he again delays or only offers vague statements, it becomes much less likely he will make a definitive announcement before October 31. This subquestion captures the crux of disagreement among forecasters: those who believe Kennedy will follow through on his latest promise versus those who expect another delay.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Between Sept 1–Oct 1, 2025, RFK Jr. or HHS must publicly release a report/press conference statement/formal announcement that EXPLICITLY claims to identify one or more SPECIFIC causes or contributing factors of rising autism rates, naming specific interventions, substances, or factors. Observable evidence: HHS press release, press conference transcript, or major news outlet reporting on such a specific named cause.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'RFK Jr HHS autism report causes September 2025' — to find any reports released; 2) 'HHS autism causes contributing factors report announcement 2025' — to find formal announcements; 3) 'Trump RFK Kennedy autism announcement press conference September 22 2025' — to find the specific press conference; 4) 'HHS autism report acetaminophen Tylenol formal announcement September 2025' — to find specifics of what was announced
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The September 22, 2025 White House press conference with Trump, RFK Jr., and FDA Commissioner Marty Makary explicitly named acetaminophen (Tylenol) use during pregnancy and folate deficiency as specific contributing factors to autism. FDA Commissioner stated: 'There is a causal relationship between prenatal acetaminophen use and neurodevelopmental disorders of ADHD and autism spectrum disorder.' HHS issued a formal press release announcing FDA physician notices and label change. RFK Jr. also named vaccines as under investigation. subquestions.question: Will the Seoul Central District Court convict Han Duck-soo in its January 21, 2026 sentencing ruling?

The special counsel has requested a 15-year prison sentence. The Seoul Central District Court's 33rd Criminal Division, presided over by Judge Lee Jin-kwan, heard closing arguments on November 26, 2025, and has scheduled the verdict for January 21, 2026. This will be the first ruling among all defendants in the insurrection case and is seen as a bellwether for other trials, including that of former President Yoon Suk-yeol. Han is charged with aiding the ringleader of insurrection, engaging in key duties related to the insurrection, and perjury. The prosecution argued that CCTV footage from the Presidential Office shows Han holding martial law documents before and after the proclamation, that he convened the Cabinet to ensure a quorum, and that he later signed the proclamation retroactively and committed perjury in the Constitutional Court impeachment trial. Han's defense maintains he had no legal authority to stop the president and denies all charges. Currently, Han is not in custody — he has been on trial while free. A conviction, particularly one resulting in a prison sentence, would likely lead to immediate detention via a court-ordered warrant, which would satisfy the ultimate question's resolution criteria for being 'in jail.'

If the court convicts him — especially with a significant prison sentence as the prosecution has requested (15 years) — it is highly likely the court would issue a detention warrant, putting him in custody. If the verdict is moved earlier into this window, a conviction would be the strongest indicator that he will end up in jail. Conversely, an acquittal or a postponement of the verdict would make it very unlikely he goes to jail by January 31. subquestions.question: Will Wicked: For Good's cumulative 2025 domestic gross exceed $350 million by December 28, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Wicked: For Good opened on November 21, 2025 to a massive $150 million domestic opening weekend, the second-largest opening of 2025 behind A Minecraft Movie ($162.7 million). As of its opening weekend, it immediately became one of the top 15 domestic grossers of the year. The film received an A CinemaScore and a 95% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, suggesting strong legs through the holiday season.

The key question for whether Wicked: For Good finishes as the third-highest-grossing film of 2025 depends on its total domestic calendar-year gross relative to competitors. As of late November 2025, the top domestic grossers of 2025 include A Minecraft Movie (~$310 million+), Lilo & Stitch (~$300 million+), and several other strong performers. Major upcoming competition includes Avatar: Fire and Ash (opening December 19), Zootopia 2, and other holiday releases.

The original Wicked (2024) had a 4.2x multiplier from its opening weekend, demonstrating exceptional legs. If Wicked: For Good achieves even a 2.5x multiplier on its $150 million opening, it would reach $375 million domestically. However, heavy competition from Avatar: Fire and Ash and Zootopia 2 could limit its later-week grosses. Reaching $350 million by December 28 would suggest the film is on track to be a top-3 grosser for the year.

Sources:
- Box Office Mojo 2025 calendar grosses: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses
- SlashFilm on Wicked: For Good's opening: https://www.slashfilm.com/1729917/wicked-for-good-dominated-box-office-reasons/
- NBC News on opening weekend: https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/movies/wicked-for-good-opening-weekend-box-office-rcna211610
- Comicbook on box office record: https://comicbook.com/movies/news/wicked-for-good-breaks-major-box-office-record-opening-weekend/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, according to Box Office Mojo's 2025 calendar year domestic grosses page (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses), Wicked: For Good has accumulated at least $350 million in the 'Gross' column by December 28, 2025. The relevant data is the cumulative domestic gross reported on that page as of December 28, 2025. If Box Office Mojo data is not yet updated by December 28, the latest available data up to and including December 30 may be used. If Box Office Mojo is unavailable, The Numbers (https://www.the-numbers.com/) or Comscore data may be used as a fallback. The resolution window is from 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-28. Only domestic (U.S. and Canada) gross counts.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Wicked: For Good reaches $350 million domestic by late December is a strong leading indicator of whether it will finish as the third-highest-grossing film of 2025. The $350 million threshold represents roughly a 2.3x multiplier on its opening weekend, which would put it firmly in contention for a top-3 finish. If it fails to reach this level, it may be overtaken by Avatar: Fire and Ash or other competitors. If it surpasses this level comfortably, it's very likely to hold a top-3 position. This is a different observable event from the ultimate question because it measures a mid-run milestone rather than the final year-end ranking, and it helps forecasters gauge the film's legs and staying power against holiday competition.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Wicked: For Good must have accumulated at least $350 million in domestic (U.S. + Canada) box office gross as reported by Box Office Mojo's 2025 calendar year page, by December 28, 2025. Observable evidence: explicit box office tracking articles citing domestic gross ≥$350M on or before December 28.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Wicked For Good box office domestic gross 2025' (Dec 1 – Dec 28) — to find cumulative totals; Query 2: 'Wicked Part 2 For Good cumulative box office total December 2025' — to find milestone reports; Query 3: 'Wicked For Good box office December 28 2025 domestic total' (Dec 20–28) — to find data closest to resolution date; Query 4: 'Wicked For Good Christmas weekend box office $340 million $350 million' (Dec 20–30) — to find threshold-crossing reports.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key data points found: Dec 22 = $320.5M (Koimoi, Box Office Mojo); Dec 24 = $322.4M (Koimoi); Dec 25/day 37 = $324.1M (Koimoi); Dec 26 = $326.3M (Deadline); Dec 27 = $331.3M (ScreenRant); Dec 28 weekend total (6th weekend) = $331.6M (Rotten Tomatoes, Dec 29). The Dec 29 Rotten Tomatoes article explicitly covers the Christmas weekend (Dec 26–28) and states the film earned $5.2M for its sixth weekend, bringing domestic total to $331.6M, projected to finish $340–350M. No article reports $350M domestic reached by December 28.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The most recent data point for Dec 28 (from the [Weekend Box Office article](https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/article/weekend-box-office-avatar-fire-and-ash-holds-on-with-64-million/) published Dec 29, covering the Dec 26–28 weekend) shows $331.6M domestic total — approximately $18.4M short of the $350M threshold. The projection of '$340–350 million' final is an upper-range estimate for the film's entire run (not just through Dec 28). The [Deadline article](https://deadline.com/2025/12/wicked-for-good-pvod-dvd-release-date-1236657066/) from Dec 26 reports $326.3M as of that date. The [ScreenRant article](https://screenrant.com/wicked-for-good-box-office-universal-domestic-charts-oppenheimer-comparison/) from Dec 27 reports $331.3M. None of the evidence confirms $350M was reached by Dec 28.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: As of 2025-12-28 (the resolution date, covered by the Dec 26–28 Christmas weekend report published Dec 29): domestic total was $331.6M. The $350M threshold was NOT reached by this date.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No article reports the film reaching $350M domestic gross. The closest projections ('$340–350M final total') indicate the upper bound of the film's entire theatrical run was around $350M — and those projections were made before the PVOD release on Dec 30 further reduced theatrical revenue. The film appears to have ended its run well under $350M domestically.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality sources consistently report domestic totals well below $350M through Dec 28: $320.5M (Dec 22), $322.4M (Dec 24), $324.1M (Dec 25), $326.3M (Dec 26), $331.3M (Dec 27), and $331.6M after the Dec 26–28 weekend. The film was also transitioning to PVOD on Dec 30, further limiting theatrical earnings. Projections of '$340–350M final' confirm the $350M threshold was at best a ceiling of the entire run, not achieved by Dec 28. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Wicked: For Good had accumulated approximately $331.6 million in domestic gross by December 28, 2025 — roughly $18.4 million short of the $350 million threshold. Multiple independent sources agree on this trajectory. The film's final run projections capped at $340–350M total, and the PVOD launch on Dec 30 suggests the film did not continue earning at a rate sufficient to bridge the gap. Resolution: No.

question: Will the ECB announce no change at the February 2026 meeting?
description:

If the deposit facility rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 basis points and will resolve to the relevant bracket.
For example, if the deposit facility rate is increased or decreased by 12.5 basis points, it will be treated as a 25 basis point change for the purposes of resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the ECB keep its deposit facility rate unchanged at 2.00% at its December 18, 2025, monetary policy meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
The ECB's Governing Council held its deposit facility rate steady at 2.00% at its October 30, 2025, meeting, citing inflation close to the 2% target and a resilient economy. Since then, hawkish comments from ECB policymaker Isabel Schnabel and other officials have pushed market expectations away from rate cuts and toward possible rate hikes later in 2026. Money markets are pricing in roughly 12.5 basis points of rate increases by December 2026, and rate cuts have been fully priced out. ECB President Christine Lagarde has emphasized that the current rate is appropriate and any change would depend on incoming data. The December 18, 2025, meeting will include updated staff macroeconomic projections, which could shape the tone of policy communication going forward. The overwhelming market expectation is for no change at the December meeting, but the outcome and accompanying communication will set the stage for February 2026.

However, if the ECB were to unexpectedly change rates in December, it would indicate a shift in the policy trajectory that would significantly alter expectations for February. Additionally, the December meeting includes new staff projections and updated risk assessments that will frame the policy debate heading into February. This makes the December decision a high-value early indicator for the February outcome.

subquestions.question: Will Spain's 2026 General State Budget (Presupuestos Generales del Estado) fail to pass an initial congressional vote or be formally withdrawn by the government between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Pedro Sánchez leads a fragile minority coalition government that has been unable to pass a budget for two consecutive years, rolling over prior budgets instead. In a September 2, 2025 interview, Sánchez stated he would present a budget and 'fight to get it approved,' while rejecting the idea of resigning if the budget fails (https://www.nzherald.co.nz). Opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has urged Sánchez to resign if he cannot secure budget approval. The government's coalition depends on support from a patchwork of smaller parties — including Catalan, Basque, and left-wing groups — making any legislative achievement difficult. Sánchez's Socialists trail the Popular Party significantly in polls (27% vs. 34.4%), and the accumulation of corruption scandals involving his wife, brother, and former aides has further weakened his negotiating position. A budget failure would be a major blow to the government's viability and could intensify calls for snap elections or a resignation. The Spanish government typically presents its budget draft to Congress in the autumn, and early October is a critical window for determining whether a budget vote will proceed or whether the government abandons the effort.

Sources:
- NZ Herald, 'Spanish PM accuses judges of doing politics in graft cases' (2025-09-02): https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/spanish-pm-accuses-judges-of-doing-politics-in-graft-cases/
- AP NEWS, 'Spain's PM refuses to step down and announces anti-graft plan despite corruption inquiries' (2025-07-09): https://apnews.com/article/spain-sanchez-corruption-anti-graft-plan
- Euronews, 'Spain's PM apologises after top aide implicated in corruption scandal' (2025-06-12): https://www.euronews.com/2025/06/12/spains-pm-apologises-after-top-aide-implicated-in-corruption-scandal
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), either: (1) the Spanish government's 2026 General State Budget (Presupuestos Generales del Estado) is voted down in Spain's Congress of Deputies at any stage (e.g., a vote on the totality or 'enmienda a la totalidad'), OR (2) the Spanish government formally announces it will not present or has withdrawn its 2026 budget proposal. Resolution will be based on official announcements from the Spanish government (https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/), the Spanish Congress of Deputies (https://www.congreso.es/), or a consensus of credible reporting from sources such as El País (https://elpais.com/), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), and AP News (https://apnews.com/). If no budget vote occurs and the government has not formally announced withdrawal or non-presentation of the budget during this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The budget is the single most important legislative test for Sánchez's minority government. A failure to pass or even present a budget would signal that Sánchez has lost the support of the coalition partners he needs to govern, dramatically increasing the probability of a confidence crisis, snap elections, or resignation before year-end. Conversely, if Sánchez manages to advance a budget, it would indicate his coalition is still functional and reduce the likelihood of him leaving power in 2025. Two forecasters who disagree on whether Sánchez will be out as PM in 2025 would likely update significantly upon learning the fate of the budget effort in October.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes condition requires: (1) Spain's 2026 budget voted down in Congress of Deputies at any stage (e.g., enmienda a la totalidad), OR (2) the Spanish government formally announces it will not present or has withdrawn the 2026 budget proposal — all within October 1–31, 2025. Observable evidence would be: official congressional voting records showing a budget defeat, or a formal government announcement (La Moncloa, Council of Ministers) withdrawing/not presenting the budget.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: (1) 'Spain 2026 General State Budget Congress vote October 2025'; (2) 'España presupuestos generales 2026 aprobación Congreso octubre 2025'; (3) 'Spain presupuestos 2026 Sanchez rejected withdrawn vote Congress Deputies October 2025'; (4) 'Spain budget 2026 Junts Sánchez parliamentary support October 2025'; (5) 'Spain 2026 budget presented Congress submitted October 2025'; (6) 'Spain presupuestos 2026 no presentados retirada formal gobierno octubre 2025'; (7) 'Spain government 2026 budget vote Congress Deputies rejected enmienda totalidad October 2025'; (8) 'Spain Sanchez government formally announces not presenting 2026 budget withdrawal October 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key events found: (A) AFP article (Oct 14, 2025): PM Sánchez confirms he 'will still put forward' 2026 budget, acknowledges delay past October 1 constitutional deadline, says government is 'comfortable with the 2023 budget.' (B) EFE article (Oct 28, 2025): Government spokesperson Alegría reaffirms 'intention to present a draft of the 2026 State General Budget' even after Junts break. (C) Multiple sources confirm the government 'has not yet submitted a 2026 budget' as of late October 2025. (D) AFP article (Oct 30, 2025): Junts members vote 87% to withdraw support — complicates but does not constitute government withdrawal. NO EVENTS found indicating: a budget vote in Congress, or a formal government withdrawal/non-presentation announcement.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event matches the Yes criteria: (1) No congressional vote on the 2026 budget occurred — the budget was never submitted to Congress during this window. Sources: [AFP Oct 14](http://doc.afp.com/78PL9T3), [Sunday Guardian Oct 27](https://sundayguardianlive.com/world/update-1-catalan-allies-on-brink-of-withdrawing-support-for-spanish-government-158420/) both explicitly confirm 'the government has not yet submitted a 2026 budget.' (2) No formal government withdrawal — to the contrary, Sánchez explicitly said he would still present it [AFP Oct 14], and the government spokesperson reaffirmed budget presentation intent on Oct 28 [EFE Oct 28](https://efe.com/espana/2025-10-28/gobierno-legislatura-junts-pactos/). The Junts withdrawal of legislative support is NOT the same as the government withdrawing its own budget proposal.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying Yes-event timestamp exists. The clearest 'anti-Yes' timestamps are: Oct 14, 2025 (Sánchez says he will still present budget) and Oct 28, 2025 (government spokesperson confirms intention to present 2026 budget). The window ends Oct 31, 2025 with no qualifying event having occurred.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradiction check: Could the Junts withdrawal (finalized Oct 30, 2025 by member vote) constitute a formal government withdrawal of the budget? No — Junts is a Catalan external support party, not part of the government. The government itself (through multiple officials) explicitly maintained its intent to present the budget. Could there have been an unreported budget vote? Extremely unlikely given the context: (a) the budget had not been submitted, (b) multiple sources from throughout the month confirm it had not been submitted, (c) Sánchez himself acknowledged the delay past the Oct 1 constitutional deadline. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The 2026 budget was never submitted to Spain's Congress of Deputies during October 2025 (it had not yet been drafted/presented), so no congressional vote could have occurred. The government did not formally withdraw or announce non-presentation — in fact, the opposite: both Sánchez (Oct 14) and the government spokesperson (Oct 28) explicitly confirmed intent to present the 2026 budget. The window closed October 31, 2025, with neither qualifying condition met.

question: Will Trump announce Chris Waller as next Fed Chair in 2025?
description:
Trump's Treasury Secretary pick Scott Bessent has floated the idea of Trump naming a successor to Jerome Powell to serve as a "shadow chair", prior to the end of Powell's term, scheduled for May 2026. (see: https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/business/money-report/fed-chair-jerome-powell-can-serve-remainder-of-term-says-trumps-treasury-pick-bessent/3788991/).

This market will resolve to according the individual Donald Trump announces as his pick for the next Federal Reserve Chair. If Donald Trump does not announce his pick for the next Federal Reserve Chair by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No announcement by December 31".  

The resolution source for this market will be official information form Donald Trump or one of his official representatives, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Scott Bessent complete second-round interviews with Fed Chair finalists and present a shortlist to Trump before November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 27-28, 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed aboard Air Force One that the administration has narrowed the Federal Reserve Chair search to five finalists: current Fed Governors Christopher Waller and Michelle Bowman, National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, former Fed Governor Kevin Warsh, and BlackRock executive Rick Rieder. Bessent stated he plans to conduct one more round of interviews and present a 'good slate' to President Trump 'right after Thanksgiving' (Thanksgiving 2025 falls on November 27). Bessent said: 'We're down to five... we hope to present a good slate to the president right after Thanksgiving.... It will ultimately be his choice.' Trump confirmed he expects to name a replacement by year's end. The timing of Bessent's shortlist presentation is a key gating event — it determines whether Trump can announce a pick in December 2025 or whether the process slips into 2026. The composition of that final slate (and whether Waller is prominently featured or has fallen out of favor) would provide strong signal about the likelihood of Waller being the ultimate pick.

Sources:
- Anadolu Agency, October 28, 2025: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-treasury-chief-bessent-lists-5-finalists-for-next-fed-chair-as-trump-to-decide-before-years-end/3400052
- Fast Company, October 29, 2025: https://www.fastcompany.com/91225678/5-people-who-could-become-the-next-federal-reserve-chair
- Fox Business, August 27, 2025: https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/bessent-vets-potential-powell-successors-trumps-shortlist-starting-take-shape
- Cryptopolitan, October 27, 2025: https://www.cryptopolitan.com/trump-narrows-fed-chair-shortlist-to-five/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), credible news reports confirm that Scott Bessent has (a) completed a second round of interviews or evaluations with Fed Chair candidates AND (b) presented or delivered a final shortlist or recommendation slate to President Trump. Resolution sources include official statements from the White House, Treasury Department, or Bessent himself, as well as credible reporting from outlets such as Fox Business (https://www.foxbusiness.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com), CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), or the Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com). The question resolves No if, by November 30, 2025, there is no credible reporting that both conditions (a) and (b) have been met. If reporting is ambiguous about whether a formal presentation has occurred (e.g., Bessent says he is 'almost done' but hasn't yet presented to Trump), the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Bessent explicitly stated he plans to present finalists to Trump 'right after Thanksgiving' (November 27, 2025). Whether this milestone is met on schedule is a critical gating indicator for whether Trump will announce any Fed Chair pick — including Waller — by year-end 2025. If the process stalls or is delayed past November, it significantly reduces the probability of a December announcement. Conversely, if Bessent delivers the slate on time, it makes a year-end announcement much more likely. This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question because it tracks a process milestone (Bessent's shortlist delivery) rather than Trump's final decision, and it provides signal about the pace and seriousness of the selection process. Forecasters who disagree on whether Trump will pick Waller specifically may update based on whether the process is proceeding on the announced timeline, since delays would change the dynamics of who ultimately gets chosen.

evidence.step1_decompose: Two conditions required for Yes within Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025: (a) Bessent completed a second round of interviews with Fed Chair finalists, AND (b) Bessent formally presented/delivered a shortlist or recommendation to President Trump. Both must be explicitly confirmed by credible reporting within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Scott Bessent Fed Chair interviews shortlist Trump 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find overall process news; 2) 'Federal Reserve Chair candidates second round interviews November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find interview completion; 3) 'Bessent presents shortlist Fed Chair Trump recommendation after Thanksgiving' (Nov 25–30) — to find presentation event; 4) 'Bessent Fed chair second round interviews completed shortlist presented Trump November 2025' (Nov 25–30) — to find explicit confirmation of formal shortlist delivery.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Nov 25, 2025: Bessent concludes/is concluding second round of interviews — confirmed by CNBC, South China Morning Post, Anadolu Agency, Business Standard, Fox Business. (2) Nov 25, 2025: Bessent states he plans to present final list to Trump 'shortly after Thanksgiving' (Thanksgiving = Nov 27). (3) Nov 26, 2025: Fox Business reports 'shortlist of five candidates is now under review by President Donald Trump.' (4) Nov 25 CNBC: Bessent says he has 'one interview remaining' before submitting recommendations — meaning as of Nov 25, formal presentation had NOT yet occurred. Rejected: Fox Business Nov 26 language ('under review by Trump') — ambiguous, does not explicitly confirm formal presentation/delivery occurred.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Condition (a) — Met: [Fox Business Nov 26](https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/bessent-wraps-up-fed-chair-interviews-trumps-decision-expected-before-christmas) explicitly states 'Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has concluded interviews for the Federal Reserve chair position.' [SCMP Nov 25](https://www.scmp.com/news/world/united-states-canada/article/3334145/trump-eyes-christmas-deadline-name-new-fed-chair-bessent-says) states 'He conducted his final second-round interviews with the candidates on November 25, 2025.' Condition (b) — NOT clearly met: [Anadolu Agency Nov 25](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-treasury-chief-says-trump-could-name-new-fed-chair-before-christmas/3753876) states Bessent 'plans to present his final list to Trump shortly after Thanksgiving' (future tense, as of Nov 25). [CNBC Nov 25](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/11/25/bessent-says-theres-a-very-good-chance-trump-names-new-fed-chair-before-christmas.html) says Bessent 'has one interview remaining' as of Nov 25. [Fox Business Nov 25](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/bessent-new-fed-chair-pick-coming-christmas) says Bessent 'expects to deliver the final list to Trump shortly after Thanksgiving.' No source within the window explicitly confirms that Bessent actually delivered/presented a formal shortlist to Trump before November 30, 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Condition (a) timestamp: November 25, 2025 (second round interviews concluded per multiple sources). Condition (b) timestamp: NOT extractable — no source explicitly confirms a formal presentation to Trump within the Nov 30 window. The planned presentation was 'shortly after Thanksgiving' (after Nov 27), and no confirmation of actual delivery was found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event was found for condition (b). Condition (a) clearly first occurred on approximately November 25, 2025. For condition (b), no qualifying event was found at all within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: CNBC (Nov 25) explicitly says Bessent 'has one interview remaining' as of that date, confirming condition (b) had NOT yet been satisfied on Nov 25. Fox Business (Nov 25) says he 'expects to deliver the final list to Trump shortly after Thanksgiving.' The Fox Business (Nov 26) statement that the shortlist 'is now under review by President Donald Trump' is at best ambiguous — it could mean Trump was informally aware of the five names (which was publicly reported) rather than that Bessent formally presented a recommendation. The resolution criteria explicitly state that ambiguity about whether a formal presentation has occurred resolves No. No source from Nov 28–30 was found confirming a completed formal delivery. The Sydney Morning Herald (Nov 27) says the process 'is expected to conclude this week' — future language. Multiple sources confirm the timeline for presentation was 'after Thanksgiving' meaning Nov 28 or later, with no confirmation it occurred by Nov 30.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Condition (a) is met: Bessent completed second-round interviews on approximately November 25, 2025. Condition (b) is NOT confirmed: No credible reporting explicitly confirms that Bessent formally presented a shortlist or recommendation to Trump before November 30, 2025. As of November 25, Bessent still had one interview remaining and planned to deliver the list 'shortly after Thanksgiving.' The resolution criteria explicitly state that ambiguous reporting (e.g., Bessent 'almost done' but hasn't presented) resolves No. Since both conditions must be met and condition (b) lacks explicit confirmation within the window, the question resolves No.

question: Will iPhone 17 cost more than iPhone 16?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the iPhone 17 base model is priced higher than $799 at the time it is launched for sale to the general public. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the pre-tax launch price in USD of the standard edition of the iPhone 17 as listed on the official Apple Store website or Apple’s retail pricing in the United States on the first official day of its release.

subquestions.question: Will Apple announce a $799 or higher starting price for the base iPhone 17 model at its September 9, 2025 event?

In the US, the iPhone 16 base model (128GB) launched at $799. The key question is whether Apple will price the standard iPhone 17 above this $799 threshold.

The ultimate question resolves Yes if the iPhone 17 base model is priced higher than $799 (i.e., $800 or more). The September 9 event will be the first official confirmation of pricing.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Apple officially announces base iPhone 17 starting price strictly greater than $799 (i.e., $800+) between Sept 1–10, 2025. Query 3: 'iPhone 17 $799 price official Apple announcement September 9' (to find specific price confirmation). evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: Apple's 'Awe Dropping' event on September 9, 2025, where iPhone 17 pricing was officially announced. Multiple articles from credible sources published on September 9, 2025 confirm the base iPhone 17 price. No conflicting announcements found within the window. AP News rounds to '$800' but notes it 'remains at $800' (likely rounding from $799 which is the exact price per all other sources). MacRumors (Sept 9) states '$799'. evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence within the window (Sept 1–9 pre-event articles were speculation, not official announcements). The official price was announced at the September 9 event — this is the first and only qualifying occurrence.
