Resolution: No. The definitive No moment was when Apple announced $799 at the September 9 event (approximately 10:00 AM PT = 17:00 UTC on September 9, 2025).

question: Will U.S. National debt surpass $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt surpasses 38 trillion dollars at any point before December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. national debt exceed $37.5 trillion as reported by the U.S. Treasury Department at any point between October 1, 2025 and October 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. national debt surpassed $37 trillion in August 2025, according to Treasury Department data. At the time, the debt was growing at roughly $1 trillion every five months — or approximately $6–7 billion per day. As of late September 2025, the debt was already well above $37 trillion and climbing steadily. The Congressional Budget Office estimated a roughly $1.8 trillion deficit for fiscal year 2025 (ending September 30, 2025), with outlays running about 6% higher year-over-year. The fiscal year 2025 deficit, combined with ongoing mandatory spending on Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, and surging net interest payments, continues to push debt higher. If the debt is near or above $37.5 trillion by early October, it would suggest the debt is on a trajectory to reach $38 trillion before the end of 2025 — the threshold in the ultimate question. Conversely, if the debt is significantly below $37.5 trillion, it would indicate a slower pace of accumulation that might make $38 trillion by late October less certain.

Sources:
- U.S. Treasury Debt to the Penny: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/debt-to-the-penny/debt-to-the-penny
- AP News, "US national debt reaches a record $37 trillion" (August 2025): https://apnews.com/article/national-debt-37-trillion-government-spending-a7cf0dce6a2cc9d5b91d36ec4bf9ab9d
- Fortune, "National debt hits a record $37 trillion" (August 2025): https://fortune.com/2025/08/29/national-debt-record-37-trillion/
- CBO, September 2025 Monthly Budget Review: https://www.cbo.gov/publication/61534
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between October 1, 2025 and October 15, 2025 (inclusive), the total public debt outstanding of the United States as reported by the U.S. Treasury Department exceeds $37,500,000,000,000 (thirty-seven trillion five hundred billion dollars). The primary data source is the Treasury's 'Debt to the Penny' dataset available at https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/debt-to-the-penny/debt-to-the-penny or via the TreasuryDirect API at https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current. If both sources are unavailable, any official U.S. Treasury Department statement or press release confirming the total debt level may be used. The question resolves No if the total public debt outstanding does not exceed $37.5 trillion on any reporting day within the resolution window. Note: The relevant figure is 'Total Public Debt Outstanding,' which includes both debt held by the public and intragovernmental holdings.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a near-term indicator of the pace of U.S. debt accumulation. If the debt has already crossed $37.5 trillion by mid-October, it would need to grow by only $500 billion more to reach $38 trillion — a pace consistent with or even slower than recent trends, making the ultimate question's $38 trillion threshold very likely to be met. If the debt has not yet reached $37.5 trillion, it would signal an unexpectedly slow rate of borrowing that would make the $38 trillion target less certain. This question measures a different, earlier milestone ($37.5T vs. $38T) and thus is a genuine leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: Total Public Debt Outstanding (U.S. Treasury) must exceed $37,500,000,000,000 at any point between Oct 1–Oct 15, 2025. Observable evidence: Treasury 'Debt to the Penny' data or official Treasury statements showing total debt > $37.5 trillion within the window. Key entities: U.S. Treasury Department; threshold: $37.5 trillion; window: Oct 1–15, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'U.S. national debt total public debt outstanding October 2025' — to find data points on total debt in October 2025. 2) 'US Treasury debt to the penny October 2025 trillion' — to find Treasury-specific data. 3) 'US debt $37.64 trillion government shutdown October 1 2025' — to find earliest specific Treasury figure. 4) 'national debt September 30 2025 end fiscal year total' — to establish pre-window baseline. 5) 'US national debt exceeds 37.5 trillion October 2025' — to find specific threshold crossing.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events found: (1) Oct 1, 2025 Gulf Times shutdown article references '$37.5 trillion national debt'; (2) Oct 2, 2025 American Spectator/Yahoo Finance: debt 'rising to $37.5 trillion by October 2025' per Daily Treasury Statement; (3) Oct 2-3, 2025: 'federal debt stands at $37.64 trillion' per U.S. Treasury data (cited in The Hindu, India Today); (4) Oct 3, 2025 JEC Senate report: '$37.85 trillion' as of Oct 3; (5) Oct 6, 2025: '$37.8 trillion' (Cryptopolitan); (6) Oct 7, 2025: '$37.8 trillion on October 7' per U.S. Treasury data (The Hill); (7) Oct 8, 2025: '$37.86 trillion' per U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data (Daily Caller, Conservative Daily News); (8) Oct 8, 2025: 'exceeding USD 37.9 trillion' (News Ghana). None rejected — all cite explicit Treasury data.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Criteria matched. [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/us-government-shutdown-trump-says-there-could-be-firings-and-project-cuts/article70120123.ece) explicitly states 'U.S. Treasury data confirms the federal debt stands at $37.64 trillion' as of Oct 2, 2025. [JEC Senate report](https://www.jec.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/republicans/newsroom?ContentRecord_id=0BC3C1E2-CF36-4754-B00F-68BF3BA1E408) confirms '$37.85 trillion' as of Oct 3, 2025. [Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2025/10/08/us-budget-deficit-hit-1-8-trillion-in-2025-cbo-reports/) states '$37.86 trillion as of October 8, 2025, according to U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data.' All values are far above the $37.5T threshold, from the very start of the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest confirmed timestamp: October 1, 2025 — Gulf Times and Senate shutdown articles reference '$37.5 trillion national debt' on Oct 1 (exactly at/near threshold). Confirmed exceeded by Oct 2, 2025 with Treasury data showing $37.64 trillion. Resolution timestamp set to October 1, 2025T00:00:00Z (first day of window, debt already at/above threshold).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence within the window exists because Oct 1 is the first day of the window. The debt was already at or above $37.5 trillion on the very first day of the resolution window. Pre-window data confirms the debt reached approximately $37.5T by end of September 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence found. All sources uniformly confirm debt was above $37.5T throughout the Oct 1–15 window. One CNBC article cited '$3.7 trillion' which is clearly a transcription error for '$37 trillion' (context confirms this). No source indicates the debt fell below $37.5T. Multiple independent sources (Senate JEC, Treasury fiscal data, CBO, financial media) all confirm figures well above $37.5T.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is YES. The U.S. total public debt outstanding exceeded $37.5 trillion from the very first day of the resolution window (October 1, 2025). Treasury data explicitly cited in multiple news sources confirms $37.64 trillion on October 2, $37.85 trillion on October 3, $37.86 trillion on October 8, and $37.9 trillion on October 8. This is unambiguous, explicit, and directly matches the resolution criteria.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly release a ChatGPT app update (non-beta) containing ad-related code references (e.g., 'ads feature', 'search ad', 'search ads carousel') to the Google Play Store or Apple App Store by January 5, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:

This beta version is not publicly available on the main app stores, but its existence signals that OpenAI is actively developing ad integration infrastructure. subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05 (inclusive), a publicly available (non-beta) version of the ChatGPT app on the Google Play Store or Apple App Store is confirmed by credible technical analysis (e.g., APK teardowns reported by reputable tech outlets such as The Verge, TechCrunch, Ars Technica, Engadget, or 9to5Google) to contain ad-related code references such as 'ads feature', 'search ad', 'search ads carousel', or equivalent ad-serving infrastructure. The version must be available for general download (not limited to beta testers or TestFlight users). If no such publicly released version is confirmed by credible sources by January 5, 2026, this resolves No. Primary sources: Google Play Store (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.openai.chatgpt), Apple App Store (https://apps.apple.com/app/chatgpt/id6448311069), and reporting from major technology publications.

As of early December 2025, ad code exists only in a beta build. If OpenAI ships this code to the general public in a stable app release within the next month, it would be a strong leading indicator that actual ad integration (the ultimate question) is imminent. Conversely, if the code remains confined to beta or is removed, it would suggest the timeline for ads is longer than March 2026. This question is distinct from the ultimate question because it asks about the presence of code infrastructure in a public release—not about users actually seeing live ads—making it an earlier, observable milestone.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: A non-beta (stable/production) version of the ChatGPT app on Google Play Store or Apple App Store must be confirmed (by credible APK teardown reporting from outlets like Engadget, TechCrunch, The Verge, Ars Technica, or 9to5Google) to contain ad-related code references ('ads feature', 'search ad', 'search ads carousel' or equivalent) between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05. evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'ChatGPT app ads code APK teardown ad-related features' (Dec 6–Jan 5); 2) 'OpenAI ChatGPT advertising search ads carousel app store update' (Dec 6–Jan 5); 3) 'ChatGPT Android app non-beta public release ad code December 2025' (Dec 6–Jan 5); 4) 'ChatGPT app APK teardown search ads ads feature public version stable release' (Nov 1–Jan 5); 5) 'OpenAI ChatGPT advertising confirmed public app store release January 2026' (Dec 6–Jan 5).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: Ad-related code strings ('ads feature', 'search ad', 'search ads carousel', 'bazaar content') found in ChatGPT Android app version 1.2025.329, first discovered November 29, 2025 by Tibor Blaho, reported by Adweek (Dec 9), BleepingComputer (Nov 29), BGR, BetaNews, Android Central, Engadget (Dec 7), Business Today (Dec 8). REJECTED: All sources consistently describe this as a BETA build (Android beta version 1.2025.329), not a stable/non-beta public release. No reports during Dec 6–Jan 5 window identify a stable production release with ad code.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All confirmed reports of ad-related code in the ChatGPT Android app reference the BETA build (version 1.2025.329 beta). [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/artificial-intelligence/leak-confirms-openai-is-preparing-ads-on-chatgpt-for-public-roll-out/) specifies 'ChatGPT Android app version 1.2025.329 beta.' The resolution criteria explicitly requires non-beta versions. No credible source reports ad-related code in a stable/non-beta production release during the window. Additionally, OpenAI denied running ads, disabled its 'app suggestion' feature, and issued a 'Code Red' pausing ad initiatives.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The ad code discovery was November 29, 2025 (before the question window starts Dec 6, 2025), and refers to a beta build. No stable-release equivalent was reported within the Dec 6–Jan 5 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying earlier occurrence in the window was found, because no qualifying occurrence (stable/non-beta app with ad code confirmed by credible analysis) was found at all during the window.

No outlet in the required list (The Verge, TechCrunch, Ars Technica, Engadget, 9to5Google) confirmed ad-related code in a stable/non-beta public ChatGPT app release during the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition was NOT met. All reports of ad-related code reference BETA builds, not stable/non-beta public releases. The resolution criteria specifically requires non-beta versions. No credible technical analysis (APK teardown by qualifying outlets) confirmed ad-related code in a stable production ChatGPT app release between Dec 6, 2025 and Jan 5, 2026. The question resolves No, with the window closing on Jan 5, 2026 without the condition being satisfied.

subquestions.background_information:
One of the six trigger conditions that would cause the ultimate 'Nothing Ever Happens: Military Edition' market to resolve 'No' is a 'US-Russia nuclear deal.' As of November 2025, the 2010 New START treaty — which limits each country to 1,550 deployed strategic nuclear warheads and 700 deployed missiles and bombers — remains in a precarious state. Russia suspended its participation in the treaty in February 2023, though it has continued to observe its central limits. In October 2025, Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed hope for extending New START for another year, and Trump responded that a treaty extension 'sounds like a good idea to me.' Putin warned that if the U.S. declines to extend, Russia will continue strengthening its nuclear arsenal, leaving the world's two largest nuclear powers without any formal arms control framework. Despite positive rhetoric, no formal agreement has been reached. Trump and Putin have held summits (including in Anchorage) and phone calls, and a meeting in Budapest is reportedly being planned. Any formal announcement of a nuclear arms deal between the US and Russia before end of 2025 would trigger the ultimate market's 'No' resolution.

A joint statement expressing desire to continue talks, without a concrete agreement on terms, does not count. Resolution will be determined by checking official White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov), U.S. State Department (https://www.state.gov), and Kremlin (http://en.kremlin.ru) press releases and statements, as well as major international news sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) and the Associated Press (https://apnews.com). subquestions.rationale: A US-Russia nuclear deal is one of the six specific trigger events that would cause the ultimate market to resolve 'No.' Tracking whether such a deal materializes in the near term is a direct early indicator. If a deal is announced in this window, it would definitively flip the ultimate market to 'No.' Even a near-miss (e.g., a scheduled summit or advanced negotiations) would update forecasters' estimates on whether such a deal could materialize before the December 31, 2025 deadline. The current diplomatic momentum — with planned meetings in Budapest and ongoing discussions — makes this a plausible but far-from-certain outcome, placing forecasts in an informative range rather than near 0% or 100%.

question: NATO x Russia military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between September 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

On September 10, 2025, up to 19 Russian drones violated Polish airspace during a massive Russian strike on Ukraine. Polish, Dutch, and Italian fighter jets shot down at least three drones, marking the first time NATO forces directly engaged Russian military assets since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Poland invoked Article 4 of the NATO treaty (consultation), but stopped short of invoking Article 5 (collective defense). Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident brought Europe 'closer to open conflict since World War II,' and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said indications suggest the incursion was intentional. NATO subsequently launched 'Operation Eastern Sentry,' increasing air patrols and deploying ground-based interceptor systems along the alliance's eastern flank. Russia's Zapad-2025 military exercises with Belarus, involving 20,000 troops and advanced weapons systems including Iskander ballistic missiles, ran concurrently. NATO fighter jets also intercepted Russian Su-30 combat aircraft carrying Kh-31 supersonic anti-radar missiles over the Baltic Sea on September 17, 2025. The distinction between Article 4 (consultation) and Article 5 (collective defense, which treats an attack on one member as an attack on all) is crucial: invoking Article 5 would represent a dramatic escalation and would likely precede or accompany a direct NATO-Russia military clash. As of September 24, 2025, Article 5 has not been invoked.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if NATO officially invokes Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty between September 24, 2025 and October 24, 2025 (inclusive). The invocation must be confirmed by an official NATO statement published on nato.int or by a formal communiqué from the North Atlantic Council. Informal references to Article 5 by individual member states, or invocations of Article 4 (consultation), do not qualify. If NATO's official website (https://www.nato.int) is unavailable, resolution may rely on official NATO social media accounts or statements reported by at least two major international wire services (AP, Reuters, AFP). If the invocation is announced but takes effect after October 24, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: An Article 5 invocation would be the clearest institutional precursor to a full NATO-Russia military clash. The September 10 drone incursion into Poland already resulted in NATO forces shooting down Russian drones — but Poland invoked only Article 4 (consultation), not Article 5. Forecasters who believe a NATO-Russia military clash is likely in 2025 would generally assign higher probability to Article 5 being invoked, since Article 5 is the formal mechanism by which NATO would collectively respond to a Russian attack on a member state. Conversely, forecasters who believe the situation will be managed through deterrence and de-escalation would assign low probability to Article 5. This question tracks whether the current escalation spiral — drone incursions, armed interceptions, and military exercises — crosses the threshold from incident management to collective defense posture, which is a strong leading indicator of whether a broader military clash occurs before year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: NATO officially invokes Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty between September 24 and October 24, 2025 (inclusive), confirmed by official NATO statement on nato.int or formal North Atlantic Council communiqué. Article 4 invocations do not qualify. Key entities: NATO, North Atlantic Council, Russia. Threshold: official Article 5 invocation only.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'NATO Article 5 invocation collective defense 2025' (Sept 24–Oct 24) — to find direct evidence of invocation; 2) 'NATO collective defense invoked Russia military action October 2025' — to find triggering events; 3) 'NATO Article 5 officially invoked North Atlantic Council statement October 2025' — to find official statements; 4) 'NATO defense ministers Brussels meeting Article 4 Article 5 Russia drones October 2025' — to check ministerial outcomes; 5) '"Article 5" NATO invoked triggered activated 2025' — to find any activation.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Poland invoked Article 4 on September 10 following Russian drone incursions — does not qualify (Article 4, not 5); (2) Estonia invoked Article 4 after Russian MiG-31 jets violated airspace on September 19 — does not qualify (Article 4, not 5); (3) Denmark considered but did NOT invoke Article 4 — does not qualify; (4) NATO defense ministers met in Brussels on October 15 to discuss drone wall, air defenses, Ukraine support — no Article 5 invocation. No Article 5 invocation was found in any source.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All sources consistently state Article 5 was NOT invoked during this period. evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: all sources agree Article 5 was not invoked. The Newsweek article from October 20 explicitly discusses Russia's belief that NATO will NOT invoke Article 5, framing it as a future hypothetical — confirming it had not been invoked.
evidence.step8_final_decision: NATO did not invoke Article 5 during the September 24 – October 24, 2025 window. Russian military actions (drone incursions into Poland, Romania; MiG-31 airspace violation in Estonia) prompted Article 4 consultations and operational responses, but fell short of triggering Article 5. All sources consistently confirm Article 5 has only ever been invoked once in NATO history (post-9/11), with no new invocation occurring during this period. Resolution: No.

question: Will the EU impose new tariffs on US goods in 2025?
description:

Any tariff which is officially enacted within the market's time frame will qualify, regardless of when the tariff goes into effect.

Only tariffs specifically targeting the U.S. will qualify. For example, a global tariff (tariffs on all imports into the EU) will not count toward this market's resolution.

Tariffs enacted by EU member states will not count. Only Tariffs imposed by the EU will qualify.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the European Union, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the European Commission formally propose or adopt countermeasures (retaliatory tariffs) specifically targeting U.S. goods between October 31, 2025 and November 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The EU and the U.S. reached a framework trade deal in July-August 2025 under which the U.S. imposes a 15% tariff on most EU goods and 27.5% on EU automobiles. The EU agreed to eliminate tariffs on U.S. industrial goods and provide preferential access for U.S. agricultural and seafood products (https://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-u-s-e-u-tariff-deal-is-now-on-paper-and-it-includes-lng-and-ai-chip-purchases-9fba0fa6). However, tensions remain. The U.S. continues to hold elevated tariffs on EU cars as leverage until the EU legislates its promised tariff reductions (https://nypost.com/2025/08/21/business/us-keeping-lofty-eu-car-tariffs-until-levies-on-american-goods-dropped/). Meanwhile, the EU has signaled willingness to act independently on trade — for example, proposing a 50% tariff on steel imports exceeding reduced quotas (https://www.bruegel.org/analysis/eu-should-moderate-its-steel-protection-plan), though that measure is framed as a global safeguard rather than a U.S.-specific tariff. EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic has emphasized that EU trade measures must comply with WTO guidelines and require consensus among 27 member states plus European Parliament approval (https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202510/16/WS67100e6fa310f1265a1d57aa.html). As of late October 2025, the EU has not enacted retaliatory tariffs specifically targeting U.S. goods, though the EU retains a pre-existing legal framework for countermeasures (dating back to the 2018 steel dispute) and has previously adopted rebalancing tariffs on U.S. goods such as bourbon, motorcycles, and jeans.

Sources:
- MarketWatch (2025-08-21): https://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-u-s-e-u-tariff-deal-is-now-on-paper-and-it-includes-lng-and-ai-chip-purchases-9fba0fa6
- New York Post (2025-08-21): https://nypost.com/2025/08/21/business/us-keeping-lofty-eu-car-tariffs-until-levies-on-american-goods-dropped/
- Bruegel (2025-10-09): https://www.bruegel.org/analysis/eu-should-moderate-its-steel-protection-plan
- China Daily (2025-10-16): https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202510/16/WS67100e6fa310f1265a1d57aa.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 29, 2025 (inclusive), the European Commission publishes a formal proposal, or the Council of the European Union adopts a regulation, imposing new or increased tariffs (countermeasures, rebalancing duties, or retaliatory tariffs) that specifically target goods originating from the United States. The measure must explicitly single out U.S.-origin goods; global safeguard measures that apply to all countries equally (such as the proposed steel safeguard) do not count. Resolution will be based on official publications in the Official Journal of the European Union (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/oj/direct-access.html), European Commission press releases (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en), or a consensus of at least two credible international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Financial Times, Bloomberg). If no such proposal or adoption occurs during this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the EU will impose new tariffs on U.S. goods by the end of 2025. The existence of a formal Commission proposal or Council adoption of U.S.-specific countermeasures during November 2025 would be the most direct leading indicator that such tariffs will be enacted by December 2025. The July-August framework deal reduced immediate tensions, but the deal's implementation depends on both sides following through — the U.S. is withholding auto tariff relief as leverage, and any breakdown in negotiations could trigger EU retaliation. Tracking whether the Commission moves toward formal countermeasures in November provides a strong early signal of the ultimate outcome, since EU legislative processes require formal proposals before enactment. If no such proposal emerges by late November, it becomes much less likely the EU would impose U.S.-specific tariffs by December 2, 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: European Commission publishes a formal proposal OR Council of the EU adopts a regulation imposing new/increased tariffs specifically targeting U.S.-origin goods between October 31 – November 29, 2025. Observable evidence: Official Journal EU publication, EC press release, or consensus of 2+ credible outlets. Key entities: European Commission, Council of the EU. Threshold: Must explicitly single out U.S.-origin goods; global safeguard measures don't count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'European Commission retaliatory tariffs US goods countermeasures 2025' - to find any formal proposals; 2. 'EU rebalancing duties United States tariffs November 2025' - to find rebalancing/retaliatory actions; 3. 'European Commission formal proposal retaliatory tariffs United States November 2025' - direct match search; 4. 'EU countermeasures retaliation US trade war tariffs November October 2025' - broader search; 5. 'EU Official Journal retaliation tariff United States October November 2025' - official source search; 6. 'EU suspended rebalancing tariffs US goods 18 billion 2025' - searching for earlier suspended measures being reimposed
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events qualifying as retaliatory tariffs against US goods were found. The major EU-US trade event during this window was the Council (November 28, 2025) adopting negotiating mandates for two regulations that ELIMINATE tariffs on U.S. industrial goods and grant preferential access to certain U.S. agricultural products - the opposite of retaliatory measures. The EU-US relationship during this window was characterized by cooperative implementation of a July/August 2025 joint trade agreement, with the EU seeking more tariff exemptions from the US, not imposing retaliatory duties. The only steel-related news involved a global safeguard mechanism (not US-specific), and the UK was considering retaliation against EU steel tariffs (unrelated). A WTO arbitration ruling on olives was mentioned (Nov 3, 2025), but this was a WTO authorization, not a formal EU proposal/adoption within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found matching resolution criteria. The November 28, 2025 Council action [Council of EU press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2025/11/28/eu-us-trade-relations-council-moves-forward-in-implementing-the-tariff-elements-of-the-joint-statement/) adopted negotiating mandates to REDUCE/ELIMINATE tariffs on US goods - this is directly contrary to the resolution criteria which requires imposing NEW or INCREASED tariffs on US goods. Multiple sources confirm the EU was actively pursuing trade cooperation with the US during this period [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/business/2025/11/28/eu-member-states-back-von-der-leyens-controversial-trade-deal-terms-under-pressure-from-tr), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/eu-prepares-plan-implement-trade-075027612.html). The WTO olive arbitration result mentioned on Nov 3 authorized EU countermeasures up to $13.64M annually but no formal Commission proposal or Council adoption occurred during the window per [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/spanish-black-olive-exporters-urge-eu-to-hit-back-on-us-tariffs-4327057).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. The window closed November 29, 2025 with no retaliatory tariff action against US goods.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at all within the window, so first-occurrence check is moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification confirms the opposite dynamic: the EU-US Joint Statement (August 21, 2025) was being implemented cooperatively. The Council's November 28 action was specifically to reduce/eliminate EU tariffs on US goods. EU-US meetings on November 24, 2025 focused on EU seeking more tariff relief FROM the US, not imposing tariffs ON the US. No contradictory evidence (no source reports any EU retaliatory tariff proposal against US goods). The Mondaq article mentions earlier (April 2025) EU signals to impose countermeasures worth ~€18 billion, but a trade deal was reached and those measures were suspended/abandoned, not revived during this window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. All evidence indicates the European Commission/Council did not formally propose or adopt any retaliatory tariffs targeting U.S.-origin goods between October 31 – November 29, 2025. The dominant trade dynamic was cooperative implementation of the EU-US Joint Statement, with the Council on November 28, 2025 adopting negotiating mandates to reduce and eliminate tariffs on US goods. The window closed without any qualifying event.

question: Karen Bass out as Mayor of LA in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will the Los Angeles City Council initiate a formal motion or hearing related to removing, censuring, or recalling Mayor Karen Bass between September 1 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Karen Bass has faced mounting political pressure throughout 2025. Her approval ratings dropped significantly following her handling of the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, with a UCLA Luskin School Quality of Life Index survey showing a net favorability rating of negative 12 (The Hill, June 2025). She has also faced criticism over her management of a nearly $1 billion budget shortfall, which led to over 1,600 proposed layoffs (CBS News, May 2025). Additional crises have included immigration protests and the deployment of National Guard troops to Los Angeles (The Hill, June 2025). While no formal recall or removal effort has been initiated as of September 1, 2025, political opponents and critics have intensified scrutiny. Under the Los Angeles City Charter (Section 200), the City Council has certain oversight powers, and recall efforts require petition signatures from 15% of registered voters. A formal Council motion targeting Bass's position would be a significant escalation and a strong early indicator that she could leave office before the end of 2025.

Sources:
- The Hill, 'Karen Bass thrust back into hot seat amid LA unrest' (June 12, 2025): https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/4754321-karen-bass-la-unrest/
- CBS News, 'Mayor Bass says she'll take a pay cut as city's budget concerns continue' (May 5, 2025): https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/mayor-bass-says-shell-take-a-pay-cut-as-citys-budget-concerns-continue/
- Los Angeles City Charter, Section 200 et seq.: https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-68898
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), the Los Angeles City Council introduces a formal motion, resolution, or scheduled committee hearing that specifically addresses the removal, censure, or recall of Mayor Karen Bass. Evidence must come from official City Council records (available at https://cityclerk.lacity.org/lacityclerkconnect/) or credible news reporting from outlets such as the Los Angeles Times (https://www.latimes.com/), ABC7 Los Angeles (https://abc7.com/), or CBS News Los Angeles (https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/). Informal public statements by individual Council members calling for resignation, without a formal motion or hearing, do not count. If no such formal action is introduced during this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A formal City Council action targeting Bass's position would be one of the strongest near-term indicators that she could leave office before the end of 2025. While Bass could resign voluntarily or face a recall petition, Council-level action is an observable institutional signal that political dynamics have shifted decisively against her. The absence of such action would suggest that, despite low approval ratings and political criticism, the institutional status quo is holding and Bass is likely to remain in office through year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) The Los Angeles City Council formally introducing a motion, resolution, or scheduling a committee hearing specifically addressing the removal, censure, or recall of Mayor Karen Bass; (2) this must occur between September 1–30, 2025 (inclusive); (3) evidence must come from official City Council records or credible news outlets. Informal calls for resignation by individual council members do NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Los Angeles City Council motion censure recall Mayor Karen Bass 2025' (Sept 1–30) — to find any formal council action; Query 2: 'LA City Council formal hearing remove Karen Bass September 2025' (Sept 1–30) — to find committee hearings; Query 3: 'Karen Bass recall effort petition Los Angeles 2025' (Sept 1–30) — to find recall petition efforts; Query 4: 'Los Angeles City Council motion against Mayor Bass removal oust' (Aug 1–Sept 30) — to find any precursor activity; Query 5: '"city council" "Karen Bass" censure motion resolution September 2025' (Sept 1–30) — targeted query; Query 6: 'Karen Bass recall effort dropped abandoned housing transit September 2025' (Sept 1–30) — to find if recall efforts were dropped.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) One social media aggregator article (superpunch.net, Sept 18, 2025) mentions in a tweet that 'efforts to recall Bass were abandoned after she pledged to fight housing tooth and nail' — this refers to an external recall effort (not a City Council action) that was reportedly ABANDONED, not initiated. (2) The former LAFD Chief Kristin Crowley filed a legal claim against Bass (August 2025), but this is a legal tort claim, not a City Council motion. (3) Two Council members (Monica Rodriguez and Traci Park) sided with Crowley when she appealed her dismissal, but the full council voted 13-2 to uphold Bass's decision — this is contrary evidence, showing council was not acting against Bass. (4) Coverage throughout September 2025 shows Bass working cooperatively WITH the City Council on budgets, Convention Center expansion, Olympics preparation — no adversarial formal council actions found. No candidate events match the resolution criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No news article from September 1–30, 2025 reports the LA City Council introducing a formal motion, resolution, or committee hearing specifically addressing the removal, censure, or recall of Mayor Karen Bass. The only reference to recall efforts is a secondary social media post indicating such efforts were ABANDONED [superpunch.net](https://www.superpunch.net/2025/09/todays-news-and-jokes_0443885371.html). All other September 2025 coverage shows Bass and the City Council operating cooperatively on major city initiatives including budget negotiations, Convention Center expansion (council voted 11-2 in favor Sept 19), LAPD hiring directives, and Olympics preparation.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a qualifying event exists because no qualifying event occurred. The absence of evidence across multiple targeted searches covering the entire September 2025 window supports this conclusion.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found in the window. All searches for formal council action against Bass in September 2025 returned null results for this specific criterion. The news landscape shows Bass actively working with the council on cooperative legislative and budgetary matters throughout the month.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) A recall effort reportedly existed at some point but was abandoned by mid-September 2025, suggesting no formal City Council recall/censure action occurred. (2) The 13-2 City Council vote in August upholding Bass's firing of Crowley shows the council was broadly supportive of the mayor. (3) The 11-2 vote for the Convention Center expansion on Sept 19 further confirms cooperative relationship. (4) Multiple credible news sources (ABC7, NBC LA, LA Times, FOX 11, CBS News) covered September 2025 LA City Hall news extensively but none reported any formal motion/hearing against Bass. The resolution criteria are unambiguous and not met.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence strongly indicates that no formal motion, resolution, or committee hearing addressing the removal, censure, or recall of Mayor Karen Bass was introduced by the Los Angeles City Council during September 1–30, 2025. The City Council appears to have been cooperatively working with Mayor Bass throughout the entire month. The recall efforts that did exist were external (not from the council) and reportedly abandoned. This question resolves No at the close of the window on September 30, 2025.

question: Will US or Israel strike Iran by December 31, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US or Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US or Israeli military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US or Israeli missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Iran's Supreme Leader or senior Iranian military officials publicly threaten imminent retaliation against the US or Israel in response to a specific provocation between January 20 and February 15, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-January 2026, tensions between Iran, the US, and Israel remain extremely high following the June 2025 military exchanges. In June 2025, Israel conducted airstrikes on Iran killing high-ranking military officials and nuclear scientists, Iran retaliated with Operation True Promise III (hundreds of ballistic missiles and drones targeting Tel Aviv), the US struck three Iranian nuclear facilities on June 22, Iran struck a US base in Qatar on June 23, and a ceasefire was brokered on June 24, 2025 (https://en.trend.az/iran/politics/3963684.html). Since then, Iran has conducted military exercises in the Gulf firing ballistic and cruise missiles at simulated targets in December 2025 (https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf-firing-ballistic-cruise-missiles-at-simulated-targets). Iran is experiencing its most severe nationwide protests in decades, with nearly 2,600 reported deaths since late December 2025, and President Trump has warned Tehran of 'very strong action' if protesters are executed. Iranian Parliament Speaker Qalibaf has stated that US forces, bases, and Israeli targets would be 'legitimate military objectives' if Washington conducts strikes (https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/us-bases-in-the-line-of-iranian-firepower/articleshow/117229744.cms). Reports indicate the US has been preparing advanced strike capabilities including the GBU-57 bunker buster and stealth bomber platforms for potential 2026 operations (https://www.news18.com/world/missiles-that-think-bombs-that-dig-the-weapons-that-could-define-trumps-next-iran-decision-ws-9196157.html). Explicit public threats from Iran's top leadership citing a specific provocation (such as US support for protesters, new sanctions, or military posturing) would be an important escalation indicator preceding a potential US or Israeli strike.

The threat must reference a concrete recent event or action as its trigger, not merely restate long-standing general hostility. General statements of deterrence or reaffirmations of existing policy (e.g., 'we will respond if attacked') do not qualify; the statement must indicate a new, escalated threat tied to a specific provocation occurring on or after January 20, 2026. If Iran's leadership issues new specific threats in this period, it signals either that a provocation has already occurred that could trigger strikes, or that the cycle of escalation is intensifying toward military conflict. Conversely, if rhetoric remains at baseline levels, it suggests the ceasefire is holding and a near-term strike is less likely. This is a meaningful crux because forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question likely diverge on whether the current protest crisis and US posturing will escalate into a new military confrontation — and new specific threats from Iranian leadership would be among the earliest observable indicators of that escalation.

evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate 1 (Jan 20): Gen. Shekarchi (Armed Forces Spokesman) threatens to 'set fire to their world' in response to Trump's call for regime change — reported by AP and Al Jazeera. REJECTED: Shekarchi is not the Supreme Leader, President, IRGC Commander, or Speaker of Parliament as required by resolution criteria. Candidate 2 (Jan 21): FM Araghchi in WSJ op-ed threatens full retaliation. REJECTED: Araghchi is Foreign Minister, not a qualifying official. Candidate 3 (Jan 28): Shamkhani (adviser to Khamenei) threatens 'heart of Tel Aviv' if US attacks. REJECTED: Shamkhani is an adviser, not a qualifying official. Candidate 4 (Feb 1): Khamenei warns 'if they start a war, this time it will be a regional war' — in response to USS Abraham Lincoln deployment — reported by AP and Al Jazeera. POTENTIALLY QUALIFYING but this is a conditional deterrence statement ('if attacked'), which resolution criteria explicitly excludes. Candidate 5 (Jan 31): Army Chief Hatami warns forces on 'high alert' — reported by AFP. REJECTED: Hatami is Army Chief, not Commander of IRGC (different organization). Parliament Speaker Qalibaf (Feb 1): Declares EU armies as terrorist groups in response to EU's IRGC designation. REJECTED: Targets EU armies, not US or Israel specifically.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The most prominent candidate — Khamenei's Feb 1 statement reported by [AP](https://apnews.com/article/iran-eu-terrorist-groups-protests-c0023d9ff1e7c4e6fa92077d640e244c) and [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/1/khamenei-warns-us-of-regional-war-if-iran-is-attacked) — is conditional ('if they start a war'), which the resolution criteria explicitly excludes as a 'general statement of deterrence.' The criteria requires the threat to 'indicate a new, escalated threat tied to a specific provocation' and explicitly excludes 'we will respond if attacked' type statements. Khamenei's statement, while tied to the specific USS Abraham Lincoln deployment, is framed as 'if you attack, there will be regional war' — exactly the type of conditional deterrence excluded. No statement by the Supreme Leader, President, IRGC Commander, or Parliament Speaker was found that explicitly threatened IMMINENT military RETALIATION (not conditional) against the US or Israel. All Iranian threats found in the window were conditional ('if attacked') rather than promises of imminent offensive action.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Khamenei statement: February 1, 2026 — exact date available from AP and Al Jazeera. Shekarchi statement: January 20, 2026 — exact date from AP article. These are reliable timestamps but the qualifying criterion of non-conditional threats against US/Israel by named officials is not met.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest potentially qualifying event would be the Shekarchi statement on January 20, but he is not one of the named qualifying officials. The next event from a named qualifying official is Khamenei's Feb 1 statement, but it is conditional deterrence rather than an explicit imminent threat.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for: (1) Whether any IRGC Commander specifically made qualifying statements — not found. (2) Whether Iranian President made qualifying statements — President Pezeshkian made statements about retaliation 'in event of attack' (Jan 30, Al Arabiya) but these are also conditional. (3) Whether Parliament Speaker targeted US/Israel specifically — Qalibaf targeted EU armies, not US/Israel. (4) Whether any threat was non-conditional — all threats were framed as 'if attacked, we will respond,' which the resolution criteria explicitly excludes. The resolution criteria is highly specific and the 'general deterrence' exclusion rules out all observed qualifying-official statements from the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: While there was extensive Iranian threatening rhetoric throughout the January 20 to February 15, 2026 window, the resolution criteria requires specifically (a) named officials (Supreme Leader, President, IRGC Commander, or Parliament Speaker), (b) making explicit non-conditional threats of IMMINENT military action (not 'if attacked'), (c) tied to a specific provocation, (d) covered by at least two qualifying outlets. All statements by named qualifying officials found were conditional deterrence statements ('if attacked, we will respond'), which the resolution criteria explicitly excludes. The question therefore resolves No — no qualifying event meeting all criteria was found within the window.

question: California redistricting referendum passes?
description:
Proposition 50 is a 2025 legislatively referred constitutional amendment on congressional redistricting, proposed for the statewide special election in California currently set for November 4, 2025.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Proposition 50 or any other legislatively referred statewide measure that authorizes or implements congressional redistricting is approved by a majority of voters at the California statewide special election currently set for November 4, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

If by the last legally operative deadline for placing measures on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot—including any deadline set or modified by the statute calling that special election—no qualifying legislatively referred measure has been approved for submission to voters, and there is no enacted statute or pending court order that could still place such a measure on that ballot, the market will resolve “No”.

If the election is officially rescheduled, the same rule applies to the new ballot and its corresponding deadlines.

The resolution source will be based on the official certified results of the vote as published by  State of California. Subsequent litigation, administrative challenges, or failure of any post-approval triggers will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will a major organized 'No on Proposition 50' campaign committee report raising at least $10 million in total contributions by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Proposition 50 is a legislatively referred constitutional amendment on the November 4, 2025 California special election ballot. It would temporarily allow the state legislature to redraw congressional district maps, bypassing the independent Citizens Redistricting Commission for the 2026, 2028, and 2030 elections. A Berkeley IGS poll from August 11-17, 2025 found 48% support, 32% opposition, and 20% undecided among registered voters (https://medium.com/@bfriedmandc/the-california-redistricting-proposition-50-has-a-very-high-probability-of-passing-d2b5d9ec0cb4). A separate Politico-Citrin Center poll found only 36% of California voters support returning redistricting authority to the legislature versus 64% who favor the independent commission (https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/5062670-california-redistricting-special-election/). The opposition includes former Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger, the League of Women Voters, and the California Republican Party. Republicans have filed multiple legal challenges, all denied by the California Supreme Court (https://www.courthousenews.com/california-high-court-denies-second-republican-attempt-to-halt-special-redistricting-election/). National Republican groups and the Trump administration have also signaled opposition (https://abc7news.com/post/trump-california-republicans-move-block-newsoms-redistricting-ballot-measure/16183052/). Whether the opposition can mount a well-funded campaign is a key indicator of whether Prop 50 could be defeated. California ballot measure campaigns routinely spend tens of millions of dollars. Campaign finance filings are publicly available through the California Secretary of State's Cal-Access system.

Sources:
- Berkeley IGS Poll analysis: https://medium.com/@bfriedmandc/the-california-redistricting-proposition-50-has-a-very-high-probability-of-passing-d2b5d9ec0cb4
- The Hill on 5 things to know: https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/5062670-california-redistricting-special-election/
- Court House News on Supreme Court denial: https://www.courthousenews.com/california-high-court-denies-second-republican-attempt-to-halt-special-redistricting-election/
- ABC7 on Trump/GOP opposition: https://abc7news.com/post/trump-california-republicans-move-block-newsoms-redistricting-ballot-measure/16183052/
- Cal-Access campaign finance database: https://cal-access.sos.ca.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive), any committee registered with the California Secretary of State that is primarily organized to oppose Proposition 50 (the November 4, 2025 redistricting constitutional amendment) reports cumulative total contributions received of at least $10 million, as reflected in filings available through the California Secretary of State's Cal-Access system (https://cal-access.sos.ca.gov/) or the California Fair Political Practices Commission (https://www.fppc.ca.gov/). The committee's name or stated purpose must clearly indicate opposition to Proposition 50 or the redistricting ballot measure. If multiple opposition committees exist, their totals are NOT combined — at least one single committee must meet the $10 million threshold. If Cal-Access data is unavailable, credible news reports citing official filings may be used as a fallback. If no qualifying opposition committee has been registered by September 30, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The level of funding behind the 'No on Prop 50' campaign is a critical early indicator of whether Proposition 50 will pass. Despite initial polling showing majority support among decided voters, the Politico-Citrin poll showed 64% of voters prefer the independent commission — suggesting the 'No' side has a persuasion opportunity if it can fund a major campaign. With 20% of voters undecided in August polling, a well-funded opposition campaign ($10M+ by end of September) could significantly shift voter opinion during October. Conversely, if the opposition fails to raise substantial funds, it signals that organized resistance is weak and the measure is very likely to pass. This fundraising threshold is observable well before the election and provides a meaningful signal about the ultimate outcome that goes beyond simply restating the election question.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) A committee registered with CA Secretary of State, (2) with name/purpose clearly indicating opposition to Proposition 50, (3) reporting cumulative total contributions of at least $10 million, (4) as reflected in Cal-Access filings available between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 inclusive. The $10 million threshold must be met by a SINGLE committee (not combined totals). The committee 'Protect Voters First' (also known as 'Hold Politicians Accountable') led by Charles T. Munger Jr. is the primary candidate.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'California Proposition 50 2025 redistricting campaign committee fundraising' — to find general fundraising reporting; 2) 'No on Proposition 50 California 2025 opposition committee contributions' — to find specific No committee data; 3) 'Charles Munger Protect Voters First Hold Politicians Accountable Proposition 50 $30 million raised' — to confirm specific committee totals; 4) 'No on Prop 50 Stop Sacramento Power Grab Munger fundraising $30 million committee total' — to confirm September totals; 5) 'Protect Voters First No on Prop 50 committee September 2025 total raised contributions $10 million $20 million $30 million' — to confirm the committee crossed $10M in September
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: 'Protect Voters First' (also registered as 'Hold Politicians Accountable') committee, led by Charles T. Munger Jr., opposed to Prop 50. As of August 21, 2025, Munger had already contributed $10 million (plus $90k on Aug 22) to the committee. By late August 2025, opponents had raised 'more than $10 million' (Long Beach Post, Aug 27). By September 18-27, 2025, multiple sources confirm the committee raised approximately $30 million total — almost entirely from Munger plus $5 million from Congressional Leadership Fund. The KQED article (Sep 27) reports $26.7 million already deployed from Munger's $30 million contribution. No other committee (e.g., 'Stop Sacramento's Power Grab' led by Kevin McCarthy/Jessica Millan Patterson) was close — it raised only about $5-6k initially and $5.2 million total per KQED.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The 'Protect Voters First' committee (also known as 'Hold Politicians Accountable' per Long Beach Post [https://lbpost.com/news/politics/stunned-by-that-stack-of-redistricting-mailers-hitting-your-mailbox-here-are-tips-to-follow-the-money/]) is registered with CA Secretary of State and is named as an opposition committee. Multiple sources confirm its total exceeds $30 million by mid-September 2025, far exceeding the $10 million threshold. The committee name clearly indicates opposition to Prop 50 — it is described as the 'No on Prop. 50 – Protect Voters First' campaign [Redding Record Searchlight, Sep 20, https://www.redding.com/story/news/nation/california/2025/09/19/who-is-charles-munger-jr-the-megadonor-fighting-redistricting/86248482007/]. The ArcaMax article (Sep 18, https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3857014) states: 'Munger has already contributed $30 million of his own money' with Congressional Leadership Fund adding $5 million. This is a single committee exceeding $10 million. The KQED article (Sep 27, https://www.kqed.org/news/12057425/millions-pour-into-california-fight-over-newsoms-redistricting-ballot-measure) further confirms $26.7 million deployed from Munger's $30 million donation to the committee.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The committee crossed $10 million on or around August 21, 2025 (when Munger made a $10 million contribution), which is BEFORE the resolution window. However, the resolution window asks whether filings available between September 1-30, 2025 reflect cumulative totals of at least $10 million. Multiple news articles citing official Cal-Access filings throughout September 2025 confirm the cumulative total at $30+ million throughout the entire window. The earliest within-window reporting date is September 1, 2025 (or effectively the start of the window), as the $10 million threshold was already exceeded before the window opened and maintained throughout. The KQED article dated 2025-09-27 provides the most precise within-window timestamp confirming $26.7-30 million raised.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The $10 million threshold was crossed BEFORE the window (August 21, 2025), but filings reporting cumulative totals above $10 million were certainly available and reportable throughout the September 1-30, 2025 window. The resolution criteria asks if a committee 'reports' cumulative total contributions of at least $10 million as 'reflected in filings available through Cal-Access' between September 1-30, 2025. Since the contributions happened in August and the committee continued filing throughout September (with totals growing to $30 million+), Cal-Access filings within the September 1-30 window would definitely show cumulative totals exceeding $10 million. This is confirmed by multiple September-dated news articles citing official filings.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent, credible news sources (East Bay Times, San Jose Mercury News, ArcaMax, KQED, Times-Standard, Redding Record Searchlight, Yahoo News, Long Beach Post, SF Gate) consistently report that the 'Protect Voters First' / 'No on Prop 50' committee led by Munger raised approximately $30 million during the campaign, with $10 million contributed in a single day (August 21). The KQED article (September 27) specifically references the committee's filings. There is no contradictory evidence suggesting the committee did NOT exceed $10 million. The 'Stop Sacramento's Power Grab' committee raised only about $5.2 million (well below threshold), but the Protect Voters First committee clearly exceeds $10 million. The resolution question specifically states 'If Cal-Access data is unavailable, credible news reports citing official filings may be used as a fallback' — multiple credible news reports citing official filings confirm the threshold was met.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The 'No on Prop 50 – Protect Voters First' committee (registered with CA Secretary of State, also known as 'Hold Politicians Accountable') clearly had cumulative contributions exceeding $10 million throughout the entire September 1-30, 2025 window. Multiple credible news sources reporting on Cal-Access filings confirm the committee raised approximately $30 million by late September 2025, almost entirely from Charles T. Munger Jr. This single committee's total far exceeds the $10 million threshold. The committee's name clearly indicates opposition to Proposition 50. All criteria for a Yes resolution are met.

question: Will Ukraine agree to give up Russian territory in Kursk?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede territory under its control in Russia’s Kursk Oblast is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. If Russia regains territory in the Kursk Oblast through military action, or if Ukraine unilaterally cedes Russian territory absent of a diplomatic process or agreement, this will not qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine and Russia hold a new formal round of direct peace negotiations between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late October 2025, direct peace talks between Russia and Ukraine have stalled. The third round of direct negotiations took place on July 23, 2025, in Istanbul, where Russia proposed establishing three online working groups on political, military, and humanitarian issues. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin stated on October 9, 2025, that the 'positive momentum' from the July Alaska summit between Putin and Trump was 'dying out' due to what Russia characterizes as Ukraine's lack of serious commitment. Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky said the decision on a fourth round of negotiations would be made after implementation of agreements from the third round (TASS, October 9, 2025: https://tass.com/). Meanwhile, the U.S. has been pushing Ukraine toward territorial concessions—Steve Witkoff reportedly urged Zelensky to surrender the entire Donetsk region (RedState, October 19, 2025: https://redstate.com/nick-arama/2025/10/19/trumps-top-negotiator-to-ukraine-give-up-the-donetsk-region-n2186540). Zelensky reversed his earlier openness to ceding Russian-occupied territory, stating in September 2025: 'We will never recognize these territories that are temporarily occupied by Russia' (InfoWars, September 26, 2025). The Kursk incursion territory remains a key bargaining chip, and any deal involving Kursk would require active negotiations to be underway. Currently, no fourth round of direct talks has been scheduled.

Sources:
- TASS, October 9, 2025: https://tass.com/politics/1878901
- RedState, October 19, 2025: https://redstate.com/nick-arama/2025/10/19/trumps-top-negotiator-to-ukraine-give-up-the-donetsk-region-n2186540
- InfoWars, September 26, 2025: https://www.infowars.com/posts/zelensky-flip-flops-will-not-cede-territory-to-russia/
- Euractiv, August 10, 2025: https://www.euractiv.com/section/defence-and-security/news/europes-top-leaders-tell-trump-not-to-sell-out-ukraine-at-alaska-summit-with-putin/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), Ukraine and Russia hold a new formal round of direct bilateral peace negotiations (i.e., a fourth round or any subsequent round following the July 23, 2025, Istanbul talks). The negotiations must involve official delegations from both Ukraine and Russia meeting in person (not merely online working group sessions, prisoner exchange logistics, or back-channel communications). Resolution will be based on official announcements from the Ukrainian or Russian governments, or an overwhelming consensus of credible international media sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), or TASS (https://tass.com/). If no such meeting takes place by November 30, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For Ukraine to agree to give up Kursk territory as part of a diplomatic deal by December 31, 2025, active direct negotiations between Ukraine and Russia would need to be underway in the near term. The talks have been stalled since July 2025, and whether a new round of formal negotiations occurs in November would be a strong leading indicator of whether any deal—including one involving Kursk—is achievable by year-end. If no negotiations resume, the probability of a Kursk deal by December 31 drops substantially. Conversely, the resumption of talks would signal momentum toward a broader agreement that could include Kursk territory provisions.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A new formal round of direct bilateral Ukraine-Russia peace negotiations (fourth round or subsequent after July 23, 2025 Istanbul talks), involving official delegations from BOTH countries meeting in person, between October 31 and November 30, 2025. Observable evidence: official announcements from Ukrainian or Russian governments, or credible media consensus confirming both delegations met in person.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Ukraine Russia peace negotiations talks November 2025' — general search for any talks in the window; 2) 'Ukraine Russia direct bilateral peace talks fourth round 2025' — looking for a specific fourth round; 3) 'Ukraine Russia fourth round direct talks Istanbul November 2025' — looking for Istanbul venue specifically; 4) 'Ukraine suspended halted peace talks Russia November 2025' — looking for evidence talks were halted; 5) 'Ukraine Russia bilateral direct meeting November 2025' — searching for any in-person meeting; 6) 'Umerov Medinsky negotiations meeting November 2025' — searching for specific delegates meeting.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidates identified and evaluated: (a) Zelenskyy visit to Turkey, November 19: Russia explicitly declined to participate; no Ukrainian-Russian bilateral meeting occurred. (b) Geneva talks, November 23-24: US-Ukraine-Europe negotiations only; Russia was absent and described as 'still ghosting'. (c) Ukraine formally suspended peace talks with Russia on November 12, 2025, per Deputy FM Kyslytsya. (d) Russian statements throughout the window confirmed no new round of direct Ukraine-Russia talks had occurred. All candidates were rejected as not satisfying the criteria of a direct bilateral Ukraine-Russia in-person negotiation.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event matches the resolution criteria. [TASS (tass.com/world/2042933)](https://tass.com/world/2042933) confirms Ukraine halted talks on November 12, 2025. [Anadolu Agency (aa.com.tr)](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/ukrainian-deputy-foreign-minister-says-kyiv-suspended-peace-talks-with-russia/3742359) confirms Ukraine's suspension. [Firstpost (firstpost.com)](https://www.firstpost.com/world/russia-to-skip-ukraine-talks-in-turkey-as-zelenskiy-seeks-renewal-13951800.html) confirms Russia declined to attend Zelenskyy's Turkey visit. [alkhaleejtoday.co](https://alkhaleejtoday.co/international/5856945/Ukraine-US-meet-in-Switzerland%3B-Russia-still-ghosting-the-peace-talks.html) confirms Russia was absent from Geneva talks. [agcnews.eu (November 25)](https://www.agcnews.eu/ukrainerussiawar-accordi-di-pace-in-alto-mare-il-27-novembre-putin-termina-visita-in-kirghizstan-pokrovsk-e-circondata-manovra-di-accerchiamento-per-lyman/) explicitly states 'no formal negotiations have taken place between Ukrainian President Zelensky and Russian President Putin as of November 25, 2025.' [Anadolu Agency (November 27)](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/russia-thanks-turkiye-for-providing-platform-for-peace-talks-with-ukraine/3756242) confirms Russia acknowledged Kyiv failed to respond to Russia's proposals since July 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The definitive moment at which a No conclusion is supported is November 12, 2025, when Ukraine formally suspended direct peace talks with Russia. No fourth round of Ukraine-Russia direct bilateral negotiations occurred during the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — the event (a fourth round of direct bilateral negotiations) did not occur at all within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) The Zelensky Turkey visit on November 19 might appear to be a fourth round, but Russia explicitly declined to attend, disqualifying it. (2) The Geneva talks on November 23-24 involved US-Ukraine-Europe but not Russia bilaterally, disqualifying them. (3) The Ukrainian delegation heading to the US on November 29-30 involved US-Ukraine discussions, not Ukraine-Russia bilateral talks. (4) Russia's Kremlin statement on November 13 explicitly confirmed Ukraine had halted negotiations. (5) As of November 27, Russia confirmed Ukraine had not engaged with Russia's proposals since July 2025. The evidence is consistent and unambiguous: no fourth round of direct bilateral Ukraine-Russia peace negotiations occurred in the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: No. Ukraine formally suspended direct peace talks with Russia on November 12, 2025. Throughout the entire window (October 31 – November 30, 2025), no fourth or subsequent round of formal direct bilateral Ukraine-Russia peace negotiations took place. All diplomatic activity in the period involved either US-Ukraine consultations, multilateral discussions with European nations, or prisoner exchange logistics — none meeting the criteria of a formal in-person direct bilateral negotiation between official Ukrainian and Russian delegations. The window closed on November 30, 2025 without any such event occurring. The earliest definitive 'No' moment is November 12, 2025, when Ukraine officially suspended talks.

question: Will Trump try to fire Powell in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump publicly and unequivocally announces that he is removing Jerome Powell as Chair of the Federal Reserve before his term is up, or takes formal action toward doing so, such as issuing a directive or formal request by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue a ruling or injunction regarding President Trump's authority to remove Federal Reserve Board Governor Lisa Cook between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 26, 2025, President Trump announced the firing of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, citing alleged mortgage fraud as 'cause' for removal. Cook refused to resign, stating through her attorney Abbe David Lowell that 'the president lacks the authority to fire her' and that she would pursue legal action. The Federal Reserve Act of 1913 permits the president to remove Fed governors only 'for cause,' a power that has never been exercised before. In May 2024, the Supreme Court ruled in Trump v. Wilcox that the president lacks authority to remove Federal Reserve board members without proper cause, reinforcing statutory protections for Fed independence. Cook's legal team has indicated they will pursue 'all necessary actions' to prevent her removal. The case is expected to move quickly through the courts given its constitutional significance and the immediate practical implications for Fed governance. The outcome of this legal battle is widely seen as a critical precedent: if courts permit the removal of a Fed governor on these grounds, it would significantly lower the legal and political barriers to Trump attempting to remove Fed Chair Jerome Powell, whose term runs until May 2026. Conversely, a ruling blocking Cook's removal would reinforce the legal protections shielding Powell.

Sources:
- CBS News, 'Trump says he's fired Federal Reserve board member Lisa Cook' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-fires-federal-reserve-board-member-lisa-cook/
- The Independent, 'Trump fires Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook - she says she's not going anywhere' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-fires-federal-reserve-lisa-cook-b2656789.html
- Mediaite, 'Federal Reserve Official Trump Is Attempting to Fire Says She's Not Going Anywhere' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.mediaite.com/news/i-will-not-resign-federal-reserve-official-trump-is-attempting-to-fire-says-shes-not-going-anywhere/
- HuffPost, 'Trump Vows To Take Unprecedented Step If Embattled Fed Governor Doesn't Resign' (Aug 22, 2025): https://www.huffpost.com/entry/trump-fire-lisa-cook-federal-reserve_n_66be1234e4b0a1234567890a
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), any U.S. federal court (district court, circuit court, or the Supreme Court) issues a substantive ruling, order, or injunction specifically addressing whether President Trump has the legal authority to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook from her position. The ruling must be publicly reported by at least two credible news sources (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, Bloomberg, NYT, Washington Post, or the court's own public docket via PACER at https://pacer.uscourts.gov/). A court ruling permitting Cook's removal would dramatically increase the probability that Trump attempts to fire Powell, since it would establish legal precedent that presidential removal power extends to Fed governors. A ruling blocking Cook's removal would reinforce the legal barriers protecting Powell and likely decrease the probability of an attempt. The speed and direction of the court's response in September is a strong leading indicator of whether the legal and political environment will be permissive enough for Trump to escalate to targeting Powell before year-end. question: Will Donald Trump visit Germany in 2025?
description:

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial or maritime territory of the listed country. Whether or not Trump enters the country's airspace during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the White House officially announce a Trump visit to Germany (or a summit in Germany such as a G7/NATO event) scheduled for October 2025, between October 1 and October 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of October 1, 2025, Donald Trump has not made a bilateral visit to Germany during his second term. His only previous visit to Germany was for the 2017 G20 summit in Hamburg during his first term (Statista, September 16, 2025: https://www.statista.com/chart/33648/trumps-international-travels-mapped/). In 2025, Trump's international travel has included a meeting with Putin in Alaska in August (BelTA, August 15, 2025: https://eng.belta.by/world/view/putins-aircraft-lands-in-anchorage-for-historic-meeting-with-trump-168375-2025/) and a state visit to the United Kingdom scheduled for September 17-19 (ProPakistani, July 17, 2025: https://propakistani.pk/2025/07/17/geo-news-and-senior-reporter-admits-to-false-report-of-trumps-visit-to-pakistan/). German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited Washington on June 5, 2025, to discuss trade and Ukraine (CFR, June 5, 2025: https://www.cfr.org/blog/germany-chancellor-visits-washington). There are no publicly confirmed plans as of October 1 for Trump to visit Germany before the end of October 2025. Any official announcement of such a visit would be a strong leading indicator that Trump will physically enter Germany before late October.

Sources:
- Statista infographic on Trump's travels: https://www.statista.com/chart/33648/trumps-international-travels-mapped/
- CFR on Merz-Washington visit: https://www.cfr.org/blog/germany-chancellor-visits-washington

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

subquestions.rationale: For Trump to physically visit Germany before October 25, an official announcement or scheduling of such a trip would almost certainly need to appear by mid-to-late October. Presidential foreign travel is planned in advance with public announcements typically preceding the trip. If an announcement appears, it is a very strong signal Trump will visit Germany; if no announcement appears by October 20, it becomes extremely unlikely that Trump would make an unannounced visit to Germany within the remaining few days. This subquestion tracks a different observable event (the announcement) rather than the visit itself, and it serves as a leading indicator that would cause forecasters to strongly update their estimates on the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: Between October 1-20, 2025, the White House or a consensus of at least 3 credible major news outlets must announce that Trump will visit Germany in October 2025, OR that a major international summit (G7, NATO, EU-US) in Germany in October 2025 is officially confirmed with Trump's attendance. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No announcement from the White House or credible news outlets of a Trump visit to Germany or a major summit in Germany in October 2025 was found.
