subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of the Treasury publicly announce a pilot, program, or initiative to send funds or settle payments via blockchain by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. Department of the Treasury will send any funds or assets via a blockchain by end of 2025. As of September 2025, several federal agencies have moved toward blockchain adoption, but the Treasury itself has not yet executed an official on-chain payment. The U.S. Commerce Department announced on August 28, 2025 that it would publish GDP data on nine public blockchains (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, etc.) in partnership with Chainlink, Pyth, Coinbase, Gemini, and Kraken (https://www.decrypt.co/283000/us-commerce-dept-puts-gdp-data-on-bitcoin-ethereum-and-solana-blockchains). Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said the program would eventually make blockchain data distribution available to the entire government. However, publishing data on-chain is fundamentally different from sending funds or assets on-chain.

The Treasury has been active in the broader crypto/blockchain policy space: it issued a request for comment on the GENIUS Act stablecoin legislation (comments due October 17, 2025), published a primer on stablecoins, and OFAC has sanctioned blockchain addresses (https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/weekly-blockchain-blog-august-2025-4-5765498/). New Treasury regulations on August 15, 2025 increased oversight of stablecoins (https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/08/blockchain-trilemma-cryptocurrency-platforms-could-scale-while-ensuring-adequate-security-and-decentralization-analysis/). The Deploying American Blockchains Act passed the House in June 2025 and awaits Senate approval, which would authorize Commerce to lead federal blockchain policy.

While the broader Trump administration is crypto-friendly — creating a Bitcoin reserve, stockpiling ETH and SOL, signing a stablecoin law, and appointing crypto-friendly agency heads — the Treasury specifically sending funds on-chain would be a distinct escalation. An announcement of such a program or pilot in September 2025 would be a strong leading indicator that an actual transaction could occur before year-end.

Sources:
- Decrypt, "US Commerce Dept. Puts GDP Data on Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana Blockchains" (Aug 28, 2025): https://www.decrypt.co/283000/us-commerce-dept-puts-gdp-data-on-bitcoin-ethereum-and-solana-blockchains
- JD Supra, "Weekly Blockchain Blog - August 2025 #4" (Aug 25, 2025): https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/weekly-blockchain-blog-august-2025-4-5765498/
- Business Standard, "US govt puts GDP data on the public blockchain in Trump's crypto push" (Aug 28, 2025): https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/us-government-puts-gdp-data-on-blockchain-trump-crypto-push-125082800550_1.html
- Crowdfund Insider, "Blockchain Trilemma" (Aug 28, 2025): https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/08/blockchain-trilemma-cryptocurrency-platforms-could-scale-while-ensuring-adequate-security-and-decentralization-analysis/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of the Treasury (including sub-agencies such as the Bureau of the Fiscal Service, but excluding OFAC sanctions actions and excluding the Commerce Department or other non-Treasury agencies) publicly announces a program, pilot, or initiative specifically designed to send, disburse, or settle government funds or financial assets using blockchain technology. The announcement must come from an official Treasury source (e.g., press release on https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases, official statements by the Treasury Secretary or other senior Treasury officials) or be confirmed by a consensus of at least two credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, Wall Street Journal). Merely publishing data on-chain, issuing regulatory guidance about blockchain, or sanctioning blockchain addresses does not count. The announcement must describe a program intended to move actual funds or financial assets (not just data or hashes) on a blockchain. If no such announcement is made by October 1, 2025, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Treasury will actually send funds on blockchain by end of 2025. A Treasury announcement of a blockchain payments program or pilot in September would be the strongest near-term leading indicator, since any actual transaction would almost certainly be preceded by a public announcement. The broader federal government's rapid adoption of blockchain (Commerce publishing GDP data on-chain, the Deploying American Blockchains Act, crypto-friendly executive actions) creates a plausible pathway, but Treasury sending funds is a distinct and higher bar. If forecasters disagree on the ultimate question, learning whether Treasury has announced such a program by early October would significantly update their estimates — an announcement would make a year-end transaction much more likely, while silence would suggest the ultimate question is less likely to resolve Yes.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: U.S. Department of Treasury (including sub-agencies like Bureau of Fiscal Service, but excluding OFAC and non-Treasury agencies) publicly announces between September 1–October 1, 2025 a program, pilot, or initiative specifically designed to SEND, DISBURSE, or SETTLE actual government funds/financial assets using blockchain technology. Announcement must come from official Treasury source (press release on home.treasury.gov or official Treasury statements) OR be confirmed by at least two credible news outlets. Regulatory guidance, data publishing, or sanctions actions do NOT qualify. Must involve actual funds movement, not just data or hashes.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'U.S. Treasury Department blockchain payment settlement program announcement 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 1) - to find direct Treasury announcements; 2) 'Treasury Department blockchain pilot funds disbursement 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 1) - to find disbursement-specific programs; 3) 'Bureau of Fiscal Service blockchain payment government funds 2025' - to find sub-agency initiatives; 4) 'Treasury Department stablecoin digital asset payment initiative announcement September 2025' - to find any payment programs; 5) 'treasury.gov press release blockchain digital asset payment September October 2025' - to find official press releases; 6) 'Scott Bessent Treasury blockchain crypto payment initiative September 2025' - to find Secretary-level announcements; 7) 'US Treasury DOGE blockchain payment modernization September 2025' - to check for payment modernization; 8) Various broader searches on US government federal blockchain payment pilots

REJECTED: This is regulatory guidance, explicitly excluded by resolution criteria. Does not involve moving actual government funds. (4) Treasury support statements for stablecoins by Secretary Bessent - REJECTED: Statements of support, not a program announcement. (5) Treasury paper check elimination (effective September 30, 2025) - REJECTED: Moving to electronic transfers (ACH/direct deposit), not blockchain.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event satisfies all resolution criteria: (a) Treasury GENIUS Act ANPRM [JD Supra, PYMNTS, Crowdfund Insider] — is regulatory guidance seeking public comment on GENIUS Act implementation, explicitly excluded by criteria ('issuing regulatory guidance about blockchain does not count'). No contradictory evidence found suggesting a qualifying announcement was made and missed by searches.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The window (September 1 – October 1, 2025) closed with no U.S. Treasury announcement of a pilot, program, or initiative to send, disburse, or settle actual government funds via blockchain. Treasury activity was limited to regulatory guidance (GENIUS Act ANPRM) and policy coordination (US-UK Taskforce), neither of which satisfies the resolution criteria. The question resolves No, with resolution datetime set to 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z (end of window).

question: Will Trump establish a Gaza “Board of Peace” by March 31?

question: Will China lift rare earths export ban by December 31?
description:

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Chinese government officially lifts, removes, or reduces any of the export restrictions placed on rare earth metals on April 4, between July 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

subquestions.question: Will the United States and China announce a new bilateral trade agreement or framework that explicitly addresses rare earth export controls between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
China imposed export licensing restrictions on seven rare earth elements (samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, and yttrium) and related magnets on April 4, 2025, as part of escalating trade tensions with the United States. These restrictions created significant supply chain disruptions globally. A temporary US-China trade deal reached in mid-2025 led to some improvement in shipments, with Beijing promising to resume rare earth exports to the US in exchange for Washington lifting certain tech-export restrictions (https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202508220340/china-tightens-controls-on-rare-earths). However, in August 2025, China further tightened oversight by issuing new regulations requiring monthly reporting to a government-run tracking system and assigning production quotas, effective July 28 (https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202508220340/china-tightens-controls-on-rare-earths). China's approach has been selective — it reportedly lifted restrictions for India following diplomatic talks in August 2025, though actual shipments have been slow to materialize (https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/world/china-yet-to-resume-rare-earth-exports-to-india-despite-wang-yi-s-assurance-ev-makers-face-crunch-report-13491841.html). The broader US-China trade relationship remains contentious, with tariffs and counter-tariffs still in effect. Any new bilateral agreement addressing rare earths would be a strong signal that China may formally lift or reduce the April 4 export restrictions before December 31, 2025.

Sources:

question: Will the Fed cut-pause-pause in 2025?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings in 2025 (September 16-17, October 28-29, and December 9-10).

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered. 

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the December meeting by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve cut the federal funds rate at its September 16-17, 2025 FOMC meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) has held the federal funds rate steady at 4.25%–4.50% for the first five meetings of 2025 (January, March, May, June, and July). At the July 30, 2025 meeting, two FOMC members (Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman and Governor Christopher Waller) dissented, calling for a quarter-point cut, indicating growing internal support for easing. As of early August 2025, the CME FedWatch Tool showed approximately a 60% probability of at least a quarter-point cut at the September meeting. Forbes reported in August 2025 that markets expect a September 17 rate cut, with further cuts possible in October and December. The Invesco Conservative Income Fund Q2 2025 commentary (published September 2, 2025) expected two 0.25% rate cuts beginning in October, implying a pause in September. The September FOMC meeting is the first of the three meetings addressed by the ultimate question ('cut-pause-pause'), and its outcome directly determines whether the 'cut-pause-pause' pattern remains possible.

Sources:
- Barron's, "Stocks Are Steady After Fed Keeps Rates on Pause" (July 30, 2025): https://www.barrons.com/livecoverage/fed-meeting-interest-rate-decision-today-july-2025
- Forbes, "What To Expect On Interest Rates For The Remainder Of 2025" (August 3, 2025): https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonmoore/2025/08/03/what-to-expect-on-interest-rates-for-the-remainder-of-2025/
- Seeking Alpha, "Invesco Conservative Income Fund Q2 2025 Commentary" (September 2, 2025): https://seekingalpha.com/article/4750000-invesco-conservative-income-fund-q2-2025-commentary
- Federal Reserve FOMC Calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
- Federal Reserve Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate, as announced in the FOMC statement following the September 16-17, 2025 meeting, is lower than the upper bound prior to that meeting (currently 4.50%). It resolves No if the upper bound remains at 4.50% or is raised. The resolution window is between 2025-09-05 and 2025-09-30. Resolution is based on the official FOMC statement published at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm and the federal funds rate target published at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm. If the September 16-17 FOMC meeting is postponed beyond September 30, 2025, or no statement is released by that date, this question resolves No. Emergency rate actions taken outside the regularly scheduled September 16-17 meeting do not count toward resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the Fed will follow a 'cut-pause-pause' pattern across its September, October, and December 2025 meetings. The September meeting is the first of these three decisions. If the Fed does NOT cut in September, the 'cut-pause-pause' outcome becomes impossible, and the ultimate question resolves to a different combination. If the Fed DOES cut, the 'cut-pause-pause' pattern remains viable. This makes the September rate decision the most immediate and decisive indicator for the ultimate question. Two forecasters who disagree on whether the ultimate pattern will be 'cut-pause-pause' are very likely to disagree on whether a September cut will happen, making this a strong crux.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes condition: The upper bound of the target federal funds rate announced in the FOMC statement following the September 16-17, 2025 meeting must be LOWER than the prior upper bound of 4.50%. Observable evidence: official FOMC statement showing new target range with upper bound below 4.50%. Key entities: Federal Reserve FOMC, federal funds rate target range. Threshold: upper bound must drop below 4.50%. Timing: statement must be released between 2025-09-05 and 2025-09-30.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Federal Reserve FOMC September 2025 rate decision' (2025-09-15 to 2025-09-30) — to find the FOMC decision. Query 2: 'Federal Reserve interest rate cut September 17 2025' (2025-09-15 to 2025-09-30) — to find specific cut details. Query 3: 'FOMC statement September 17 2025 federal funds rate 4.00 4.25 percent' (2025-09-17 to 2025-09-18) — to verify exact new rate target.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Federal Reserve FOMC statement published on September 17, 2025, announcing a 25 basis point cut from 4.25%-4.50% to 4.00%-4.25%. Multiple sources confirm this including the official Fed press release at federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20250917a.htm. One article from time.news stated rates were unchanged (fifth consecutive hold), but this appears to be an erroneous pre-meeting article; the overwhelming majority of sources including the official Fed release confirm the cut. That article is rejected as contradicted by the official Fed source.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require the upper bound to fall below 4.50%. The FOMC statement (federalreserve.gov) explicitly states: 'the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4 to 4‑1/4 percent.' The new upper bound is 4.25%, which is lower than the prior upper bound of 4.50%. This exactly matches the resolution criteria. Sources: [Federal Reserve FOMC Statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20250917a.htm), [WFLA](https://www.wfla.com/news/national/federal-reserve-cuts-interest-rates-amid-weakening-job-market/), [News18](https://www.news18.com/business/economy/us-fed-rate-cut-jerome-powell-fomc-reduces-interest-rates-by-25-bps-first-in-9-months-9579537.html), [Santa Clarita Valley Signal](https://signalscv.com/2025/09/federal-reserve-cuts-interest-rates-for-first-time-in-2025/)
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The FOMC statement was published on September 17, 2025, at the conclusion of the September 16-17 meeting. The official Fed press release URL is monetary20250917a.htm, confirming the date. Multiple news sources published reports on September 17, 2025. The announcement was made during the afternoon of September 17, 2025, following a 2:30 p.m. press conference by Chair Powell. Exact ISO 8601 datetime: 2025-09-17T14:00:00Z (approximate time of FOMC announcement — the Fed typically releases its statement at 2:00 PM ET = 18:00 UTC). This falls within the resolution window of 2025-09-05 to 2025-09-30.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question specifies this is for the regularly scheduled September 16-17 FOMC meeting. The resolution criteria also exclude emergency rate actions outside the scheduled meeting. There is no evidence of an earlier qualifying event; the previous rate was at 4.25%-4.50% (unchanged for five consecutive meetings), and this September 17 cut is the first rate change since December 2024. This is confirmed as the first (and only) occurrence within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: One article (time.news) stated rates were unchanged and described it as the 'fifth consecutive hold,' but this is contradicted by: (1) the official Federal Reserve press release (federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20250917a.htm), (2) 10+ additional news sources from reputable outlets (WFLA/Fox, CBS News, CNA, Austin American-Statesman, News18, TASS, FTAdviser, InstaForex, etc.), and (3) direct quotes from the FOMC statement. The time.news article appears to have been written in anticipation of the meeting or contains errors. The overwhelming weight of evidence including the primary source (Fed.gov) confirms the rate was cut to 4.00%-4.25%. No contradictory evidence from reliable sources exists. The cut was at the regularly scheduled September 16-17 meeting (not an emergency action), satisfying the resolution criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Federal Reserve's FOMC, at the conclusion of its September 16-17, 2025 meeting, announced a 25-basis-point cut to the federal funds rate, lowering the target range from 4.25%-4.50% to 4.00%-4.25%. The new upper bound of 4.25% is lower than the prior upper bound of 4.50%. This was announced on September 17, 2025, within the resolution window of 2025-09-05 to 2025-09-30. The official FOMC statement explicitly states the cut was made. Therefore, this question resolves Yes.

A key geographic feature is the railway line running roughly north-south through Myrnohrad, which serves as a natural defensive barrier. The eastern outskirts include industrial areas and the approaches from Novoekonomichne and the mine complex areas where fighting has been concentrated. If the ISW map becomes unavailable, the DeepState Map (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used as an alternative. Temporary map glitches do not count. If Russian forces have not even entered the eastern urban area by September 21, it becomes extremely unlikely they could advance several more kilometers through urban terrain to reach the central intersection by September 30. Conversely, if they have already breached the eastern urban perimeter by September 21, the probability of reaching the target intersection rises substantially. evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: ISW or DeepState map shows red (Russian-controlled) shading in residential/urban blocks of Myrnohrad east of the north-south railway line, within the municipal boundary. subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Supreme Court act on Ghislaine Maxwell's certiorari petition (grant, deny, or otherwise dispose of it) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?

Ghislaine Maxwell is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence for sex trafficking. She has been subpoenaed by the House Oversight Committee to testify, but her attorneys have demanded that any testimony be scheduled after the resolution of her Supreme Court petition and her forthcoming habeas petition. Maxwell's legal team has argued that testifying while her appeal is pending could compromise her constitutional rights, prejudice her legal claims, and potentially taint a future jury pool. If these demands are not met, her attorneys have stated she will invoke her Fifth Amendment rights and decline to answer questions.

The Supreme Court's October 2025 term begins on October 6, 2025, and the Court regularly issues orders on pending certiorari petitions during its conference sessions throughout the term. If the Supreme Court denies Maxwell's cert petition in October, one of the key conditions her attorneys set for testimony would be resolved, potentially clearing the path for her to testify before Congress before year-end. Conversely, if the Court grants certiorari, further litigation could delay or prevent testimony entirely. If no action is taken in October, the standoff between Maxwell's legal team and the Oversight Committee is likely to continue.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. publicly issue an explicit military threat (beyond existing rhetoric) against Colombia, Mexico, Cuba, or Iran between January 6, 2026, and January 31, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
On January 3, 2026, the U.S. launched 'Operation Absolute Resolve,' a military strike on Venezuela that resulted in the capture of President Nicolás Maduro. In the immediate aftermath, President Trump made threatening remarks toward several other countries. He suggested potential 'Operation Colombia,' called Colombia 'very sick,' said Cuba is 'ready to fall,' threatened military entry into Mexico, and warned Iran of potential Israeli military action backed by the U.S. if it resumes nuclear activities. Colombia's President Petro warned that any U.S. attack on its sovereignty would be treated as a declaration of war, while Mexico's President Sheinbaum declined to schedule a call with Trump after his threats. Cuba's President Díaz-Canel called the Venezuela operation a 'criminal US attack.' As of January 5, 2026, these remain rhetorical threats, but the precedent set by the Venezuela strike has raised the plausibility of follow-on actions. A new explicit military threat — such as an official order to prepare military options, a formal ultimatum with a deadline, deployment of additional forces to a staging area near one of these countries, or a presidential directive publicly announced — would be a significant escalation beyond the current rhetorical posture and a meaningful indicator of whether an actual strike could follow before March 31, 2026.

Sources:
- Yahoo News, 'World reaction to U.S. strikes on Venezuela pours in' (Jan 4, 2026): https://www.yahoo.com/news/world-reaction-us-strikes-venezuela-pours-in.html
- Zero Hedge / Newsquawk, 'Crude falls following US strike on Venezuela' (Jan 5, 2026): https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/crude-falls-following-us-strike-venezuela-european-equity-futures-point-positive-open
- CNA, 'Stocks, energy shares, oil jump after US strikes Venezuela' (Jan 5, 2026): https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/stocks-energy-shares-oil-jump-after-us-strikes-venezuela
- FXStreet, 'US Dollar Index rises above 98.50 on US-Venezuela tensions' (Jan 5, 2026): https://www.fxstreet.com/news/us-dollar-index-rises-above-9850-on-us-venezuela-tensions
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between January 6, 2026, and January 31, 2026 (inclusive), the U.S. government issues a new, explicit military threat against Colombia, Mexico, Cuba, or Iran that goes beyond the rhetorical statements already made as of January 5, 2026. Qualifying escalations include any of the following, as reported by at least two major credible English-language news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, NYT, Washington Post, CNN, The Guardian):

1. A formal presidential or Secretary of Defense public statement announcing the preparation or authorization of military options against one of these countries (e.g., 'I have ordered the Pentagon to prepare strike plans for Colombia');
2. A publicly announced deployment of additional U.S. military assets (carrier strike groups, bomber wings, troop deployments) to staging areas specifically stated to be for potential operations against one of these countries;
3. A formal public ultimatum with a specific deadline directed at one of these countries, threatening military action if demands are not met;
4. An official executive order or National Security Council directive, made public, authorizing planning for strikes on one of these countries.

General rhetorical threats, social media posts repeating prior rhetoric, or vague warnings that do not represent a concrete new escalation beyond the January 3-5 statements do not qualify. The question resolves No if no such qualifying escalation is reported by January 31, 2026.

Primary resolution sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- The Guardian: https://www.theguardian.com
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. will strike Venezuela again or strike Iran, Colombia, Mexico, or Cuba before March 31, 2026. The Venezuela operation already occurred, and Trump has made rhetorical threats against all four remaining countries. A key leading indicator of whether rhetoric will turn into action is whether the U.S. escalates from general threats to concrete military preparations or formal ultimatums. If forecasters observe a concrete new military threat by the end of January, they should significantly update toward a strike occurring before March 31. If no escalation beyond current rhetoric occurs, this suggests the threats may remain bluster, updating toward 'Yes' (nothing happens) on the ultimate question. This subquestion captures a different observable — escalation of threat posture — rather than simply asking about strikes with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Requires between Jan 6–31, 2026: a new explicit military threat against Colombia, Mexico, Cuba, or Iran going beyond rhetoric as of Jan 5, 2026. Qualifying events include: (1) formal presidential/SecDef statement announcing preparation/authorization of military options; (2) publicly announced deployment of military assets to staging areas specifically stated for operations against these countries; (3) formal public ultimatum with specific deadline threatening military action; (4) official executive order/NSC directive authorizing strike planning. Must be reported by at least two major credible English-language outlets.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'US military threat Colombia Mexico Cuba Iran 2026' (general threats); Query 2: 'Trump military action Colombia Mexico ultimatum January 2026' (specific escalations); Query 3: 'Trump formal military order Pentagon preparation strike Colombia Mexico Iran January 2026' (formal orders); Query 4: 'US military deployment carrier strike group bomber Colombia Mexico Cuba Iran January 2026' (deployments); Query 5: 'Trump ordered Pentagon prepare Iran strike reversed WSJ Wall Street Journal January 13 2026' (specific Jan 13 event); Query 6: 'Trump ultimatum Iran nuclear deal deadline January 29 30 2026' (ultimatum events)
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key candidate events identified: (A) Jan 13 2026 — Pentagon briefed Trump on wide range of Iran strike options; Trump directed Pentagon to prepare strike on Iran (WSJ, NYT via Haaretz, CBS, Economic Times); White House confirmed airstrikes 'on the table'; (B) Jan 15-16 2026 — Pentagon officially announced movement of USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group from South China Sea to Middle East, explicitly in context of Iran tensions (The Hill, ABC News, The Telegraph, Al Jazeera); (C) Jan 23 2026 — Trump publicly stated 'massive fleet' heading to Iran 'just in case'; (D) Jan 26 2026 — USS Abraham Lincoln carrier group officially arrived in CENTCOM area (AFP, CENTCOM, Anadolu Agency); (E) Jan 28-29 2026 — SecDef Hegseth formally told Trump Pentagon 'is prepared on Iran' at cabinet meeting (MarketScreener/Reuters, Al Arabiya); Trump issued ultimatum to Iran to 'make a deal or face US military'; (F) Jan 30 2026 — Trump confirmed he gave Iran a deadline (AFP, Fox News, AP News). Colombia/Mexico: Trump's Jan 6-9 statements about hitting Mexico 'on land' and Colombia 'sounds good' were rhetorical; de-escalation followed Jan 7-8 Petro phone call. These may not qualify as going beyond Jan 5 rhetoric.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: CRITERION 2 CLEARLY MET: The Hill (https://thehill.com/policy/defense/5691421-defense-department-carrier-strike-grouo-iran-tensions/) reported January 15, 2026: 'The Pentagon announced on January 15, 2026, that it is deploying a carrier strike group, including the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier, from the South China Sea toward the Middle East amid escalating tensions between the U.S. and Iran.' ABC News (https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/pentagon-eyes-surging-carrier-group-middle-east-amid/story?id=129290227) also reported the Pentagon 'expected to surge additional military assets to the Middle East... including possibly the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group... to also provide Trump with expanded military options should he choose to strike Iran.' The Telegraph confirmed the diversion (https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2026/01/16/us-aircraft-carrier-strike-group-divert-iran-donald-trump/). Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/17/us-air-authority-warns-of-military-activities-over-mexico-south-america) also confirmed. This meets criterion 2: publicly announced deployment of carrier strike group to staging area specifically stated to be for potential operations against Iran. CRITERION 1 ALSO MET: TASS/WSJ (https://tass.com/world/2072733) reported: 'On January 13, 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump directed the Pentagon to prepare for a military strike on Iran.' White House press secretary confirmed airstrikes 'one of many, many options on the table' (Economic Times). SecDef Hegseth told Trump 'Pentagon is prepared on Iran' (MarketScreener https://www.marketscreener.com/news/hegseth-tells-trump-pentagon-is-prepared-on-iran-ce7e5bdfdd80f423, Al Arabiya https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2026/01/29/pentagon-chief-tells-trump-us-military-is-prepared-on-iran). CRITERION 3 ALSO MET: WKRC/local12 (https://local12.com/news/nation-world/trump-gives-iran-an-ultimatum-make-a-deal-or-face-the-us-military-tehran-islamic-republic-irgc-protests-middle-east) reported January 29: 'Trump issued a stark ultimatum to Iran: negotiate a comprehensive deal or face direct U.S. military action.' AFP (https://apnews.com/article/trump-iran-united-states-protests-nuclear-5cac82fc0230b761361706cdd9b249d9) and multiple others confirmed on Jan 30 Trump confirmed he set a 'deadline' for Iran.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest qualifying event: Pentagon briefing on Iran strike options with public White House confirmation — January 13, 2026. Carrier strike group movement announcement — January 15, 2026. These are explicitly dated by multiple credible sources. The Hill article explicitly states 'January 15, 2026' for the carrier deployment announcement. ABC News also published on that date. The Telegraph published January 16, 2026 confirming the diversion. Resolution datetime set to January 15, 2026, as the first confirmed qualifying event (Criterion 2: publicly announced deployment of carrier strike group specifically stated for potential Iran operations).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence (before Jan 15) meets Criteria 2 precisely. The Jan 13 events (Pentagon briefing on strike options, White House confirming airstrikes 'on the table') could qualify under Criterion 1, but involve language like 'options on the table' and 'weighing strikes' which is borderline vs. a 'formal statement announcing preparation' of military options. However, WSJ specifically reported Trump 'directed the Pentagon to prepare for a military strike on Iran' on Jan 13 — this is a formal direction to prepare. Either way, both Jan 13 and Jan 15 are within the Jan 6–31 window, confirming Yes resolution.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Trump reversed the Jan 13 direction and stated on Jan 16 he had 'changed his mind' about striking Iran. However, this reversal does not negate the qualifying act of directing Pentagon preparation — the question asks whether the U.S. 'issues a new, explicit military threat' not whether an attack was carried out. The carrier deployment and formal ultimatums continued after Jan 16. The carrier group officially arrived Jan 26, and SecDef Hegseth confirmed Pentagon preparedness on Jan 29. Multiple major outlets (The Hill, ABC News, The Telegraph, Al Jazeera, AFP, Fox News, AP, MarketScreener/Reuters) all confirm these events independently. The Jan 15 carrier deployment is explicitly reported by The Hill, ABC News, and The Telegraph as being in the context of potential Iran strikes — meeting the 'specifically stated to be for potential operations against' criterion.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves YES. Multiple qualifying events occurred within the January 6–31, 2026 window: (1) On January 13, 2026, Trump directed the Pentagon to prepare military strike options against Iran (WSJ, NYT, CBS), with White House confirming airstrikes 'on the table' — qualifying under Criterion 1; (2) On January 15–16, 2026, the Pentagon publicly announced the deployment of the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group toward the Middle East, explicitly stated to be for potential Iran operations, providing Trump military strike options — qualifying under Criterion 2, reported by The Hill, ABC News, The Telegraph, Al Jazeera, and others; (3) On January 28–30, 2026, SecDef Hegseth formally confirmed Pentagon preparedness on Iran (Criterion 1), and Trump issued a formal ultimatum with a deadline for Iran to make a deal or face military action (Criterion 3), reported by AFP, Fox News, AP, WKRC/local12, NDTV. All events are explicitly stated, well within the window, reported by multiple major credible English-language outlets, and represent concrete new escalations beyond the rhetorical statements of January 3–5, 2026. The earliest qualifying event is January 13, 2026 (Pentagon directed to prepare Iran strike options) or January 15, 2026 (carrier group deployment announced for Iran).

If the @nikitabier account is deleted, suspended, or made private during the resolution window such that posts cannot be verified, and no archived evidence (e.g., via Wayback Machine at https://web.archive.org/) confirms at least 10 posts with at least one work-related post, the question resolves No.

subquestions.rationale: Nikita Bier is known as an extremely active poster on X, and he frequently discusses his product work publicly. His continued active posting about X product initiatives is a strong behavioral signal that he remains in his role as Head of Product. If Bier were to be fired or resign (or be in the process of doing so), one of the earliest observable signs would likely be a sharp drop in posting frequency or a cessation of posts referencing his role at X. This subquestion tracks an observable behavioral indicator — his public activity pattern — rather than simply asking about his employment status with an earlier deadline. If this question resolves No (he goes quiet or stops referencing X work), it would be a meaningful update toward the ultimate question resolving Yes (departure). If it resolves Yes (he remains active and engaged), it reduces the probability of an imminent departure.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: (1) at least 10 posts (original tweets, quote tweets, or thread starters - not simple retweets) by @nikitabier between Oct 15-Nov 14, 2025 inclusive, AND (2) at least one post referencing his work, X's product, or his role at X in a product leadership capacity. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Criterion 1 (10+ posts): At least 7-8 distinct product-related posts are documented by news coverage alone. Multiple qualifying work-related posts confirmed.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First qualifying work-related post: Oct 15, 2025 - Nikita Bier's post announcing 'About this account' transparency feature, as reported by The Register (published Oct 15, 2025) and India Today (published Oct 15, 2025). question: Will Amazon acquire Warner Bros. Discovery?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if it is announced that Warner Bros. Discovery will be, has been, or is being acquired by or merged with the listed entity by 11:59 PM ET on May 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If no merger or acquisition takes place by the specified date, this market will resolve to "No Acquisition by May 31, 2026".

An official announcement will qualify for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether the merger or acquisition is ultimately completed. 

Any merger or acquisition will qualify regardless of whether it regards Warner Bros Discovery's entire company or separate transactions for its Warner Bros. or Discovery Global businesses.

The primary resolution source for this market is official information from the listed individual and/or Warner Bros. Discovery; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Amazon publicly confirm it has submitted or is preparing a formal bid or expression of interest to acquire all or part of Warner Bros. Discovery by November 23, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) formally announced on October 21, 2025, that it is conducting a strategic review of alternatives after receiving unsolicited acquisition interest from multiple parties. The company has engaged financial advisors Allen & Company, J.P. Morgan, and Evercore, along with legal counsel, to evaluate options including a full company sale, partial sales, or mergers. Paramount Skydance, led by David Ellison, reportedly offered $20 per share, which was rejected as too low. Media reports have indicated that WBD CEO David Zaslav has been courting tech giants including Amazon, Apple, and Netflix to create a competitive bidding environment, hoping to drive the price toward $40 per share. Amazon is frequently cited as a natural acquirer due to synergies with its existing MGM Studios acquisition (completed in 2022 for $8.45 billion) and its Prime Video streaming platform. Amazon's interest in premium content—demonstrated by its $1 billion/year Lord of the Rings series and its NFL Thursday Night Football deal—makes it a plausible bidder for WBD's assets, which include HBO, Warner Bros. Studios, DC Studios, and a vast film/TV library. However, as of October 24, 2025, Amazon has not publicly confirmed any bid or formal expression of interest. Any Amazon acquisition of WBD would face significant antitrust scrutiny given Amazon's existing market power across multiple sectors.

Sources:
- Yahoo Finance: WBD begins 'strategic review' of offers, 'unsolicited' interest (Oct 21, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/wbd-begins-strategic-review-offers-unsolicited-interest-130000123.html

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23 (inclusive), Amazon (Amazon.com, Inc. or any subsidiary) publicly confirms—via an official press release, SEC filing, or on-the-record statement by an Amazon executive—that it has submitted a bid, made a formal offer, or filed a formal expression of interest to acquire all or part of Warner Bros. Discovery. Credible reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., Wall Street Journal, Reuters, Bloomberg, New York Times) citing people directly familiar with the matter that Amazon has submitted a formal bid will also count. Mere speculation, unnamed-source rumors about Amazon 'considering' or 'exploring' a bid, or reports that Amazon has held preliminary conversations do NOT qualify. The question resolves No if no such confirmation occurs by 11:59 PM UTC on November 23, 2025. Primary sources for resolution include Amazon's investor relations page (https://ir.aboutamazon.com/), SEC EDGAR filings (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?company=amazon&CIK=&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40&search_text=&action=getcompany), Warner Bros. Discovery's investor relations page (https://ir.wbd.com/), and major financial news outlets.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Amazon will acquire WBD by May 31, 2026. A necessary precursor to any acquisition is Amazon formally entering the bidding process. WBD's strategic review is actively underway, and the next few weeks are a critical window during which serious bidders would be expected to emerge. If Amazon submits a formal bid or expression of interest by late November 2025, this would be a very strong positive signal that an Amazon-WBD deal could materialize. Conversely, if Amazon remains silent while other bidders (like Paramount Skydance) advance, it significantly reduces the probability of an Amazon acquisition. This subquestion tracks a concrete, observable precursor event rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: Amazon publicly confirms (via official press release, SEC filing, on-the-record executive statement, OR credible reporting from ≥2 major outlets citing people directly familiar) that it has submitted a formal bid or formal expression of interest to acquire all or part of Warner Bros. Discovery between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23. Mere speculation, unnamed-source rumors about 'considering' or 'exploring', or preliminary conversations do NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Amazon bid Warner Bros Discovery acquisition formal offer' (Oct 24–Nov 23) — to find formal bid confirmation; 2) 'Amazon Warner Bros Discovery merger deal' (Oct 24–Nov 23) — to find deal confirmation; 3) 'Amazon formal bid Warner Bros Discovery November 20 deadline submitted' (Nov 18–23) — to find post-deadline confirmation; 4) 'Amazon Warner Bros Discovery bid confirmed offer November 2025' (Nov 15–23) — to find explicit bid confirmation; 5) 'Amazon declined passed Warner Bros Discovery bid acquisition' (Oct 24–Nov 23) — to find evidence of non-participation.
evidence.step3_event_detection: The key event in this window was the November 20, 2025 deadline for first-round (non-binding) bids for WBD. evidence.step8_final_decision: The November 20 deadline passed with only Paramount, Netflix, and Comcast submitting formal non-binding bids. question: Will Italy win the third most gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the third most gold medals at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most gold medals won will use most overall medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most gold medals won, and Norway wins more overall medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the gold medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

subquestions.question: Will Italy have won at least 3 gold medals at the 2026 Winter Olympics by end of day February 16, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Italy is hosting the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milano-Cortina (February 6–22, 2026). Pre-Games prediction markets gave Italy only about a 2% chance of leading the overall gold medal count, with longshot odds of +4000 for most golds (CBS Sports, https://www.cbssports.com/olympics/news/2026-winter-olympics-medal-predictions-odds-expert-reveals-milano-cortina-best-bets/). Norway, the USA, and Germany are the three favorites for the top gold medal positions. At the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics, the third-place finisher in golds (Sweden) had 8 gold medals, while the host nation China tied for third with the USA at 9 golds each. For Italy to finish third in golds, it would likely need to accumulate a substantial number throughout the Games. Italy won 2 gold medals at the 2022 Beijing Olympics and 0 at the 2018 PyeongChang Olympics. However, home advantage and strong Italian athletes in short track speed skating, alpine skiing, and ski mountaineering (a new sport) could boost their tally. Reaching 3 golds by February 16 (with about 80% of medal events completed) would indicate Italy is on a pace consistent with a realistic shot at third place in the final standings.

Sources:
- CBS Sports medal predictions: https://www.cbssports.com/olympics/news/2026-winter-olympics-medal-predictions-odds-expert-reveals-milano-cortina-best-bets/
- Kalshi prediction market data via SportsBookReview: https://www.sportsbookreview.com/picks/winter-olympics/medal-odds/
- Sports Illustrated odds: https://www.si.com/betting/odds-to-win-most-gold-medals-2026-winter-olympics
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Italy has been awarded at least 3 gold medals in events completed at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics between 2026-02-07 and 2026-02-16 (inclusive), based on the official medal standings published on the International Olympic Committee website (https://www.olympics.com/) or the official Milano Cortina 2026 results page. Only gold medals awarded during this window (plus any awarded on February 6, the first day of competition) count toward the total. If there is any dispute or data source issue, the IOC's official medal table as displayed on olympics.com at end of day UTC on February 16, 2026 will be used. If the Games are suspended or cancelled before February 16, this question resolves based on golds awarded before the suspension/cancellation.
subquestions.rationale: Italy finishing third in gold medals would require a strong performance well above its recent Winter Olympic baselines (0–2 golds per Games). Tracking whether Italy reaches 3 golds by February 16—when roughly 80% of medal events will have been completed—serves as a meaningful mid-Games indicator. If Italy has not reached 3 golds by then, its chances of finishing third overall are very low. Conversely, if Italy has 3+ golds at that point, it signals genuine competitiveness for a top-3 gold medal finish. This subquestion helps distinguish between scenarios where Italy's home advantage translates into a historically strong performance versus a typical result, which is the key crux for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: Italy must have been awarded at least 3 gold medals at the 2026 Winter Olympics between Feb 7–16, 2026 (inclusive). Observable evidence: official or highly reliable reports of Italy's cumulative gold medal count reaching 3 within the window. Key entities: Italy, 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, gold medal count ≥3, window Feb 7–16 2026.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Italy gold medals 2026 Winter Olympics Milano Cortina' (Feb 7–16) — to find all Italy gold medals. evidence.step3_event_detection: Identified gold medals for Italy: (1) Feb 7: Lollobrigida women's 3,000m speed skating [multiple sources]; (2) Feb 10: Mixed short-track relay [ANSA, USA Today]; (3) Feb 11: Women's luge doubles (Voetter & Oberhofer) [CNA, AP, The Star]; (4) Feb 11: Men's luge doubles (Rieder & Kainzwaldner) [CNA, The Star]; (5) Feb 12: Federica Brignone super-G [Heavy, Day 6 articles]; (6) Feb 12: Lollobrigida women's 5,000m [Sunday Guardian, Bleacher Report]. All within window. ANSA article (Feb 12) confirms Italy had 4 golds after the two luge events, citing the previous two golds as: short-track relay (Tuesday, Feb 10) and speed skating (Saturday, Feb 7).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Italy's 3rd gold medal was won on February 11, 2026, in the women's luge doubles by Andrea Voetter and Marion Oberhofer, as confirmed by [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/sport/luge-italian-men-complete-golden-doubles-double-hosts-5924406), [AP](https://apnews.com/68be884f9feb0579f53fd1fe083e6eb9), [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2026/02/12/italy-sweeps-both-luge-doubles-golds-at-milan-cortina-winter-olympics), and [ANSA](https://www.ansa.it/english/news/sports/2026/02/12/milano-cortina-italy-flying-high-after-two-luge-golds_222a46b4-a17f-4648-a154-dd490c2c1628.html). This is within the Feb 7–16 window. The ANSA article explicitly confirms Italy's 4 golds sequence: (1) Lollobrigida speed skating Feb 7, (2) short-track relay Feb 10, (3) women's luge doubles Feb 11, (4) men's luge doubles Feb 11. By end of day Feb 11, Italy had 4 golds — exceeding the threshold of 3.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The women's luge doubles event was held on February 11, 2026 (Day 5 of the Games). Multiple AP and CNA sources confirm this date. evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Italy's 1st gold: Feb 7 (Lollobrigida 3,000m). Italy's 2nd gold: Feb 10 (short-track relay). Italy's 3rd gold: Feb 11 (women's luge doubles by Voetter & Oberhofer). No evidence of an earlier 3rd gold. The sequence is clearly documented across multiple authoritative sources. The ANSA article from Feb 12 explicitly states the luge golds on 'day six' brought Italy's total to 4 golds, with the previous two being Feb 7 and Feb 10.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: all sources consistently list Italy's gold medals in the same sequence (Feb 7, Feb 10, Feb 11 x2, Feb 12 x2). No source disputes this sequence. As of Feb 9 (USA Today), Italy had only 1 gold (Lollobrigida); as of Feb 10 evening (USA Today), Italy had 2 golds (2 Gold in the standings). By Feb 11, Italy had 4 golds per ANSA published Feb 12. The threshold of 3 golds was clearly reached on Feb 11, well within the Feb 7–16 window. No evidence of cancellation or suspension of Games.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Italy reached 3 gold medals on February 11, 2026, when Voetter and Oberhofer won the women's luge doubles — Italy's 3rd gold of the Games. This is within the Feb 7–16 window. Multiple corroborating sources confirm this. The question resolves Yes, with the threshold crossed on February 11, 2026.

question: Will Rodrigo Paz Pereira win by 15–20%?
description:
A second-round (runoff) vote for the Bolivia Presidential election is scheduled to take place on October 19, 2025 

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the 2025 Bolivian Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the 'margin of victory' is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first and second-place candidate. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the second round of the Bolivian Presidential Election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the results of the election aren’t known by March 31, 2026 ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve solely based on the first official vote count released by the Bolivian Government, specifically the Plurinational Electoral Body (Órgano Electoral Plurinacional, OEP) (https://www.oep.org.bo/).

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

subquestions.question: Will Rodrigo Paz Pereira lead Jorge 'Tuto' Quiroga by at least 15 percentage points in the average of publicly released Bolivian runoff polls conducted between September 15 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Bolivia will hold its first-ever presidential runoff on October 19, 2025, between centrist Rodrigo Paz Pereira (PDC) and right-wing former President Jorge 'Tuto' Quiroga (Libre). In the August 17 first round, Paz received approximately 32.1% of valid votes and Quiroga received approximately 26.9%, a gap of roughly 5 percentage points (AS/COA, https://www.as-coa.org/articles/three-things-know-about-bolivias-2025-first-round-election-results). Third-place finisher Samuel Doria Medina, who captured about 20% of the vote, has endorsed Paz, which could significantly widen his lead (AS/COA, https://www.as-coa.org/articles/reaction-bolivias-runoff-surprise-candidate-faces-conservative). The leftist MAS vote (Andrónico Rodríguez at ~8.1% and Eduardo del Castillo at ~3.1%) and the null-vote campaign (~19.1%) represent large blocs of undecided or protest voters whose behavior in the runoff is uncertain (Counter Punch, https://www.counterpunch.org/2025/08/22/bolivia-elections-restore-established-order-socialists-are-dismissed/). Pre-runoff polling will be a key indicator of whether Paz can build a commanding lead consistent with a 15–20 percentage point victory margin, or whether the race tightens. Bolivia's major polling firms include Ciesmori, Ipsos Bolivia, and others that typically publish results in national media outlets such as Página Siete and El Deber.

Sources:
- AS/COA, "Three Things to Know About Bolivia's 2025 First-Round Election Results" (2025-08-19): https://www.as-coa.org/articles/three-things-know-about-bolivias-2025-first-round-election-results
- AS/COA, "REACTION: Bolivia's Runoff" (2025-08-19): https://www.as-coa.org/articles/reaction-bolivias-runoff-surprise-candidate-faces-conservative
- Counter Punch, "Bolivia Elections Restore Established Order" (2025-08-22): https://www.counterpunch.org/2025/08/22/bolivia-elections-restore-established-order-socialists-are-dismissed/
- NBC News, "Bolivia heads to a presidential runoff" (2025-08-19): https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/bolivia-presidential-runoff-left-wing-dominance-ends-rcna197744
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the simple arithmetic average of Paz's lead over Quiroga across all publicly released head-to-head Bolivian presidential runoff polls with fieldwork dates falling entirely between September 15, 2025 and September 30, 2025 (inclusive) is 15 percentage points or greater. A 'publicly released poll' is defined as a survey published by a recognized polling firm (e.g., Ciesmori, Ipsos, Mercados y Muestras, or equivalent) and reported in at least one major Bolivian or international news outlet. The lead is defined as Paz's vote-intention percentage minus Quiroga's vote-intention percentage among respondents who state a preference for one of the two candidates (excluding undecided/blank/null responses if the poll reports such a figure; otherwise, using raw topline numbers as published). If fewer than two qualifying polls are publicly released with fieldwork entirely within this window by October 1, 2025, this question resolves as ambiguous (N/A). Polling data will be sourced from reports in Página Siete (https://www.paginasiete.bo/), El Deber (https://eldeber.com.bo/), or the polling firms' own published reports, as well as international aggregators such as Wikipedia's 'Opinion polling for the 2025 Bolivian general election' page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2025_Bolivian_general_election). The resolution window for qualifying polls is fieldwork conducted between 2025-09-15 and 2025-09-30, with the question resolving on 2025-10-01.
subquestions.rationale: Pre-election polling is the most direct observable indicator of the final margin of victory. question: Will India strike Pakistan by Dec 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if India initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Pakistani territory by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Indian military forces that impact Pakistani territory (e.g., if an Indian missile or drone hits a target within Pakistan’s borders, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted before reaching Pakistani territory, as well as surface-to-air missile strikes, will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether debris lands on Pakistani soil or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or any operation conducted by Indian ground forces will not qualify as a strike under this market.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will India publicly announce or be credibly reported to have placed its armed forces on a heightened state of alert (e.g., elevated readiness, forward deployment, or mobilization) directed at Pakistan between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14?
subquestions.background_information:
India conducted Operation Sindoor in May 2025 in retaliation for the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, striking nine terrorist targets inside Pakistan. The operation involved Su-30MKI, Rafale, Mirage 2000, and Tejas aircraft using BrahMos, SCALP, and SPICE precision munitions (News18, 2025-11-10: https://www.news18.com/india/su-30mki-rafale-mirage-tejas-these-fighter-jets-and-weapons-were-used-in-operation-sindoor-9195498.html). Following the ceasefire, both sides have engaged in escalatory rhetoric. Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh warned that India's restraint would not be repeated and referenced India's ability to reach Karachi (Firstpost, 2025-11-07: https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/we-didnt-kill-pakistani-citizens-rajnath-on-how-india-carried-operation-sindoor-13855802.html). Pakistan's Army Chief Asim Munir stated Pakistan would respond 'decisively, beyond proportion' to any provocation (DNA India, 2025-10-18: https://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-pakistan-asim-munir-once-again-resorts-to-hollow-anti-india-rhetoric-if-a-fresh-war-is-triggered-3133218). Cross-border arms smuggling from Pakistan into India has surged, with BSF recovering 215 drones and 180 weapons in Punjab as of October 23, 2025 (The Tribune, 2025-10-28: https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/rpg-seizure-signals-rising-terror-threat-in-state). A renewed Indian military alert or mobilization directed at Pakistan would be a strong leading indicator that a strike is being prepared or considered imminent.

Sources:
- News18, 2025-11-10: https://www.news18.com/india/su-30mki-rafale-mirage-tejas-these-fighter-jets-and-weapons-were-used-in-operation-sindoor-9195498.html
- Firstpost, 2025-11-07: https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/we-didnt-kill-pakistani-citizens-rajnath-on-how-india-carried-operation-sindoor-13855802.html
- DNA India, 2025-10-18: https://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-pakistan-asim-munir-once-again-resorts-to-hollow-anti-india-rhetoric-if-a-fresh-war-is-triggered-3133218
- The Tribune, 2025-10-28: https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/rpg-seizure-signals-rising-terror-threat-in-state
- MoneyControl, 2025-10-15: https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/india/dgmo-lt-gen-rajiv-ghai-big-statement-on-operation-sindoor-indian-navy-sailed-into-arabian-sea-12965481.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 (inclusive), at least two credible major international or Indian news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, The Hindu, Times of India, NDTV, Hindustan Times) report that India has placed its military forces on a heightened state of alert, conducted significant forward deployments, or mobilized forces specifically in the context of tensions with Pakistan. This includes reports of fighter aircraft squadrons being moved to forward airbases near the Pakistan border, naval task forces being deployed to the Arabian Sea in an operational posture directed at Pakistan, or official Indian government or military statements announcing elevated military readiness directed at Pakistan. Routine exercises, scheduled deployments, or readiness postures directed at China or other countries do not count. If no such credible reports emerge by 2025-12-14 at 23:59 UTC, the question resolves No. Resolution sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news), NDTV (https://www.ndtv.com), The Hindu (https://www.thehindu.com), Hindustan Times (https://www.hindustantimes.com).
subquestions.rationale: A military strike on Pakistan would almost certainly be preceded by heightened military readiness, forward deployments, or mobilization — as was the case before Operation Sindoor in May 2025, when the Indian Navy sailed into the Arabian Sea and the IAF forward-deployed multiple fighter types. Observing such preparatory military posturing within the next month would be a strong early indicator that India is contemplating or preparing another strike on Pakistan before the end of 2025. Conversely, if Indian forces remain in normal peacetime posture, a strike by December 31 becomes much less likely. This subquestion is meaningfully different from the ultimate question because it asks about observable military preparations rather than the strike itself, and such preparations would typically precede any strike by days to weeks.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: India publicly announces or is credibly reported (by 2+ major outlets like Reuters, BBC, The Hindu, NDTV, Hindustan Times, Times of India) to have placed armed forces on heightened alert, conducted forward deployments, or mobilized forces specifically directed at Pakistan between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14. This includes: fighter jets to forward airbases near Pakistan, naval task forces in operational posture vs Pakistan, or official Indian statements of elevated military readiness vs Pakistan. Must NOT be routine exercises or China-directed activity.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'India military alert Pakistan border 2025' (to find direct alert reports); 2) 'India armed forces mobilization Pakistan heightened readiness November December 2025' (to find mobilization reports); 3) 'India forward deployment aircraft Pakistan border November December 2025' (to find forward air deployments); 4) 'India Pakistan military tensions escalation alert deployment 2025' (to find escalation reports); 5) 'India heightened military alert Pakistan official announcement November December 2025' (to find official statements); 6) 'India Pakistan war preparation mobilization forces November 2025' (to find mobilization news); 7) 'India Navy Arabian Sea Pakistan operational posture December 2025' (to find naval deployment); 8) 'India fighter jets forward airbase Pakistan border deployment readiness 2025' (to find air force deployments).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) BSF troops on alert at LoC/IB for infiltration prevention (Nov 29, Dec 12) - REJECTED: routine counter-terrorism posture, not a new heightened alert directed at Pakistan; (2) Indian Army Chief Dwivedi warning Pakistan on Nov 17 (Operation Sindoor was 'trailer') - REJECTED: rhetorical statement, not an announcement of heightened military readiness or deployment; (3) Navy Chief Admiral Tripathi statement Dec 2 saying 'Operation Sindoor remains in progress' - REJECTED: refers to posture established in May 2025, not a new deployment within window; (4) Western Command Chief Katiyar (Dec 7) saying 'can't compromise readiness' vs Pakistan/China - REJECTED: general readiness statement, not a new heightened alert or deployment announcement; (5) Exercise Trishul (Nov 3-13) - REJECTED: outside the resolution window (ended Nov 13, before window begins Nov 14); (6) India-France-UAE air exercise over Arabian Sea Dec 10-11 - REJECTED: does not appear to be directed specifically at Pakistan, described as training exercise; (7) BSF preparing for 'Operation Sindoor 2.0' if ordered - REJECTED: conditional statement of readiness, not actual deployment or alert order.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No identified candidate event exactly matches the resolution criteria. The criteria requires India to PLACE forces on heightened alert directed at Pakistan (a new action), with reports from 2+ specified credible outlets. What was found includes: (a) Ongoing/routine border security posture since May 2025 Operation Sindoor - not a newly placed heightened alert; (b) Rhetorical warnings by military/civilian officials - not force deployments or alert announcements; (c) Navy Chief's reference to Operation Sindoor 'remaining in progress' per [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/indian-navys-defiant-posture-during-operation-sindoor-kept-pakistan-navy-confined-to-coast-says-naval-chief/article70350486.ece) and [News18](https://www.news18.com/india/forced-pakistan-navy-to-remain-docked-admiral-dinesh-tripathi-on-indian-navys-role-in-op-sindoor-ws-l-9744784.html) - these describe the May 2025 posture, not a new deployment in the window. No report from Reuters, BBC, The Hindu, NDTV, Hindustan Times, or Times of India explicitly states India placed forces on a NEW heightened alert directed at Pakistan during Nov 14 - Dec 14, 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with exact timestamp found within the window. The Nov 17 Army Chief warning is not a force deployment announcement. The Dec 2 Navy Chief statement references the May 2025 Operation Sindoor posture, not a new action. No exact timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove conclusion: (1) Pakistan's defence minister warned of 'all-out war' preparations (Nov 20), suggesting he perceived India as a threat - but this is Pakistan's statement about India, not India announcing alerts. (2) BSF Dec 12 report mentions 'heightened alert along the IB from Jammu to Kathua' and 'intensified counter-terror measures' - but this is ongoing border security, not a newly announced heightened alert directed at Pakistan in an escalatory sense. (3) India-France-UAE exercise Dec 10-11 near Karachi - Pakistan expressed concerns, but this appears to be an exercise, not a unilateral alert vs Pakistan. (4) Sentinel newspaper article (Nov 29) mentions 'India on high alert as Imran Khan rumours push Pakistan towards chaos' - but this is about internal Pakistan instability, not India's military posture directed at Pakistan. No contradictory evidence found that would reverse the No conclusion.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying event found. While India-Pakistan tensions remain elevated from the May 2025 Operation Sindoor, and there are ongoing BSF alerts and rhetorical warnings, no credible reports from 2+ major specified outlets exist within the Nov 14 - Dec 14, 2025 window showing India newly placing armed forces on a heightened state of alert (elevated readiness, forward deployment, or mobilization) specifically directed at Pakistan. The existing security posture is a continuation of the post-Operation Sindoor environment, not a new heightened alert. Resolution: No.

question: Will Norway win the second most gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the second most gold medals at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most gold medals won will use most overall medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most gold medals won, and Norway wins more overall medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the gold medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

subquestions.question: Will Norway hold the #1 position in gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics medal table as of the end of competition on February 18, 2026?

Norway has topped the gold medal table at the last three consecutive Winter Olympics: 16 golds in 2022 (Beijing), 14 in 2018 (PyeongChang), and 11 in 2014 (Sochi). Norway's gold medal strength comes primarily from biathlon, cross-country skiing, ski jumping, and alpine events. Germany and the United States are considered the next most likely nations to lead the gold count, at roughly 12-14% and 18-19% implied probability respectively. If Norway leads the gold medal count heading into the final days of competition, it significantly constrains which nations could finish second — and makes it more likely that the second-place finisher is one of the traditional strong nations (Germany, USA) rather than a surprise contender. Conversely, if Norway is NOT leading, the entire top of the standings is more competitive, making it harder to predict who finishes second.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, as of the end of all medal events completed on or before February 18, 2026, Norway holds the #1 position in gold medals on the official 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics medal table published by the International Olympic Committee at https://www.olympics.com/. subquestions.rationale: Whether Norway leads the gold medal count heading into the final few days of the 2026 Winter Olympics is a strong indicator of whether Norway finishes second in golds (the ultimate question). If Norway is leading on Feb 18, it is very unlikely Norway finishes second — the question would then hinge on whether another country overtakes them, or a different pair of nations fights for second. If Norway is NOT leading, then Norway itself becomes a plausible candidate for second place. This subquestion helps forecasters distinguish between scenarios where Norway dominates (making the second-place race about Germany vs. USA vs. others) and scenarios where the gold race is more competitive (making Norway a candidate for second). This is a genuinely different observable than the ultimate question, since it asks about first place at a mid-point rather than second place at the end.

The question asks about 'as of the end of competition on February 18, 2026' — at that point Norway had 15 golds (14 entering + 1 from men's team sprint on Feb 18), far ahead of Italy's ~9-10 golds.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Norway held the #1 position in gold medals on the 2026 Winter Olympics medal table as of the end of competition on February 18, 2026. subquestions.question: Will A Minecraft Movie's cumulative domestic gross remain above the cumulative domestic gross of every other 2025 release except one (i.e., remain in the top 2) on Box Office Mojo's 2025 calendar-year domestic gross chart as of September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Superman sits in third place at roughly $332 million. These three films have largely completed their theatrical runs, so their domestic totals are unlikely to change dramatically in September. However, several major films are still in theaters or set for release in September (e.g., Avatar: Fire and Ash is expected in December), meaning the domestic rankings could shift over the remaining months of 2025. For A Minecraft Movie to finish 2025 as the second-highest domestic grosser, it needs to avoid being overtaken by more than one other film. Tracking whether it holds a top-2 position through September provides an early signal of whether it can maintain that rank through year-end.

- Box Office Mojo 2025 Calendar Grosses: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses
- ScreenRant (Aug 20, 2025): Disney's Lilo & Stitch vs Minecraft domestic totals: https://screenrant.com
- Newsday (Aug 21, 2025): 2025 box office overview: https://www.newsday.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, on September 30, 2025, A Minecraft Movie's cumulative 2025 domestic gross (as reported in the 'Gross' column on Box Office Mojo's 2025 calendar-year domestic gross chart at https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses) is the first or second highest among all films listed. If a Minecraft Movie has already slipped to #3 or lower by the end of September—before major holiday releases even open—that would be a strong negative signal for the ultimate question. Conversely, if it holds top-2 status through September, forecasters would need to assess only whether one or more late-year blockbusters can overtake it, narrowing the uncertainty considerably.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes condition: As of September 30, 2025, A Minecraft Movie's cumulative 2025 domestic gross must be #1 or #2 on Box Office Mojo's 2025 calendar-year domestic gross chart (no more than one other film has a higher cumulative domestic gross). The outcome of Cook's legal challenge is a critical indicator for whether Trump will actually need to name a replacement. If Cook's removal is upheld or she resigns, Trump has signaled he would move quickly to name a replacement, with David Malpass and Stephen Miran as the leading candidates.

As of late September 2025, the legal proceedings are ongoing, and Cook appears to still be contesting her removal.

Conversely, if Cook's removal is upheld or she steps down, Trump has indicated he would move quickly to name a nominee, and Malpass is one of the two most frequently mentioned candidates. This subquestion thus tracks a key precondition for the ultimate question without simply restating it.

description:
