subquestions.question: Will Omar Fateh be within 5 percentage points of Jacob Frey in the final publicly released pre-election poll of the 2025 Minneapolis mayoral race?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question ('Progressive Cities Parlay') requires all three progressive candidates—Zohran Mamdani (NYC), Omar Fateh (Minneapolis), and Katie Wilson (Seattle)—to win their respective mayoral elections on November 4, 2025. The weakest link in this parlay is widely considered to be Omar Fateh's challenge to incumbent Jacob Frey in Minneapolis. As of early October 2025, Fateh trailed Frey by approximately 5 points in polls, making Minneapolis the most uncertain of the three races. Mamdani leads his NYC race by roughly 18–20 points and Wilson defeated Harrell in Seattle's August primary, making both of those races more favorable for the progressive candidates. Whether Fateh can close the gap with Frey in the final days is the key swing factor for this parlay.

A report from October 4, 2025, noted Fateh was 'just five points behind Frey in the polls' (https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/the-next-mamdani-meet-minneapolis-muslim-socialist-mayoral-candidate). DSA-affiliated candidates like Fateh have been buoyed by the 'Mamdani bump' in progressive organizing (https://localnews8.com/news/national-world/ap-national-news/2025/10/19/democratic-socialists-see-their-moment-in-zohran-mamdanis-rise/). However, incumbent Frey has significant structural advantages in Minneapolis.

Sources:
- Donald J. Trump (news site): https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/the-next-mamdani-meet-minneapolis-muslim-socialist-mayoral-candidate
- LocalNews8 (AP): https://localnews8.com/news/national-world/ap-national-news/2025/10/19/democratic-socialists-see-their-moment-in-zohran-mamdanis-rise/
- Yahoo News: https://www.yahoo.com/news/believe-not-election-next-month-090025498.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, in the last publicly released poll of the 2025 Minneapolis mayoral race conducted and/or published between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-03 (inclusive), Omar Fateh is within 5 percentage points of Jacob Frey (i.e., Frey's share minus Fateh's share is ≤ 5 points, or Fateh is ahead). The poll must be conducted by a recognized polling firm (e.g., one listed on FiveThirtyEight's pollster ratings or a major local/national news outlet-commissioned poll). If multiple polls are released on the same final date, the question resolves based on the average of those polls' margins. If no publicly released poll meeting these criteria is published between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-03, this question resolves as ambiguous/N/A. Sources to check include FiveThirtyEight (https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/polls/), RealClearPolitics, 538/Silver Bulletin, Star Tribune polling, and other major outlets covering the Minneapolis mayoral race.
subquestions.rationale: The Minneapolis race is the most competitive and uncertain of the three races in the parlay. Mamdani holds a commanding lead in NYC and Wilson is favored in Seattle, so the parlay's outcome hinges most heavily on whether Fateh can beat the incumbent Frey. A late poll showing Fateh within striking distance (≤5 points) would be a strong indicator that the parlay has a realistic chance of hitting. Conversely, if Fateh falls further behind, the parlay is very unlikely to resolve Yes regardless of the other two races. This subquestion thus serves as the most informative early indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: (1) A poll published Oct 23–Nov 3, 2025, (2) by a recognized polling firm (FiveThirtyEight-listed or major news outlet-commissioned), (3) showing Fateh within 5 percentage points of Frey (Frey−Fateh ≤ 5, or Fateh ahead). If no qualifying poll exists in this window, resolves ambiguous/N/A.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: 'Minneapolis mayoral race poll 2025 Omar Fateh Jacob Frey' (Oct 23–Nov 3); 'Minneapolis mayor election poll 2025' (Oct 23–Nov 3); 'Minneapolis mayor poll survey October November 2025 Frey Fateh percentage points' (Oct 23–Nov 3); 'Star Tribune poll Minneapolis mayoral 2025 Frey leading' (Oct 1–Nov 3); 'Minneapolis for the Many progressive PAC poll Frey Fateh 5 points survey' (Aug–Nov 3); 'FiveThirtyEight Minneapolis mayor 2025 poll rating' (Oct 1–Nov 3); 'Minneapolis mayor 2025 pre-election poll recognized firm survey results October' (Oct 23–Nov 3).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Two polls found: (A) August 2025 All of Mpls PAC poll: Frey 41%, Fateh 28% (13-point gap, Frey-aligned PAC, August, outside window). (B) Late August 2025 Minneapolis for the Many PAC poll: Frey 34%, Fateh 28-29% (5-6 point gap, progressive-aligned PAC, August, outside window). No polls from Oct 23–Nov 3, 2025 by recognized/independent polling firms were identified. Multiple sources (Star Tribune Oct 25, ArcaMax Oct 25, AP Oct 30) noted 'limited polling' available. Zero Hedge (Nov 2) references 'a recent poll' at 34% for Frey but does not identify the pollster or Fateh's number — this appears to reference the same August poll.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Neither identified poll satisfies all criteria: both were conducted in August 2025 (outside Oct 23–Nov 3 window), and both were commissioned by partisan PACs (All of Mpls and Minneapolis for the Many), not recognized independent polling firms. [Star Tribune Oct 25](https://www.startribune.com/minneapolis-mayor-election-2025-polling-fundraising/601496188) explicitly notes 'limited polling' characterizes this race. [ArcaMax Oct 25](https://www.arcamax.com/politics/politicalnews/s-3897954) confirms both PAC polls from August. No Star Tribune-commissioned poll, FiveThirtyEight-tracked poll, or major news outlet-commissioned poll was published in the Oct 23–Nov 3 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying poll was published with a timestamp in the Oct 23–Nov 3, 2025 window. The August polls precede the window. No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found in the window at all, so first occurrence check is not applicable.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple major news articles from the window (Star Tribune, AP, CBS News) discuss the race without referencing any new qualifying poll. The consistent reporting of 'limited polling' and reference only to August PAC polls confirms no recognized-firm poll was published in the Oct 23–Nov 3 window. The resolution criteria explicitly state: 'If no publicly released poll meeting these criteria is published between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-03, this question resolves as ambiguous/N/A.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: No publicly released poll by a recognized polling firm (FiveThirtyEight-listed or major news outlet-commissioned) was published between Oct 23–Nov 3, 2025. Only PAC-commissioned polls from August 2025 exist, which are outside the required window and do not meet the recognized-firm criteria. Per the explicit resolution criteria, this resolves as ambiguous/N/A, not Yes or No.

question: Ahmed al-Sharaa out as leader of Syria in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Ahmed al-Sharaa, the President of Syria, is removed from power for any length of time between July 15,, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Al-Sharaa will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, is officially dismissed, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as leader of Syria within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Ahmed al-Sharaa deliver a speech at the UN General Assembly high-level week (September 22–30, 2025)?
subquestions.background_information:
Ahmed al-Sharaa, Syria's interim president since December 2024, is scheduled to speak at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) high-level week in New York, set for September 22–30, 2025. A Syrian foreign ministry official confirmed this plan, noting he would be 'the first Syrian president to speak at the United Nations since former president Nureddin al-Atassi (in 1967)' (Firstpost, August 25, 2025). Al-Sharaa remains under UN sanctions and a travel ban due to his past as a designated jihadist, meaning he must request a sanctions exemption for each foreign trip. The United States has been pushing for his delisting from the UN Security Council terrorism sanctions list (bne IntelliNews, August 7, 2025). His ability to attend and speak at UNGA would be a strong signal that he remains firmly in power, retains international backing, and faces no immediate domestic threat to his rule. Conversely, failure to appear could indicate a crisis—whether a travel ban not being lifted, domestic instability preventing his departure, or a loss of power.

Sources:
- Firstpost (2025-08-25): https://www.firstpost.com/world/al-sharaa-to-speak-at-unga-next-month-first-syrian-leader-to-do-so-in-decades-13838291.html
- bne IntelliNews (2025-08-07): https://www.intellinews.com/us-pushes-to-remove-syrian-officials-from-un-terrorism-sanctions-list-366029/
- Asharq Al-Awsat (2025-08-31): https://english.aawsat.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Ahmed al-Sharaa delivers a speech (in person or via a live video address as head of the Syrian delegation) at the UN General Assembly high-level segment between September 22 and September 30, 2025. It resolves No if, by September 30, 2025 (23:59 UTC), he has not delivered such a speech. The resolution window is September 1, 2025 to September 30, 2025. Primary resolution sources will be official UN General Assembly records (https://gadebate.un.org/), UN Web TV (https://media.un.org/), and a consensus of credible international news reporting (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP). If the high-level week is postponed beyond September 30, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Al-Sharaa's UNGA appearance is a strong near-term observable indicator of his continued hold on power. To travel to New York, he must (1) still be Syria's recognized leader, (2) maintain enough domestic stability to leave the country, (3) receive a UN sanctions exemption, and (4) retain sufficient international support. If any of these conditions fail—particularly if he is removed from power, faces a coup, or domestic unrest prevents his departure—he would not appear. Thus, his UNGA speech is a meaningful early indicator for the ultimate question of whether he remains Syria's leader through 2025. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question would likely also disagree on whether he can successfully make this trip, making it a useful crux.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Ahmed al-Sharaa (Syrian interim/transitional president) must deliver a speech — in person or via live video — as head of the Syrian delegation at the UN General Assembly high-level segment between September 22 and September 30, 2025. Observable evidence: news reports, UN records, or video confirming he spoke at UNGA in the specified window. Key entities: Ahmed al-Sharaa, UN General Assembly High-Level Week, September 22–30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Ahmed al-Sharaa UN General Assembly speech September 2025' — to find direct evidence of the speech. 2) 'Syria UN General Assembly high-level week 2025' — for broader context and confirmation. 3) 'Ahmed al-Sharaa UNGA speech date September 24 25 2025' — to pin down the exact date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple independent sources report that Ahmed al-Sharaa delivered an in-person speech at the UNGA on September 24, 2025 (Middle East Monitor, Anadolu Agency, WION, SANA, Hazard Herald, MoneyControl all citing September 24; Yahoo and Businessday citing September 25; DW mentioning September 29). The most frequently cited date across highest-quality sources is September 24, 2025. The speech was delivered in person in New York. No sources indicate the event did not happen or was cancelled.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require: (1) Ahmed al-Sharaa delivers a speech; (2) in person or via live video as head of the Syrian delegation; (3) at the UN General Assembly high-level segment; (4) between September 22–30, 2025. All four criteria are explicitly satisfied: [Middle East Monitor](https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20250924-in-landmark-un-speech-president-sharaa-vows-to-rebuild-syria-calls-for-world-support/) confirms a 'nine-minute address at the United Nations General Assembly in New York' on September 24, 2025. [SANA (official Syrian state agency)](https://sana.sy/en/breaking-news/2269342/) confirms 'President Ahmad al-Sharaa addressed the United Nations General Assembly on 24 September 2025.' [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/in-landmark-un-speech-syrian-president-vows-to-rebuild-syria-calls-for-world-support/3698004) confirms 'Syrian President Ahmad Al-Sharaa delivered a historic speech at the UN General Assembly on 24 September 2025.' The speech was delivered in person (he traveled to New York with a delegation, per SANA). This is clearly within the September 22–30 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple sources published on 2025-09-24 explicitly state the speech occurred on September 24, 2025. The Middle East Monitor article (published 2025-09-24) describes 'On September 24, 2025, Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa delivered a nine-minute address at the United Nations General Assembly in New York.' SANA (official state news) also confirms September 24. Resolution timestamp: 2025-09-24T00:00:00Z (within the resolution window). The precise time within September 24 is not specified, but the date is clearly established by multiple independent sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: All sources consistently point to September 24, 2025 as the date of the UNGA speech. No sources indicate an earlier speech by al-Sharaa at UNGA in the September 22–30 window (i.e., no reports of a speech on September 22 or 23). The first and only UNGA speech occurred on September 24, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradiction check: Some articles mention different dates (Sept 25 in Yahoo/Businessday, Sept 29 in DW), but these appear to be either publication date discrepancies or reporting errors, as the majority of contemporaneous sources (Middle East Monitor, WION, Anadolu Agency, SANA, Hazard Herald — all published September 24) explicitly state September 24 as the speech date. The DW article dated September 29 may be a retrospective commentary piece using an imprecise date, while SANA (official Syrian state news) and multiple international wire services all confirm September 24. There is no evidence contradicting that the speech occurred within the September 22–30 window. The speech was in-person (al-Sharaa traveled to New York with a delegation). It was delivered as head of the Syrian delegation. The UNGA high-level week was not postponed beyond September 30.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Ahmed al-Sharaa delivered an in-person speech at the UN General Assembly high-level week on September 24, 2025 — explicitly within the September 22–30, 2025 window. This is confirmed by multiple independent, high-quality sources including official Syrian state media (SANA), Anadolu Agency, Middle East Monitor, WION, and others. All resolution criteria are satisfied. The question resolves Yes.

question: Will Venezuela invade Guyana in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Venezuela commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of Guyana between January 29 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be will be official confirmation by Venezuela, Guyana, the United Nations, or any permanent member of the UN Security Council, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Venezuela conduct a new armed incursion or cross-border firing incident targeting Guyanese military, police, or civilian personnel in the Essequibo or border region between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Venezuela has been steadily escalating provocations against Guyana over the disputed Essequibo region throughout 2025. In March 2025, a Venezuelan naval gunboat intercepted ExxonMobil operations in Guyanese waters. On May 15, 2025, Guyana's military reported three armed attacks on its patrols along the Cuyuni River, believed to be carried out by Venezuelan operatives or proxies. On August 31, 2025, a Joint Services patrol escorting ballot boxes along the Upper Cuyuni River was fired upon from the Venezuelan side. Venezuelan Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino López warned in September 2025 that Venezuela would respond in 'legitimate defense' to any attack launched from Guyanese or Trinidadian territory, accusing both nations of collaborating with the United States. The U.S. has deployed a major naval presence in the Southern Caribbean, including seven warships, a nuclear-powered submarine, and over 4,500 service members. Trinidad and Tobago has offered the U.S. military access to its territory in the event of Venezuelan aggression against Guyana. The pattern of escalating cross-border armed incidents — from naval interceptions to proxy attacks to direct fire on patrols — serves as a leading indicator of whether Venezuela is moving toward a full military offensive. A further escalation in October 2025 would signal heightened risk of an invasion before year-end.

Sources:
- Zero Hedge, 'Venezuela's Shadow War Over Oil-Rich Essequibo Is Escalating' (May 29, 2025): https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/venezuelas-shadow-war-over-oil-rich-essequibo-escalating
- BNO News, 'Guyana says patrol came under fire from Venezuela; no injuries reported' (Aug 31, 2025): https://bnonews.com/index.php/2025/08/guyana-says-patrol-came-under-fire-from-venezuela/
- Latin Times, 'Venezuela Warns Neighbors of Retaliation Over Support for U.S. Military Operations' (Sep 15, 2025): https://www.latintimes.com/venezuela-warns-neighbors-retaliation-over-support-us-military-operations-well-act-legitimate-578641
- bne IntelliNews, 'Trinidad backs US access in case of Venezuelan escalation over Essequibo' (Aug 25, 2025): https://www.intellinews.com/trinidad-backs-us-access-in-case-of-venezuelan-escalation-over-essequibo-370123/
- Newsroom Guyana, 'Guyana on high alert as Venezuela threatens international peace and order' (May 25, 2025): https://newsroom.gy/2025/05/25/guyana-on-high-alert-as-venezuela-threatens-international-peace-and-order/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), there is at least one credible report — from Guyana's government (e.g., the Guyana Defence Force, Ministry of Foreign Affairs), Reuters, AP, BBC, or the Associated Press — of a new armed incident in which Venezuelan military personnel, Venezuelan-flagged vessels or aircraft, or armed actors operating from Venezuelan territory fire upon, attack, or physically engage Guyanese military, police, or civilian personnel, or Guyanese-licensed commercial operations (e.g., ExxonMobil), within Guyana's internationally recognized territory or territorial waters (including the Essequibo region and its maritime zone). The incident must involve the use of firearms, explosives, or other lethal weaponry. Verbal threats, diplomatic protests, troop movements within Venezuelan territory, or overflights that do not involve the use of weapons do not count. If no such incident is reported by credible sources by November 5, 2025, the question resolves No. If reports are ambiguous regarding the origin of fire (i.e., it is not confirmed that the fire came from Venezuelan territory or Venezuelan-affiliated actors), the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The pattern of escalating armed incidents in 2025 — from naval interceptions in March, to armed attacks on patrols in May, to cross-border fire during elections in August — forms a clear escalation ladder. Whether this pattern continues or accelerates in October is a strong leading indicator of whether Venezuela will move from shadow-war provocations to an outright military offensive by year-end. If armed incidents intensify, the probability of invasion increases significantly; if they cease or de-escalate (perhaps due to U.S. naval deterrence or diplomatic pressure), invasion becomes much less likely. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question would likely update substantially based on whether October sees further armed provocations.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Between Oct 1-31, 2025, at least one credible report (from Guyana's GDF/MFA, Reuters, AP, BBC, or AP) of a NEW armed incident where Venezuelan military personnel, Venezuelan-flagged vessels/aircraft, or armed actors operating from Venezuelan territory use firearms, explosives, or other lethal weaponry against Guyanese military, police, or civilian personnel, or Guyanese-licensed commercial operations, within Guyana's internationally recognized territory (including Essequibo) or territorial waters. Key exclusions: verbal threats, diplomatic protests, troop movements within Venezuela, overflights without weapons use. Ambiguous origin of fire resolves No.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Venezuela armed incursion Guyana Essequibo October 2025' — to find any military attacks in the region; 2) 'Venezuela Guyana military attack border shooting 2025' — to find cross-border incidents; 3) 'Georgetown Guyana bombing gas station attack October 2025 Venezuelan' — to investigate bombing incident details; 4) 'Guyana gas station bombing Venezuelan military government connection terrorism October 2025' — to determine state-link of bombing; 5) 'Venezuela Guyana Essequibo gunboat naval vessel incursion attack October November 2025' — to find any maritime military incidents; 6) 'Venezuela Guyana Defence Force attack cross-border armed incident October 2025' — to find direct military attacks
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Georgetown gas station bombing, Oct 26, 2025 — Venezuelan national Daniel Alexander Ramirez Peodomo, linked to criminal gang 'R Syndicato/Organización R,' planted explosive at Mobil gas station, killing 6-year-old Soraya Bourne. Explosive smuggled from Venezuela. REJECTED: Perpetrator is a criminal gang member, not Venezuelan military or government-directed actor; no confirmed state link; target was not Guyanese military/police in Essequibo; (B) Venezuelan gunboat ABF Guaiqueri PO-11 incident — occurred March 1, 2025, BEFORE the window; (C) U.S. military strikes on Venezuelan drug boats — not Venezuela attacking Guyana; (D) U.S. fighter jets near Venezuela, Venezuelan military buildups — these are Venezuela vs. U.S. tensions, not Venezuela vs. Guyana armed attacks; (E) No other direct Venezuelan military attack on Guyana found in October 2025
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Georgetown bombing [AP](https://apnews.com/article/guyana-gas-station-attack-953752fc189a5baeb5caa11e779fe2d8) and [Stabroek News](https://www.stabroeknews.com/2025/10/29/news/guyana/main-suspect-in-deadly-gas-station-blast-confessed-crime-chief/) was an explosive attack within Guyana (Oct 26, 2025), committed by a Venezuelan national affiliated with criminal gang 'R Syndicato' who brought the device from Venezuela. However, it does NOT meet resolution criteria because: (1) The perpetrator is a criminal gang member, not Venezuelan military personnel or Venezuelan-flagged vessel/aircraft; (2) No evidence that the actor was 'operating from Venezuelan territory' in the sense of a Venezuelan government/military operation; (3) The motive remains under investigation — no confirmed state direction; (4) The AP article reports this as a criminal terrorist attack, not a Venezuelan military/state incursion. Articles on Essequibo tensions [OilPrice](https://oilprice.com/Energy/Crude-Oil/Essequibo-Tensions-Rise-as-Trump-Engages-in-Gunboat-Diplomacy.html), [bne IntelliNews](https://www.intellinews.com/guyana-venezuela-border-tensions-simmer-as-exxonmobil-production-continues-407114/) describe general tensions and military buildups but no armed cross-border incident in October 2025. No credible source reports Venezuelan military/state-directed lethal force against Guyanese personnel in the Essequibo or border region during October 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found within the window. The Georgetown bombing (Oct 26, 2025, ~7:30 PM local time) does not meet resolution criteria as explained.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event found at all within the window, so first occurrence check is moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find: (1) Venezuelan government-linked actors attacking Guyanese targets — not found; (2) Venezuelan military cross-border firing — not found; (3) Naval/maritime incidents in Essequibo — March 2025 gunboat incident referenced, but occurred before window; (4) The Georgetown bombing was carried out by a criminal gang with Venezuelan connection, but is clearly characterized as criminal/terrorist activity by a non-state actor, not a Venezuelan military/state operation. Multiple sources confirm the Essequibo situation involved 'tensions' and 'military buildups' but no actual armed cross-border attacks. The resolution criteria's requirement for 'Venezuelan military personnel, Venezuelan-flagged vessels or aircraft, or armed actors operating from Venezuelan territory' (in a state-directed military context) is not met by the criminal bombing. The criteria also notes ambiguous origin of fire resolves No — the bombing's connection to the Venezuelan state is ambiguous at best.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying event occurred within the October 1-31, 2025 window. The most significant incident — the Georgetown gas station bombing by a Venezuelan national — does not meet the resolution criteria because: (a) the perpetrator is a criminal gang member, not Venezuelan military personnel; (b) there is no confirmed Venezuelan government/military direction; (c) the motive is still under investigation; (d) it does not target Guyanese military/police in the Essequibo border region specifically. All other activity in October 2025 consists of diplomatic tensions, Venezuelan military buildups within Venezuela's own territory, and U.S.-Venezuela confrontations. No credible source reports a Venezuelan state-directed armed incident against Guyanese personnel within Guyana's territory during this period. Resolution: No.

question: Will Samsung release a trifold phone by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Samsung releases a phone with three foldable screens by the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

In order to be considered released, the product must be available for purchase by the general public within the specified timeframe. An announcement or unveiling alone is not sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from Samsung. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Samsung's trifold phone become available for purchase by the general public in at least one market (e.g., South Korea, China, Singapore, Taiwan, or UAE) by December 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Samsung officially unveiled its trifold smartphone at the APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea on October 31–November 1, 2025. Samsung confirmed in an official statement to SamMobile that it plans to bring the device to users 'within this year.' The initial launch is expected to be limited to select Asian markets — South Korea, China, Singapore, Taiwan, and possibly the UAE — with an initial production run reportedly of only 50,000 units. Multiple reports from September–November 2025 indicated the device was already in mass production and could go on sale shortly after the APEC unveiling, potentially in November 2025. However, as of November 12, 2025, no confirmed on-sale date has been publicly announced by Samsung, and the device has not yet been made available for purchase by the general public.

Sources:
- Forbes (Nov 1, 2025): https://www.forbes.com/sites/jaymcgregor/2025/11/01/samsung-galaxy-trifold-unveil-release-date/
- TechStory (Oct 27, 2025): https://techstory.in/the-galaxy-trifold-set-for-ultra-limited-debut/
- Mashable ME (Sep 3, 2025): https://me.mashable.com/tech/50093/samsung-galaxy-z-trifold-tipped-to-launch-in-october-with-limited-availability
- TechRadar (Oct 28, 2025): https://www.techradar.com/phones/samsung-galaxy-phones/the-samsung-galaxy-tri-fold-just-got-officially-shown-off
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-12 and 2025-12-01 (inclusive), Samsung's trifold phone becomes available for purchase by the general public in at least one country. 'Available for purchase' means individual consumers can order or buy the device through Samsung's official website, Samsung retail stores, or authorized retailers in at least one market (e.g., South Korea, China, Singapore, Taiwan, UAE, or any other country). An announcement, unveiling, pre-registration, or waitlist without the ability to complete a purchase does not count. Resolution will be based on official Samsung announcements (https://news.samsung.com/ or samsung.com), credible tech publication reporting (e.g., The Verge, Forbes, TechRadar, SamMobile), or evidence of the product being listed for sale on Samsung's official online store in any market. If no credible evidence of the device being available for purchase by the general public emerges by end of day December 1, 2025 (UTC), this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Samsung will release a trifold phone available for public purchase by December 12, 2025. This subquestion asks whether the phone goes on sale by December 1, which is a strong early indicator. Samsung has unveiled the device and stated it will arrive 'within this year,' with multiple reports suggesting a November launch in limited markets. If the phone is purchasable by December 1, it almost certainly resolves the ultimate question. If it is NOT purchasable by December 1, the remaining 11-day window becomes very tight, making a 'No' resolution on the ultimate question more likely (though still possible). This subquestion tracks a concrete, observable milestone — actual retail availability — that is distinct from the ultimate question's deadline and provides strong directional evidence.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Samsung's trifold phone must be available for individual consumers to order or buy (not just announced/unveiled) in at least one market between 2025-11-12 and 2025-12-01 (inclusive). Observable evidence: Samsung's official website listing for purchase, credible tech publication reporting a sale date within the window, or evidence of the product listed for sale on Samsung's official online store. Key entities: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold; key timing: Nov 12–Dec 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Samsung trifold phone release date sale purchase 2025' (Nov 1–Dec 1) — to find any sale dates; 2. 'Samsung tri-fold foldable phone available buy general public' (Nov 1–Dec 1) — to find purchase availability; 3. 'Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold on sale purchase buy November 2025' (Nov 12–Dec 1) — to find in-window sales; 4. 'Samsung trifold phone December 5 launch sale date confirmed' (Nov 25–Dec 1) — to confirm launch date; 5. 'Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold early sale pre-order official available' (Nov 12–Dec 1) — to check for pre-orders or early sales.
evidence.step3_event_detection: ALL sources consistently report the Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold launch/sale date as December 5, 2025 — which is OUTSIDE the resolution window. question: Will Trump act to ban mail-in voting or voting machines in 2025?
description:
On August 18, 2025, President Donald J. Trump announced his commitment to eliminate mail-in voting and voting machines in U.S. elections, ahead of the 2026 midterms.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that inhibits mail-in voting or voting machines from use for the 2026 midterm election by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any executive action or legislation that restricts, limits, or prohibits the use of mail-in voting or voting machines in any way will qualify, even if the action is delayed, suspended, or subsequently blocked by judicial or other actions.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration publish or release the text of a new executive order targeting mail-in voting, voting machines, or voter ID requirements between November 30, 2025 and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
President Donald Trump announced on August 18, 2025, that his administration was drafting an executive order to ban mail-in voting and voting machines ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. On August 30-31, he further announced plans for an executive order mandating voter ID for every vote and limiting mail-in voting to the very ill and overseas military. As of late November 2025, Trump has made multiple public statements and Truth Social posts about these intentions but the key question is whether a formal executive order has been or will be signed.

Trump previously signed an executive order in March 2025 requiring documentary proof of citizenship for federal elections and that all ballots be received by Election Day; a federal judge blocked the citizenship-proof requirement in April 2025, citing that election regulation is a state and congressional power. Legal experts have consistently noted that the Constitution's Article I, Section 4 grants states authority over election administration, making executive orders in this area legally vulnerable.

Despite months of announcements, no executive order specifically banning mail-in voting or voting machines has been publicly signed as of late November 2025. The question is whether one will materialize before the end of December 2025.

Sources:
- USA Today, "Trump says he will issue executive order mandating voter ID requirement" (Aug 31, 2025): https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/08/31/trump-voter-id-executive-order/75487291007/
- Al Jazeera, "Trump to order voter ID for every vote, 'no exceptions'" (Aug 31, 2025): https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/31/trump-to-order-voter-id-for-every-vote-no-exceptions
- KOMO, "Election officials speak out as Trump pushes to eliminate mail-in voting" (Aug 24, 2025): https://komonews.com/news/nation-world/election-officials-speak-out-as-trump-pushes-to-eliminate-mail-in-voting
- USAfricaOnline, "Trump pushes to end mail-in voting ahead of 2026 elections" (Aug 19, 2025): https://usafricaonline.com/2025/08/19/trump-pushes-to-end-mail-in-voting-ahead-of-2026-elections/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between November 30, 2025 and December 29, 2025 (inclusive), the Trump administration officially publishes, signs, or releases the text of a new executive order (distinct from the March 2025 order on proof of citizenship) that specifically targets mail-in voting, voting machines, or imposes new voter ID requirements for federal elections. The executive order must be published on the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/) or announced via official White House communications (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/). If no such executive order text is published or signed during this window, the question resolves No. Draft announcements, Truth Social posts promising future action, or verbal statements alone do not count — the order must be formally signed or officially released.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Trump will 'act' to ban mail-in voting or voting machines by signing legislation or performing executive action by December 31, 2025. The most likely pathway is an executive order, which Trump has repeatedly promised since August 2025. Tracking whether an actual executive order is signed and published in December 2025 is a direct leading indicator: if one appears by December 29, it is almost certain the ultimate question resolves Yes. If no order materializes by then, only two days remain, making a No resolution highly likely. This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question because it focuses specifically on the observable event of an executive order being formally released (not just announced or promised), and its window ends slightly before the ultimate deadline, providing early signal.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Trump administration must officially publish, sign, or release the text of a NEW executive order (distinct from the March 2025 order) specifically targeting mail-in voting, voting machines, or imposing new voter ID requirements for federal elections, published on the Federal Register or announced via official White House communications, between November 30, 2025 and December 29, 2025. Truth Social posts, verbal statements, or draft announcements do not count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump executive order mail-in voting voter ID voting machines 2025' (Nov 30 - Dec 29) — to find any signed EO; 2) 'Trump executive order election integrity December 2025' — to find any election-related EO; 3) 'Trump signs executive order voting mail-in ballots December 2025 White House' — to find signing events; 4) 'Trump executive order election voting Federal Register December 2025' — to check Federal Register publications; 5) 'Trump new executive order voter ID voting machines election December 2025 whitehouse.gov' — to check White House official releases; 6) 'Trump executive order ban mail-in voting 2026 midterms White House sign' — to find any formal action.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Trump's December 4 Truth Social post calling for voter ID — REJECTED: this is a social media post, not a formal EO. (2) Trump's verbal statements/threats about issuing an EO on mail-in voting — REJECTED: verbal statements explicitly excluded. (3) Ohio Governor DeWine signing SB 293 on Dec 19 — REJECTED: this is state legislation, not a federal executive order. (4) The March 2025 executive order — REJECTED: explicitly excluded by resolution criteria as pre-existing. (5) December 11, 2025 EO on proxy advisors — REJECTED: unrelated to voting/elections. (6) December 18 EO on marijuana reclassification — REJECTED: unrelated to elections. (7) December 18 EO on Christmas Eve holiday — REJECTED: unrelated to elections. Multiple sources explicitly state no new EO on mail-in voting or voter ID was issued during the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event satisfies the criteria. Multiple sources explicitly confirm: [Ohio Capital Journal](https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2025/12/10/repub/voting-by-mail-faces-uncertain-moment-ahead-of-midterm-elections/) states 'vowing an executive order to end the mail-in ballot hoax, though none has been issued.' [ArcaMax](https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3951538) states Trump 'has promised an executive order to end it—though none has been issued.' [The Review](https://www.the-review.com/story/news/politics/state/2025/12/19/mike-dewine-signs-bill-to-change-ohio-mail-in-ballot-deadline/87379073007/) (Dec 19) describes Trump 'threatening an executive order to end mail-in voting,' implying no EO yet signed. These sources are contemporaneous and consistent throughout the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no qualifying event occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event was found at any point in the window, so a first occurrence check is moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: no source anywhere within the Nov 30 - Dec 29 window reports a new executive order targeting mail-in voting, voting machines, or voter ID requirements. The consistent reporting across multiple independent sources (Ohio Capital Journal, ArcaMax, The Review, Missouri Independent, Yahoo, The Independent) uniformly confirms that Trump promised such an EO but had not issued one as of mid-to-late December 2025. The only election-related federal EO referenced is the pre-existing March 2025 order, which is explicitly excluded by the resolution criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence consistently shows that no new executive order targeting mail-in voting, voting machines, or voter ID requirements was formally signed or published by the Trump administration during the November 30 - December 29, 2025 window. Multiple reliable sources explicitly stated throughout the window that Trump promised such an order but had not issued one. The question resolves No, with the resolution datetime being the end of the window (2025-12-29T23:59:59Z) since there was no earlier discrete event that made it definitively impossible.

question: Will US GDP growth in Q3 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP "Advance Estimate" release for Q3 of 2025 scheduled for October 30, 2025.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the Atlanta Fed GDPNow model estimate for Q3 2025 real GDP growth be between 2.0% and 3.0% as of its last update on or before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Atlanta Federal Reserve's GDPNow model provides a running real-time estimate of U.S. real GDP growth for the current quarter based on incoming economic data. It is widely followed as an early indicator of the official BEA GDP advance estimate. As of late August 2025, Q2 2025 GDP was revised upward to 3.3% annualized growth, rebounding from a -0.5% Q1 contraction. However, economists have cautioned that the tariff-induced drag on imports (which artificially boosted Q2 GDP) may fade, and full-year growth could slow to around 1.5%. The GDPNow tracker updates frequently as key economic data releases (ISM manufacturing, jobs reports, retail sales, etc.) come in during September. A GDPNow reading in the 2.0%-3.0% range heading into October would suggest that Q3 growth is tracking near the 2.0%-2.5% window specified in the ultimate question, since GDPNow estimates tend to converge toward the actual advance estimate as the quarter progresses. The GDPNow model is published at: https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow

Sources:
- Atlanta Fed GDPNow: https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow
- BEA Q2 2025 GDP second estimate: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
- Reuters on Q2 GDP revision and AI investment: https://www.zawya.com/en/economy/north-america/us-second-quarter-gdp-revised-higher-as-businesses-boost-investment-in-ai-y7ffjy1b
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Atlanta Fed GDPNow model's most recent estimate of Q3 2025 real GDP growth (seasonally adjusted annualized rate), as published on the Atlanta Fed GDPNow page (https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow), is at or above 2.0% and strictly below 3.0% as of the last update released between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The relevant estimate is the final GDPNow update published on or before October 1, 2025. If the estimate is exactly 2.0%, it resolves Yes. If it is exactly 3.0%, it resolves No (as that would be at the boundary of 3.0% or above). If the Atlanta Fed discontinues or suspends the GDPNow model during this period and no update is available, this question resolves as ambiguous/N/A.
subquestions.rationale: The GDPNow model is the single best real-time tracker of the official BEA GDP advance estimate. By early October, the GDPNow estimate will have incorporated most of the major Q3 data releases (employment, retail sales, trade balance, industrial production) and will be a strong predictor of the October 30 advance estimate. If two forecasters disagree on whether Q3 GDP growth will land in the 2.0%-2.5% range, the GDPNow reading as of October 1 provides critical evidence: a reading in the 2.0%-3.0% band would indicate that the 2.0%-2.5% outcome is plausible but not certain, while a reading well above 3.0% or below 2.0% would strongly update against that bracket. The slightly wider 2.0%-3.0% range for the subquestion (vs. the ultimate question's 2.0%-2.5%) accounts for the fact that GDPNow still has some revision potential in October and avoids producing an uninformatively low probability.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Atlanta Fed GDPNow model's last update on or before October 1, 2025 must show Q3 2025 real GDP growth (SAAR) at ≥2.0% AND <3.0% (strictly below 3.0%). If ≥3.0%, resolves No. Observable evidence: The specific numerical GDPNow estimate from the Atlanta Fed's final update during the window Sept 1–Oct 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Atlanta Fed GDPNow Q3 2025 real GDP growth estimate' (Sept 1–Oct 1). Query 2: 'GDPNow model estimate third quarter 2025 September October'. Query 3: 'Atlanta Fed GDPNow September 26 2025 Q3 GDP estimate 3.9%'. Query 4: 'GDPNow last update September 29 30 October 1 2025 Q3 forecast'. Query 5: 'Atlanta Fed GDPNow October 1 2025 3.8% Q3 GDP update'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple GDPNow updates found during the window: Sept 4: 3.0%; Sept 10: 3.1%; Sept 16: 3.4%; Sept 17/21: 3.3%; Sept 23-25: 3.3%; Sept 26: 3.9%; October 1: 3.8%. The October 1, 2025 update is explicitly stated in an InstaForex article published October 1, 2025 as '3.8%, revised from 3.9%'. This is the last update on or before October 1, 2025. Multiple other articles from September 30 and October 1 reference GDPNow at 3.9%, which was the pre-October-1 update, consistent with the Oct 1 revision to 3.8%.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The October 1, 2025 GDPNow estimate for Q3 2025 is 3.8%, per [InstaForex article](https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2763148) published October 1, 2025: 'The Atlanta Federal Reserve's GDPNow model, updated on October 1, 2025, projects a slight slowdown in U.S. economic growth for the third quarter of 2025, revising the forecast from 3.9% to 3.8%.' This is 3.8%, which is ≥3.0%, so does NOT satisfy the resolution criteria (must be ≥2.0% AND <3.0%). Per the resolution criteria, 3.8% ≥ 3.0% → resolves No.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The InstaForex article is published on 2025-10-01 and explicitly states the model was 'updated on October 1, 2025.' Other articles from Sept 30 and Oct 1 also reference a 3.9% estimate, consistent with the Sept 26 update (before the Oct 1 revision to 3.8%). No exact UTC time is provided, but the article clearly states the date as October 1, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The relevant event is the LAST update on or before October 1, not the first. The last update is October 1, 2025, at 3.8%. There is no later update within the window. The Sept 26 update at 3.9% preceded the Oct 1 update at 3.8%. The Oct 1 update is confirmed as the final update within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checking: Multiple articles from Sept 30 reference GDPNow at 3.9% (consistent with the Sept 26 update). The InstaForex October 1 article specifically notes a revision FROM 3.9% TO 3.8% on October 1 — this corroborates the sequence. CNBC/Breitbart articles on Oct 1 still reference 3.9% (possibly written before the Oct 1 GDPNow update was posted), but the InstaForex article directly reporting the Oct 1 GDPNow update shows 3.8%. Both 3.9% and 3.8% are well above the required <3.0% threshold. No contradictory evidence suggests the estimate fell below 3.0% at any point during the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Atlanta Fed GDPNow model's last update on or before October 1, 2025 showed Q3 2025 real GDP growth at 3.8% (updated October 1, 2025). This is well above the 3.0% upper boundary required for a Yes resolution. Per the resolution criteria, the estimate must be ≥2.0% AND strictly <3.0%. At 3.8%, it fails the <3.0% criterion. Resolution: No.

question: GTA 6 launch postponed?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if by May 26, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, Rockstar Games or its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, officially announces that Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) will not be released by May 26, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Grand Theft Auto VI is otherwise not released in the US by May 26, 2026, 11:59 PM ET this will qualify as a postponement.

For the purposes of this market, "release" refers to the game becoming publicly available for purchase or download in the US. Early access, beta versions, other forms of pre-release availability, or leaks will not count as an official release. If the release is only for certain consoles (e.g. Xbox Series X/S) it will count.

The resolution source will be official information from Rockstar Games or its parent company, Take-Two Interactive.

subquestions.question: Will Take-Two Interactive announce or hint at a delay of GTA VI's May 26, 2026 release date during its Q2 FY2026 earnings call or related investor communications in October or November 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, is expected to hold its Q2 FY2026 earnings call in early November 2025 (typically the first or second week of November). Industry insider Tom Henderson of Insider Gaming has specifically predicted that a GTA VI delay announcement will come during this November earnings call, pushing the game from May 2026 to around October 2026 (https://gameranx.com/features/id/527889/article/insider-believes-a-grand-theft-auto-vi-delay-announcement-will-come-this-november/). However, as of late September 2025, Take-Two has repeatedly confirmed the May 26, 2026 release date — at its Annual Meeting of Shareholders on September 18, 2025, on the game's official website, and in CEO Strauss Zelnick's public statements (https://gameranx.com/features/id/528553/article/gta-6-still-on-schedule-for-may-2026-take-two-promises-more-details-in-the-future/). Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier has also noted that 'there's no guarantee that May 2026 is a sure thing' (https://mashable.com/article/gta-vi-delay-what-we-know). Take-Two typically files preliminary earnings materials (such as press releases and investor letters) on or around the earnings call date, and sometimes issues pre-announcements or guidance updates before the call. Any indication — such as language changes on the official website, removal of the specific May 26 date, SEC filings adjusting Fiscal Year 2027 guidance, or pre-earnings press releases — would serve as early warning signals of a delay.

Sources:
- Gameranx (Sep 15, 2025): https://gameranx.com/features/id/527889/article/insider-believes-a-grand-theft-auto-vi-delay-announcement-will-come-this-november/
- Gameranx (Sep 19, 2025): https://gameranx.com/features/id/528553/article/gta-6-still-on-schedule-for-may-2026-take-two-promises-more-details-in-the-future/
- Mashable (Sep 20, 2025): https://mashable.com/article/gta-vi-delay-what-we-know
- Rockstar Games GTA VI official page: https://www.rockstargames.com/VI
- Take-Two Interactive investor relations: https://ir.take2games.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), any of the following occur: (1) Take-Two Interactive or Rockstar Games issues an official statement, press release, SEC filing, investor letter, or earnings-related communication indicating that GTA VI will not launch on May 26, 2026, or that the release date has been changed to a later date; OR (2) The official GTA VI website (https://www.rockstargames.com/VI) removes or changes the 'Coming May 26, 2026' language to a later date or a vaguer timeframe (e.g., 'Coming 2026' without specifying May 26); OR (3) Take-Two Interactive files an SEC document (e.g., 8-K, 10-Q, or investor presentation) that no longer references a May 26, 2026 launch date or references a different launch window. The question resolves No if none of the above occur by 11:59 PM ET on October 31, 2025. Resolution sources: the Rockstar Games official website (https://www.rockstargames.com/VI), Take-Two Interactive's investor relations page (https://ir.take2games.com/), and SEC filings via EDGAR (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000946581&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40).
subquestions.rationale: The insider prediction of a delay announcement specifically targets November 2025, but any pre-announcement activity — such as changes to the official website, SEC filings adjusting guidance, or early communications from Take-Two — would likely appear in October as the company prepares for earnings. If Take-Two signals a delay in October, it is very strong evidence that GTA VI will be postponed past May 26, 2026 (resolving the ultimate question Yes). Conversely, if Take-Two continues to maintain the May 26, 2026 date through October without any wavering, it reduces (but does not eliminate) the probability of a delay being announced before November 6, 2025. This subquestion captures the most likely early indicator channel — official corporate communications — rather than relying on insider rumors.

evidence.step1_decompose: Resolution requires: (1) official Take-Two/Rockstar statement that GTA VI won't launch May 26, 2026, OR (2) official GTA VI website removes/changes 'Coming May 26, 2026' language, OR (3) Take-Two SEC filing no longer references May 26, 2026. All must occur between Oct 1-31, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: GTA VI delay October 2025; Take-Two Q2 FY2026 earnings call October-November 2025; GTA 6 delay announcement official statement October 2025; Take-Two SEC filing October 2025; Rockstar website 'May 26' removed October 2025; GTA VI official release date change October/November 2025.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key events: (1) Take-Two Q2 FY2026 earnings call scheduled for November 6, 2025 (outside October window). (2) Rockstar updated website on/around Oct 29, which removed 'Coming May 26, 2026' text from key art per Game Rant article. (3) Take-Two CEO Zelnick spoke Oct 29 at CNBC Tech Summit saying GTA 6 'approaches perfection' - no delay hint. (4) Multiple sources Oct 29-30 note the website was redesigned but still confirmed May 26, 2026. (5) GTA Online trailer released Oct 29 with no official delay mention. Rejected: insider speculation articles, fan theories about delay, analyst predictions - none constitute official statements.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Criterion 1: No official Take-Two/Rockstar statement was issued in October declaring GTA VI would not launch May 26, 2026. Criterion 2: The Game Rant article (Oct 29) notes 'removal of the Coming May 26, 2026 text from the game's key art' during website redesign. However, this is mentioned as a speculative concern, not confirmed as the GTA VI website officially removing its release date language. Multiple other sources from the same period (Oct 29-30) still cite May 26, 2026 as the official date. The Sportskeeda Oct 29 article states 'The game's official release date has been confirmed as May 26, 2026' alongside the website update. Criterion 3: No SEC filing was found that changed the GTA VI release date.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The website update with key art change occurred around October 29, 2025 per Game Rant. However, this was part of a general Rockstar website redesign (updating decade-old design), not an explicit official change of release date language on the dedicated GTA VI page.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event found. The October 29 website change is the only potential candidate, but it does not satisfy the resolution criteria as an explicit official change.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: (a) Multiple sources from Oct 29-30 confirm May 26, 2026 still as official date even after website redesign. (b) Take-Two CEO Zelnick's Oct 29 comments praise GTA 6 without any delay hints. (c) The Q2 earnings call (the main expected communication) was scheduled for Nov 6, outside the window. (d) The website key art change was mentioned in context of fan speculation, not as a confirmed delay signal. (e) ScreenRant Oct 30 states 'a delay is considered highly unlikely' based on available information.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. The Q2 FY2026 earnings call occurred on November 6, 2025 (outside the October 31 window). No official delay announcement was made in October. The Rockstar website redesign around Oct 29 removed the 'Coming May 26, 2026' text from key art, but this was a cosmetic/design change - not an official change of the release date language on the dedicated GTA VI page, and multiple sources published alongside this news still confirmed May 26, 2026 as the active release date. No SEC filing changed the release date. All three resolution criteria remain unmet within the October 1-31, 2025 window.

question: Will US GDP growth in 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted real GDP growth rate for the United States in 2025, as reported in the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) "Advance Estimate" release for Q4 of 2025, scheduled for January 29, 2026.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: The relevant data will be the full-year real GDP growth rate as stated in the advance estimate, typically expressed as the percentage change from the annual level in 2024 to the annual level in 2025. Any revisions to this figure made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the BEA's final Q3 2025 GDP estimate (released January 22, 2026) show annualized quarterly growth of 4.0% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
The BEA released its initial estimate of Q3 2025 real GDP growth on December 23, 2025, reporting an annualized rate of 4.3%, well above the consensus forecast of 3.3%. This followed Q2 2025 growth of 3.8% and a Q1 2025 contraction of 0.6%. The BEA noted that the first three quarters of 2025 averaged approximately 2.5% annualized growth. The final (third) estimate for Q3 2025 is scheduled for January 22, 2026. Historical analysis shows that GDP revisions from the advance/initial release to the final release average about 0.65 percentage points, meaning the final Q3 figure could plausibly range from roughly 3.0% to 5.6%. question: Will Tulsi Gabbard be the first to leave the Trump Cabinet before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve based on the next individual announced to leave the Trump Cabinet, or who otherwise ceases to be a member of the administration. If no one leaves by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “None before 2027”.

An announcement of an individual's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the resignation/removal takes effect.

If multiple individuals announce departures or are removed at the same time, the market will resolve to the individual who actually leaves office first. If they leave simultaneously, the market will resolve to the individual whose last name comes first alphabetically.

For the purposes of this market, the Cabinet includes Vice President, the heads of the 15 executive departments, as well as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the President’s Chief of Staff, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Ambassador to the United Nations, the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA). Acting officials serving in these roles are not included. The Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) is not considered Cabinet-level under the current Trump administration and is excluded from this market.

An individual will be considered to have left the Cabinet if they resign from or are removed from any Cabinet-level position, even if they are subsequently appointed to a different Cabinet-level role.

If a candidate who is not already listed, assumes a listed cabinet position they will be added to the market. However, candidates who have merely been nominated for a cabinet position will not be considered to have left, even if their nomination is rejected or withdrawn.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible reopening may also be used.

question: Will the next government funding bill be a clean CR?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the next government funding bill that becomes law in the United States by December 31, 2025, is a clean continuing resolution. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

A clean continuing resolution is defined as a funding measure that temporarily extends current government spending at the previous fiscal year’s levels for a specified period, without incorporating any additional policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Senate pass a clean continuing resolution (CR) to reopen the government between October 31, 2025 and November 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late October 2025, the U.S. federal government is in a shutdown. Republicans in the Senate have repeatedly brought up votes on a clean continuing resolution (CR) that would fund the government at current levels through mid-November, but these efforts have failed to gain sufficient bipartisan support. As of October 17, 2025, the Senate had held at least ten votes on a clean CR without success, and lawmakers adjourned without a resolution (Star Local, October 17, 2025: referenced in provided articles). Meanwhile, the shutdown has caused cascading impacts, including threats to community health center funding in Virginia and other states (WSLS, October 21, 2025). The key sticking point appears to be disagreement between parties on whether additional policy provisions or spending changes should be attached to any funding bill. A Senate vote passing a clean CR would be a strong signal that the next government funding bill to become law is indeed a clean CR, as it would indicate bipartisan momentum toward that outcome rather than a more complex omnibus or policy-laden package.

Sources:
- Star Local (Oct 17, 2025): https://starlocalmedia.com/news/no-progress-on-funding-as-trump-cuts-programs-amid-shutdown/
- WSLS (Oct 21, 2025): https://www.wsls.com/news/virginia/2025/10/21/watch-virginia-community-health-centers-face-funding-crisis/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 10, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. Senate passes (by a recorded vote or unanimous consent) a standalone clean continuing resolution — defined as a bill that temporarily extends government funding at previously enacted levels for a specified period without incorporating additional policy riders, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations beyond what is necessary to maintain current funding levels. The resolution source will be official Senate roll call vote records available at https://www.senate.gov/legislative/votes_new.htm, supplemented by credible reporting from outlets such as the Associated Press, Reuters, The Washington Post, or The New York Times. If no such vote occurs or the Senate only passes a funding bill that includes substantial policy provisions beyond a simple extension of current funding levels, this question resolves No. If the Senate passes a bill that is ambiguous as to whether it constitutes a 'clean' CR, resolution will rely on a consensus of at least three major credible news outlets characterizing it as a clean CR.
subquestions.rationale: The Senate passing a clean CR is a necessary precursor to a clean CR becoming law. If the Senate cannot pass a clean CR in this window, it becomes much less likely that the next government funding bill signed into law by December 31, 2025 will be a clean CR — either a more complex bill with policy riders will be needed to secure enough votes, or the shutdown will persist longer. Conversely, if the Senate does pass a clean CR, it significantly raises the probability that the House will follow suit and the President will sign it, making it the next government funding bill. This is a direct observable legislative event that serves as a strong leading indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: U.S. Senate passes a standalone clean CR (extending funding at current levels without substantial policy riders) between Oct 31-Nov 10, 2025. Observable evidence: Senate roll call votes, major news reporting. Key threshold: 'clean' means no substantial policy provisions beyond simple funding extension at previously enacted levels.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'U.S. Senate clean continuing resolution CR vote November 2025' (Oct 31-Nov 10); 2) 'Senate government funding vote continuing resolution October November 2025' (Oct 25-Nov 10); 3) 'Senate passes continuing resolution government reopens November 9 10 2025' (Nov 8-12); 4) 'Senate vote minibus appropriations CR funding bill November 2025 passage' (Nov 8-12)
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Multiple failed Senate votes on House-passed clean CR (H.R. 5371) throughout October-early November — all failed to reach 60-vote threshold. (B) Senate voted 60-40 to invoke cloture on amended bill on Nov 9/10. (C) Senate passed amended bill (H.R. 5371 with amendments) by 60-40 on Nov 10 or 11. Event (A) is rejected — the votes failed. Events (B) and (C) are the same bill but it is NOT a clean CR — it's a minibus package with additional provisions.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The bill passed was NOT a clean CR. Multiple sources confirm it included: (1) three full-year appropriations bills (military construction/VA, agriculture/FDA, legislative branch) — [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/government-shutdown-senate-deal/), [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/senate-passes-bill-reopen-government-sends-to-house-rcna243120); (2) provisions reversing Trump-era RIFs and reinstating fired workers; (3) back pay for furloughed workers; (4) a new expiration date of January 30, 2026 instead of November 21. [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5597463-thune-vote-government-shutdown/) specifically contrasts this with 'the House-passed clean CR.' [JD Supra Nov 10 update](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/government-shutdown-update-monday-8339843/) confirms the bill 'includes provisions reversing reductions-in-force (RIFs) since October 1, preventing future RIFs through January 31, and providing backpay for furloughed workers' — clearly not a 'clean' CR under the resolution criteria. The criteria require 'no additional policy riders, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations beyond what is necessary to maintain current funding levels,' which this bill clearly does not meet.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The cloture vote occurred on Sunday night November 9 into November 10, 2025 (after 10:45 PM, per Gateway Pundit). Final passage: JD Supra (Nov 11) states 'On Monday, November 10, 2025, the U.S. Senate passed an amended continuing resolution.' NBC News (Nov 11) says passed 'on November 11.' Some ambiguity about exact timestamp of final passage, but within or at edge of window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event (clean CR passage) was found. The original clean House-passed CR (H.R. 5371, through Nov 21) failed 14+ times in the Senate throughout the window period.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Breitbart headline called Trump's support 'Trump Supports Senate's Clean CR' but this was clearly a political framing — the actual bill contents included a minibus with three full-year appropriations bills and worker protection provisions. Multiple authoritative sources (CBS News, NBC News, The Hill, JD Supra) explicitly characterize it as a 'minibus' or 'package' — not a clean CR. The resolution criteria require consensus of three major credible outlets calling it a 'clean CR' for ambiguous cases; no such consensus exists — instead, the consensus is that this was NOT a clean CR.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Senate passed a bill on November 10 (or possibly early November 11) that reopened the government, but that bill was NOT a standalone clean CR. It was a minibus package including three full-year appropriations bills and multiple additional policy provisions (worker reinstatement, back pay, RIF prohibition). The House-passed clean CR was never passed by the Senate within the window. Therefore, the question resolves No. The window closed on Nov 10 without a clean CR passing; the bill that passed on Nov 10/11 was not a clean CR per the resolution criteria.

subquestions.question: Will Israel and Syria engage in publicly confirmed, direct or U.S.-mediated face-to-face negotiations (not just 'contacts' or 'channels') between December 12, 2025 and January 11, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of early December 2025, Israel-Syria security negotiations have been ongoing but have repeatedly stalled. Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa confirmed in November 2025 that his government is engaged in direct negotiations with Israel, with the U.S. acting as broker (https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/israel-news/2317541/syrian-president-confirms-direct-negotiations-with-israel-for-first-time-since-assads-fall.html). Israeli FM Gideon Sa'ar disclosed to the Knesset Foreign Affairs Committee on December 2, 2025 that Israel has been engaged in unofficial, U.S.-facilitated talks with Syria (https://english.almanar.com.lb/2318940). However, a Washington Times report from December 9, 2025 indicated that PM Netanyahu withdrew from a U.S.-brokered agreement at the UN General Assembly in September 2025, halting negotiations (https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/9/netanyahu-behind-stalled-israel-syria-negotiations/). Netanyahu's office denied any final agreement, calling reports 'fake news,' though a Syrian source told Channel 12 that a final draft was nearly complete but paused on Israel's side (https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5117581-netanyahu-denies-contacts-syria-have-led-final-agreement). Key sticking points include Israel's insistence on retaining Mount Hermon and establishing a demilitarized buffer zone, versus Syria's demand for full Israeli withdrawal to pre-December 8, 2024 borders. Netanyahu stated on December 4 that a deal is possible only with a buffer zone from Damascus to Mount Hermon (https://www.breitbart.com/middle-east/2025/12/04/netanyahu-says-deal-with-syria-possible-if-security-buffer-zone-included/). The current status is one of stalled but not terminated diplomatic engagement, making the resumption of active, structured negotiations a key precursor to any final agreement.

Sources:
- Al-Manar TV: https://english.almanar.com.lb/2318940
- Washington Times: https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/9/netanyahu-behind-stalled-israel-syria-negotiations/
- Asharq Al-Awsat: https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5117581-netanyahu-denies-contacts-syria-have-led-final-agreement

- Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/20/after-israel-pms-trip-to-occupied-syria-is-a-deal-off-the-table
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between December 12, 2025 and January 11, 2026 (inclusive), credible reporting from at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, Washington Post) confirms that Israeli and Syrian officials held structured, face-to-face negotiations — either direct or through a U.S.-mediated format where both delegations were present at the same venue — specifically focused on a security agreement or broader peace framework. The negotiations must be described as formal or structured meetings (not merely indirect 'contacts,' 'channels,' or back-channel communications). Official statements from either the Israeli government, the Syrian government, or the U.S. State Department confirming such meetings also suffice. If no such confirmed meetings are reported by January 11, 2026, this resolves No. Primary resolution sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), Times of Israel (https://www.timesofisrael.com), Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com).
subquestions.rationale: The resumption of active, structured negotiations is a necessary precondition for reaching a formal security agreement by January 31, 2026. If talks remain stalled through early January — as they appear to have been since September 2025 — it becomes extremely unlikely that a comprehensive agreement could be finalized in the remaining weeks. Conversely, if face-to-face negotiations resume, it signals that key political obstacles (particularly Netanyahu's reluctance and the territorial disagreements) may be resolving, significantly increasing the probability of a deal. This subquestion asks about an observable diplomatic event that is a leading indicator, rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Israeli and Syrian officials held structured, face-to-face negotiations (not indirect contacts), either direct or U.S.-mediated (both delegations at same venue), focused on a security agreement or peace framework, confirmed by at least two major international news outlets, within Dec 12, 2025–Jan 11, 2026.

Roman Gofman, Gil Reich. Syrian delegation: FM Asaad al-Shaibani, intelligence chief Hussein al-Salama. US delegation: Tom Barrack, Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All criteria explicitly satisfied: (1) Structured face-to-face negotiations confirmed — described as 'fifth round' of formal negotiations over two days in Paris, not merely contacts [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/another-round-of-israel-syria-negotiations-reportedly-to-begin-monday-in-paris/); (2) U.S.-mediated with both delegations present at same venue (Paris) [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/6/israel-syria-agree-to-dedicated-communication-line-in-us-brokered-talks); (3) Focused on security agreement and 1974 Disengagement Agreement framework [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/89MW9KE); (4) Confirmed by multiple major outlets: Times of Israel, Al Jazeera, AFP, France24, Haaretz, Anadolu Agency, Fox News — well exceeding the required two; (5) Official U.S. State Department joint statement released Jan 6, Israeli PM office confirmed, Syrian SANA confirmed [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/syria-israel-agree-to-set-up-joint-coordination-mechanism-during-us-backed-paris-talks/3791672).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Talks began January 5, 2026 (confirmed by Times of Israel liveblog published Jan 5, 2026; AFP article published Jan 5, 2026; Syrian SANA report). evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event found in the window. evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence found.
