The U.S. State Department's joint statement is particularly authoritative and directly matches the resolution criteria ('Official statements from either the Israeli government, the Syrian government, or the U.S. State Department confirming such meetings also suffice'). Alternative interpretation check: Could these be described as 'contacts' rather than formal meetings? No — all sources describe them as formal negotiations/talks (fifth round), with named delegations, structured agendas, two-day duration, and an official joint statement outcome.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All resolution criteria are unambiguously met: Israeli and Syrian officials held structured, face-to-face, U.S.-mediated negotiations in Paris on January 5–6, 2026 (within the window Dec 12, 2025–Jan 11, 2026), focused on a security agreement/peace framework, confirmed by at least two (in fact, many) major international news outlets including Times of Israel and Al Jazeera, and confirmed by official U.S. State Department joint statement. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will Trump veto a bill in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump issues a presidential veto of any bill by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source will be official congressional records and a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Congress pass a bill to end the government shutdown and send it to President Trump's desk by November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. federal government has been shut down since October 1, 2025, after Congress failed to pass any of the 12 full-year appropriations bills or a stopgap continuing resolution before the fiscal year deadline. As of late October 2025, the shutdown is in its fifth week — the second-longest in U.S. history — with Democrats and Republicans deadlocked over the inclusion of healthcare provisions (such as ACA enhanced premium tax credits) and the scope of spending cuts. President Trump has blamed Democrats for the impasse, while Democrats have demanded that any funding bill address expiring health-insurance subsidies and roll back Medicaid cuts from the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act.' Prediction markets as of mid-October gave an 84% chance that no funding bill would pass before November 30, 2025 (https://news.yahoo.com/news/congress-won-t-pass-funding-150036498.html). The Senate requires 60 votes to advance most legislation, meaning at least 7 Democrats must join the 53 Republicans. The House's narrow GOP majority means near-unanimous Republican support is also needed. If Congress does pass a funding bill, it would be sent to the President, creating the first major opportunity for Trump to either sign or veto legislation in this Congress. Trump has expressed openness to a clean continuing resolution but has also signaled willingness to use the shutdown as leverage for deeper spending cuts.

Sources:
- ABC13: Senate to reconvene amid funding stalemate (Oct 27, 2025): https://abc13.com/post/government-shutdown-2025-senate-reconvene-monday-funding-stalemate/15617329/
- Yahoo/Polymarket: Congress won't pass funding bill until November (Oct 14, 2025): https://news.yahoo.com/news/congress-won-t-pass-funding-150036498.html
- Epoch Times: Government appears poised to shut down (Sept 30, 2025): https://www.theepochtimes.com/us/government-appears-poised-to-shut-down-amid-partisan-standoff-5765092
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), both chambers of Congress (the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate) pass a bill that funds the federal government (whether a continuing resolution, omnibus appropriations bill, or any other funding measure) and that bill is formally presented to the President for signature or veto. The bill must be enrolled and transmitted to the White House; mere passage by one chamber does not count. Resolution will be based on official congressional records available at https://www.congress.gov/ and corroborated by credible news reporting (e.g., AP, Reuters, NYT, Washington Post). If no such bill is presented to the President by 11:59 PM ET on November 30, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The government shutdown is the dominant legislative conflict in Congress right now. If Congress manages to pass a funding bill and send it to President Trump, it creates the most plausible scenario for a presidential veto in 2025 — Trump could veto the bill if it contains provisions he opposes (e.g., ACA subsidies, Medicaid rollbacks, or insufficient spending cuts). Conversely, if no bill reaches his desk, there is nothing for him to veto related to this issue. This subquestion tracks whether the legislative precondition for a veto materializes in November, serving as a key early indicator for whether Trump will veto any bill by year-end. It is distinct from the ultimate question because a bill reaching the President's desk could result in either a signature or a veto — but it is a necessary condition for the most likely veto scenario.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Both chambers of Congress (House and Senate) must pass a government funding bill, AND it must be formally presented/transmitted to the President between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive. Key entities: U.S. House of Representatives, U.S. Senate, President Trump. Threshold: enrolled bill transmitted to the White House. Timing: within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'government shutdown November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find status of shutdown and any funding bills; Query 2: 'federal government funding bill Congress Trump 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find any bill passed and presented to Trump; Query 3: 'House passed government funding bill November 12 2025 vote 222-209' — to confirm House vote; Query 4: 'Trump signed government funding bill November 13 2025 shutdown end' — to confirm signing.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: H.R. 5371 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026). Senate passed amended bill on November 11, 2025 (60-40 vote). House passed the bill on November 12-13, 2025 (222-209 vote). Trump signed on November 13, 2025 (~9:45 PM ET). No earlier qualifying events in the window (shutdown began Oct 1, 2025; prior Senate votes all failed).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Both chambers passed the bill: Senate passed H.R. 5371 on November 11, 2025 [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-house-passes-funding-measure-to-end-longest-ever-government-shutdown/3742523); House passed on November 13, 2025 with 222-209 vote [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/live-updates/government-shutdown-latest-house-vote-senate-deal-trump/); Bill transmitted to and signed by Trump on November 13, 2025 [AP News](https://apnews.com/4f04d5992fb5aecebfc892ed5599c468), [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-signs-government-funding-bill-ending-record-43-day-shutdown). All within the Oct 31–Nov 30 window. Bill is a continuing resolution/funding measure. Criteria exactly satisfied.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Senate passage: November 11, 2025 (60-40 vote). House passage: November 12-13, 2025 (222-209 vote, multiple sources indicate the vote occurred on the evening of Nov 12 ET or early Nov 13). Trump signed: November 13, 2025, approximately 9:45 PM ET (~2025-11-14T02:45:00Z). All timestamps within window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event exists within the window. All prior Senate votes on H.R. 5371 (14 failed votes before Nov 11) did not pass. The government shutdown began Oct 1, 2025. The November 11-13 sequence is the first and only qualifying occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality independent sources confirm the event: AP News, PBS NewsHour, CBS News, TIME, France 24, NDTV, Euronews, Washington Examiner, San Jose Mercury News, India Today, Business Standard. All consistently report Trump signed the bill on November 13, 2025, ending the 43-day shutdown. No contradictory evidence found. The bill (H.R. 5371) is explicitly identified as a government funding/continuing resolution bill.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves Yes. H.R. 5371 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026) passed the Senate on November 11, 2025 (60-40) and the House on November 12-13, 2025 (222-209), and was signed by President Trump on November 13, 2025. This is explicitly within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window, satisfying all resolution criteria.

question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch tool show a probability of 75% or higher for a 25-basis-point rate cut at the October 28–29, 2025 FOMC meeting as of October 27, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether the Fed will follow a Cut–Pause–Pause pattern across its next three FOMC meetings (October 28–29, December 9–10, and January 27–28). The first step in that sequence is a 25-basis-point cut at the October meeting. As of mid-September 2025, the CME FedWatch tool showed approximately 93% probability of a 25-bps cut at the October meeting (source: Coingape article from September 17, 2025). The current federal funds target range is 4.00%–4.25% after the September 17, 2025 cut. The CME FedWatch tool aggregates futures-market pricing to derive implied probabilities for each FOMC meeting outcome, and is widely used by economists and traders as a leading indicator of Fed action. If the probability of a cut at the October meeting remains very high on the eve of the meeting, this strongly suggests the first leg of the Cut–Pause–Pause pattern will materialize. Conversely, if market pricing shifts away from a cut (e.g., due to stronger-than-expected inflation data or labor market strength), it would reduce the likelihood of the Cut–Pause–Pause sequence.

- Coingape, 'FOMC Meeting: Fed Makes First Rate Cut of the Year' (Sept 17, 2025): https://coingape.com/fomc-meeting-fed-makes-first-rate-cut-of-the-year-lowers-rates-by-25-bps/

If the CME FedWatch tool is unavailable, the resolution may use the equivalent implied probability from 30-Day Federal Funds Futures contracts on CME as reported by a major financial news outlet (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC). If no reliable data is available by October 31, 2025, the question resolves ambiguously. The resolution window is between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31.

If the probability is high (≥75%), it strongly indicates the first leg of the pattern will materialize, which is a necessary condition for the ultimate question to resolve in favor of Cut–Pause–Pause. If the probability drops below 75%, it signals that economic data (inflation, jobs, tariff effects) released between now and late October have shifted expectations, making Cut–Pause–Pause less likely. question: Will TikTok be banned in 2025?
description:
On April 4, 2025, President Trump signed an executive order extending the delay of enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, which prohibits TikTok in the United States, until September 17, 2025 (see: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/06/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay/)

This market will resolve to "Yes" if a U.S. government ban that prohibits access or use of the TikTok app by the majority of Americans in the United States becomes legally enforceable for any amount of time between July 24, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

If Trump’s executive order delaying enforcement of the ban expires or is removed without TikTok coming into compliance with U.S. laws and regulations, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether enforcement action is taken by the U.S. government.

If TikTok is sold to another entity in such a way that it comes into compliance with U.S. laws and regulations this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will President Trump sign an executive order or take other official action to extend the TikTok enforcement deadline beyond September 17, 2025, before September 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act requires ByteDance to divest TikTok's U.S. operations or face a ban. The original deadline was January 19, 2025, but President Trump has issued three consecutive executive orders delaying enforcement — first on January 20, then in April, and most recently on June 18, 2025, extending the deadline to September 17, 2025 (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/06/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay/). As of late August 2025, no sale or divestiture deal has been finalized. On August 22, 2025, Trump publicly stated he was open to a fourth extension, saying 'we just extend a little bit longer' while buyers are being sought, though he noted a deal would require Chinese government approval that may not come in time (https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/22/us/politics/trump-tiktok-deadline-extension.html). The White House also launched an official TikTok account on August 19, 2025, further signaling that the administration is not preparing to enforce the ban imminently. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has said TikTok would 'go dark' if China did not approve a deal, suggesting the administration views the ban as a real possibility absent a deal but has shown repeated willingness to delay.

Sources:
- White House Executive Order (June 2025): https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/06/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay/
- Trump open to fourth extension (Aug 22, 2025): https://www.latestly.com/agency-news/world-news-us-extend-tiktok-ban-deadline-again-fourth-delay-6591508.html
- White House joins TikTok (Aug 20, 2025): https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/white-house-joins-tiktok-as-president-trumps-deadline-for-potential-ban-gets-closer/3388261
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-17 (inclusive), President Trump signs an executive order, presidential memorandum, or other official action that extends the enforcement deadline of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act beyond September 17, 2025. The action must be published on the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/) or announced via official federal government channels. If no such action is taken by 11:59 PM ET on September 17, 2025, this question resolves No. Note: a legislative act by Congress that delays enforcement would also count as Yes. If TikTok is sold or comes into compliance before September 17, rendering an extension moot, and no extension is issued, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This is the most critical near-term observable event for the ultimate question. If Trump extends the deadline again (a fourth time), TikTok will not be banned on September 17 and the ban becomes less likely for the remainder of 2025, since it establishes a strong pattern of repeated delays. If no extension is issued and no sale is completed, the ban could take effect, making the ultimate question much more likely to resolve Yes. Trump has publicly signaled openness to another extension, but the outcome is not certain — Congress may push back, a deal could materialize, or the administration could allow enforcement. This subquestion directly differentiates between the two main scenarios that drive the ultimate question's resolution.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: President Trump must sign an executive order, presidential memorandum, or other official action between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-17 (inclusive) that extends the TikTok enforcement deadline of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act beyond September 17, 2025. Key entities: President Trump, TikTok/ByteDance, White House, Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act. Threshold: deadline must be pushed beyond September 17, 2025. Timing: action must occur within window.

evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: President Trump signed an executive order titled 'Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Ban' on September 16, 2025, extending the enforcement deadline to December 16, 2025. This is reported by: Boston Globe, CNET, AP (via The Facts), Yahoo/Reuters, Hindustan Times, Social Media Today, Newser, A.V. Club, PCMag, Business Standard, Mainichi, News18, KTVH, Search Engine Land. No candidate events were rejected — all sources converge on September 16, 2025 as the signing date.

Sources include [Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/09/16/nation/trump-extends-tiktok-shutdown-deadline/), [CNET](https://www.cnet.com/news/social-media/trump-shifts-tiktok-deadline-again-skirting-a-ban-as-talks-drag-on/), [Social Media Today](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/trump-signs-fourth-executive-order-to-keep-tiktok-in-US/760325/), and [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-postpones-tiktok-ban-deadline-190742421.html). The Social Media Today article quotes the order text: 'The enforcement delay specified in section 2(a) of Executive Order 14166 of January 20, 2025 ... is further extended until December 16, 2025.'

evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event within the September 1–17 window. evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence found. evidence.step8_final_decision: President Trump signed an executive order titled 'Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Ban' on September 16, 2025 — within the resolution window of September 1–17, 2025. This order extends the TikTok enforcement deadline to December 16, 2025, which is beyond September 17, 2025. This directly satisfies all resolution criteria. Resolution: Yes. Resolution datetime: 2025-09-16T00:00:00Z (the signing date; exact time of signing not specified but confirmed as September 16, 2025).

subquestions.question: Will Canadian employment decline by 20,000 or more jobs in the January 2026 Labour Force Survey release (for the December 2025 reference month)?
subquestions.background_information:
The Bank of Canada's March 2026 rate decision will be heavily influenced by labour market conditions. At its December 10, 2025 meeting, the BoC held rates at 2.25% and indicated uncertainty about whether the next move would be a hike or a cut (https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/currency/CANADIAN-DOLLAR-US-DOLL-2392426/news/Bank-of-Canada-can-t-tell-if-next-rate-move-will-be-a-hike-or-a-cut-say-minutes-49345299/). A key factor in previous rate cuts was labour market weakness — Canada lost over 100,000 jobs in two months leading up to the September 2025 cut (https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/bank-of-canada-interest-rate-decision-sept-17-1.7320479), and the unemployment rate climbed to 7.1%. The October 2025 cut was also motivated by a soft labour market (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bank-canada-considered-waiting-longer-200000399.html). As of the most recent data, the Canadian unemployment rate stands near multi-year highs, and the BoC has signaled that employment is now the binding constraint rather than inflation (https://www.mpamag.com/ca/mortgage-industry/industry-trends/bank-of-canada-to-ease-further-as-fiscal-spending-picks-up-steam/524247). Statistics Canada publishes the Labour Force Survey monthly; the next release covering the December 2025 reference period is expected around January 10, 2026.

Sources:
- Market Screener: BoC December 2025 minutes: https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/currency/CANADIAN-DOLLAR-US-DOLL-2392426/news/Bank-of-Canada-can-t-tell-if-next-rate-move-will-be-a-hike-or-a-cut-say-minutes-49345299/
- CBC News: BoC September 2025 cut: https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/bank-of-canada-interest-rate-decision-sept-17-1.7320479

- Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/251206/dq251206a-eng.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey release covering the December 2025 reference month (expected around January 10, 2026) reports a net employment decline of 20,000 or more jobs compared to the previous month (November 2025). The resolution window is between 2025-12-24 and 2026-01-23. The primary resolution source is Statistics Canada's official Labour Force Survey release at https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/catalogue/71-001-X. If the release is delayed beyond 2026-01-23, this question resolves as ambiguous (N/A). The relevant figure is the month-over-month change in total employment (seasonally adjusted) as reported in the headline release.
subquestions.rationale: Labour market data is one of the most important inputs to the Bank of Canada's rate decisions. Significant job losses in December 2025 would strengthen the case for a 25 bps cut at the March 2026 meeting, as the BoC has explicitly cited employment weakness as a reason for past cuts. Conversely, stable or positive employment would support the BoC's view that the current 2.25% rate is 'about right' and reduce the probability of a March cut. This is a genuine leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question, and it captures a key crux on which forecasters who disagree about the March decision are likely to diverge.

The Q2 2025 data would cover April–June 2025 births. The CDC's VSRR Natality Dashboard (https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm) is the authoritative source. However, there is uncertainty about whether Q2 2025 data will be posted before the ultimate question's resolution deadline of September 19, 2025. Historically, VSRR provisional data appears with roughly a 2–4 month lag, meaning Q2 data (through June 2025) could plausibly appear in August or September 2025, but it is not guaranteed. If the data is not yet published, the ultimate question cannot resolve Yes (it would resolve No by default per the question's rules). Whether the data appears in time is therefore a key crux: if forecasters believe the data won't be published before September 19, the ultimate question trivially resolves No regardless of the underlying fertility trend.

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. federal government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025 last longer than 21 consecutive days?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 1, 2025, the U.S. federal government entered a partial shutdown after Congress failed to pass a funding bill before the fiscal year deadline. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) has announced it will 'suspend all operations' during the lapse, ceasing all data collection and publication activities. According to the Department of Labor's 73-page contingency plan, the BLS workforce would shrink from 2,055 employees to just 1 during a shutdown. Key economic releases at risk include the September jobs report (originally due October 3), the Consumer Price Index (October 15), the Producer Price Index (October 16), and JOLTS data.

The duration of the shutdown is a critical variable for whether BLS could miss three consecutive scheduled releases of any report — one of the triggers for the ultimate question's resolution. Historical shutdowns have varied in length: the 2018-19 shutdown lasted 34 days, the 2013 shutdown lasted 16 days, and the 1995-96 shutdown lasted 21 days. A shutdown exceeding 21 days would encompass multiple scheduled BLS release dates and increase the risk that the BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of at least one report series, potentially triggering resolution of the ultimate question.

President Trump was scheduled to meet with congressional leaders on September 29 to negotiate, but no deal was reached before the deadline. Senate Republicans rejected a House-passed short-term funding bill.

Sources:
- Fortune: https://fortune.com/2025/09/28/government-shutdown-jobs-report-fed-rate-cuts/
- FinanzNachrichten.de: https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2025-09/63876543-bureau-of-labor-statistics-to-cease-operations-if-govt-shuts-down.htm
- Fox Business: https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/partisan-standoff-threatens-crucial-economic-data-leaving-fed-families-dark
- UPI: https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/09/29/bls-jobs-report-government-shutdown/3451727618432/
- EconoTimes: https://www.econotimes.com/US-Government-Shutdown-Threatens-Release-of-Key-Economic-Data-1720345
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. federal government shutdown that began on or around October 1, 2025 continues without interruption for more than 21 consecutive calendar days — i.e., the government has not been funded and reopened by October 22, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. The resolution window is between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31.

If the government does not shut down (i.e., Congress passes funding before operations cease on October 1), this question resolves No.

If the government shuts down but reopens on or before October 22, 2025, this question resolves No.

If the government shuts down, briefly reopens (for less than 48 hours), and then shuts down again, the days are counted cumulatively toward the 21-day threshold.

Resolution sources: Official announcements from the Office of Management and Budget (https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/), reporting from major news outlets (Reuters, AP, Bloomberg), and the BLS release calendar (https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/). If there is ambiguity about the exact reopening time, credible reporting from at least two major news outlets will be used.
subquestions.rationale: The duration of the current government shutdown is the single most important near-term indicator for whether BLS will 'cease regular publication' of payroll data. The ultimate question resolves Yes if BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of any covered report without providing data within 30 days. BLS has confirmed it will suspend all operations during a shutdown. A shutdown lasting more than 21 days would span multiple scheduled release dates for jobs reports, CPI, PPI, and JOLTS, making it increasingly likely that three consecutive releases of at least one series are missed — directly threatening the ultimate question's Yes resolution. Conversely, a short shutdown (under 21 days) would likely result in only temporary delays followed by publication, which explicitly does not count as cessation under the ultimate question's criteria. This question thus serves as a meaningful early indicator: forecasters who believe the shutdown will be prolonged should assign higher probability to BLS ceasing publication, while those expecting a quick resolution should assign lower probability.

question: Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes be impeached 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the the Federal Senate (Senado Federal) votes to proceed with any impeachment of Minister of the Supreme Federal Court of Brazil Alexandre de Moraes by December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the results of the first such vote the Senate undertakes (e.g., if the Federal Senate decides to vote on the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes and it fails to pass, this market will resolve to "No").

This market will resolve to "Yes" as soon as the Senate successfully votes to proceed with this impeachment, regardless of the impeachment's outcome.

If it becomes impossible to impeach Alexandre de Moraes while he is in his role as Minister (e.g., he resigns) and the "Yes" condition has not yet been met, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the government of Brazil, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the President of the Brazilian Senate formally accept or initiate proceedings on any impeachment request against Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of August 2025, there have been approximately 30 impeachment requests filed against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, but none have advanced to a formal vote in the Brazilian Senate. The process requires the President of the Senate (currently Davi Alcolumbre) to accept and forward an impeachment request before any vote can take place. Senate President Alcolumbre has so far declined to advance impeachment proceedings against Moraes, despite mounting political pressure from right-wing parties.

On July 30, 2025, the U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned Moraes under the Global Magnitsky Act for alleged 'serious human rights abuses and arbitrary detentions' (https://home.treasury.gov/). Following the sanctions, five senators from the Liberal Party filed the 30th impeachment request against Moraes in early August 2025 (https://www.breitbart.com/latin-america/2025/08/07/brazil-tries-to-impeach-for-the-30th-time-judge-who-put-jair-bolsonaro-under-house-arrest/). Right-wing groups have planned mass protests for September 7, 2025 (Brazil's Independence Day) to demand Moraes' impeachment (https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/). A Quaest poll found 46% of Brazilians support impeaching Moraes while 43% oppose it.

The impeachment of a Supreme Court minister requires a two-thirds majority vote in the Senate (54 of 81 senators). However, the critical gateway is the Senate President's decision to formally accept and initiate proceedings on any of the filed requests.

Sources:
- Breitbart: https://www.breitbart.com/latin-america/2025/08/07/brazil-tries-to-impeach-for-the-30th-time-judge-who-put-jair-bolsonaro-under-house-arrest/
- NZ Herald: https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/
- U.S. Treasury sanctions announcement: https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases
- Devdiscourse: https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/politics/3299123-high-stakes-diplomacy-brazilian-judge-in-trumps-crosshairs
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), the President of the Brazilian Federal Senate (Senado Federal) formally accepts, forwards to a committee, or otherwise initiates official proceedings on any impeachment request against Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. This includes publishing an official dispatch (despacho), referring the request to the relevant Senate committee, or scheduling a formal session to consider the impeachment request. Mere filing of new impeachment requests by senators does NOT count — the Senate President must take affirmative procedural action to advance the process.

This question resolves No if no such action is taken by October 1, 2025.

Primary resolution sources will be official communications from the Brazilian Senate (https://www.senado.leg.br/), the Senate's official gazette (Diário do Senado Federal), and a consensus of credible Brazilian news outlets such as Folha de S.Paulo (https://www.folha.uol.com.br/), O Globo (https://oglobo.globo.com/), and G1 (https://g1.globo.com/).
subquestions.rationale: The Senate President's decision to formally accept and initiate impeachment proceedings is the essential procedural prerequisite for any impeachment vote. Without this step, no vote can occur and the ultimate question must resolve No. If the Senate President takes this action in September 2025, it would be a strong signal that impeachment proceedings will advance to a vote before year-end. Conversely, if September passes — a period of heightened pressure due to the September 7 protests and U.S. sanctions — without the Senate President acting, it significantly reduces the probability of an impeachment vote occurring by December 31, 2025. This subquestion tracks a distinct, observable procedural event rather than merely restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Brazilian Senate President Davi Alcolumbre must take formal affirmative procedural action (official dispatch/despacho, committee referral, or formal session scheduling) on an impeachment request against STF Justice Alexandre de Moraes between September 1 and October 1, 2025. Observable evidence: official Senate communications, Diário do Senado Federal entries, or credible Brazilian news reports documenting such an action. Key entities: Davi Alcolumbre (Senate President), Alexandre de Moraes (STF Justice/Minister), Brazilian Federal Senate. Threshold: Mere filing of new impeachment requests does NOT count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Brazilian Senate President impeachment Alexandre de Moraes 2025' (Sept-Oct window) — looking for Senate President actions; 2) 'impeachment Alexandre de Moraes Senado Federal setembro 2025' — Portuguese-language search for Senate proceedings; 3) 'Alcolumbre impeachment Moraes Senado despacho comissão setembro outubro 2025' — targeted search for formal dispatch or committee referral; 4) 'Brazil Senate 41 senators impeachment Moraes vote process accepted 2025' — seeking any Senate formal action; 5) 'Brazil senators impeach supreme court justice Moraes formal action Senate president accept reject' — disproof search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events found. The searches returned extensive coverage of: (a) the Bolsonaro trial (Sept 2-14), (b) US sanctions on Moraes, (c) the 'Banditry Bill' immunity debate and Senate rejection (Sept 24), (d) Alcolumbre's request to STF about deputies' seats (Sept 29). One article (Yahoo, Sept 1) noted that '41 senators have lined up to remove Moraes, but 54 votes are needed for impeachment' — indicating the political context but NO formal action. No article mentions Alcolumbre formally accepting, dispatching, referring to committee, or scheduling any session on any impeachment request against Moraes.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event matching the resolution criteria was found. The [Yahoo September 1 article](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/brazilian-judge-defying-trump-testing-100655004.html) confirms that while 41 senators had 'lined up' to remove Moraes, this is far short of the 54 needed, and no formal proceedings had been initiated. The [AFP September 24 article](https://afp.com/) shows Alcolumbre praised the Senate's courage in rejecting the immunity bill, indicating he was not an ally of anti-Moraes forces. The [atarde.com.br September 29 article](https://atarde.com.br/eleicoes/alcolumbre-faz-pedido-ao-stf-apos-lula-vetar-aumento-de-deputados-1362723) shows Alcolumbre's only formal STF-related action was about deputies' seat distribution, completely unrelated to impeachment. No evidence of any impeachment-related formal action by the Senate President against Moraes.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event was found; therefore no timestamp can be extracted for a Yes resolution. The window closed on October 1, 2025, without any formal action taken.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: N/A — no qualifying occurrence found within or outside the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification: (1) Multiple searches in both English and Portuguese found no Senate President action on Moraes impeachment. (2) Background context: 41 senators supportive of impeachment were still short of the 54 needed, making it politically unfeasible. (3) Alcolumbre's actions during the period were focused on other matters (immunity bill rejection, deputies' seats). (4) The STF itself was focused on the Bolsonaro trial, with Moraes serving as vice-president of the court from September 29 — making impeachment against him even less politically viable. (5) No contradictory evidence suggesting any formal action was taken was found in any source.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Despite 41 senators publicly supporting impeachment of Moraes (short of the 54 needed), and despite the heated political environment around the Bolsonaro trial and US sanctions, no evidence exists of the Brazilian Senate President taking any formal affirmative procedural action on any impeachment request against Moraes during the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window. The window closed on October 1, 2025, with no such action taken.

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the US conduct a qualifying aerial strike (drone, missile, or air strike) on a third distinct country's territory between January 13, 2026 and February 12, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of January 13, 2026, the US has already conducted qualifying strikes on at least two distinct countries' territories in 2026:

1. **Venezuela**: On January 3, 2026, the US launched Operation Absolute Resolve, involving over 150 aircraft including F-18s, F-35s, F-22s, B-1 bombers, and drones, conducting offensive strikes on Venezuelan government infrastructure and air defenses in Caracas (https://theintercept.com/2026/01/05/pentagon-official-on-venezuela-war/).

2. **Syria**: On January 10, 2026, the US conducted large-scale airstrikes across Syria targeting at least 35 Islamic State locations, involving approximately 20 aircraft and over 90 bombs and missiles (https://www.opindia.com/2026/01/us-airstrikes-hit-islamic-state-targets-across-syria-after-attack/).

For the ultimate question to resolve Yes at 'exactly 3 countries,' the US would need to strike exactly one more country (but not more). Historically, the US has conducted strikes in countries such as Yemen (against Houthi targets), Somalia (against al-Shabaab), Iraq, Libya, Pakistan, and Afghanistan. The US currently maintains counterterrorism operations in several regions, and the Trump administration has shown willingness to use force aggressively. The Council on Foreign Relations has warned of potential India-Pakistan conflict in 2026, and various global flashpoints remain active.

Sources:
- The Intercept, Pentagon Official on Venezuela War: https://theintercept.com/2026/01/05/pentagon-official-on-venezuela-war/
- OpIndia, US airstrikes hit Islamic State targets across Syria: https://www.opindia.com/2026/01/us-airstrikes-hit-islamic-state-targets-across-syria-after-attack/
- Next Big Future, USA Stealth Drones and Special Operations: https://www.nextbigfuture.com/2026/01/usa-stealth-drones-and-special-operations-give-military-domination.html
- India TV News, India-Pakistan conflict warning: https://www.indiatvnews.com/news/world/india-pakistan-likely-to-engage-in-conflict-in-2026-warns-us-think-tank-cites-terror-activities-2025-12-31-971057
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between January 13, 2026 and February 12, 2026 (inclusive), the United States conducts at least one qualifying aerial strike (defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles launched by US military forces that impact ground territory) on the soil of a country other than Venezuela and Syria — i.e., a third distinct country struck by the US in 2026. The strike must be officially acknowledged by the US government or confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., from Reuters, AP, BBC, or US Central Command press releases at https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/). Intercepted missiles or drones that do not impact ground territory do not count. Artillery, small arms, ground operations, cyberattacks, and naval shelling do not count. If no such strike on a third country occurs in this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the US will strike exactly 3 countries in 2026. As of January 13, 2026, the US has already struck two countries (Venezuela and Syria). Whether the US strikes a third country in the near term is the key crux: the US has ongoing counterterrorism operations in Yemen, Somalia, and Iraq where strikes are plausible but not certain. If a third country is struck by mid-February, forecasters would significantly update upward on the probability that 3+ countries will be struck by year-end. Conversely, if no third-country strike occurs in this window despite active global tensions, it may suggest restraint. This subquestion is a direct early indicator without merely restating the ultimate question, because it focuses on the marginal next strike rather than the total count, and the time window is much shorter.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the US to conduct at least one qualifying aerial strike (using aerial bombs, drones, or missiles by US military forces that impact ground territory) on any country other than Venezuela and Syria between January 13, 2026 and February 12, 2026 (inclusive). The strike must be officially acknowledged by the US government or confirmed by credible reporting. Venezuela and Syria are excluded as they were already struck by the US in 2026 before this window (Venezuela via Operation Absolute Resolve on Jan 3, 2026; Syria via ongoing CENTCOM operations). Somalia, Nigeria, Yemen, Iraq, and other countries would qualify as 'third distinct' countries.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US military airstrike drone strike 2026' (general, Jan 13-Feb 12 window) — to detect any US strikes in the window; 2) 'US airstrike Somalia Yemen Iraq January 2026' (specific countries, window) — found extensive Somalia strike reporting; 3) 'AFRICOM Somalia airstrike January 13 14 15 16 2026' (narrow date range) — confirmed Jan 13 strike in Somalia; 4) 'US airstrike Nigeria January February 2026' — found Nigeria strikes were Dec 25, 2025 (outside window), not in window; 5) 'CENTCOM US airstrikes Yemen Iraq January 2026' — found Syria strikes (inside window, but Syria excluded); 6) 'US Somalia bombing strike January 2026 list dates' — confirmed 25+ strikes throughout January 2026.
evidence.step3_event_detection: CANDIDATE EVENTS IDENTIFIED: (1) January 13, 2026 — US-supported airstrike in Jabad Godone, Middle Shabelle region, Somalia (AFRICOM + SNA + ATMIS joint operation) — ACCEPTED as qualifying event (aerial strike on Somalia's territory, AFRICOM confirmed, credibly reported). (2) Multiple US strikes in Somalia throughout January 2026 (23 total per AFRICOM as of Jan 27, 25 by end of January, 26 in total for January per Fox News) — ACCEPTED. (3) January 18, 2026 — US CENTCOM strike in Syria killing al-Qaeda leader Bilal Hassan al-Jasim (Operation Hawkeye Strike) — REJECTED as qualifying 'third country' because Syria is explicitly excluded from resolution. (4) February 3, 2026 — US Somalia airstrike in Puntland (27th of year) — ACCEPTED but not first. (5) Nigeria Christmas Day 2025 airstrikes — REJECTED as outside window (Dec 25, 2025). No new Nigeria airstrikes confirmed within window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The January 13, 2026 AFRICOM-supported airstrike in Jabad Godone, Somalia exactly satisfies all criteria: (a) It is an aerial strike using air power that impacted ground territory, killing 17 militants and destroying a compound — not an intercepted missile or naval/artillery fire; (b) It is officially supported/acknowledged by AFRICOM per [allAfrica](https://allafrica.com/stories/202601130172.html); (c) It occurred on January 13, 2026, the first day of the resolution window; (d) Somalia is neither Venezuela nor Syria — it is a 'third distinct country'; (e) It is confirmed by multiple credible sources. The resolution criteria is clearly met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The allAfrica article explicitly dates the operation to January 13, 2026 in the Jabad Godone area of Middle Shabelle region, Somalia. Fox News, IntelliNews, and Western Journal articles published January 14, 2026 all reference a wave of Somalia strikes culminating in the January 12 strike (just before the window) and continuing after. The allAfrica source specifically reports a January 13, 2026 date with AFRICOM involvement, placing it exactly on the first day of the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question asks whether a qualifying strike on a 'third distinct country' (not Venezuela or Syria) occurred in the window. The January 13, 2026 Somalia strike is on the very first day of the window. There is no evidence of an earlier event within the Jan 13–Feb 12 window since this IS the first day. Pre-window strikes (Jan 12, Jan 11, Jan 9 in Somalia; Dec 25 Nigeria) fall outside the window. Therefore, January 13 is the first qualifying occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: (1) No evidence that the allAfrica January 13 Somalia report is inaccurate — multiple other sources confirm a high pace of US Somalia strikes in January 2026; (2) The question's exclusion of Venezuela and Syria is clear — Somalia is neither; (3) The Jan 13 allAfrica report explicitly names AFRICOM as a supporting entity, satisfying the requirement for US government acknowledgment; (4) The strike used aerial assets ('targeted airstrike') that impacted ground territory (destroyed a compound, killed militants) — not a missile intercept or ground/naval operation; (5) The strike is within the Jan 13–Feb 12 window (it's the first day). No contradictory evidence found. This is a highly confident Yes resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The US conducted a qualifying aerial strike on Somalia on January 13, 2026 — the first day of the resolution window. Somalia is a third distinct country (not Venezuela or Syria). The strike was officially supported by AFRICOM and confirmed by multiple credible sources. The resolution criteria is met. Resolution: Yes, with resolution_datetime of 2026-01-13T00:00:00Z (the strike occurred on January 13, 2026, though exact sub-day time is not specified, the date is firm).

question: Will Trump try to fire another Fed Governor by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump publicly and unequivocally announces that he is removing another Fed Governor before their term is up, or takes formal action toward doing so, such as issuing a directive or formal request between August 25 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue a ruling that permits President Trump to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 25, 2025, President Trump announced the firing of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, citing alleged mortgage fraud as 'cause' for removal. Cook has refused to resign and filed a lawsuit challenging the removal in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., before Judge Jia Cobb. A hearing on whether to block the removal was scheduled for August 30, 2025. The legal question centers on whether the Federal Reserve Act's 'for cause' removal provision (Section 10) permits a president to dismiss a Fed governor based on conduct alleged to have occurred before the governor's Senate confirmation, and whether such conduct constitutes the statutory grounds of 'inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance in office.' In May 2025, the Supreme Court issued an order distinguishing the Fed as a unique institution with a 'distinct historical tradition' of independence, suggesting Fed governors may have stronger removal protections than officials at other agencies. If the court blocks Cook's removal, Trump's ability to secure a 4-3 majority on the Fed Board is stalled, making it less likely he would attempt to fire another governor (since the legal avenue would appear closed). Conversely, if a court permits the removal, it establishes precedent that could embolden further dismissals.

Sources:
- CNN: 'We just jumped into the unknown: Inside Trump's attempt to put his mark on the Fed' (Aug 28, 2025) https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/politics/trump-fed-lisa-cook/index.html
- Yahoo Finance: 'Trump's firing of Fed Governor Cook could be blocked by US judge' (Aug 29, 2025) https://www.yahoo.com/finance/news/trumps-firing-fed-governor-cook-blocked-judge/
- The Straits Times: 'Trump fires Lisa Cook, escalating his war on the Federal Reserve' (Aug 27, 2025) https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/trump-fires-lisa-cook-escalating-his-war-on-the-federal-reserve
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive), a U.S. federal court (district court, appeals court, or the Supreme Court) issues a ruling, order, or decision that permits President Trump's removal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook to proceed — meaning no injunction or restraining order blocking the removal is in effect as of the ruling, OR a previously issued injunction blocking the removal is vacated or overturned. The question resolves No if, as of 2025-09-30, a court order blocking Cook's removal remains in effect, or if no court has ruled to permit the removal. Resolution will be based on official court filings available through PACER (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/) or the court's public docket, supplemented by credible reporting from major news outlets such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), or Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/). If the lawsuit is withdrawn or dismissed (e.g., because Cook resigns), the question resolves Yes, since no court order would be blocking the removal. If no ruling has been issued by September 30, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The outcome of the Lisa Cook litigation is a critical leading indicator for whether Trump will attempt to fire another Fed governor. If courts uphold Trump's authority to remove a Fed governor for cause, it substantially lowers the legal and political barriers to firing additional governors, making a second firing attempt much more likely before October 31. If courts block the removal, Trump faces a clear legal obstacle that would likely deter additional firing attempts. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question would likely update significantly upon learning the court outcome — one of the strongest cruxes for this prediction.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question resolves Yes if, between Sept 1-30, 2025, a federal court issues a ruling PERMITTING Trump's removal of Lisa Cook — meaning either no injunction blocking removal is in effect, OR a previously issued injunction is vacated/overturned. It resolves No if, as of Sept 30, a court order blocking Cook's removal remains in effect, OR no court has ruled to permit removal. Key entities: Lisa Cook, Fed Board Governor; Judge Jia Cobb (D.C. District); D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals; U.S. Supreme Court. Threshold: court order permitting removal vs. injunction blocking it.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'federal court ruling Lisa Cook Federal Reserve removal Trump' (Sept 1-30) — to find any court rulings permitting removal. Query 2: 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve Governor Trump fire removal lawsuit' (July 1 - Sept 30) — to get full legal history. Query 3: 'Supreme Court Lisa Cook Federal Reserve ruling September 2025' (Sept 1-30) — to find any Supreme Court action. Query 4: 'Trump Lisa Cook appeals court injunction vacated overturned September 2025' — to check for vacated injunctions. Query 5: 'Supreme Court Lisa Cook Federal Reserve emergency stay granted denied' (Sept 20-30). Query 6: 'Supreme Court Lisa Cook decision ruled stay granted allowed fired removal' (Sept 22-30). Query 7: 'Supreme Court Lisa Cook Federal Reserve stay decision September 29 30 2025' (Sept 27-30).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key events identified: (1) Sept 9-10: District Judge Jia Cobb issued preliminary injunction BLOCKING Trump from removing Cook [Cryptopolitan, Independent]. (2) Sept 15-16: D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals 2-1 denied Trump's emergency request to stay/overturn the injunction [Business Insider, Investopedia, Daily Caller, Adnkronos]. (3) Sept 18: Trump administration filed emergency petition to U.S. Supreme Court [AP, Florida Politics, The Hill]. (4) Sept 25: Cook filed opposition brief to Supreme Court [TribLive, Yahoo/CNA]. (5) Sept 25-26: Former Fed chairs Greenspan, Bernanke, Yellen filed amicus briefs supporting Cook [Jackson Hole News & Guide]. (6) Sept 27-29: Multiple reports indicate Supreme Court is 'poised to decide' but has NOT yet ruled [CNBC, Mint, JD Supra, Morningstar]. NO candidate event found where a court permitted the removal or vacated the injunction during the resolution window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All identified court rulings went AGAINST permitting Cook's removal: [District Court - blocked removal](https://www.cryptopolitan.com/judge-blocks-trump-from-firing-lisa-cook/), [D.C. Circuit - upheld injunction blocking removal](https://www.investopedia.com/appeals-court-blocks-trump-s-effort-to-immediately-remove-fed-governor-lisa-cook-11810690), [AP report on Supreme Court petition](https://apnews.com/article/supreme-court-trump-lisa-cook-federal-reserve-d7cd7bf7b8bca591b1748591836c3645). The Supreme Court had NOT ruled by September 30, 2025, according to multiple articles from September 27-29 indicating the case was still pending before the Court. The injunction blocking Cook's removal remained in effect throughout the resolution window. No ruling permitting the removal was issued.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The most recent articles up to September 29-30, 2025 (JD Supra Sept 29, Morningstar Sept 29, Investopedia Sept 29, Yahoo Finance Sept 28, CNBC Sept 27) all confirm the Supreme Court had not yet ruled and that the injunction blocking Cook's removal remained in effect. The Supreme Court was described as 'poised to decide' — indicating no ruling had been issued by the end of the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: N/A — no qualifying event (court ruling permitting removal) was found within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory check: The Daily Caller article from Sept 16 mentions 'The court granted a temporary stay of a Sept. 9 injunction' citing due process grounds — but examining other sources more carefully, the D.C. Circuit actually denied the administration's emergency request and upheld the injunction blocking removal. The Daily Caller article appears to be inaccurately characterizing the ruling, as all other sources unanimously confirm the D.C. Circuit upheld Cook's protection. Additionally, the Sept 22 Supreme Court FTC ruling is about a different official (Rebecca Slaughter at FTC), not Lisa Cook. No Supreme Court ruling on Lisa Cook/Fed was found by September 30, 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: As of September 30, 2025, the preliminary injunction issued by Judge Jia Cobb on September 9-10, 2025, blocking Trump from removing Lisa Cook, remained in full effect. The D.C. Circuit upheld that injunction on September 15-16, 2025. The Trump administration's emergency petition to the Supreme Court, filed September 18, 2025, had not been decided by the Supreme Court as of September 30, 2025. No court issued a ruling permitting Cook's removal during the resolution window. Therefore, the question resolves No.

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that lowers, pauses, delays, or removes any tariffs on imports from Canada by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. and Canada announce the start of formal bilateral trade negotiations (or a new trade framework/deal) between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late October 2025, U.S.-Canada trade relations remain strained. President Trump raised tariffs on Canadian goods not covered by CUSMA to 35% in August 2025 (https://www.wtae.com/article/trump-tariffs-canada-countries-delayed/63492181), and eliminated the de minimis exemption for all imports effective August 29, 2025 (https://www.globalnews.ca/news/11045678/duty-free-shipping-us-ends-friday-canadian-businesses/). Canada has removed retaliatory tariffs on CUSMA-covered goods but maintains steel, aluminum, and auto tariffs. Unlike with Mexico, where Trump agreed to a 90-day negotiating period in August 2025, no equivalent formal negotiation framework has been publicly announced with Canada. The ultimate question asks whether Trump will lower, pause, delay, or remove tariffs specifically targeting Canada by December 31, 2025. A formal announcement of bilateral trade negotiations or a new trade deal framework would be a strong leading indicator that tariff relief is imminent, as such negotiations typically precede any executive action on tariff reduction. Conversely, the absence of any formal negotiation track in November would suggest that the status quo of elevated tariffs is likely to persist through year-end.

Sources:
- Pittsburgh's Action News 4, "New tariffs on Canada take effect Friday; Dozens of other countries delayed" (2025-08-01): https://www.wtae.com/article/trump-tariffs-canada-countries-delayed/63492181
- Global News, "Duty-free shipping to U.S. ends Friday. Canadian businesses are 'fearful'" (2025-08-27): https://www.globalnews.ca/news/11045678/duty-free-shipping-us-ends-friday-canadian-businesses/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. government (via the White House, USTR, State Department, or President Trump) and the Canadian government (via the Prime Minister's Office, Foreign Affairs Ministry, or Trade Ministry) jointly or separately announce the commencement of formal bilateral trade negotiations, a new trade deal or framework agreement, or a formal negotiating period aimed at resolving tariff disputes between the two countries. The announcement must be confirmed by at least two major credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, CBC, Globe and Mail, Wall Street Journal, New York Times) or by official government press releases from either the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or the Prime Minister of Canada's office (https://www.pm.gc.ca/). Informal or background-level discussions, or statements of willingness to negotiate without a concrete announcement, do not qualify. Trump's pattern has been to use tariffs as leverage and then negotiate reductions (as seen with the 90-day negotiating period offered to Mexico in August 2025). If formal negotiations are announced in November, it significantly increases the probability that Trump will lower tariffs on Canada before December 31. If no negotiations materialize by the end of November, the two-month window remaining would be very tight for any tariff relief to occur, making it a strong negative indicator. This question thus serves as a meaningful early signal that distinguishes between scenarios where tariff relief is plausible versus unlikely.

subquestions.question: Will Cracker Barrel's board of directors announce any significant leadership or governance changes (e.g., new board members, committee restructuring, or executive departures other than the CEO) between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Cracker Barrel has been under intense pressure throughout 2025 following a botched logo redesign and broader rebranding effort led by CEO Julie Felss Masino. The company reverted to its original logo in August 2025 and suspended its remodel program in September 2025. In early October 2025, Cracker Barrel ended its relationship with Prophet, the consultancy behind the rebrand, and announced organizational changes to 'streamline leadership' and support field operations (https://www.nrn.com/quick-service/cracker-barrel-ends-relationship-design-company). Activist investor Sardar Biglari has waged a long-running campaign against Cracker Barrel's management, having launched seven proxy solicitations in 14 years and securing a board seat in 2022 under a standstill agreement that expired in October 2024. After the standstill expired, Biglari released a 7-page open letter attacking the board's strategic transformation plan (https://www.foxbusiness.com/lifestyle/cracker-barrel-hits-back-self-interested-steak-n-shake-ceos-poor-leadership-after-online-attacks). Public calls for Masino's resignation have been widespread, with conservative influencers, customers, and even former President Trump weighing in (https://www.newsweek.com/cracker-barrel-ceo-pressure-resign-logo-1948340). At a late October 2025 investor summit, Masino publicly defended the logo change as a visibility improvement rather than an ideological decision (https://thehill.com/blogs/in-the-know/5057191-cracker-barrel-ceo-explains-reason-for-attempt-to-change-logo/). Cracker Barrel's fiscal year Q1 2026 earnings report is typically released in November, which often serves as a catalyst for governance changes.

Sources:
- Nation's Restaurant News: https://www.nrn.com/quick-service/cracker-barrel-ends-relationship-design-company
- Fox Business: https://www.foxbusiness.com/lifestyle/cracker-barrel-hits-back-self-interested-steak-n-shake-ceos-poor-leadership-after-online-attacks
- Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/cracker-barrel-ceo-pressure-resign-logo-1948340
- The Hill: https://thehill.com/blogs/in-the-know/5057191-cracker-barrel-ceo-explains-reason-for-attempt-to-change-logo/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive), Cracker Barrel Old Country Store Inc. announces any of the following through official SEC filings (8-K, DEF 14A, or proxy statements), press releases, or confirmed credible reporting: (1) the appointment or departure of one or more members of the board of directors; (2) the departure of any C-suite executive other than the CEO (e.g., CFO, COO, CMO); or (3) any formal restructuring of board committees. Routine operational hires below the C-suite level do not count. The primary resolution sources will be Cracker Barrel's SEC filings available at https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001067294&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40 and official press releases at https://investor.crackerbarrel.com/. A consensus of credible reporting (e.g., Reuters, Wall Street Journal, Nation's Restaurant News) will serve as a fallback source. If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM ET on November 30, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Board and senior leadership changes at Cracker Barrel are a strong leading indicator of whether the CEO herself will be ousted. Companies under activist investor pressure and public backlash typically see governance changes—board reshuffles, executive departures, committee restructurings—before or simultaneously with a CEO departure. Cracker Barrel already announced organizational streamlining in early October 2025 and ended its consultancy relationship. If additional leadership changes occur in November (especially around an earnings report), it would signal escalating internal pressure that makes a CEO departure by year-end significantly more likely. Conversely, if the board holds steady, it suggests the company is rallying behind Masino through the holiday season. This subquestion captures an observable, distinct event that is different from the ultimate question but highly informative about its outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025, Cracker Barrel announces (1) appointment or departure of board member(s), OR (2) departure of C-suite executive other than CEO, OR (3) formal restructuring of board committees — via SEC filings, press releases, or credible reporting. Key entity: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store Inc. (CBRL). Timing: Oct 31, 2025 00:00:00Z to Nov 30, 2025 23:59:59Z.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Cracker Barrel board of directors leadership changes 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find board-level announcements. evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: YES. Gilbert Dávila's resignation from Cracker Barrel's board of directors on November 20, 2025 — explicitly within the October 31–November 30, 2025 resolution window — directly satisfies criterion (1) of the resolution criteria ('the appointment or departure of one or more members of the board of directors'). The event is explicitly stated by multiple high-quality sources including Fox Business, New York Post, The Independent, GuruFocus (official press release text), and Yahoo Finance. The board was reduced from 10 to 9 members. This is unambiguously a qualifying governance change announced via press release and followed up in SEC Form 8-K filing. No inference is required.

subquestions.question: Will Bitcoin's price fall below $75,000 at any point between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
MicroStrategy's mNAV (market-cap-to-net-asset-value ratio) is fundamentally driven by two factors: the price of MSTR stock and the value of Bitcoin held on its balance sheet. As of late September 2025, Bitcoin trades around $63,000–$65,000 (per recent market data), and MSTR's mNAV sits at approximately 1.5×. Strategy holds roughly 638,460 BTC with an average purchase price of ~$73,880 per BTC (per a September 8, 2025 SEC filing). For mNAV to reach 1.00, MSTR's market capitalization would need to fall to equal the net value of its Bitcoin holdings minus liabilities. A sharp Bitcoin price decline is the most direct mechanism that could collapse mNAV toward 1.0, because it simultaneously reduces the value of the underlying asset while also pressuring MSTR's stock price (which historically trades at a premium or discount to BTC). If Bitcoin drops below $75,000 — roughly a 15–20% decline from recent levels — this would significantly erode the value of Strategy's holdings and likely cause MSTR stock to decline proportionally or more, compressing mNAV. Conversely, if Bitcoin remains above $75,000, it becomes much harder for mNAV to reach 1.00 by year-end.

A drop below $75,000 would bring BTC close to or below Strategy's average cost basis (~$73,880), dramatically increasing the probability that mNAV compresses to 1.0 or below. subquestions.background_information:

question: Half-Life 3 released in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Half-Life 3 or a differently titled game continuing the Half-Life series is officially released in the US by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, "release" refers to the game becoming publicly available for purchase or download in the US. Early access, beta versions, other forms of pre-release availability, or leaks will not count as an official release. If the release is only for certain consoles (e.g. Xbox Series X/S) it will count.

The resolution source will be official information from Valve Corporation.

subquestions.question: Will Valve officially announce Half-Life 3 (or a new mainline Half-Life game) between November 10, 2025 and December 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Multiple credible insiders and fan analyses suggest Valve may be on the verge of announcing Half-Life 3. Tyler McVicker, a well-known Valve insider and host of the HLX Files podcast, has claimed that Half-Life 3's development is complete and that a trailer is in production, with Valve reportedly planning to release the announcement and the game in close succession (https://www.gamereactor.eu/half-life-3-trailer-is-reportedly-in-the-works/). Fan speculation has centered on November 18, 2025, as a potential announcement date, based on analysis of Steam's top banner scheduling showing an unusual gap between November 18 and December 8, coinciding with the anniversary of Half-Life: Alyx's announcement on November 18, 2019 (https://www.eurogamer.net/half-life-fans-believe-theyve-worked-out-a-possible-announcement-date-for-half-life-3-and-its-very-very-soon). Valve also moved its annual Autumn Sale from November to September 2025, which some interpret as clearing space for a major reveal (https://www.screenrant.com/half-life-3-reveal-imminent-steam-schedule/). The Game Awards, scheduled for December 11, 2025, has also been cited as a likely venue for a full trailer (https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/half-life-3-fans-figured-out-when-game-revealed/). Despite this mounting speculation, Valve has remained officially silent, with no confirmed leaks, datamines, or teasers. As of November 10, 2025, there has been no official announcement from Valve regarding Half-Life 3.

Sources:
- Eurogamer: https://www.eurogamer.net/half-life-fans-believe-theyve-worked-out-a-possible-announcement-date-for-half-life-3-and-its-very-very-soon
