- Comicbook: https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/half-life-3-fans-figured-out-when-game-revealed/
- GamingBible: https://www.gamingbible.com/news/half-life-3-could-be-announced-this-month-mark-your-calendars-961526-20251109
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between November 10, 2025 and December 10, 2025 (inclusive), Valve Corporation makes an official public announcement — via its own website (https://www.valvesoftware.com), the Steam store (https://store.steampowered.com), official Valve social media accounts, or an official appearance at a public event such as The Game Awards — confirming the existence and forthcoming release of a new mainline Half-Life game (titled 'Half-Life 3' or otherwise). An 'official announcement' means a public communication from Valve that explicitly names the game and confirms it is in development or coming soon; leaked materials, unofficial rumors, or insider claims do not count. If no such official announcement is made by 11:59 PM UTC on December 10, 2025, this question resolves No. Resolution sources: Valve's official website (https://www.valvesoftware.com), Steam store page (https://store.steampowered.com), and Valve's official social media channels.
subquestions.rationale: An official announcement is a necessary precursor to a 2025 release. If Valve intends to release Half-Life 3 by December 31, 2025, they would almost certainly need to announce it by early December at the latest, given that even a 'shadow drop' requires a public reveal. Insider reports suggest Valve plans to release the game close to its announcement. Therefore, whether an official announcement occurs in this window is a strong leading indicator: if no announcement materializes by December 10, a 2025 release becomes extremely unlikely. Conversely, an announcement in this window would dramatically increase the probability of a 2025 release. This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question because it asks about announcement rather than release, and because an announcement could occur without a same-year release.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Valve Corporation makes an official public announcement between 2025-11-10 and 2025-12-10 (inclusive) explicitly naming and confirming a new mainline Half-Life game, via its official website, Steam store, official social media, or at a public event like The Game Awards. Observable evidence: an article or official source explicitly reporting Valve announced the game. Key timing: window ends December 10, 2025; The Game Awards is December 11, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Valve Half-Life 3 official announcement 2025' (Nov 10–Dec 10) — to find any official Valve announcement. 2) 'Half-Life 3 announced Steam store page' (Nov 10–Dec 10) — to find a Steam store listing. 3) 'Half-Life 3 Game Awards December 11 2025 reveal announcement' (Dec 9–10) — to check if any pre-announcement or early reveal occurred. 4) 'Valve Half-Life new game official announcement December 2025' (Dec 1–10) — broad December search. 5) 'Valve Half-Life 3 HLX officially announced confirmed' (Nov 10–Dec 10) — exhaustive search for confirmed announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Valve's Nov 12 Steam hardware announcement (Steam Machine, Steam Frame, Steam Controller) — no Half-Life 3 announcement made. (2) Various insider/leaker claims (GabeFollower, Tyler McVicker, Mike Straw) suggesting imminent announcement — these are unofficial rumors, not official Valve announcements. (3) Unlisted game on Valve's Steam developer page — speculation only, no official naming. (4) Drew Gottlieb cryptic social media post — not an official game announcement. (5) The Game Awards scheduled December 11 — outside resolution window; articles from December 9 still treat HL3 reveal as speculative/future event. All candidate events rejected as they do not satisfy the resolution criteria of an official Valve announcement explicitly naming a new mainline Half-Life game.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple authoritative sources explicitly state no official announcement was made: [dsogaming.com](https://www.dsogaming.com/news/in-case-youre-wondering-valve-hasnt-announced-half-life-3-yet/) (Nov 12: 'Valve Hasn't Announced Half-Life 3 Yet'); [pcgamer.com](https://www.pcgamer.com/games/fps/sorry-pc-gamers-valve-isnt-announcing-half-life-3-today/) (Nov 12: 'Valve isn't announcing Half-Life 3 today'); [kotaku.com](https://kotaku.com/the-steam-machine-is-the-perfect-time-to-launch-half-life-3-2000644102) (Nov 13: 'Valve has not officially announced Half-Life 3'); [howtogeek.com](https://www.howtogeek.com/are-the-steam-machines-specs-a-sign-that-half-life-3-is-almost-here/) (Dec 4: 'no official announcement has been made as of December 4, 2025'); [gamerant.com](https://gamerant.com/half-life-3-rumors-game-awards-reveal-when-bad/) (Dec 9: cautioning 'very real chance that the talk about Half-Life 3 is merely speculation'). Articles from Dec 9 still discuss The Game Awards (Dec 11) as the next potential venue — confirming nothing happened before Dec 10.

The most recent articles (December 9, 2025) still describe the situation as pending, with The Game Awards on December 11 being the next anticipated opportunity.

evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No article contradicts the finding that Valve made no official announcement. The pattern across all articles (Nov 10 through Dec 9) is consistent: extensive speculation and rumors exist, but all sources explicitly state no official Valve confirmation. The December 9 articles still treat a Half-Life 3 announcement as a future event contingent on The Game Awards (Dec 11), which is outside the resolution window. No conflicting evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No official Valve announcement of a new mainline Half-Life game was made between November 10 and December 10, 2025. Every article found within the window explicitly states Valve has not officially confirmed Half-Life 3 or any new mainline Half-Life game. The most likely venue for such an announcement (The Game Awards, December 11, 2025) falls outside the resolution window. The window closed at December 10, 2025, 23:59:59 UTC with no qualifying event occurring. Resolution: No.

question: Will Trump publicly disparage Netanyahu by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump makes any public statement in which he insults, mocks, or attacks Benjamin Netanyahu personally or professionally in a clearly negative manner by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will Israel announce or carry out a major military operation (e.g., large-scale airstrike campaign, ground incursion, or strike on a foreign country) that is publicly opposed or criticized by the Trump administration between October 25 and November 24, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Trump-Netanyahu relationship has been tested repeatedly in 2025 by Israeli military actions that embarrassed or contradicted U.S. diplomatic efforts. In September 2025, Israel struck targets in Qatar during sensitive negotiations, which Haaretz described as Netanyahu making 'a mockery of Trump' (https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2025-09-16/ty-article/.premium/netanyahu-made-a-mockery-of-trump-in-qatar-and-paid-no-price-for-it/0000019). In a TIME interview published October 24, 2025, Trump claimed 'I stopped Netanyahu' from continuing the war in Gaza and said the Israeli strike on Hamas negotiators in Doha was 'a tactical mistake' (https://www.donaldjtrump.com). A May 2025 call between Trump and Netanyahu revealed 'sharp disagreements over Iran strategy,' with Trump favoring diplomacy and Netanyahu pushing for more aggressive action (https://www.worthynews.com/82849-trump-netanyahu-call-reportedly-marked-by-sharp-disagreements-over-iran-strategy). JD Vance condemned a far-right Israeli annexation bill as 'a very stupid political stunt' during a visit to Israel on October 24, 2025. The pattern shows that Israeli unilateral military actions that undercut Trump's diplomatic posture are a key trigger for rising tensions between the two leaders. A significant Israeli military escalation that publicly embarrasses Trump would substantially increase the likelihood that Trump disparages Netanyahu personally.

Sources:
- Haaretz: Netanyahu made a mockery of Trump in Qatar: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2025-09-16/ty-article/.premium/netanyahu-made-a-mockery-of-trump-in-qatar-and-paid-no-price-for-it/0000019
- Worthy Christian News: Trump-Netanyahu sharp disagreements: https://www.worthynews.com/82849-trump-netanyahu-call-reportedly-marked-by-sharp-disagreements-over-iran-strategy
- TIME interview with Trump (Oct 24, 2025): Referenced via https://time.com and Trump official site https://www.donaldjtrump.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 25, 2025 and November 24, 2025 (inclusive), Israel announces or carries out a major military operation — defined as a large-scale airstrike campaign (more than a single targeted strike), a ground incursion into new territory, or a military strike on a foreign country's sovereign territory — AND a senior Trump administration official (President Trump, Vice President Vance, Secretary of State, Secretary of Defense, or National Security Advisor) publicly criticizes, opposes, or expresses displeasure with the operation in an on-the-record statement, press briefing, interview, or social media post. Resolution will be based on credible reporting from major outlets including Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com), The Washington Post (https://www.washingtonpost.com), or Times of Israel (https://www.timesofisrael.com). Both the Israeli military action and the U.S. administration's public criticism must occur within the resolution window. If either element is absent, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Trump's public disparagement of Netanyahu is most likely to be triggered by a specific Israeli action that embarrasses Trump or undermines his diplomatic achievements. The 2025 track record shows that Israeli military escalations (like the Qatar strike) create friction, but Trump has so far stopped short of personal attacks on Netanyahu. A new Israeli military operation publicly opposed by the Trump administration would be a strong leading indicator that the relationship is deteriorating toward the kind of personal rhetorical attack the ultimate question asks about. If no such friction-generating event occurs in the next month, it significantly reduces the probability of a public disparagement by year-end. Conversely, if such an event does occur, it raises the probability substantially, since Trump has shown a pattern of escalating rhetoric when he feels personally embarrassed by allies.

evidence.step1_decompose: Requires: (1) Israeli major military operation (large-scale airstrike campaign, ground incursion into new territory, or strike on foreign country) between Oct 25–Nov 24, 2025; AND (2) senior Trump official (Trump, Vance, Rubio, Hegseth, NSA) publicly criticizes/opposes that specific operation in an on-record statement. Both must occur in the same window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: Israeli military operations Oct–Nov 2025; Trump administration criticism of Israel military Nov 2025; Vance 'stupid political stunt'; US condemns Israel Lebanon strikes Nov 2025; Rubio Hegseth oppose Israel strikes; Trump response Beirut strike Nov 23 2025; US reaction refugee camp strike.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple qualifying Israeli military operations found: (1) Oct 30: ground incursion into Blida, south Lebanon; (2) Nov 6: large-scale airstrike campaign on multiple towns in south Lebanon; (3) Nov 11-12: ground incursions into Syria's Quneitra region; (4) Nov 18-19: airstrike on Ein el-Hilweh Palestinian refugee camp killing 13 people; (5) Nov 22-23: large-scale Gaza strikes killing 20+ and Beirut airstrike killing Hezbollah chief of staff. For criticism element: Vance called West Bank annexation vote 'stupid political stunt'—but this was about a parliamentary vote, not a military operation. Trump defended Israel strikes in Gaza (Oct 29). Rubio affirmed Israel's right to strike. US official expressed approval of Beirut strike with 'Yalla, mazal tov, mabruk.' No criticism of military operations found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Israeli military operations clearly satisfy the definition. However, no senior Trump official (Trump, Vance, Rubio, Hegseth, NSA) publicly criticized any Israeli military operation during the window. Vance's 'stupid political stunt' remark [yalibnan.com, Oct 25] was about a Knesset annexation vote, not a military operation. Rubio defended Israel's right to strike [AP, Oct 29]. Trump said Israel 'should hit back.' US official expressed approval of Nov 23 Beirut strike [worthynews.com]. Rubio's 'some concern' about settler violence [Times of Israel, Nov 12] was not about a military operation and fell short of opposition/criticism threshold. No evidence found of on-record opposition to any qualifying military operation from any listed senior official.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Not applicable for Yes resolution. For No: the window closed Nov 24, 2025, with no qualifying criticism of a military operation found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Searched specifically for any earlier qualifying criticism within the window. None found. The only substantial Trump admin pushback on Israeli actions during the window concerned the West Bank annexation vote (a political/legislative act, not a military operation).
evidence.step7_verification: Checked from multiple angles: Trump admin response to Lebanon strikes (supportive/neutral), response to Gaza strikes (Trump defended Israel, Rubio affirmed right to strike), response to Beirut strike Nov 23 (US official expressed approval). The pattern is consistent: Trump admin supported Israeli military operations while occasionally pushing back on political moves like annexation. No contradictory evidence found suggesting any senior official opposed a specific military operation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: While multiple qualifying Israeli military operations occurred during the window (Lebanon strikes, Syria incursions, refugee camp strike, Beirut strike), no senior Trump administration official publicly criticized, opposed, or expressed displeasure with any of these military operations during the resolution window. The Vance 'stupid political stunt' comment was about a parliamentary annexation vote, not a military operation. Resolution: No.

question: Will Russia enter Toretske by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Toretske by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of Toretske is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will the ISW map show Russian forces having advanced into or within 2 km of Toretsk's administrative boundaries between November 28 and December 21, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Toretsk (also known as Toretske or formerly Dzerzhynsk) is a city in the Donetsk Oblast of Ukraine with a pre-war population of roughly 32,000. It has been on the front line of fighting in the Donbas for much of the 2022–2025 war. As of late November 2025, Russian forces have been conducting offensive operations in the broader Toretsk direction for months. ISW daily assessments have regularly noted Russian attacks in and around Toretsk, with Russian forces making incremental advances in the city's outskirts and surrounding settlements such as Shcherbynivka, Nelipivka, and Pivnichne (which is administratively part of Toretsk). According to ISW's interactive map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375), as of late November 2025, Russian forces have been assessed to have infiltrated or gained control of portions of the eastern and southeastern approaches to Toretsk proper. DeepState Map (https://deepstatemap.live/) similarly shows Russian positions in close proximity to or partially within Toretsk's boundaries. The pace of Russian advances has been slow but persistent, characterized by small infantry assaults, drone strikes, and artillery bombardment. Whether Russian forces can convert these peripheral gains into actual control of territory within the city of Toretsk itself before year-end is the core question at stake.

Sources:
- ISW Interactive Ukraine Map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
- DeepState Map: https://deepstatemap.live/
- ISW daily assessments (example): https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-november-27-2025
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between November 28, 2025 (start_date) and December 21, 2025 (end_date), the ISW interactive map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) shows any new Russian advance — depicted as 'Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine,' 'Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours,' 'Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine,' or 'Assessed Russian Control' — into territory that is within the built-up urban area of Toretsk city itself (not merely surrounding villages like Shcherbynivka, Nelipivka, or other settlements outside Toretsk's contiguous urban footprint), AND this shading persists through at least the next full ISW daily update cycle. If the ISW map becomes unavailable, DeepState Map (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used as a fallback. The question resolves No if no such advance is depicted on the ISW map (or fallback source) during the resolution window. For clarity, advances into Pivnichne (which is administratively part of Toretsk municipality but geographically separate from the main Toretsk urban area) count only if the ISW map labels them as within Toretsk proper.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion tracks whether Russian forces are making meaningful progress toward entering the urban core of Toretsk in the weeks leading up to the December 31 deadline. If by December 21, Russian forces have already advanced into or very near Toretsk's built-up area on the ISW map, it would be a strong leading indicator that the ultimate question resolves Yes. Conversely, if no such advance is observed by December 21, it becomes much less likely (though not impossible) that Russia would capture territory within Toretsk in the remaining 10 days. This is a genuine crux because forecasters who disagree about the December 31 outcome likely disagree about the near-term pace of Russian advances — this subquestion directly measures that pace. It differs from the ultimate question because it asks about any advance toward or into Toretsk's urban footprint over a shorter window, rather than the specific resolution criteria of captured territory by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: ISW map must show new Russian advance (any of the four categories) into Toretsk city's built-up urban area (not surrounding villages like Shcherbynivka, Nelipivka, etc.) between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-21, persisting through at least one full ISW update cycle. Observable evidence: explicit ISW assessment showing shaded territory inside Toretsk city proper OR news articles citing such ISW depiction. Key entities: Toretsk city (Donetsk Oblast), ISW map, Russian Assessed Advances.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'ISW Toretsk Russian advance December 2025' — to find explicit ISW reporting on Toretsk. 2) 'Toretsk battle frontline Russian forces urban area 2025' — to find battle reports inside Toretsk. 3) 'ISW Toretsk map Russian control December 2025 urban' — to find ISW map assessments. 4) 'Toretsk Kostiantynivka front fighting November December 2025' — to find Kostiantynivka front reports mentioning Toretsk. 5) 'Toretsk Pivnichne ISW Russian advance December 2025' — to find Pivnichne advances. 6) 'Toretsk ISW assessment territory control November December 2025' — broader ISW Toretsk assessments. 7) 'Toretsk Russian forces fighting streets urban December 2025' — urban combat. 8) 'Toretsk Donetsk Russian forces battle 2025 Shcherbynivka' — surrounding villages. 9) 'Kostiantynivka front ISW Russian advance December 2025' — broader front reporting. 10) 'Toretsk Russian control city proper map December 2025' — map-specific search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Found: (1) December 4 Ukrinform article about 'Toretsk axis/front' — mentions defensive actions but no advance into city proper. (2) November 29 article mentioning challenges 'similar to Toretsk and Chasovy Yar' — historical reference only. (3) Multiple articles on Kostiantynivka front attacks near Shcherbynivka, Oleksandro-Shultyne, Pleshchiivka — these are surrounding villages, not Toretsk urban area. (4) Meduza December 12 article mentions 'small part of southern Kostiantynivka' under Russian attack — but this is Kostiantynivka, not Toretsk. (5) December 12 mention of Russian 'tightening encirclement of Kostiantynivka.' No article explicitly stated Russian forces advanced into Toretsk's built-up urban area per ISW map during the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the found articles explicitly confirms ISW map depiction of Russian advances into Toretsk city proper during November 28 – December 21, 2025. Fighting reports on the 'Kostiantynivka front' (which administratively includes Toretsk's district) consistently name surrounding villages (Shcherbynivka, Pleshchiivka, Oleksandro-Shultyne, Kleban-Byk, Rusyn Yar, Ivanopillia, Yablunivka, Sofiivka) but not Toretsk's urban core. The December 4 'Toretsk axis' article describes defensive actions, not Russian capture of urban territory. No articles explicitly cite ISW showing advances into Toretsk proper during the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. No article within the window explicitly states Russian forces advanced into Toretsk city's built-up area per ISW assessment.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: Ukrainian General Staff reports consistently list Kostiantynivka front attacks at surrounding villages, not Toretsk urban proper. Meduza December 12 mentions encirclement of Kostiantynivka (different city). One article notes Russian forces 'contesting Konstantinovka' (Putin December 19 RT article) but again refers to Kostiantynivka, not Toretsk specifically. The broader context shows the Toretsk battle was a long-running conflict with Russian forces already partially inside some areas — but no new advance into the urban area per ISW is explicitly reported during the window. The absence of specific ISW reporting on Toretsk during this period, combined with consistent reports showing attacks on surrounding villages rather than the city center, supports a No resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying event explicitly found within the resolution window. All available reporting on the Kostiantynivka/Toretsk front during November 28 – December 21, 2025 describes fighting at surrounding villages (Shcherbynivka, Pleshchiivka, etc.) and does not explicitly confirm ISW map showing new Russian advances into Toretsk's built-up urban area. The resolution window closes at December 21, 2025 with no qualifying event confirmed.

question: Will Elon and DOGE cut 100-150k employees in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve based on the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) under the "All Employees, Federal" series (CES9091000001), displayed here (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001)

This market will resolve according to the decrease in the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees between the December 2024 report and the December 2025 report.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The difference will be calculated as the December 2024 value minus the December 2025 value.

The December 2024 figure will be based on the initial December 2024 BLS Employment Situation report scheduled for release on January 3, 2025, and the initial December 2025 figure will be based on the report scheduled for release on January 9, 2026. Revisions made to these figures will not be considered, only the values reported in the initial reports will be used.

The resolution source will be the BLS Employment Situation data, specifically the series CES9091000001, available at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 or the official BLS website.

subquestions.question: Will the BLS report that seasonally adjusted federal employment (CES9091000001) for any month in 2025 released by December 16, 2025, show a level at or below 2,780,000?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether DOGE-driven federal workforce reductions will result in 100,000–150,000 fewer federal employees by December 2025 compared to December 2024. The December 2024 initial BLS report (released January 10, 2025) showed federal employment at approximately 2,997,000 on a seasonally adjusted basis (CES9091000001). A drop to 2,780,000 or below would represent a reduction of roughly 217,000—well beyond the 150,000 upper bracket—while staying above 2,780,000 would indicate a more moderate decline.

Due to the federal government shutdown, the BLS did not release employment reports for September and October 2025. As of late November 2025, the most recent official BLS employment data covers August 2025. The BLS has rescheduled the November 2025 Employment Situation report (which covers October data) to December 16, 2025, and is expected to release catch-up data for missed months around the same time. Revelio Labs' alternative data for October 2025 showed government employment declining by 22,200 jobs in that month alone, suggesting continued federal workforce reductions.

Elon Musk's DOGE initiative has been driving federal employee reductions through buyouts, layoffs, and agency restructuring throughout 2025. The pace of these reductions is a key indicator of whether the 100,000–150,000 cut target will be met by December 2025.

Sources:
- FRED CES9091000001 series: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001
- TalkMarkets on BLS delays and government shutdown: https://talkmarkets.com/content/us-markets/u-s-nonfarm-employment-drops-in-october-2025?post=453215

subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question hinges on the December 2025 federal employment level compared to December 2024. Since the December 2025 BLS data won't be released until January 9, 2026, we need an earlier indicator. If any BLS data released in December 2025 already shows federal employment at or below 2,780,000, it would strongly suggest the trajectory is toward exceeding the 150,000 cut threshold. This question captures the pace and magnitude of federal workforce reductions as revealed by official data becoming available after the BLS reporting delays, providing a concrete mid-trajectory indicator for the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Any BLS Employment Situation release published between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30 must report a seasonally adjusted 'All Employees, Federal' (CES9091000001) value at or below 2,780,000 for any reference month in 2025. Observable evidence: BLS report released in this window containing the specific CES9091000001 series value ≤ 2,780,000. Key entities: BLS Employment Situation report; series CES9091000001; threshold 2,780,000. Only initial reported values count (not revisions).
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'BLS Employment Situation report federal employment December 2025' — to find what reports were released in the window. evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: BLS released a combined October/November Employment Situation report on December 16, 2025 (within the resolution window of Nov 30 - Dec 30, 2025). This report covered both October 2025 payroll data (first release) and full November 2025 data. Multiple sources (Daily Caller, Conservative Daily News, New York Post citing FRED, PYMNTS.com, Cryptopolitan, HotAir, Breitbart) all report that federal employment fell by 162,000 in October and 6,000 in November, with the November level at 2,744,000 — its lowest since December 2014. The total decline from January 2025 peak of ~3,015,000 was 271,000, putting November at 2,744,000. Working backwards: October = 2,744,000 + 6,000 = 2,750,000, and September ≈ 2,750,000 + 162,000 = 2,912,000. Both October and November 2025 federal employment levels were below 2,780,000.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: EXACT MATCH confirmed. The BLS Employment Situation report was published on December 16, 2025 [Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2025/12/16/trump-federal-workforce-cuts-jobs/), [Conservative Daily News](https://conservativedailynews.com/2025/12/trump-cuts-federal-workforce-back-to-obama-levels/), [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/personnel/2025/federal-government-employment-dropped-in-october-as-doge-cuts-took-effect/). The October 2025 value, also initial release, was approximately 2,750,000 (= 2,744,000 + 6,000), also ≤ 2,780,000. evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The BLS Employment Situation release was published on December 16, 2025. Multiple sources published on that date confirm this: Daily Caller (2025-12-16), Conservative Daily News (2025-12-17, reporting on the Dec 16 release), PYMNTS (2025-12-16), NBC News (2025-12-16), Business Times (2025-12-16). Exact UTC timestamp: 2025-12-16T08:30:00Z is typical for BLS releases (8:30 AM ET = 13:30 UTC), but the precise time is not explicitly stated in any article. The date December 16, 2025 is confirmed. Using the end of that publication day as the resolution timestamp: 2025-12-16T13:30:00Z (standard BLS release time).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This was the FIRST BLS Employment Situation release in the window (Nov 30 - Dec 30, 2025) containing CES9091000001 data. Earlier reports were not published in this window — the BLS could not release October data during the shutdown (which ended November 12). The December 16 release was specifically delayed from December 5 due to the shutdown's data collection disruption. No earlier Employment Situation release in the window is found. Multiple independent sources (Daily Caller, Conservative Daily News, New York Post/Elon Musk post, Breitbart, Cryptopolitan) all cite the 2,744,000 November level from FRED/BLS. The resolution criteria require the 'initial reported value' — this IS the initial reported value for November 2025 (December 16 release). question: Pakistan strike on India by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Pakistan initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Indian territory by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Pakistani military forces that impact Indian territory (e.g., if a Pakistani missile or drone hits a target within India’s borders, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted before reaching Indian territory, as well as surface-to-air missile strikes, will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether debris lands on Indian soil or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or any operation conducted by Pakistani ground forces will not qualify as a strike under this market.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will India or Pakistan formally withdraw from or suspend the May 2025 ceasefire agreement between October 15, 2025 and November 14, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Following the India-Pakistan military escalation in May 2025 — triggered by the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack and India's retaliatory Operation Sindoor — the two countries agreed to halt all military operations on land, air, and sea effective from the evening of May 10, 2025. During the conflict, Pakistan launched 'Operation Bunyan Ul Marsoos,' targeting 26 locations across Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan, and Gujarat with drones, missiles, and artillery. India retaliated with BrahMos cruise missiles and ballistic missiles striking Pakistani air bases including Chaklala (Nur Khan), Sargodha, Jacobabad, and others. The ceasefire was fragile from the start — Pakistani drones were detected and intercepted over Indian territory hours after the agreement took effect, and India accused Pakistan of violating the ceasefire (NDTV, May 17, 2025: https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/india-has-launched-missiles-pak-pm-shehbaz-sharif-recounts-230-am-asim-munir-call-8347291). As of October 2025, the ceasefire has broadly held, but tensions remain elevated with both sides maintaining heightened military readiness along the Line of Control and international border. Any formal withdrawal from or suspension of the ceasefire would be a strong precursor to renewed strikes.

Sources:
- NDTV, 'India Has Launched Missiles: Pak PM Shehbaz Sharif Recounts 2:30 AM Asim Munir Call' (May 17, 2025): https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/india-has-launched-missiles-pak-pm-shehbaz-sharif-recounts-230-am-asim-munir-call-8347291
- NDTV, 'Less Than 50 Weapons Fired By IAF To End Conflict' (Aug 30, 2025): https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/less-than-50-weapons-fired-by-iaf-to-end-conflict-op-sindoor-exclusive-8674521
- India Today, 'Pak's Fatah-1 rocket debris fished out of Srinagar's Dal Lake' (Sep 22, 2025): https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/paks-fatah-1-rocket-debris-fished-out-of-srinagars-dal-lake-2737891-2025-09-22
- News18, 'Battle Escalates, India Retaliates' (May 10, 2025): https://www.news18.com/india/battle-escalates-india-retaliates-3-pakistani-airbases-hit-overnight-missile-fired-at-delhi-shot-down-ws-live-blog-9372123.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 15, 2025 and November 14, 2025 (inclusive), either India or Pakistan officially announces the withdrawal from, suspension of, or termination of the ceasefire agreement reached on May 10, 2025. An official announcement means a public statement by the head of state, head of government, foreign ministry, or military spokesperson of either country explicitly declaring that the ceasefire is no longer in effect or that the country is withdrawing from the agreement. The announcement must be reported by at least two of the following credible sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), BBC (https://www.bbc.com), NDTV (https://www.ndtv.com), or Dawn (https://www.dawn.com). Mere accusations of ceasefire violations, without a formal declaration of withdrawal or suspension, do not count. If no such formal announcement is made by November 14, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A Pakistani strike on Indian territory by December 31, 2025 would almost certainly require the collapse of the May 2025 ceasefire agreement. The ceasefire is the primary mechanism preventing renewed hostilities. If either side formally withdraws from or suspends the ceasefire in the October-November timeframe, this would be a critical leading indicator that the risk of a Pakistani strike on India before year-end has dramatically increased. Conversely, if the ceasefire remains formally intact through mid-November, it substantially reduces (though does not eliminate) the probability of a strike by December 31. This subquestion captures a necessary precondition for renewed strikes rather than simply asking about the strike itself with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official announcement by head of state, head of government, foreign ministry, or military spokesperson of India or Pakistan explicitly declaring that the May 10, 2025 ceasefire is no longer in effect or that the country is withdrawing from the agreement, between Oct 15–Nov 14, 2025, reported by at least two of: Reuters, AP, BBC, NDTV, or Dawn.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'India Pakistan ceasefire withdrawal suspension October November 2025' — to find formal withdrawal announcements; 2) 'India Pakistan May 2025 ceasefire agreement status' — to check ceasefire status; 3) 'India Pakistan ceasefire terminated suspended withdrawn formal announcement' — looking for formal declarations; 4) 'India Pakistan May 10 2025 ceasefire formally ended terminated declaration' — targeted search for termination; 5) 'India Pakistan ceasefire violation withdrawal DGMO Operation Sindoor 2.0' — looking for military-level announcements; 6) 'India Pakistan war resumed hostilities November 2025' — to find if conflict resumed.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Indian Defense Minister Rajnath Singh stated on Nov 7, 2025, that Operation Sindoor is 'paused not finished' — REJECTED because this is rhetorical statement about military preparedness, not a formal declaration of ceasefire withdrawal; (2) Pakistan PM Sharif thanked Trump for the May 2025 ceasefire on Nov 8-9, 2025 — shows ceasefire is still referenced as active; (3) Pakistan ISPR warned India against 'provocative propaganda' on Oct 15, 2025 — not a ceasefire withdrawal; (4) Delhi car bombing Nov 10, 2025 and Islamabad bombing Nov 12, 2025 — these are terrorist incidents, not formal ceasefire withdrawals; (5) India conducting large-scale military exercises (Trishul, Oct 30–Nov 10) — military exercises, not ceasefire withdrawal; (6) Afghanistan-Pakistan ceasefire negotiations collapse — about a different ceasefire between different countries.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that matches the resolution criteria. The May 10, 2025 India-Pakistan ceasefire was still being referenced as in effect throughout the window: Pakistan PM Sharif publicly praised Trump for securing it as recently as Nov 8-9, 2025 [Outlook India](https://www.outlookindia.com/international/pm-sharif-once-again-thanks-us-president-trump), [The New Indian Express](https://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2025/Nov/09/pakistan-pm-shehbaz-sharif-thanks-trump-again-for-mediating-indo-pak-ceasefire). India's 'paused not finished' language from Defense Minister Rajnath Singh [MoneyControl](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/india/rajnath-singh-says-operation-sindoor-paused-not-finished-pakistan-begged-for-ceasefire-13660811.html) does not constitute a formal withdrawal from the ceasefire — it refers to military readiness for future operations if needed, not a declaration that the ceasefire is terminated. The Trishul exercise near the Pakistan border [Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/sir-creek-a-new-live-frontier-emerges-in-india-pakistan-tensions-amid-indian-tri-service-combat-exercise-trishul/articleshow/124869502.cms) and anti-infiltration operations at LoC [TOI](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/army-kills-2-on-loc-amid-jk-police-crackdown-on-terrorist-support-systems/articleshow/125190316.cms) are not formal ceasefire withdrawals.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found. Cannot extract a timestamp for an event that did not occur.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence: Pakistan PM Sharif publicly thanking Trump for the ceasefire as late as Nov 8-9, 2025 confirms the ceasefire was not formally terminated. India allowing Sikh pilgrims through Wagah on Nov 4-5, 2025 [The Independent](https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/south-asia/pakistan-sikh-pilgrims-guru-nanak-wagah-b2858794.html) further shows the ceasefire between India and Pakistan remained nominally in place. The Eurasian Times op-ed about 'Operation Sindoor 2.0' is opinion, not a formal government declaration. Al Jazeera's Nov 12 article about Delhi and Islamabad blasts refers to ongoing tensions but confirms no formal ceasefire termination has been declared.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No formal withdrawal from or suspension of the India-Pakistan May 10, 2025 ceasefire was made by either country during October 15–November 14, 2025. While there was heightened rhetoric, military exercises, ongoing low-level tensions, and border incidents, none of these constituted an official announcement by head of state, head of government, foreign ministry, or military spokesperson explicitly declaring the ceasefire terminated. The question resolves No, with the window closing without the specified event occurring.

question: Clarity Act signed into law in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R.3633) is passed by both chambers of the U.S. Congress and signed into law by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source is Congress.gov’s legislation tracker (https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633) and other official information from the government of the United States, however other credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Senate Banking Committee hold a markup or vote on digital asset market structure legislation (the CLARITY Act or a Senate counterpart such as the RFIA) between September 1 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633) passed the U.S. House of Representatives on July 17, 2025, with a bipartisan 294-134 vote. The bill is now in the Senate, where it must pass through both the Senate Banking Committee and the Senate Agriculture Committee before reaching the full Senate floor. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) stated at the SALT Wyoming Blockchain Symposium on August 20, 2025, that she hopes the Senate Banking Committee will move on the bill in September, followed by the Senate Agriculture Committee in October, with a goal of reaching President Trump's desk before Thanksgiving. As of late August 2025, Polymarket bettors gave the CLARITY Act only a 35% chance of being signed into law by year-end, down from 87% on July 17. The Senate Banking Committee has also released a discussion draft of the Responsible Financial Innovation Act (RFIA), a potential Senate counterpart to the CLARITY Act, with a Request for Information deadline of August 5, 2025. Whether the Senate Banking Committee acts on this legislation in September is a critical near-term milestone for the bill's chances of becoming law in 2025.

Sources:
- Polymarket odds and Lummis timeline: https://cryptonews.com/news/clarity-act-has-35-chance-of-passing-in-2025-polymarket/
- House passage of CLARITY Act: https://www.timesnownews.com/business-economy/economy/house-passes-crypto-clarity-act-with-bipartisan-294-134-senate-next-article-152449994
- Senate RFIA discussion draft and Banking Committee RFI: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/the-future-of-u-s-crypto-regulation-1083055/
- CLARITY Act status on Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633
- Blockchain and Digital Assets News July 2025: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/blockchain-and-digital-assets-news-and-2068592/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs holds a formal committee markup session or committee vote on (a) the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633), (b) a Senate companion or counterpart bill addressing digital asset market structure regulation (such as the RFIA or any successor/amended version), or (c) any legislative vehicle that substantially incorporates the CLARITY Act's provisions. Evidence must come from the Senate Banking Committee's official website (https://www.banking.senate.gov/), Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/), or credible mainstream news sources reporting on the committee action. A hearing alone (without a markup or vote) does not count. If the committee schedules a markup but postpones it to after September 30, 2025, the question resolves No. If no relevant committee action is announced or reported by these sources by October 5, 2025 (allowing a few days for reporting lag), the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Senator Lummis explicitly stated a goal of moving the bill through the Senate Banking Committee in September 2025. If the committee fails to act on digital asset market structure legislation in September, it significantly compresses the remaining timeline for Senate committee markups, floor votes in both the Banking and Agriculture committees, full Senate passage, conference reconciliation with the House bill, and presidential signature — all before December 31, 2025. A September Banking Committee markup is the single most important near-term milestone. Its occurrence (or non-occurrence) would substantially update forecasters' estimates of whether the CLARITY Act can be signed into law in 2025. If the committee does not act in September, the Thanksgiving deadline Lummis mentioned becomes very difficult to meet, and year-end passage becomes unlikely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs holds a formal committee markup session OR committee vote on digital asset market structure legislation (CLARITY Act/RFIA/successor) between September 1–30, 2025. Observable evidence: official Senate Banking Committee announcement of markup/vote, or credible news reporting on such an event occurring. Key entities: Senate Banking Committee, RFIA 2025, Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633), Chairman Tim Scott.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Senate Banking Committee markup digital asset market structure CLARITY Act September 2025' — to find direct reports of markup/vote in September. Query 2: 'Senate Banking Committee RFIA digital asset legislation vote markup 2025' — to find any vote/markup events. Query 3: 'Senate Banking Committee markup vote September 30 2025 crypto digital asset RFIA postponed delayed' — to find evidence of postponement. Query 4: 'Senate Banking Committee Tim Scott crypto markup October 2025 postponed delayed' — to confirm delay to October.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Sept 5 and Sept 8 releases of updated RFIA discussion drafts — rejected, not markup/vote. (2) Sept 17 Senate Banking Committee roundtable — rejected, roundtable is not a markup. (3) Tim Scott stated goal of Sept 30 markup — this is a stated intention, not an actual event. (4) Cryptonews.com (Sept 22) reports 'aides now suggest a possible delay to the week of October 20.' (5) CoinDesk (Sept 30) explicitly states 'The Senate Banking Committee postponed a markup on market structure draft legislation to October.' No actual markup or vote in September window found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: CoinDesk article from September 30, 2025 explicitly states: 'The Senate Banking Committee postponed a markup on market structure draft legislation to October.' [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/09/30/bitcoin-steady-but-bitfinex-warns-of-downside-risks-as-government-shutdown-looms). Cryptonews.com (Sept 22) confirms 'Scott set a September 30 deadline for markup, but aides now suggest a possible delay to the week of October 20.' [Cryptonews](https://cryptonews.com/news/democrats-back-bipartisan-crypto-market-structure-bill-as-senate-vote-looms/). JD Supra (Oct 3): 'Chairman Tim Scott expressed hope that the bill would advance out of the committee by the end of September 2025, but bipartisan skepticism among senators suggests this timeline is uncertain.' No source reports an actual markup or vote occurring within September 1–30.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The CoinDesk article from September 30, 2025 provides explicit confirmation of postponement to October. The JD Supra article published October 3, 2025 also confirms no markup happened in September. No markup or vote occurred in the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying markup or vote event was found in the September 1–30 window. The markup was definitively postponed to October, as confirmed by CoinDesk (published 2025-09-30).
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources consistently confirm: (1) Chairman Scott targeted Sept 30 for markup but it did not happen; (2) aides confirmed possible delay to Oct 20 by Sept 22; (3) CoinDesk on Sept 30 explicitly confirms postponement to October; (4) Senator Kennedy warned committee was 'not ready' as of Sept 10. No source reports a markup or vote occurring in September. The roundtable on Sept 17 is explicitly not a markup. The RFIA discussion draft releases are not markups. Evidence is consistent across multiple independent sources.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Senate Banking Committee explicitly postponed its markup of digital asset market structure legislation to October, as confirmed by CoinDesk on September 30, 2025 and corroborated by cryptonews.com (Sept 22) and JD Supra (Oct 3). No markup or vote occurred within the September 1–30, 2025 window. Resolution is definitively No. The earliest definitive No moment is September 30, 2025, when CoinDesk explicitly reported the postponement to October.

subquestions.question: Will MrBeast's YouTube subscriber count reach 450 million by October 12, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson) became the first YouTuber to surpass 400 million subscribers on June 1, 2025 (https://hypebeast.com/2025/6/mrbeast-first-youtuber-surpass-400-million-subscribers). As of early September 2025, his channel had approximately 430-431 million subscribers, based on multiple reports from that period (https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/09/36682890/mrbeast-could-be-the-next-celebrity-to-turn-a-phone-into-a-fortune). At the time he hit 400 million, his channel was growing at an average rate of roughly 350,000 subscribers per day. From 400 million on June 1 to approximately 430 million by September 3 is about 94 days, implying roughly 319,000 subscribers per day over that period. If this rate continues, he would gain roughly 9.6 million subscribers in the 30 days between September 12 and October 12, potentially reaching approximately 440-441 million. Reaching 450 million by October 12 would require a faster growth rate of about 667,000 per day (assuming he starts at ~430 million), which would be roughly double his recent pace. This subquestion is relevant because the ultimate question asks whether MrBeast will hit 500 million subscribers before December 31, 2025. His trajectory over the next month is a key indicator of whether the 500 million milestone is feasible within the timeframe.

Sources:
- HYPEBEAST: MrBeast Makes History as First-Ever YouTuber To Surpass 400 Million Subscribers: https://hypebeast.com/2025/6/mrbeast-first-youtuber-surpass-400-million-subscribers
- Benzinga: MrBeast Could Be The Next Celebrity To Turn A Phone Into A Fortune: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/09/36682890/mrbeast-could-be-the-next-celebrity-to-turn-a-phone-into-a-fortune
- Social Blade (MrBeast channel statistics): https://socialblade.com/youtube/user/mrbeast6000
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if MrBeast's main YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCX6OQ3DkcsbYNE6H8uQQuVA) reaches 450,000,000 (450 million) or more subscribers at any point between 2025-09-12 and 2025-10-12 (inclusive), as reported by Social Blade (https://socialblade.com/youtube/user/mrbeast6000) or the channel's publicly displayed subscriber count on YouTube. If Social Blade is unavailable, the publicly displayed subscriber count on the YouTube channel page on October 12, 2025 may be used as a fallback. If the subscriber count reaches 450 million at any point during the resolution window and is later reduced (e.g., due to YouTube purging inactive accounts), it still counts as having been reached. The question resolves No if the subscriber count does not reach 450 million at any point during this window.
subquestions.rationale: One of the three conditions that would cause the ultimate question to resolve 'No' is MrBeast hitting 500 million subscribers by December 31, 2025. Tracking whether MrBeast reaches 450 million by mid-October provides a meaningful early indicator of his subscriber growth trajectory. If he reaches 450 million by October 12, that means he's gaining subscribers at a pace that makes 500 million by year-end plausible (needing ~50 million more in ~80 days, or ~625K/day). If he doesn't reach 450 million, it suggests his growth rate is slower and 500 million becomes much less likely. This is a genuinely different observable event (an intermediate milestone) rather than simply the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, and it directly informs the probability of one of the three triggering conditions.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: MrBeast's main YouTube channel must reach exactly 450,000,000 (450 million) or more subscribers at any point between 2025-09-12T00:00:00Z and 2025-10-12T23:59:59Z inclusive. Observable evidence: explicit reporting of ≥450M subscribers on Social Blade or YouTube channel page within the window. Key threshold: 450 million. Key entity: MrBeast main channel (UCX6OQ3DkcsbYNE6H8uQQuVA).
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'MrBeast YouTube subscriber count 450 million 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) — to find any reports of 450M milestone. subquestions.question: Will a Russian drone breach the airspace of a NATO member state (other than Romania) between November 30 and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Since September 2025, Russian drones have repeatedly violated NATO airspace, particularly along the alliance's eastern flank. Poland experienced a swarm of ~20 Russian drones entering its airspace on September 10, prompting NATO to shoot some down — the first direct NATO-Russia kinetic confrontation since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Romania has experienced at least 13 airspace breaches, including a record-deep incursion on November 25, 2025, when a drone penetrated over 100 km inland. Estonia saw a suspected Russian drone shot down near a U.S. military base on October 17. Denmark, Belgium, Germany, Lithuania, and other NATO states have also reported drone sightings near airports and military installations. The pattern has been escalating, with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen characterizing it as 'hybrid warfare.' Romania has been the most frequent target due to its 650 km border with Ukraine and proximity to Russian drone flight paths targeting Ukrainian Danube ports, but breaches in other NATO states (Poland, Estonia, the Baltics) would be particularly significant because they could trigger different national shoot-down policies and escalatory dynamics. As of late November 2025, NATO nations are actively developing a 'drone wall' and deploying new counter-UAS capabilities along eastern borders.

Sources:
- AP, 'Mysterious drone flights in NATO airspace have caused alarm across Europe,' November 5, 2025: https://apnews.com/article/europe-drones-nato-russia-ukraine
- News18, 'Nato Jets Scrambled As Russian Drones Breach Romanian Airspace For The 13th Time,' November 25, 2025: https://www.news18.com/world/nato-jets-scrambled-as-russian-drones-breach-romanian-airspace-for-the-13th-time-ws-live-9179420.html
- The National Interest, 'Suspected Russian Drone Shot Down Near Estonian Military Base,' October 31, 2025: https://nationalinterest.org/blog/buzz/suspected-russian-drone-shot-down-near-estonian-military-base
- CNN, 'Poland scrambles jets after Russian drone reports,' September 9, 2025: https://edition.cnn.com/2025/09/09/europe/poland-scramble-jets-russian-drone-reports-intl-hnk-ml
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between November 30, 2025, and December 29, 2025 (inclusive), credible reporting (from at least two major international news outlets such as Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, or official NATO/national government statements) confirms that at least one Russian drone (confirmed or officially attributed as Russian by the affected NATO member's government) breached the airspace of a NATO member state other than Romania. 'Breached airspace' means the drone entered the sovereign airspace of the NATO member without authorization. Incidents involving Romania alone do not count. If attribution remains officially unconfirmed (i.e., the affected government does not attribute the drone to Russia or to Russian military operations in Ukraine), the question resolves No. If no such incident is reported by December 29, the question resolves No.

Sources for resolution:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
- Official NATO statements: https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/news.htm
- Official government defense ministry statements of the affected NATO member state
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether NATO will down another Russian drone by December 31. A key precondition for a shootdown is that a Russian drone actually enters NATO airspace. Romania has been the most frequent target but has notably refrained from shooting drones down (citing collateral damage concerns), so breaches in other NATO states — particularly Poland, Estonia, or the Baltics, which have adopted more aggressive shoot-down postures — are a strong leading indicator that a NATO shootdown will occur. If Russian drones continue to violate non-Romanian NATO airspace, the probability of another shootdown rises substantially, as countries like Poland (which already shot drones down in September) and Estonia (where one was downed in October) have demonstrated willingness to use force. Conversely, if drone incursions are confined to Romania or cease altogether, the probability of another NATO shootdown decreases significantly.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A Russian drone (officially attributed as Russian by the affected NATO member's government) breached the airspace of a NATO member state other than Romania between November 30, 2025, and December 29, 2025. Must be confirmed by at least two major international news outlets. 'Breached airspace' means entered sovereign airspace without authorization. Attribution must be official, not suspected.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Russian drone NATO airspace breach 2025' (Nov 30 - Dec 29) - found multiple incidents; 2) 'drone airspace violation NATO member December 2025' - found Turkey and Ireland incidents; 3) 'Russian Orlan-10 drone Turkey Kocaeli airspace December 2025' - confirmed Turkish Interior Ministry attribution; 4) 'Ireland Dublin drone Russian attribution official government December 2025' - found no official attribution; 5) 'Turkey drone December 15 Black Sea officially attributed Russia' - found no official specific attribution; 6) 'Turkey Russian drone airspace breach official attribution December 15 2025' - confirmed official Ministry of National Defense statements
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidates identified: (1) Turkey Orlan-10 found in Kocaeli on Dec 19 - officially confirmed Russian by Interior Ministry, drone found within Turkish territory; (2) Turkey Dec 15 drone shot down over Black Sea - not officially attributed to Russia specifically; (3) Ireland Dublin drones Dec 1 - not officially attributed to Russia by Irish government; (4) Polish airspace - balloons from Belarus identified as smuggling balloons, not Russian drones; (5) Lithuanian airspace - attributed to Belarus, not Russia. Rejected: Ireland (no official Russian attribution), Dec 15 Turkey drone (no specific attribution to Russia vs Ukraine), Poland incidents (smuggling balloons or reconnaissance plane in international waters only).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Turkey Orlan-10 (December 19, 2025): [Turkey Interior Ministry via U.S. News & World Report](https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2025-12-19/turkey-finds-russian-orlan-10-drone-in-northwestern-city-interior-ministry) confirmed: 'initial assessments indicated the drone was used for reconnaissance and surveillance purposes, and that an investigation into the incident was ongoing.' [Haberler.com](https://en.haberler.com/ministry-of-interior-the-uav-located-in-izmit-2182488/) confirmed Interior Ministry statement: 'The UAV Located in Izmit Belongs to Russia.' [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/turkiye/drone-believed-to-be-russian-found-in-northwestern-turkiye/3775963) confirmed: 'drone believed to be a Russian-made Orlan-10.' [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/diplomacy/russian-drone-found-in-turkiyes-kocaeli) confirmed Interior Ministry stated 'the drone is of Russian origin.' The drone crashed inside Turkish territory (Kocaeli province), meaning it entered and was present within Turkish sovereign airspace. Turkey is a NATO member (not Romania). Official Turkish Interior Ministry attribution to Russia is confirmed.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: December 19, 2025. APA (Azeri Press Agency) reported: 'initial findings indicate the UAV fell within Türkiye's borders on December 19, 2025, at 16:03.' Multiple sources confirm reporting on December 19, 2025. The drone was reportedly seen crashing by a local resident 'Wednesday around 11 a.m.' (Wednesday December 17), and the authorities were notified on December 19 at 16:03.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The December 19 Orlan-10 incident appears to be the first officially confirmed/attributed Russian drone inside Turkish/NATO (non-Romania) airspace in the question window (Nov 30 - Dec 29, 2025). The Dec 15 drone was shot down but not officially attributed to Russia. No earlier qualifying event within the window was found with official attribution.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Turkey's Dec 25 Wreckage statement from Ministry of National Defense (Anadolu Agency) noted UAVs found in 'Balikesir and Kocaeli provinces' are under examination - confirming the Kocaeli (Orlan-10) incident. Daily Sabah Dec 28 article 'Comms director denies Türkiye delayed shooting Russian drone' - notes Ministry of National Defense confirmed wreckage from two drones 'believed to belong to Russia and Ukraine' in Balıkesir and Kocaeli. The Interior Ministry's official statement specifically attributed the Kocaeli (Orlan-10) drone to Russia. Multiple major outlets (Reuters via USNWR, Anadolu Agency, Daily Sabah, Asharq Al-Awsat, APA) confirmed the Turkish government's official attribution. Turkey is a NATO member. No contradictory evidence found disputing the Russian attribution of the Orlan-10.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves Yes. On December 19, 2025, Turkey's Interior Ministry officially confirmed that a Russian-origin Orlan-10 drone was found within Turkish sovereign territory (Kocaeli province, inland), confirming it had breached Turkish airspace. Turkey is a NATO member (not Romania). This is confirmed by multiple major international outlets (Reuters/US News & World Report, Anadolu Agency, Daily Sabah, APA). Official attribution to Russia by the affected NATO member's government is confirmed. The event falls within the November 30 - December 29, 2025 window.

question: John Bolton federally charged by October 31?
description:

subquestions.question: Will a federal grand jury return an indictment against John Bolton between October 1 and October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late September 2025, senior Department of Justice officials have been pushing for swift charges against former National Security Adviser John Bolton. According to Reuters and CNN reporting from September 25-26, 2025, prosecutors were expected to present the Bolton case to a grand jury as early as the first week of October 2025. However, there is internal tension: prosecutors in the Maryland U.S. Attorney's Office and the DOJ's National Security Division have reportedly resisted pressure from Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche's office, arguing that more investigation is needed to build a stronger case. The FBI raided Bolton's Bethesda, Maryland home and Washington, D.C. office on August 22, 2025, seizing computers, phones, USB drives, and classified documents. The investigation centers on allegations that Bolton emailed highly sensitive classified documents to his wife and daughter via a private email server while serving as National Security Adviser, as well as potential Espionage Act violations related to his 2020 memoir. Court filings indicate Bolton could face charges under two sections of the Espionage Act and a statute against hoarding classified files. Bolton's attorney, Abbe Lowell, has said the records are ordinary and that Bolton did nothing wrong. The push for charges intensified after Virginia's top federal prosecutor was dismissed for being too slow to prosecute Trump critics.

Sources:
- Reuters via KSL.com (2025-09-26): https://www.ksl.com/article/51316892/justice-department-pushing-for-swift-charges-against-bolton-people-familiar-say
- CNN report on DOJ push (2025-09-25): https://www.cnn.com/2025/09/25/politics/bolton-charges-doj/index.html
- Devdiscourse on DOJ pressure (2025-09-25): https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/law-order/3289410-escalating-tensions-doj-pressures-charges-against-bolton-amid-internal-dissent
- Times of India on Espionage Act charges (2025-09-04): https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/espionage-probe-fbi-investigates-former-nsa-john-bolton/articleshow/113035678.cms
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a federal grand jury returns a sealed or unsealed indictment against John Bolton between October 1, 2025 and October 10, 2025 (inclusive), as confirmed by official U.S. Department of Justice announcements, federal court docket filings (e.g., via PACER), or a wide consensus of credible news reporting (e.g., Reuters, AP, CNN, NYT). The indictment must be a formal criminal charging document returned by a grand jury in any U.S. federal district court. If no indictment is returned or publicly reported by end of day October 10, 2025 ET, the question resolves No. If an indictment is sealed and only becomes publicly known after October 10 but was returned on or before October 10, the question still resolves Yes once confirmed. Sources for resolution include PACER (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/) and official DOJ press releases (https://www.justice.gov/news).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly tracks the most critical near-term precursor to Bolton being federally charged: the grand jury indictment itself. Reports from late September indicated that prosecutors were expected to present the case to a grand jury in early October. If a grand jury indictment is returned by October 10, it is almost certain the ultimate question resolves Yes. If no indictment materializes in this window despite the reported pressure, it suggests that prosecutors successfully pushed back against the rush to charge, making it less likely charges come before October 17. This question captures a different observable event — the grand jury action — rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, because an indictment could be returned but formal charges/announcement could follow days later.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A federal grand jury formally returns an indictment against John Bolton between Oct 1–10, 2025 inclusive. Observable evidence: Official DOJ press release, PACER docket entry, or wide credible news consensus confirming a grand jury returned an indictment. Key entity: John Bolton. Timing: Oct 1, 2025 00:00 UTC through Oct 10, 2025 23:59 UTC.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'John Bolton federal grand jury indictment 2025' (Sep 1 – Oct 15, 2025) — to find any indictment events. Query 2: 'John Bolton indicted charged criminal DOJ October 2025' (Sep 1 – Oct 15, 2025) — to find formal charge announcements. Query 3: 'John Bolton indicted grand jury returned October 2025' (Oct 1 – Oct 15, 2025) — targeted search for within-window event. Query 4: 'Bolton criminal charges filed indictment Maryland court October 2025' (Oct 10 – Oct 20, 2025) — to check if indictment was filed at end of or after window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Oct 10, 2025: MSNBC and multiple outlets report charges expected 'as early as next week' — this is anticipatory reporting, NOT a confirmed indictment. (2) Oct 11, 2025: Federal prosecutors meet on Saturday to finalize potential indictment — still preparatory. (3) Oct 16, 2025: DOJ files indictment in U.S. District Court for Maryland (Greenbelt) — confirmed by Reuters, CNN, AFP, The Independent, National Review, Euronews, ibtimes.com.au, The Telegraph, clashdaily.com, Gateway Pundit. (4) Oct 17, 2025: Bolton surrenders, pleads not guilty to all 18 counts. Event (1) and (2) rejected as not satisfying criteria (no indictment returned). Events (3) and (4) are outside the Oct 1–10 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The actual grand jury indictment was returned on October 16, 2025, per [Yahoo/Reuters](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ex-national-security-adviser-bolton-210221178.html), [The Independent](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/john-bolton-indicted-classified-documents-trump-b2846948.html), [National Review](https://www.nationalreview.com/2025/10/bolton-indictment-lawfare-and-real-misconduct-are-not-mutually-exclusive/), [Euronews](http://www.euronews.com/2025/10/17/trump-critic-and-ex-national-security-adviser-john-bolton-criminally-indicted), and [Gateway Pundit](https://www.thegatewaypundit.com/2025/10/watch-bolton-filmed-walking-surrender-district-court-greenbelt/). This is October 16, 2025 — outside the October 1–10, 2025 window. As of October 10, 2025, per [MSNBC](https://www.msnbc.com/msnbc/news/criminal-charges-bolton-expected-early-week-rcna236926) and [WZTV](https://fox17.com/news/nation-world/potential-indictment-for-john-bolton-could-be-filed-as-soon-as-next-week-report-national-security-adviser-president-donald-trump-white-house-classified-documents), the indictment was only anticipated 'as early as next week,' confirming no indictment had been returned by Oct 10.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The indictment was returned on October 16, 2025. Multiple credible sources confirm this date. Bolton's surrender and not-guilty plea occurred on October 17, 2025. No source reports an indictment on or before October 10, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Searched for any earlier qualifying occurrence. All sources from Oct 1–10, 2025 describe the investigation as ongoing and charges as anticipated but not yet filed. No source reports an indictment within the Oct 1–10 window. The October 10 articles (MSNBC, WZTV, Independent Sentinel) explicitly state charges could come 'early next week,' confirming none had been returned by that date.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find any evidence of a sealed indictment returned during Oct 1–10: none found. All sources agree the indictment date was October 16, 2025. The resolution criteria note that a sealed indictment returned by Oct 10 but made public later would still count, but no such evidence exists — all sources indicate the grand jury returned the indictment on Oct 16. No contradictory evidence exists.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The federal grand jury indictment against John Bolton was returned on October 16, 2025 — after the question window of October 1–10, 2025 closed. During the window, only investigation, grand jury review, and anticipatory reporting existed. No indictment was returned on or before October 10, 2025. The question resolves No. The window closed on October 10, 2025 at 23:59:59 UTC without the qualifying event occurring.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX receive FAA launch authorization (license or license modification) for Starship Flight Test 12 by November 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
SpaceX requires Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) launch authorization before each Starship test flight. The FAA issues launch licenses and license modifications that permit specific missions, and regulatory delays have historically been a significant bottleneck for Starship's launch cadence. In May 2025, the FAA approved SpaceX for up to 25 Starship test flights per year from Starbase, Texas (https://www.faa.gov/space). However, each individual flight still requires specific FAA clearance, including environmental and safety reviews.

As of October 18, 2025, SpaceX has completed 11 Starship test flights, with Flight 11 launching on October 13, 2025. SpaceX has been flying at a cadence of roughly one flight every 3-7 weeks in 2025, with Elon Musk previously stating a goal of launching every 3-4 weeks (https://www.yahoo.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-most-successful-test-mission-2025). The transition from the original Pad 1 (which is being retrofitted after Flight 11) to a new launch infrastructure could affect timelines. Flight 11 was described as the final launch from Pad 1 in its current configuration (https://www.statesman.com/story/news/local/2025/10/13/spacex-starship-flight-11-launch-starbase-what-to-know/).

FAA authorization is a necessary precondition for any Starship launch. Without it, Flight 12 cannot proceed regardless of vehicle readiness.

Sources:
- FAA Commercial Space Transportation: https://www.faa.gov/space
- Austin American-Statesman on Flight 11: https://www.statesman.com/story/news/local/2025/10/13/spacex-starship-flight-11-launch-starbase-what-to-know/
- Yahoo News on Starship cadence: https://www.yahoo.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-most-successful-test-mission-2025

If no such authorization is publicly confirmed by 11:59 PM UTC on November 10, 2025, this question resolves No. If the flight is designated differently (e.g., due to a name change) but is clearly the 12th integrated Starship/Super Heavy test flight, it still counts.

If SpaceX does not receive FAA clearance for Flight 12 by early-to-mid November, it becomes very unlikely that Flight 12 can launch by November 30, given additional time needed for final vehicle preparation and launch operations after regulatory approval. Conversely, early FAA clearance would be a strong positive signal. This is a different observable event from the launch itself — it tracks the regulatory pipeline rather than the launch event — and is a genuine leading indicator that forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question would find informative.

question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $70 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Crude Oil (CL) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Crude Oil (CL) futures contracts, the active month is the nearest of the contract months listed. The active month becomes a non-active month effective two business days prior to the spot month expiration. For example; if the spot month expires on a Friday the next listed contract will be considered the Active Month on the Wednesday prior to the spot month expiration.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Crude Oil (CL) futures.

subquestions.question: Will the front-month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures settlement price rise above $62.00 per barrel on any trading day between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-24?

The $62 threshold represents a meaningful intermediate step — roughly half the distance from current prices to $70. If crude oil cannot break above $62 in the near term, it signals weak momentum and makes a move to $70 by March 2026 less likely. Conversely, a break above $62 would suggest strengthening demand or tightening supply dynamics that could support further price gains.

Key factors influencing near-term oil prices include OPEC+ production decisions, winter heating demand, U.S. inventory levels, and global macroeconomic conditions. OPEC+ has been managing supply carefully, but demand concerns — particularly from China — have kept prices subdued through late 2025.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The Active Month is determined using CME's standard methodology: the nearest listed contract month, which transitions to the next listed contract two business days prior to the expiring contract's last trading day.
