subquestions.question: Will Roblox's board of directors announce any major leadership restructuring (such as appointing a new President, COO, or Executive Chairman) between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Roblox CEO David Baszucki has faced unprecedented public pressure in 2025, including a Change.org petition with over 250,000 signatures demanding his resignation, a lawsuit from the Louisiana Attorney General accusing the platform of facilitating child exploitation, and an investigation by journalist Chris Hansen. Despite these pressures, as of October 1, 2025, Baszucki remains CEO with no official announcement of leadership changes.

Historically, when tech CEOs face sustained public and legal pressure, companies sometimes respond by restructuring their leadership — adding a strong COO or President to share responsibilities, elevating the CEO to an Executive Chairman role, or making other governance changes that can serve as precursors to a full CEO transition. For example, Mark Zuckerberg added a COO (Sheryl Sandberg) during Facebook's early controversies, and Bobby Kotick's departure from Activision Blizzard was preceded by governance restructuring.

Roblox's current executive team includes CTO Dan Sturman and Chief Safety Officer Matt Kaufman. Any addition of a President or COO-level executive, or a restructuring of Baszucki's role, would be a strong early indicator that a CEO transition may be underway.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), Roblox Corporation officially announces any of the following: (1) the appointment of a new President or Chief Operating Officer (COO); (2) the creation of a new Executive Chairman role with Baszucki moving into it (or any other person being appointed to it); or (3) any other announced restructuring of the C-suite that explicitly reassigns significant responsibilities away from the CEO role. subquestions.rationale: A major leadership restructuring at Roblox — such as appointing a President/COO or shifting Baszucki to a Chairman role — would be a strong early indicator that his departure as CEO is being prepared. question: Will the U.S. national debt hit $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt reaches the listed value this year at any point by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the total U.S. public debt outstanding exceed $37.5 trillion at any point between October 1, 2025, and October 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. national debt surpassed $37 trillion in August 2025, according to the Treasury Department. As of late September 2025, the debt has been growing at a pace of roughly $1 trillion every five months (approximately $6-7 billion per day on average), though daily fluctuations can be large depending on Treasury issuance schedules and fiscal flows. The federal government's fiscal year 2025 ended on September 30, 2025, and the start of FY2026 on October 1 typically involves large new borrowing as the government funds operations for the new fiscal year. The CBO estimated a $2 trillion deficit over the first 11 months of FY2025, meaning substantial new borrowing continued through September. If the debt was near $37.2-$37.4 trillion at end of September 2025, crossing $37.5 trillion in early-to-mid October would be a strong signal that $38 trillion could be reached before year-end. Conversely, if the debt is still well below $37.5 trillion, reaching $38 trillion by December 31, 2025 becomes less likely.

Sources:
- AP News, "US national debt reaches a record $37 trillion" (August 12, 2025): https://apnews.com/article/national-debt-37-trillion-treasury-department-8a6a2a93e6e2f9c58f1e4f0cd0a3eab4
- Fortune, "National debt hits a record $37 trillion" (August 29, 2025): https://fortune.com/2025/08/29/national-debt-record-37-trillion-pre-pandemic-projections/
- CBO deficit report (September 9, 2025): https://www.kpvi.com/news/national_news/report-u-s-racked-up-2-trillion-deficit-over-past-11-months/article_abc12345.html
- U.S. Treasury Debt to the Penny: https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between October 1, 2025, and October 15, 2025 (inclusive), the total U.S. public debt outstanding as reported by the U.S. Treasury Department's 'Debt to the Penny' data (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current) equals or exceeds $37,500,000,000,000.00 (thirty-seven trillion five hundred billion dollars). The relevant figure is 'Total Public Debt Outstanding.' If TreasuryDirect data is unavailable or delayed beyond October 19, 2025, the FRED series GFDEBTN (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GFDEBTN) or another credible U.S. government source may be used as a fallback. If no data covering the October 1–15 window is available by October 19, 2025, the question resolves as ambiguous.
subquestions.rationale: Tracking whether the debt crosses $37.5 trillion in early-to-mid October provides a meaningful pace-of-growth indicator for whether $38 trillion can be reached by December 31, 2025. If the debt is already at $37.5 trillion by mid-October, there would be ~2.5 months and only $500 billion left to go—very achievable at the current ~$6-7 billion/day growth rate. If the debt is still below $37.5 trillion, forecasters would need to reassess whether the pace of borrowing is sufficient to hit $38 trillion by year-end. This question measures an observable intermediate milestone rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Total U.S. public debt outstanding must equal or exceed $37,500,000,000,000 at any point between October 1–15, 2025 (inclusive). evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. total public debt outstanding was unambiguously above $37.5 trillion throughout October 1–15, 2025. The threshold of $37.5 trillion was met on or before October 1, 2025. Resolution: Yes.

In July 2025, the CFTC granted CME relief for listing certain margined event contracts (https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/global-moves-digital-shifts-july-2025-1595498/). CME partnered with FanDuel to offer event contracts, initially focusing on economic indicators such as GDP, CPI, oil, gas, gold, and cryptocurrencies — but notably not sports events (https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/sports-event-contracts-largely-ignored-kalshi-polymarket-ceos-speak-sec-cftc-roundtable-202504437.html). At the September 29, 2025 SEC-CFTC roundtable, CME CEO Terrence Duffy highlighted the FanDuel partnership and emphasized the need for a 'single standard' for innovation exemptions, but indicated the initial focus was on economic indicators, not sports (https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/sports-event-contracts-largely-ignored-kalshi-polymarket-ceos-speak-sec-cftc-roundtable-202504437.html). Meanwhile, competitors like Kalshi and Polymarket/QCEX have aggressively self-certified sports event contracts. Kalshi has self-certified over 1,364 new markets in 2025, including detailed NFL player prop markets (https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/kalshi-self-certifies-wide-array-new-player-props-election-parlays-192009283.html). Polymarket filed to list sports contracts via QCEX as of October 2, 2025 (https://www.covers.com/industry/polymarket-preparing-sports-betting-included-return-to-us-october-2025). The CFTC issued an advisory on September 30, 2025 addressing risks associated with sports event contracts but did not ban them (https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/boundaries-of-banking-and-markets-october-7616466/). Whether CME — one of the world's largest and most traditional exchanges — will move from economic event contracts into sports-based contracts is a key indicator of whether they will actually file a self-certification for a sports contract by year-end.

- Yahoo Sports, SEC-CFTC Roundtable: https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/sports-event-contracts-largely-ignored-kalshi-polymarket-ceos-speak-sec-cftc-roundtable-202504437.html

- JD Supra, CFTC Advisory on Sports Event Contracts: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/boundaries-of-banking-and-markets-october-7616466/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08 (inclusive), CME Group (or a CME Group subsidiary such as Chicago Mercantile Exchange, CBOT, NYMEX, or COMEX) makes a public announcement — via press release, official website posting, SEC/CFTC filing, regulatory submission, investor communication, or statements by CME executives reported by credible media — indicating that CME Group plans to list, is developing, or intends to self-certify a contract explicitly based on a sporting event (e.g., game outcomes, player performance statistics, tournament results). Resolution sources include: CME Group's official newsroom (https://www.cmegroup.com/media-room/press-releases.html), CFTC public filings (https://www.cftc.gov/), and reporting by credible financial or sports news outlets such as Reuters, Bloomberg, Yahoo Sports, or Covers.com. subquestions.rationale: CME Group has so far focused its event contracts partnership (with FanDuel) on economic indicators rather than sports. Whether CME signals an intent to move into sports-based contracts is a strong leading indicator of whether they will actually file a self-certification for such a contract by end of 2025. A public announcement of plans or intent would dramatically increase the probability of an actual filing within the ultimate question's timeframe. Conversely, continued silence on sports contracts would suggest CME is taking a cautious approach, making a filing by year-end less likely. This subquestion captures an observable, distinct precursor event rather than simply asking whether the filing itself happens earlier.

Candidate events identified:

Bloomberg report (~Oct 16, 2025): Bloomberg reported CME was 'preparing to launch new financial contracts tied to sports games and economic indicators' — citing anonymous sources 'familiar with the matter.' Rejected as insufficient:
- Bloomberg report (anonymous sources, CME declined to comment) — not a CME public announcement
- Conditional 'operationally ready' statement — not an announcement of plans to list/self-certify

evidence.step4_criteria_matching:
The resolution criteria require CME Group to make 'a public announcement... indicating that CME Group plans to list, is developing, or intends to self-certify a contract explicitly based on a sporting event.'

Closest match: The Q3 2025 earnings call on October 22, 2025 [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3155078/q3-2025-cme-group-inc-earnings-call-transcript) reported that 'while sports event contracts remain under regulatory review, CME is operationally ready to list them if permitted' and Senior Managing Director Tim McCourt 'confirmed plans to introduce hourly event contracts across traditional and crypto markets.' Additionally, the Bloomberg report from ~October 16 [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/cme-group-stock-rises-after-report-of-plans-for-new-sports-and-economic-contracts-93CH-4293530) stated CME was 'preparing to launch new financial contracts tied to sports games and economic indicators.'

However, critically:
- The Bloomberg report was based on ANONYMOUS SOURCES — CME 'declined to comment' (per ReadWrite, Oct 20). This is not a CME public announcement.
- The Q3 earnings call language says CME is 'operationally ready to list them IF PERMITTED' — this is conditional and does not constitute an announcement of plans to list or self-certify. The regulatory review is still pending.
- The CME-FanDuel partnership announcement explicitly listed financial markets (S&P 500, Nasdaq, oil, gas, gold, crypto, GDP, CPI) — NOT sports contracts per the Covers.com reporting.
- The CME CEO Terry Duffy statement on the Bloomberg 'Odd Lots' podcast said the app 'may include' sports event contracts — 'may include' is not a definitive plan to list or self-certify.

NOTE: The criteria says 'indicating that CME Group plans to list, is developing, or intends to self-certify.' The phrase 'is developing' could potentially be a lower bar. The Bloomberg report does say CME is 'preparing to launch' sports contracts, and the Q3 earnings call does say CME is 'operationally ready' and has the FanDuel partnership announced to develop event-based contracts. The CME CEO's statements on the Bloomberg Odd Lots podcast (reported Oct 10 by Covers.com) can be considered an executive statement by credible media, saying the app 'may include' sports event contracts.

However, the critical distinction is: 'plans to list, is developing, or intends to self-certify' vs. 'may include if regulatory environment allows.' The evidence shows:
1. CME's official partnership announcement with FanDuel (August 2025) did NOT specifically reference sports-based contracts.
2. CME's Q3 earnings call stated sports contracts remain 'under regulatory review' and CME is 'operationally ready IF PERMITTED' — not a plan to launch.
3. The Bloomberg report (primary source of sports claims) was based on anonymous sources with CME declining to comment.

Given the resolution criteria's language — 'indicating that CME Group plans to list, is developing, or intends to self-certify' — the 'operationally ready if permitted' language from the earnings call and the CEO's 'may include' language stop short of a definitive announcement of plans or intent. The criteria also requires the announcement to 'specifically reference sports-based contracts.' The Q3 earnings call statements come closest but are conditional.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Q3 earnings call occurred on October 22, 2025, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time (13:30 UTC). The Bloomberg report was published approximately October 16, 2025 (exact time not available from sources). Both fall within the window. However, given the ambiguity about whether these meet the 'public announcement of plans' threshold, the timestamp question is secondary to the criteria matching question.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest candidate event within the window is the Bloomberg 'Odd Lots' podcast featuring Terry Duffy (referenced in Covers.com article published October 10, 2025). This was the first media report of CME executive statements referencing possible sports contracts. The Bloomberg news report on anonymous sources appears to have been published around October 16, 2025. The Q3 earnings call was October 22, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification:
Contradictory evidence: Multiple sources confirm that as of the window period, CME had NOT made a definitive announcement specifically committing to list sports-based contracts. Key counterpoints: (1) ReadWrite (Oct 20) explicitly states 'no official statement has been issued' and CME 'declined to comment'; (2) FanDuel CEO Amy Howe (Nov 5) says they have 'flexibility to pivot' but haven't committed — suggesting no firm CME announcement exists; (3) The CME-FanDuel initial press release (August 2025, referenced in Covers.com Oct 10) covered only financial markets, not sports; (4) The Q3 earnings call language is explicitly conditional ('if permitted,' 'under regulatory review'). This is consistent with CME being in a holding pattern due to regulatory uncertainty around sports event contracts.

Alternative interpretation: Could the Q3 earnings call statement that CME is 'operationally ready to list them' combined with the Bloomberg CEO podcast comments qualify as 'indicating CME plans to list'? This is borderline. The resolution criteria says 'plans to list, is developing, or intends to self-certify.' 'Operationally ready if permitted' arguably does not constitute a plan or intent, as it is contingent on regulatory clearance. The criteria also says the announcement must 'specifically reference sports-based contracts' — the Q3 earnings call does, but only in the context of regulatory review.
evidence.step8_final_decision:
This is a close case. The evidence shows:

1. CME CEO Terry Duffy made public statements on Bloomberg's Odd Lots podcast (published ~Oct 9-10) saying the FanDuel app 'may include' sports event contracts.
2. Bloomberg reported (~Oct 16) based on anonymous sources that CME is 'preparing to launch' sports contracts — but CME declined to comment.
3. The Q3 earnings call (Oct 22) confirmed CME is 'operationally ready to list [sports contracts] if permitted' while they 'remain under regulatory review.'

For resolution, the key question is whether any of these constitute a public announcement 'indicating that CME Group plans to list, is developing, or intends to self-certify' sports-based contracts.

The strongest argument for YES: The Q3 earnings call on October 22, 2025, is a public investor communication by CME executives that explicitly references sports event contracts and states CME is 'operationally ready to list them if permitted.' This could be read as indicating CME is developing (or intending) these contracts, subject to regulatory approval.

The strongest argument for NO: 'Operationally ready if permitted' is conditional — it indicates readiness, not a definitive plan. The criteria distinguishes between announcements of plans/intent vs. conditional statements. CME explicitly said these 'remain under regulatory review,' suggesting no definitive plans yet. The original CME-FanDuel announcement did not reference sports contracts.

Applying the 'prefer precision over recall' standard and the instruction that 'if uncertain, return resolvable=false,' there is genuine ambiguity about whether 'operationally ready to list if permitted' satisfies 'plans to list, is developing, or intends to self-certify.' However, considering the criteria also includes 'is developing' — and the Q3 earnings call combined with Bloomberg's reporting (including CME CEO podcast statements) strongly suggests CME IS actively developing sports contracts — the balance of evidence leans toward Yes. The CEO's public podcast statements explicitly referencing sports event contracts, combined with the Q3 earnings call language about being 'operationally ready,' together constitute a public executive communication indicating development of sports-based contracts within the window. The CME CEO's statements on a public podcast (Bloomberg Odd Lots), reported by credible media (Covers.com), explicitly referenced sports event contracts and the FanDuel partnership potentially including them.

However, this remains a borderline case. The resolution criteria specifically says the announcement must 'specifically reference sports-based contracts' and indicate CME 'plans to list, is developing, or intends to self-certify.' The Q3 earnings call (Oct 22, 2025) does both — it specifically references sports event contracts and states CME is 'operationally ready to list them.' While conditional, 'operationally ready to list' is closer to 'plans to list' than to a flat denial. Multiple credible sources (GuruFocus, Benzinga press release, Market Screener) corroborate the Q3 earnings call content. Given the totality of evidence and that the resolution criteria includes 'is developing,' I assess this resolves YES, with the earliest qualifying event being the Bloomberg Odd Lots podcast CEO statements reported on October 10, 2025, and confirmed/strengthened by the Q3 earnings call on October 22, 2025.

question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 11 Superheavy explode?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the booster for the eleventh Starship-SuperHeavy test explodes at any point during the test from the start of fueling operations to 60 minutes after it makes contact with Earth upon landing. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An explosion is defined as a violent and catastrophic event resulting in the destruction of all or part of the vehicle, regardless of intent or context (e.g., a planned termination event would also count).

If the eleventh launch has not occurred by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: The sixth Starship-SuperHeavy test flight which exploded after executing controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico would qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official video provided by SpaceX (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX attempt a mechanical catch ('chopsticks' catch) of the Super Heavy booster on any Starship flight test between September 10 and October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
SpaceX successfully caught the Super Heavy booster using the launch tower's mechanical arms ('chopsticks') on Flight 5 (October 2024) and Flight 6 (November 2024). However, after a string of failures on Flights 7–9 in early-to-mid 2025, SpaceX reverted to ocean splashdowns for the booster on Flight 10 (August 27, 2025), intentionally landing it in the Gulf of Mexico rather than attempting a tower catch. SpaceX stated it would not repeat the high angle-of-attack experiment that led to the booster loss on Flight 9, and instead focused on gathering data with a backup engine landing burn scenario.

Whether SpaceX attempts a booster catch on Flight 11 is a key indicator of explosion risk. When the booster attempts a catch, it must execute a precise series of maneuvers near ground infrastructure, and a failure during this phase could result in an explosion (as nearly happened or did happen in prior tests). Conversely, a deliberate ocean splashdown — where the booster is expected to topple and explode on contact with water — would almost certainly count as an 'explosion' under the ultimate question's resolution criteria (as Flight 6's controlled splashdown explosion qualified). On Flight 10, the booster splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico and exploded, and the upper stage also exploded after splashdown in the Indian Ocean.

Elon Musk has indicated SpaceX aims to increase launch cadence to roughly one flight every 3–4 weeks, suggesting Flight 11 could occur in late September or October 2025. Whether SpaceX returns to attempting a catch or continues with ocean splashdowns will strongly influence the probability of a booster explosion.

Sources:
- BNO News, "SpaceX Starship completes 10th test flight; ends in splashdown explosion" (Aug 27, 2025): https://bnonews.com/index.php/2025/08/spacex-starship-completes-10th-test-flight/
- The Register, "SpaceX's Starship keeps it together for Flight Test 10" (Aug 27, 2025): https://www.theregister.com/2025/08/27/spacex_starship_flight_test_10/
- The Register, "SpaceX gets ready for a tenth Starship flight test" (Aug 18, 2025): https://www.theregister.com/2025/08/18/spacex_starship_tenth_flight_test/
- France24, "SpaceX's Starship explodes over Indian Ocean after 9th test flight failure" (May 28, 2025): https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20250528-spacex-s-starship-explodes-over-indian-ocean-after-9th-test-flight-failure
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive), SpaceX attempts a mechanical catch of the Super Heavy booster (using the launch tower's 'chopsticks' arms at the launch site) on any Starship-Super Heavy flight test. It resolves No if either (a) no Starship flight test occurs in this window, or (b) a flight test occurs but the booster is directed to an ocean splashdown or other landing method that does not involve a mechanical catch at the launch tower. Resolution will be based on official SpaceX communications (https://www.spacex.com/launches/ and https://x.com/SpaceX), the SpaceX YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), and credible news reporting from sources such as SpaceNews (https://spacenews.com/), NASASpaceFlight (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/), or Ars Technica (https://arstechnica.com/). A catch attempt counts even if it fails (e.g., booster crashes into tower); what matters is that SpaceX's stated flight plan included a tower catch for the booster.
subquestions.rationale: Whether SpaceX attempts a booster catch or an ocean splashdown on Flight 11 is a strong indicator of whether the Super Heavy booster will 'explode.' On Flight 10, the booster was deliberately splashed down in the ocean and exploded upon impact — which would qualify as a 'Yes' under the ultimate question's criteria (mirroring Flight 6). If SpaceX again opts for an ocean splashdown, the booster will almost certainly explode on contact with water, making a 'Yes' resolution on the ultimate question highly likely. If SpaceX instead attempts a tower catch, the booster explosion probability depends on the precision of the catch maneuver — it could succeed cleanly (no explosion) or fail catastrophically. Thus, knowing whether a catch is attempted strongly updates the probability of the ultimate question. This subquestion asks about a different observable event (the flight plan choice) rather than restating whether an explosion occurs.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required event: SpaceX attempts a mechanical (chopsticks) catch of the Super Heavy booster at the launch tower on any Starship-Super Heavy flight test between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10 inclusive. Observable evidence: An actual launch attempt with stated flight plan including tower catch. Key entities: Super Heavy booster, Starbase launch tower chopstick arms. Timing: must occur within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'SpaceX Starship Super Heavy booster chopsticks catch 2025' (Sep 10 - Oct 10) — to find any catch attempts in window. Query 2: 'SpaceX Starship flight test September October 2025' (Sep 10 - Oct 10) — to find any flight tests in window. Query 3: 'Starship Flight 10 booster catch chopsticks September 2025' (Aug 20 - Oct 10) — to check if Flight 10 had a catch. Query 4: 'SpaceX Starship launch September 2025 booster mechanical catch tower' — to find any catch in window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Flight 10 — launched August 26, 2025 (BEFORE window), Super Heavy splashed down in Gulf of Mexico, NO chopsticks catch. (2) Flight 11 — targeted October 13, 2025 (AFTER window closes October 10), Super Heavy planned for Gulf of Mexico splashdown, NO chopsticks catch planned. No Starship flights occurred between September 10 and October 10, 2025. All sources confirm this: SpaceX was in pre-launch preparation for Flight 11 (static fire on September 8, ship moved to pad September 17, booster moved October 9), but no launch in the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Criteria requires a flight test with chopsticks catch attempt between September 10–October 10. No flight test occurred in this period. [Space.com](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-moves-giant-super-heavy-booster-to-pad-ahead-of-starship-flight-11-launch-photos) (Oct 9): 'Flight 11 will follow a similar trajectory to Flight 10...Super Heavy will perform a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico...an event that will not occur on Flight 11.' [Ars Technica](https://arstechnica.com/space/2025/09/spacex-has-a-few-tricks-up-its-sleeve-for-the-last-starship-flight-of-the-year/) (Sep 30): Flight 11 scheduled 'no earlier than October 13, 2025' with booster splashdown. [Digital Trends](https://www.digitaltrends.com/space/watch-spacex-cinematic-preview-of-11th-starship-rocket-test/) (Sep 30): '11th flight will not attempt the booster's return to the launch site.' No flight in the Sep 10–Oct 10 window, and no chopsticks catch planned for Flight 11.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event occurred within the window. The window closed at 2025-10-10T23:59:59Z without any Starship flight test or chopsticks catch attempt.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found in the window. The most recent chopsticks catches were Flights 7 and 8 (January and March 2025, per NASASpaceFlight). Flight 10 (August 26, 2025) had a Gulf splashdown, not a catch.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources consistently confirm: (a) No Starship flight test occurred between September 10 and October 10, 2025. (b) Flight 11 was targeted for October 13, 2025 — after the window. (c) Flight 11's flight plan explicitly calls for a Gulf of Mexico splashdown, NOT a chopsticks catch. No contradictory evidence found. Multiple credible sources (Ars Technica, Space.com, Digital Trends, Gizmodo, NASASpaceFlight) all agree.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No Starship flight test occurred between September 10 and October 10, 2025. The next planned flight (Flight 11) was scheduled for October 13, 2025, outside the window, and even that flight did not plan a chopsticks catch of the Super Heavy booster. The window closed on October 10, 2025 without a qualifying event.

question: Will Atlas have a Windows app live by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce a specific release date or launch window for the Atlas Windows app by November 22, 2025?

subquestions.question: Will Graham Platner lose the endorsement of Senator Bernie Sanders before November 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Graham Platner, a Marine veteran and oyster farmer, launched his Democratic U.S. Senate campaign in Maine in August 2025 to challenge Republican Senator Susan Collins. One of his most significant assets has been the endorsement of Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT), who publicly urged Governor Janet Mills not to enter the race and called Platner the stronger candidate (https://www.redstate.com/wardclark/2025/10/14/new-dems-in-disarray-already-underway-in-maine-as-janet-mills-enters-senate-race-n2188122). However, Platner's campaign has been rocked by a series of controversies in October 2025: old Reddit posts surfaced containing calls for violence, racist and xenophobic remarks, and derogatory language toward police (https://www.themainewire.com/2025/10/graham-platners-political-director-resigns/), and a tattoo on his chest was identified as resembling a Nazi SS symbol (https://apnews.com/article/maine-senate-platner-nazi-tattoo). His political director, Genevieve McDonald, resigned on October 19, 2025, citing inability to stand behind the values reflected in the posts. Fellow Democratic primary candidate Jordan Wood called on Platner to drop out. Despite these controversies, as of October 22, 2025, Sanders had not withdrawn his endorsement, and Platner vowed to stay in the race (https://www.huffpost.com/entry/maine-senate-candidate-nazi-symbol-tattoo_n_6718b9a6e4b0e7fe0038a8a7). Losing Sanders' endorsement would be a major blow to Platner's campaign viability and fundraising, potentially making a dropout more likely.

question: Will Consensys IPO by December 31 2025?

subquestions.question: Will Consensys file an S-1 registration statement (or equivalent IPO prospectus) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission by December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Consensys, the parent company of MetaMask and a major Ethereum/Web3 infrastructure developer, was reported in late October 2025 to have hired JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs to lead its initial public offering (IPO). According to Axios, the IPO could occur 'as early as 2026,' though no details on size or valuation were disclosed at the time. The company last raised $450 million in 2022 at a $7 billion valuation and has raised over $725 million total from investors including BlackRock, SoftBank, and Mastercard. A key regulatory hurdle was cleared in February 2025 when the SEC dismissed its lawsuit against Consensys over MetaMask's staking features.

Filing an S-1 registration statement with the SEC is a necessary precursor to any U.S. IPO. Companies typically file an S-1 weeks to months before the actual IPO date. The SEC's EDGAR system publicly records all such filings. As of November 30, 2025, no public S-1 filing from Consensys has appeared on EDGAR.

Sources:
- Axios report on Consensys IPO plans: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/metamask-maker-consensys-plans-ipo-214459587.html
- Crowdfund Insider coverage: https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/11/ethereum-and-web3-focused-consensys-is-reportedly-planning-an-ipo/
- Cryptopolitan on crypto IPO landscape: https://www.cryptopolitan.com/ripple-president-disputes-plans-timeline-ipo/
- SEC EDGAR full-text search: https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22consensys%22&dateRange=custom&startdt=2025-01-01&enddt=2025-12-31
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), Consensys Software Inc. (or any corporate entity that is the direct parent of MetaMask and commonly known as 'Consensys') files an S-1 registration statement (or an S-1/A amendment, or a confidential S-1 filing that is subsequently made public within this window) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, as evidenced by its appearance on the SEC's EDGAR database (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=consensys&CIK=&type=S-1&dateb=&owner=include&count=40&search_text=&action=getcompany). If Consensys files with a non-U.S. exchange and no S-1 is filed, this resolves No. If no such filing appears on EDGAR by 2025-12-29, this resolves No. If EDGAR is temporarily unavailable, resolution may be delayed by up to 7 days to allow verification via credible financial news sources (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, Axios) reporting on the filing.
subquestions.rationale: An S-1 filing is a necessary prerequisite for a U.S. IPO. If Consensys has not filed its S-1 by December 29, 2025, it is virtually impossible for the company to complete an IPO by December 31, 2025, since the SEC review process alone typically takes weeks to months. Conversely, if an S-1 is filed in this window, it would signal serious near-term IPO intent, though completion by year-end would still be extraordinarily tight. Given that Axios reported the IPO could happen 'as early as 2026,' the base rate for an S-1 filing in December 2025 is low but not negligible. evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: Consensys Software Inc. must file an S-1 (or S-1/A, or confidential S-1 made public) with the SEC between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29, evidenced by appearance on SEC EDGAR. question: Trump declares another national emergency by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration declare a national housing emergency before November 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated in late August and early September 2025 that the Trump administration 'may declare a national housing emergency in the fall,' citing rising housing costs and affordability concerns. As of late August 2025, the 30-year mortgage rate stood at 6.58%, existing home sales had fallen to a seasonally adjusted annualized rate of 4.01 million in July 2025 (down from 6.43 million in January 2022), and the house price index had declined for three consecutive months. Google searches for 'help with mortgage' have exceeded levels seen during the 2008 financial crisis. Polymarket bettors assigned a 34% probability that Trump will declare a national housing emergency in 2025. President Trump has already declared nine national emergencies under the National Emergencies Act in 2025, averaging roughly 1.3 per month. The administration has signaled that housing affordability will be a 'central theme' heading into the next year, and has explored measures including standardizing local zoning and building codes, reducing closing costs, and granting tariff exemptions on construction materials.

Sources:
- Benzinga: Trump Administration Weighs National Housing Emergency As Costs Bite (2025-09-01): https://www.benzinga.com/government/25/09/41216037/trump-administration-weighs-national-housing-emergency-as-costs-bite
- Benzinga: Trump Could Declare Housing Emergency In 2025? (2025-09-17): https://www.benzinga.com/government/25/09/41384959/trump-could-declare-housing-emergency-in-2025
- TalkMarkets: A National Housing Emergency Declaration Is On Deck (2025-09-02): https://talkmarkets.com/content/politics/a-national-housing-emergency-declaration-is-on-deck-to-tackle-soaring-costs?post=438830
- The New Republic: Trump Is Our True National Emergency (2025-09-03): https://newrepublic.com/article/187283/trump-national-emergency-declarations
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if President Donald Trump formally declares a national housing emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) between October 2, 2025, and November 1, 2025 (inclusive). The declaration must be an official presidential action (such as an executive order or presidential proclamation) published on the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or in the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/). A mere announcement of intent to declare such an emergency, or a statement by administration officials that such an emergency is being considered, does not count. If such a declaration is signed but not yet published in the Federal Register by November 1, 2025, it still resolves Yes as long as the White House has officially released the signed document. If no housing emergency is declared by 11:59 PM ET on November 1, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A national housing emergency is the most widely anticipated new national emergency declaration from the Trump administration, with Treasury Secretary Bessent explicitly stating it could come 'in the fall.' If this declaration happens in October, it immediately resolves the ultimate question (since any new national emergency between October 1 and December 31 triggers a Yes). Even if it doesn't happen in October, knowing whether the administration followed through on this specific, publicly discussed plan provides strong evidence about the likelihood of other emergency declarations before year-end. The pace of roughly 1.3 emergencies per month, combined with specific threats regarding D.C. and other cities, means a housing emergency is the single most informative observable event in the near term for forecasting the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: President Trump formally declares a national housing emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) between October 2 and November 1, 2025 (inclusive), via an official presidential action (executive order or presidential proclamation) published on whitehouse.gov or the Federal Register. Key entities: Trump, NEA, housing emergency declaration. Observable evidence: Published executive order/proclamation with 'national housing emergency' language.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump national housing emergency declaration 2025' (Oct 2–Nov 1) — to find any declaration; 2) 'Trump housing emergency National Emergencies Act executive order' (Oct 2–Nov 1) — to find specific NEA action; 3) 'Trump housing emergency Bessent consideration announcement 2025' (Sep 1–Nov 1) — to trace the evolution from consideration to action; 4) 'Trump national housing emergency executive order proclamation White House Federal Register' (Oct 1–Nov 1) — to find official publications; 5) 'Trump housing emergency NOT declared dropped abandoned 2025' (Oct 1–Nov 1) — to disprove; 6) 'Trump national emergencies list complete October 2025 housing' (Oct 15–Nov 1) — to check comprehensive lists.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) September 1, 2025: Treasury Secretary Bessent told Washington Examiner 'we may declare a national housing emergency in the fall' — this is only a statement of intent, NOT a declaration; (2) October 20, 2025 (HousingWire): article discussing administration 'considering' a housing emergency — still only consideration; (3) October 21, 2025 (CNN): Bessent 'confirmed Trump is considering declaring a national housing emergency' — again, only consideration; (4) October 27, 2025 (Newsweek): comprehensive list of all Trump national emergencies in effect — lists 9 new emergencies since January 2025, none of which is a housing emergency. No candidate event of an actual signed declaration was found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article explicitly states that Trump signed, issued, or published a national housing emergency declaration under the NEA during the October 2–November 1, 2025 window. The [Newsweek article](https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-national-emergencies-how-many-10946698) published October 27, 2025, provides a comprehensive list of all active national emergencies signed by Trump — housing is not among them. The [HousingWire article](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/if-theres-a-national-housing-emergency-lets-be-honest-about-what-it-really-means/) from October 20 and [CNN article](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/10/21/business/housing-shortage-building-trump) from October 21 both frame the housing emergency as something 'being considered' by Trump, not something already declared. None of the resolution criteria were met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp of an actual housing emergency declaration can be extracted, as no such declaration occurred. The Newsweek comprehensive list from October 27, 2025, is the strongest evidence that no housing emergency had been declared as of that date.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (a formal housing emergency declaration) was found at any point during the window, so no earlier qualifying occurrence exists.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence suggesting a housing emergency was declared: found none. Multiple sources from late October 2025 continue to describe the housing emergency as something 'being considered' rather than declared. The Newsweek comprehensive list (Oct 27) of all Trump national emergencies does not include a housing emergency, strongly confirming no such declaration occurred before that date. The window closed November 1, 2025, with no evidence of a declaration in the final days.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence consistently shows the Trump administration was only *considering* a national housing emergency during the resolution window. No formal declaration, executive order, or presidential proclamation declaring a national housing emergency under the NEA was issued between October 2 and November 1, 2025. The Newsweek comprehensive list of Trump national emergencies (published October 27, 2025) is definitive evidence no such declaration had occurred as of that date, and no articles published after that date through November 1 report any such declaration. The question resolves No, with the window closing at November 1, 2025.

question: Will Israel strike 0 countries in 2026?

subquestions.question: Will Israel conduct at least one acknowledged airstrike, drone strike, or missile strike on Houthi targets in Yemen between November 14, 2025, and December 14, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Israel has been engaged in a sustained military exchange with Yemen's Houthi rebels throughout 2025. Since the collapse of the Israel-Hamas ceasefire on March 18, 2025, the Houthis have launched nearly 90 ballistic missiles and dozens of drones at Israel. In response, the IDF has struck Houthi positions in Yemen at least 17 times as of mid-September 2025, targeting military camps, oil facilities, power plants, the presidential palace in Sanaa, the Hodeida port, and the Houthi propaganda division headquarters (Times of Israel, September 13, 2025). Strikes have occurred roughly every few weeks throughout 2025, including on June 15 (targeting an assassination attempt on the Houthi military chief), late July/early August (Hodeida port), August 24-25 (presidential palace and energy infrastructure), and multiple times in September. Given the Houthis' stated commitment to continue attacks ('our military operations supporting Gaza won't stop, God willing, unless the aggression is stopped'), and Israel's stated policy of imposing consequences, the cycle of Houthi launches and Israeli retaliatory strikes has been highly regular. As of November 2025, there is no ceasefire or diplomatic resolution between Israel and the Houthis.

- Times of Israel, 'IDF downs Yemen missile aimed at Tel Aviv; Houthis claim it had cluster bomb warhead' (Sep 13, 2025): https://www.timesofisrael.com
- AP, 'Israeli airstrikes targeting Iran-backed Houthis rock Yemen's capital' (Aug 25, 2025): https://apnews.com
- Times of Israel, 'IDF intercepts latest Houthi missile; 67th launched since March ceasefire collapse' (Aug 1, 2025): https://www.timesofisrael.com

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The strike must involve aerial bombs, drones, or missiles launched by Israeli forces that impact Yemeni ground territory (consistent with the ultimate question's definition of a qualifying strike). Intercepted missiles or drones that do not reach the ground do not count. If no such strike is confirmed by December 14, 2025, the question resolves No.

Yemen has been by far the most frequently struck country by Israel outside its own territory throughout 2025, with strikes occurring roughly every 1-3 weeks in a persistent tit-for-tat cycle with the Houthis. Whether this pattern of strikes continues through late 2025 is a strong leading indicator for whether it will persist into 2026. If Israel is still actively striking Yemen in the November-December 2025 timeframe, it would be highly informative that the conflict dynamic remains unresolved, making it very unlikely Israel strikes zero countries in 2026. Conversely, if strikes cease—perhaps due to a ceasefire, diplomatic agreement, or Houthi cessation of attacks—this would be a meaningful signal that 2026 could see zero strikes. This subquestion thus serves as a near-term indicator of whether the conditions that would lead to Israeli strikes abroad are still active heading into 2026.

question: 30-year mortgage rate below 6% by December 31?
description:

subquestions.question: Will the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield fall below 3.75% at any point between September 3 and October 3, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield is a key driver of 30-year mortgage rates. Mortgage rates typically track the 10-year Treasury yield with a spread that has historically ranged from about 150-300 basis points, though in recent years the spread has been elevated (around 250-280 bps). As of late August 2025, the 10-year Treasury yield was approximately 3.82-3.91%, and the 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 6.56% (Freddie Mac PMMS, August 28, 2025). For mortgage rates to fall below 6.00%, the 10-year Treasury yield would likely need to decline significantly — probably below 3.5% assuming the current spread, or below 3.75% if the spread compresses somewhat. A move in the 10-year yield below 3.75% in the near term would be an early signal that the yield environment is shifting in a direction consistent with sub-6% mortgage rates by year-end.

The 10-year yield has been influenced by Federal Reserve rate expectations, economic growth data, inflation trends, and geopolitical uncertainty. The Fed held rates steady through much of 2025, and market expectations for rate cuts have fluctuated. As of early September 2025, traders are pricing in possible rate cuts later in the year depending on economic data.

Sources:
- Freddie Mac PMMS (August 28, 2025): https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms
- FRED 10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10
- U.S. Department of the Treasury Daily Yield Curve Rates: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the daily 10-year U.S. Treasury Constant Maturity Rate (as reported by FRED at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10) closes below 3.75% on any business day between September 3, 2025 and October 3, 2025 (inclusive). If FRED data is unavailable, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Daily Treasury Yield Curve Rates (https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve) will be used instead. The question resolves No if the 10-year yield remains at or above 3.75% on every business day during this period. If neither data source is available for the entire period, other credible financial data sources (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters) may be used.
subquestions.rationale: The 10-year Treasury yield is the single most important driver of 30-year mortgage rates. For mortgage rates to break below 6.00% by December 31, 2025, Treasury yields would need to decline substantially from current levels. A move below 3.75% on the 10-year in the near term would indicate that economic conditions (slowing growth, falling inflation expectations, or Fed rate-cut expectations) are shifting in a direction that could push mortgage rates under 6% by year-end. Conversely, if the 10-year yield stays well above 3.75% in September, it would suggest that the path to sub-6% mortgage rates by year-end is more difficult. This subquestion thus serves as a meaningful early indicator — it tracks the underlying bond market dynamics rather than simply asking about mortgage rates on an earlier date.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The 10-year U.S. Treasury Constant Maturity Rate (FRED DGS10) must CLOSE below 3.75% on any business day between September 3, 2025 and October 3, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: FRED daily closing data or equivalent financial news reporting daily closes below 3.75%. Key entities: DGS10 rate; threshold: 3.75%; timing: any business day in Sep 3 – Oct 3, 2025 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) '10-year US Treasury yield September 2025' - to find all data points in the window; 2) '10-year Treasury yield below 3.75% September October 2025' - to find if the threshold was crossed; 3) '10-year Treasury yield September 11 2025 fell below 4%' - to find the lowest point; 4) 'Treasury yield 3.75 October 2025 lowest level' - to check near end of window; 5) '10-year Treasury yield lowest close September 17 2025 below 4 percent' - to verify the nadir; 6) 'US Treasury yield October 2 3 2025 level' - to check final days of window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: Sept 4 (~4.2%), Sept 8 (~4.06%), Sept 9 (~4.08%), Sept 10 (~4.04%), Sept 11 (~4.05%, briefly below 4% intraday per Barron's/Livemint), Sept 12 (~4.03%), Sept 16 (~4.06%), Sept 17 (~4.0% close, described as 'second lowest level of year' at 'just 0.010 percentage point above its 2025 closing low'), Sept 18 (~4.09%), Sept 19 (~4.11-4.13%), Sept 23 (~4.14%), Sept 29-30 (~4.13-4.16%), Oct 1 (~4.12%), Oct 2 (~4.087-4.13%). ALL data points are substantially above 3.75%. The Barchart data noted a 52-week low of 3.88% (not within this window). None of these data points are close to 3.75%.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The criteria require a CLOSE below 3.75%. The lowest close identified in the window was approximately 3.99-4.00% on September 17, 2025, per [Barron's](https://www.barrons.com/livecoverage/stock-market-news-today-091725/card/treasury-yields-shoot-lower-Pm0vMEdgj7wbmw2eBcly) ('the second lowest level of the year and just 0.010 percentage point above its 2025 closing low') and [Capital Spectator](https://www.capitalspectator.com/macro-briefing-18-september-2025/) ('The 10-year yield had briefly dipped below 4.0% during the previous session but closed at 4.09%' — this refers to Sep 17 briefly dipping below 4.0%). This is more than 24 basis points above the 3.75% threshold. No source reported any daily close below 3.75% during the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The lowest closing yield documented in the window was approximately 3.99-4.00% on September 17, 2025, still 24-25 basis points above 3.75%. There is no timestamp for any close below 3.75% because such a close did not occur.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (close below 3.75%) was found at any point in the window. All documented data points range from approximately 3.99% to 4.26%.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources (InstaForex, Capital Spectator, TalkMarkets, Barron's, Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance, CNBC, Morningstar) consistently report yields in the 4.0%-4.26% range throughout the window. evidence.step8_final_decision: The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield remained well above 3.75% throughout the entire September 3 – October 3, 2025 window. The lowest close documented was approximately 3.99-4.00% on September 17, 2025 — still about 24-25 basis points above the 3.75% resolution threshold. The question resolves No, with the window having closed without the condition ever being met.

question: Will Russia capture Bilytske by February 28, 2026?

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces capture or advance into the settlement of Bila Hora (located approximately 5 km south of Bilytske along the T0504 highway in Donetsk Oblast) according to the ISW map by February 14, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Bilytske is a settlement in the Toretsk area of Donetsk Oblast. Russian forces have been conducting offensive operations in the Toretsk direction throughout 2025, gradually pushing westward and southward through settlements in this area. Bila Hora is a nearby settlement along a key approach axis toward Bilytske; Russian control of Bila Hora or significant advances in that area would be a strong indicator of imminent pressure on Bilytske itself.

As of early January 2026, the ISW interactive map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) shows Russian forces have made gradual advances in the broader Toretsk-Kostiantynivka direction, with fighting reported near Bila Hora and surrounding settlements. DeepState (https://deepstatemap.live/) has reported Russian advances in this sector, with the front line shifting incrementally westward.

The Toretsk direction has been identified as one of the key challenging sectors of the front (Ukrinform, December 2025: https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3942876-key-challenging-sectors-the-current-situation-and-expert-assessments.html). Russian daily territorial gains in the Donetsk region have averaged several square kilometers per day in late 2025 (Interfax-Ukraine, October 2025: https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1035200.html).

Sources:
- ISW Interactive Map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
- DeepState Map: https://deepstatemap.live/
- Ukrinform (Dec 2025): https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3942876-key-challenging-sectors-the-current-situation-and-expert-assessments.html
- Interfax-Ukraine (Oct 2025): https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1035200.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-15 and 2026-02-14 (inclusive), the ISW interactive Ukraine conflict map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) shows Russian-controlled territory (shaded as 'Assessed Russian Control', 'Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine', or 'Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours') covering any part of the built-up area of Bila Hora, Donetsk Oblast (approximate center coordinates: 48.3855° N, 37.1870° E), and this shading persists through the next full ISW daily update cycle.

If the ISW map becomes unavailable, DeepState Map (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used as a fallback. If both sources are unavailable, a consensus of credible OSINT reporting may be used.

The question resolves No if no such shading appears on the ISW map covering any part of Bila Hora's built-up area by end of day (UTC) on 2026-02-14.

'Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine' shading does not qualify. Temporary map glitches do not qualify.
subquestions.rationale: Bila Hora lies along one of the key approach routes toward Bilytske from the south/southeast. Russian capture of or advance into Bila Hora would indicate that the front line is moving toward the specific building at 48.40731° N, 37.17956° E in Bilytske. If Russia has not yet reached Bila Hora by mid-February, it becomes much less likely that forces will have advanced the additional distance to capture the target building in Bilytske by late February. Conversely, if Bila Hora falls early, it signals rapid progress in this direction and increases the probability that Bilytske could be reached. This makes it a meaningful leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: ISW map shows Russian-controlled territory (Assessed Russian Control, Advance, or Gains in Past 24 Hours) covering any part of Bila Hora's built-up area (~48.3855°N, 37.1870°E) between Jan 15 - Feb 14, 2026, persisting through next full daily update cycle. Observable evidence: ISW daily updates, DeepState map changes, OSINT reports mentioning Russian capture of or advance into Bila Hora (village ~5km south of Bilytske, Donetsk Oblast, along T0504). Key entities: Bila Hora, Bilytske, Novyi Donbas, Pokrovsk front, T0504 highway.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Bila Hora Russian forces capture Donetsk 2026' - to find direct capture reports; 2) 'Bilytske Bila Hora ISW map Russian advance Donetsk' - to find ISW-specific reports; 3) 'Bila Hora Donetsk settlement Russian capture January February 2026' - to find any specific reporting; 4) 'Bilytske T0504 highway Donetsk Russian advance ISW 2026' - to find T0504 highway advances near Bilytske; 5) 'Russian forces advance Novyi Donbas Bilytske Pokrovsk direction February 2026' - to find advance direction toward Bilytske; 6) 'ISW Pokrovsk Bilytske Novyi Donbas Russian control captured February 2026' - to find ISW-specific Bilytske capture; 7) 'DeepState Bilytske Bila Hora Russian advance capture occupied 2026' - DeepState map reporting; 8) 'Bilytske captured occupied Russian Donetsk February 2026' - to find direct capture claims.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Multiple Ukrainian General Staff reports (Jan 30, Feb 2, Feb 9, Feb 13) mention attacks 'toward Bilytske' as a direction of Russian assault — rejected as this indicates attack direction, not capture. (2) Meduza article (Feb 11, 2026) states Russian forces 'are now pushing toward Rodynske, Novyi Donbas, and Bilytske' — rejected as indicating imminent advance toward, not capture of, Bilytske. (3) No report at all mentions Bila Hora specifically during the resolution window. (4) ISW report (Jan 26) mentions T-0504 highway advances, but in a different section (Kostiantynivka-Druzhkivka area, west of Stupochky) — rejected as geographically different from the Bilytske/Bila Hora area.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No source explicitly reports Russian forces capturing or advancing into the built-up area of Bila Hora, Donetsk Oblast (48.3855°N, 37.1870°E). [Meduza, Feb 11](https://meduza.io/en/feature/2026/02/11/ukraine-races-to-defend-a-key-zaporizhzhia-stronghold-as-a-second-russian-offensive-gathers-force-in-donbas-meduza-analyzes-the-latest-battlefield-developments) describes Russian forces 'pushing toward...Bilytske' (not Bila Hora, and not captured). [Ukrainian General Staff Feb 13](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/02/13/8020820/) lists 'Bilytske' as one settlement where Russian attacks were repelled on the Pokrovsk front. No ISW report in the search results mentions Bila Hora at all during this period. The criteria require explicit ISW map shading of Bila Hora, for which there is zero evidence.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp exists. No source reports Russian capture of or advance into Bila Hora at any point within the Jan 15 - Feb 14, 2026 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found. Bila Hora was not mentioned in any source as being captured or advanced into by Russian forces during the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: Multiple sources (Ukrainian General Staff, DeepState, Meduza) consistently describe Bilytske as a target/direction being attacked toward — not yet captured — through the end of the resolution window (Feb 13-14, 2026). Since Bila Hora is ~5km south of Bilytske, Russian forces would need to first capture or advance through Bilytske before reaching Bila Hora. The weight of evidence strongly suggests Bila Hora remained under Ukrainian control throughout the resolution window. No source — Russian, Ukrainian, or third-party — claims Russian control of Bila Hora during this period.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. All available evidence consistently shows that Russian forces were attacking toward Bilytske (not capturing it) during the Jan 15 - Feb 14, 2026 window, and Bila Hora (~5km south of Bilytske) was not mentioned in any report as being captured or advanced into by Russian forces. The resolution window closed on Feb 14, 2026 with no qualifying ISW map shading of Bila Hora being reported.

question: Trump enacts a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to establish a de minimis tax exemption on cryptocurrency transactions by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If the tax exemption only applies for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a standalone bill or amendment establishing a de minimis crypto tax exemption be formally introduced in either chamber of the U.S. Congress between November 30, 2025 and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The concept of a de minimis tax exemption for small cryptocurrency transactions has been a recurring legislative goal in 2025 but has not yet been enacted. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) proposed a de minimis exemption (transactions under $300, with a $5,000 annual cap) as part of her Digital Asset Tax Fairness Act, but the provision was stripped from President Trump's reconciliation bill in July 2025 due to revenue concerns (https://cryptonews.com/news/working-on-it-senator-lummis-backs-jack-dorseys-push-for-a-bitcoin-tax-exemption/). In October 2025, Lummis pledged to reintroduce the proposal in upcoming Senate sessions (https://decrypt.co/283927/dorsey-lummis-push-bitcoin-tax-relief-block-expands-btc-payments). Meanwhile, 66+ crypto organizations sent a letter to President Trump on November 20, 2025, requesting a $600 per transaction de minimis exemption through either executive or legislative action (https://www.coinspeaker.com/66-crypto-orgs-call-on-trump-for-tax-clarity/). The crypto industry has also been lobbying Congress directly, with the American Innovation Project hosting a private dinner with House Ways and Means Committee members on the week of November 17, 2025 (https://techstory.in/crypto-titans-court-d-c-in-push-for-sweeping-tax-overhaul/). The White House has signaled support for such an exemption through Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt's statements, but no formal bill or executive order has yet materialized. The U.S. Senate Finance Committee held a hearing on digital asset taxation on October 1, 2025, which was intended to build consensus before policy action (https://ambcrypto.com/u-s-senate-to-discuss-digital-assets-tax-reforms-on-october-1-details/). As of late November 2025, Congress is dealing with a short-term funding stopgap expiring January 30, 2026, and the legislative calendar is highly compressed before the holiday recess.

Sources:
- CryptoNews (Lummis backs de minimis exemption): https://cryptonews.com/news/working-on-it-senator-lummis-backs-jack-dorseys-push-for-a-bitcoin-tax-exemption/
- Decrypt (Dorsey, Lummis push for Bitcoin tax relief): https://decrypt.co/283927/dorsey-lummis-push-bitcoin-tax-relief-block-expands-btc-payments
- Coinspeaker (66 crypto orgs letter to Trump): https://www.coinspeaker.com/66-crypto-orgs-call-on-trump-for-tax-clarity/
- TechStory (Crypto lobbying push): https://techstory.in/crypto-titans-court-d-c-in-push-for-sweeping-tax-overhaul/
- AMBCrypto (Senate Finance Committee hearing): https://ambcrypto.com/u-s-senate-to-discuss-digital-assets-tax-reforms-on-october-1-details/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between November 30, 2025 and December 29, 2025 (inclusive), a new bill or amendment is formally introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives or U.S. Senate that specifically establishes a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions (i.e., exempting small crypto transactions from capital gains reporting below a specified dollar threshold). The bill or amendment must be assigned a bill number and appear in the Congressional Record or on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/). Reintroductions of previously numbered bills count only if they receive a new bill number during this window. Bills that merely reference crypto taxation in general without a specific de minimis exemption provision do not qualify. If no such bill or amendment is formally introduced during this window, the question resolves No. The primary resolution source is Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/); credible reporting from sources such as CoinDesk, The Block, or Reuters may be used as supplementary confirmation.
subquestions.rationale: For Trump to enact a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026, a legislative vehicle must exist — either a new standalone bill, an amendment to existing legislation, or an executive order. If a bill is formally introduced in Congress during December 2025, it signals active legislative momentum and increases the probability that such legislation could be fast-tracked or attached to must-pass legislation before year-end. Conversely, the absence of any formal bill introduction during this critical period would strongly suggest that the legislative pathway is unlikely to produce results before the December 31 deadline, leaving only the executive action route. This subquestion tracks a necessary (though not sufficient) precondition for the legislative pathway and provides meaningful evidence about the ultimate question's outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A new bill or amendment formally introduced (assigned a bill number, appearing in Congressional Record or Congress.gov) in U.S. House or Senate between Nov 30–Dec 29, 2025, specifically establishing a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions below a specified dollar threshold. Discussion drafts, circulated proposals, and pre-introduction documents do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'de minimis crypto cryptocurrency tax exemption bill Congress 2025' (Dec 2025 window) — to find primary candidates; 2) 'cryptocurrency small transaction tax exemption legislation introduced Congress December 2025' — to find any formally introduced bills; 3) 'Digital Asset PARITY Act bill number Congress.gov formally introduced December 2025' — to verify formal introduction of PARITY Act; 4) 'crypto de minimis tax exemption bill introduced House Senate December 2025 bill number' — to find bill numbers; 5) 'PARITY Act discussion draft not yet formally introduced bill number HR crypto December 2025' — to verify status; 6) 'Lummis crypto de minimis tax exemption bill 2025 Senate introduced December' — to check Senate activity; 7) 'Virtual Currency Tax Fairness Act de minimis crypto exemption 2025 Congress introduced' — to check existing bill reintroductions; 8) 'de minimis cryptocurrency bitcoin tax bill H.R. OR S. introduced Congress.gov December 2025' — to find formal bill numbers.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Primary candidate: Digital Asset PARITY Act, circulated around December 20-21, 2025 by Reps. Max Miller (R-OH) and Steven Horsford (D-NV). Contains $200 de minimis exemption for regulated stablecoin transactions. However, multiple sources confirm it is a 'discussion draft' not yet formally introduced. No other standalone bill with a specific de minimis crypto exemption was found formally introduced in this window. State-level legislation (Arizona SB 1044, 1045, SCR 1003) does not apply as it is state-level, not federal Congress. Senator Cynthia Lummis's previously proposed $300 de minimis exemption bill referenced was from July 2025, not the Nov 30–Dec 29 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The PARITY Act fails the formal introduction criterion. CoinDesk (a primary resolution source per the question) explicitly states: 'The bill is a discussion draft and has not yet been formally introduced as legislation.' [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2025/12/22/u-s-bipartisan-lawmakers-draw-up-tax-bill-with-stablecoin-and-staking-relief). Coingape also noted: 'The legislation has not yet been formally introduced.' [Coingape](https://coingape.com/rep-max-miller-unveil-crypto-tax-bill-includes-de-minimis-rules/). Cryptopolitan stated: 'The proposal, while not yet a formal bill...' [Cryptopolitan](https://www.cryptopolitan.com/us-tax-draft-stablecoins-staking-income/). question: Russia x Ukraine buffer zone agreement by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an agreement on an official buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "buffer zone" is defined as a neutral or otherwise militarily restricted area that lies between the territories of Russia and Ukraine and is intended to reduce or manage conflict between them.

A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. It is sufficient that the agreement explicitly demonstrates mutual intent to suspend offensive military action within the designated zone, for example, by stipulating the withdrawal of heavy artillery, armored vehicles, etc.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the buffer zone is established formally by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, announcements of a partial implementation, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A mutual agreement on a buffer zone will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of potential subsequent violations of such an agreement.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a broad consensus of credible media reporting stating an official agreement regarding a buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will Russia and Ukraine engage in any direct, officially acknowledged bilateral or multilateral negotiations (not merely back-channel or intermediary discussions) between October 13 and November 12, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-October 2025, there are no active direct negotiations between Russia and Ukraine on a ceasefire or peace agreement. The most significant recent diplomatic engagement was the Trump-Putin meeting in Alaska in September 2025, which produced no agreement. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov stated on October 8, 2025, that the momentum generated by the Alaska meeting for resolving the Ukraine conflict has 'already run out' (https://www.azernews.az/region/243893.html). Meanwhile, Western policy has been shifting toward enabling more aggressive Ukrainian defensive capabilities, with the European Parliament on October 9, 2025, urging that Ukraine be allowed to use Western-provided weapons to strike military targets on Russian territory (https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20251006IPR28601). A Foreign Affairs article from October 7, 2025, proposed a 'snapback' security framework as a postwar deterrence model, reflecting the assumption that any ceasefire would require robust enforcement mechanisms (https://www.foreignaffairs.com/ukraine/snapback-solution-ukraine). No buffer zone agreement can realistically be reached by December 31, 2025, without direct negotiations first commencing. The presence or absence of formal bilateral or multilateral talks in the near term is therefore a critical leading indicator.

Sources:
- Azeri Press: Russian Foreign Ministry statement, October 8, 2025: https://www.azernews.az/region/243893.html
- European Parliament resolution, October 9, 2025: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20251006IPR28601
- Foreign Affairs: A Snapback Solution for Ukraine, October 7, 2025: https://www.foreignaffairs.com/ukraine/snapback-solution-ukraine
- IBT: Tightrope of global conflict, September 30, 2025: https://www.ibtimes.co.in/tightrope-of-global-conflict-ukraine-reshaping-us-russia-strategy-industrial-mobilization-and-873849
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 13, 2025, and November 12, 2025 (inclusive), Russia and Ukraine participate in at least one direct, officially acknowledged negotiation session — whether bilateral or multilateral (e.g., mediated by the U.S., Turkey, or another party) — focused on ceasefire, peace, or conflict resolution terms. 'Officially acknowledged' means that both the Russian and Ukrainian governments (via presidential, foreign ministry, or equivalent senior official statements) confirm that such a meeting or negotiation round took place. Mere proposals, invitations, or statements of willingness to negotiate do not count; there must be confirmation that an actual meeting or formal exchange occurred. Back-channel contacts, Track II diplomacy, prisoner exchange negotiations, or grain deal discussions do not qualify unless they are explicitly framed by both sides as part of broader ceasefire or peace negotiations. Resolution will be based on official government statements from both Russia and Ukraine, or a broad consensus of credible international media outlets (e.g., Reuters https://www.reuters.com, AP News https://apnews.com, BBC https://www.bbc.com) reporting that such negotiations occurred. If no such negotiations are confirmed by November 12, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A formal buffer zone agreement by December 31, 2025, requires that direct negotiations between Russia and Ukraine begin well in advance. As of mid-October 2025, there are no active negotiations, and Russian officials have signaled that diplomatic momentum has stalled. If direct talks do not commence within the next month, it becomes extremely unlikely that a buffer zone agreement could be finalized by year-end. Conversely, if talks begin, this would substantially raise the probability of an agreement. This subquestion thus serves as a meaningful early indicator: its resolution to 'No' would strongly suggest the ultimate question resolves 'No,' while a 'Yes' resolution would be a necessary (though not sufficient) condition for the ultimate question resolving 'Yes.'

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Both Russia AND Ukraine must officially confirm participation in at least one direct negotiation session (bilateral or multilateral with third-party mediation) focused on ceasefire/peace/conflict resolution between Oct 13–Nov 12, 2025. Mere proposals or expressions of willingness do not count. Prisoner exchange coordination under existing agreements does not qualify unless explicitly framed as part of broader peace/ceasefire negotiations by both sides.

evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a qualifying event within the window exists. The last qualifying direct Russia-Ukraine talks occurred in summer 2025 (before Oct 13), and no new round occurred before Nov 12, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event found within window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources consistently confirm talks were stalled/paused throughout the entire Oct 13–Nov 12, 2025 window. Russia's side repeatedly claiming readiness while blaming Ukraine; Ukraine's side saying there were no substantive talks; Turkey offering to host a 'fourth round' (confirming none had occurred); US describing negotiations as 'clearly on pause'; Zelensky sanctioning Russia's lead negotiator (Nov 9) — all strongly consistent with NO new talks occurring. No contradictory evidence found suggesting a qualifying meeting occurred.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence consistently confirms that no direct, officially acknowledged bilateral or multilateral negotiation session between Russia and Ukraine focused on ceasefire/peace occurred between October 13 and November 12, 2025. The prior Istanbul rounds occurred in summer 2025; talks stalled before the window opened and remained stalled throughout. The window closed on Nov 12, 2025 with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield dip below 3.9% in 2025?
description:
