The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve cut its federal funds rate target at the December 17-18, 2025 FOMC meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions are a key driver of Treasury yields across the curve. A rate cut typically puts downward pressure on shorter-term yields and can also pull down longer-term yields like the 10-year Treasury, especially if it signals a more dovish policy trajectory. As of mid-November 2025, the 10-year Treasury yield stands around 4.10-4.12%, having briefly dipped to 3.95% on October 22, 2025 (its lowest closing level in over a year) before rebounding. The ultimate question asks whether the 10-year yield will dip below 3.90% before year-end 2025.

Market expectations for a December 2025 rate cut have been volatile. As of November 14, 2025, the probability of a 25 basis point cut at the December 17-18 FOMC meeting had fallen to approximately 50%, down sharply from over 95% a month earlier (InstaForex, Nov 14, 2025). Boston Fed President Susan Collins has emphasized caution regarding further easing, while other officials like Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee have focused on inflation concerns. The longest government shutdown in U.S. history, which ended on November 12, 2025, delayed critical economic data releases, adding uncertainty to the Fed's decision-making framework.

A December rate cut would likely push yields lower across the curve and increase the probability that the 10-year yield could breach 3.90% before year-end, while a hold would likely keep yields elevated near or above current levels.

Sources:
- InstaForex, "US 10-Year Yield Holds Advance," Nov 14, 2025: https://www.instaforex.com/news

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Federal Reserve announces a reduction in the federal funds rate target range at the conclusion of the FOMC meeting on December 17-18, 2025. This question resolves No if the Fed holds rates steady or raises rates. Resolution is based on the official FOMC statement published on December 18, 2025 (or the final day of the meeting), available at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm. The resolution window is between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-18 (the meeting conclusion date falls within one day of the subquestion end date). If the FOMC meeting is postponed beyond December 31, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A December Fed rate cut is one of the most significant near-term catalysts that could push the 10-year Treasury yield below 3.90%. The 10-year yield briefly touched 3.95% on October 22 when rate cut expectations were high, but rebounded as those expectations faded. If the Fed cuts in December, it would likely trigger a rally in Treasuries that could push the 10-year yield below 3.90%. If the Fed holds, yields are more likely to remain elevated above 4%, making a sub-3.90% reading much less probable. The current ~50% market-implied probability makes this a genuinely uncertain question with high informational value for the ultimate question. Two forecasters who disagree on whether the 10-year yield will breach 3.90% are likely to disagree on whether the Fed will cut in December, making this a strong crux.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: Federal Reserve announces a reduction in the federal funds rate target range at the conclusion of an FOMC meeting on December 17-18, 2025. Observable evidence: Official FOMC statement from December 18, 2025 announcing a rate cut. Key constraint: meeting must specifically be December 17-18, 2025 within the resolution window of 2025-11-17 to 2025-12-17.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Federal Reserve FOMC December 2025 interest rate decision' (find Dec 2025 rate decision); 2) 'Fed funds rate cut December 18 2025 FOMC meeting' (find any Dec 18 rate cut); 3) 'FOMC meeting December 17-18 2025 federal funds rate' (confirm if Dec 17-18 meeting existed); 4) 'Federal Reserve December 2025 FOMC meeting schedule calendar' (confirm the actual meeting schedule); 5) 'Federal Reserve rate decision December 10 2025 25 basis points cut' (confirm what happened at the actual December meeting).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event identified: Federal Reserve cut rates by 25 basis points on December 10, 2025 at the December 9-10 FOMC meeting, lowering the target to 3.50%-3.75%. REJECTED for resolution purposes because: (a) the meeting was held December 9-10, NOT December 17-18, (b) multiple sources confirm December 9-10 was the 'eighth and final' FOMC meeting of 2025, (c) no FOMC meeting occurred on December 17-18, 2025. After Dec 10, the next meeting was in late January 2026.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require a rate cut announcement at the FOMC meeting concluding on December 17-18, 2025. The actual December 2025 FOMC meeting concluded on December 10, 2025 [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/10/fed-meeting-today-live-updates.html), [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4852310-feds-interest-rate-decision-december-10-2025), [Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2025/12/10/fed-approves-third-straight-25-bps-cut-signals-a-cautious-path/). There was NO FOMC meeting on December 17-18, 2025. The criteria are not satisfied because the specific meeting date does not exist.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The actual FOMC meeting concluded on 2025-12-10T14:00:00 EST (2025-12-10T19:00:00Z) with a 25bps rate cut announcement. However, this is irrelevant because the question requires a meeting concluding on December 17-18, 2025, which did not occur.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no FOMC meeting occurred on December 17-18, 2025. The December 2025 FOMC meeting was held December 9-10, 2025 (concluded December 10). The next FOMC meeting after that was in late January 2026.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality sources confirm: (1) December 9-10 was the 'eighth and last' scheduled FOMC meeting of 2025 [Yahoo Finance, AOL Finance, Republic World]; (2) The Fed cut rates 25bps on December 10 to 3.50%-3.75% [Invezz, Seeking Alpha, NASDAQ, Global Times]; (3) After December 10, the next FOMC meeting was in late January 2026 [CoinCentral, AOL Finance updated Dec 10]; (4) No sources mention any FOMC meeting on December 17-18, 2025. The question's premise (December 17-18 meeting) does not match reality (December 9-10 meeting). No contradictory evidence found — all sources consistently confirm the December meeting was Dec 9-10.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The FOMC meeting specified in the question (December 17-18, 2025) did not occur. The actual December 2025 FOMC meeting was held on December 9-10, 2025, which concluded before the resolution window (2025-11-17 to 2025-12-17). Since no FOMC meeting took place on December 17-18, 2025, there could be no rate decision made at that non-existent meeting. The resolution criteria require a specific meeting on December 17-18, 2025 — which never happened. This resolves No. The condition became definitively impossible once the December 10, 2025 meeting concluded (confirming no further December meeting would occur), which is within the resolution window.

question: Lisa Cook out as Fed Governor by February 28?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Lisa Cook announces her resignation or otherwise ceases to be a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors for any period of time between December 8, 2025, and February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only official announcements of Cook's resignation or removal before her term is scheduled to end, made by either Cook or the Board of Governors, will qualify. Announcements from Trump or his administration will not alone qualify.

Temporary absences or attempts at termination which do not actually remove Cook from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be information from the U.S. Government however a consensus of credible reporting will also suffice.

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue a ruling or order by January 8, 2026, that effectively allows Trump's removal of Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve Board of Governors to take effect?
subquestions.background_information:
In August 2025, President Trump announced via Truth Social that he was firing Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook 'effective immediately,' citing alleged mortgage fraud. Cook refused to resign, stating that Trump has 'no authority' to remove her and that she would continue serving. Her lawyer, Abbe Lowell, filed a lawsuit in federal court to block the removal. The Federal Reserve Act allows removal of governors only 'for cause,' which has traditionally been interpreted as inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance. No president has ever successfully removed a Fed governor. The Supreme Court in late May 2025 suggested that Fed board members are insulated from at-will presidential firings. As of early December 2025, the legal battle is ongoing. Cook remains on the Board of Governors and continues to participate in Fed activities. The outcome of this legal dispute is a critical factor in whether Cook will actually cease to be a Fed Governor by February 28, 2026. If the courts rule in Trump's favor or decline to block the removal, it would dramatically increase the likelihood of Cook leaving the board.

Sources:
- Trump Says Fed's Lisa Cook Is Out 'Effective Immediately' (Investopedia, Aug 26, 2025): https://www.investopedia.com/trump-says-feds-lisa-cook-is-out-effective-immediately-11692180
- White House says Fed's Cook should 'go on leave' (Yahoo Finance, Aug 27, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/white-house-says-feds-cook-should-go-on-leave-until-fraud-accusations-are-resolved-193722498.html
- Fed Governor Cook won't leave, saying Trump lacks authority (Daily Sabah, Aug 26, 2025): https://www.dailysabah.com/business/economy/fed-governor-cook-wont-leave-saying-trump-lacks-authority-to-fire-her
- Inside Trump's attempt to put his mark on the Fed (CNN, Aug 28, 2025): https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/business/trump-fed-cook-firing/index.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 (inclusive), a U.S. federal court (district court, circuit court, or the Supreme Court) issues a ruling, order, or decision that effectively permits or upholds the removal of Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve Board of Governors — for example, by dissolving an injunction protecting her position, ruling that the president has authority to remove Fed governors, or declining to block the removal. The ruling must be reported by at least two credible major news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, CNN, NYT, Washington Post). If no such ruling is issued during the resolution window, or if all rulings during this period maintain Cook's position on the Board, this question resolves No. Court filings, motions, or oral arguments that do not result in an actual order or ruling do not count.

Resolution sources:
- PACER (Public Access to Court Electronic Records): https://pacer.uscourts.gov/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
subquestions.rationale: The key mechanism through which Cook could be removed from the Fed Board by February 28, 2026, is a court ruling that permits Trump's firing to take effect. Cook has firmly stated she will not resign voluntarily, and the Fed has deferred to the courts. If a court rules in Trump's favor in the near term (by early January 2026), it would be a strong leading indicator that Cook will indeed be out by the ultimate deadline. Conversely, if courts continue to protect Cook's position, it becomes very unlikely she will leave before February 28. This is the central crux on which forecasters disagreeing about the ultimate question would most likely diverge — whether the legal challenge succeeds or fails.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: A U.S. federal court (district, circuit, or Supreme Court) issues a ruling/order between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 (inclusive) that effectively PERMITS or UPHOLDS the removal of Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve Board — e.g., by dissolving an injunction, ruling president has removal authority, or declining to block the removal. Must be reported by at least two credible major news sources. Key entities: Lisa Cook, Federal Reserve Board of Governors, Trump administration, Trump v. Cook case.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve removal court ruling Trump' (Dec 9 2025 - Jan 8 2026) — to find any qualifying rulings; 2. 'Federal Reserve Board governor fired removed Trump 2025' — to find removal actions; 3. 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve court order injunction ruling December 2025 January 2026' — to find specific orders; 4. 'Supreme Court Lisa Cook Federal Reserve stay injunction dissolved ruling' — to find stay-related orders; 5. 'Lisa Cook remains Federal Reserve injunction court order December January 2026' — to confirm Cook's status; 6. 'Trump Cook Federal Reserve removal allowed court January 2026' — to find any ruling allowing removal; 7. 'Lisa Cook Supreme Court allowed fired removal ruling order January 2026' — to check specific claim in one source.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Supreme Court's prior order (October 2025) allowing Cook to remain pending January 2026 oral arguments — pre-dates resolution window. (B) Supreme Court oral arguments in Trump v. Slaughter (December 8, 2025) — one day before window, about FTC not Fed, not a ruling. (C) One article (The Hindu Business Line, Jan 6, 2026) stated 'The Court also allowed the firing of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, though the legality of for cause removal remains contested' — this appears to be an error/inaccurate summary. All other credible major sources consistently report Cook remained in office protected by court order throughout the window. (D) January 21, 2026 oral arguments in Trump v. Cook — scheduled AFTER the resolution window closes. REJECTED: Event (C) is contradicted by all other major credible sources; Event (B) is pre-window and about different case; Events (A) and (D) don't qualify as within-window rulings allowing removal.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No ruling within the resolution window that effectively permits or upholds Cook's removal was found in credible major sources. Multiple credible sources confirm throughout the window that Cook remained in office pending Supreme Court oral arguments on January 21, 2026 — well after the window closes: [Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2025/12/09/trump-reveals-litmus-test-for-next-fed-pick/) (Dec 9): 'she was reinstated after the Supreme Court allowed her to remain on the board until at least January 2026'; [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/five-supreme-court-rulings-change-america-11276144) (Dec 28): 'the Court ruled she must remain in office until arguments are heard in January'; [Raw Story](https://www.rawstory.com/supreme-court-donald-trump-2674840969/) (Jan 1): 'whose removal by Trump was blocked by the Supreme Court, which allowed her to remain in office while the case remains pending'; [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/03/federal-reserve-powell-face-challenges-in-2026.html) (Jan 3): 'A Supreme Court hearing on January 21, 2026, will determine whether Trump has the authority to remove Cook'; [Baltimore Sun](https://www.baltimoresun.com/2026/01/05/supreme-court-to-tackle-executive-power-social-issues-in-2026-term/) (Jan 5): oral arguments 'scheduled for this month' (January 2026, after window); [Korea Times](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20260107/with-trumps-tariffs-on-the-line-us-supreme-court-plans-rulings-for-friday) (Jan 6): confirms arguments on January 21. The one outlier (Hindu Business Line) appears to be an error or refers to possible future rulings — its claim is directly contradicted by all major credible news sources and by the consistent narrative that arguments were scheduled post-window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp of a qualifying ruling could be extracted because no such ruling was identified within the window. The resolution window closed at 2026-01-08T23:59:59Z with the case still pending and oral arguments not yet heard (scheduled for January 21, 2026).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found — no court issued a ruling allowing Cook's removal within the window. The first potential ruling opportunity would be after oral arguments on January 21, 2026, which falls outside the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence examined: The Hindu Business Line (Jan 6, 2026) contained a statement 'The Court also allowed the firing of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook.' However, this is directly contradicted by: CNBC (Jan 3, 2026), Raw Story (Jan 1, 2026), Cryptopolitan (Jan 3, 2026), Market Screener (Jan 5, 2026), Korea Times (Jan 6, 2026), Baltimore Sun (Jan 5, 2026), JD Supra (Jan 5, 2026), and multiple earlier December 2025 sources. The overwhelming consensus from credible major sources is that Cook remained in office throughout the window, protected by court order, with oral arguments scheduled for January 21, 2026. The Hindu Business Line statement appears to be an error, or may refer to the broader summary of the ongoing case context (perhaps conflating the Slaughter FTC ruling with the Cook Fed ruling) — it is not corroborated by any second credible major source as required by resolution criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: No. Throughout the entire resolution window (December 9, 2025 - January 8, 2026), all credible major news sources consistently reported that Lisa Cook remained in office at the Federal Reserve, protected by a Supreme Court order, pending oral arguments in Trump v. Cook scheduled for January 21, 2026. No court issued a ruling during the window that permitted or upheld her removal. The question resolves No, with the window closing at 2026-01-08T23:59:59Z without any qualifying event occurring.

question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between October 30 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a Russian drone or missile enter the airspace of a NATO member state (Poland, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, or any other NATO country) between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Throughout 2025, there has been a pattern of Russian aerial objects—primarily drones launched during strikes on Ukraine—entering the airspace of NATO member states. In September 2025, Polish radar logged 19 drone violations of Polish airspace, with several drones approaching four airports including Warsaw Chopin (https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/uk-news/nato-braced-more-russian-drones-30174898). NATO fighter jets intercepted three Russian MiG-31 aircraft that violated Estonian airspace in an incident described as 'unprecedentedly brazen,' prompting Estonia to request NATO Article 4 consultations (https://www.india.com/news/world/suicide-drones-ballistic-missiles-and-poland-in-tension-scramble-fighter-jets-with-nato-as-russia-attacks-7648505/). Denmark attributed drone incidents near Copenhagen and Oslo airports to a 'professional actor' and could not rule out Russian involvement (https://www.twincities.com/2025/10/02/other-voices-russias-airspace-incursions-are-a-test-for-u-s-allies/). Russian drones have also violated Romanian airspace. Poland has been scrambling jets repeatedly during large Russian barrages against Ukraine, with F-35s from the Netherlands assisting in defending Polish airspace (https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2025/09/03/ukraine-russia-aerial-assault/3001725360685/). The frequency of these incursions has been increasing as Russia intensifies its aerial campaigns against Ukraine, with strikes involving hundreds of drones at a time—705 aerial targets were launched in the October 29-30 barrage alone (https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3972456-ukraines-air-defenses-down-623-drones-and-missiles-out-of-705-launched.html). These airspace violations represent a key escalation pathway: each incursion tests NATO's response and raises the probability that a deliberate or accidental strike on NATO territory could occur.

Sources:
- WalesOnline: https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/uk-news/nato-braced-more-russian-drones-30174898
- India.com: https://www.india.com/news/world/suicide-drones-ballistic-missiles-and-poland-in-tension-scramble-fighter-jets-with-nato-as-russia-attacks-7648505/
- Twin Cities: https://www.twincities.com/2025/10/02/other-voices-russias-airspace-incursions-are-a-test-for-u-s-allies/
- Ukrinform: https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3972456-ukraines-air-defenses-down-623-drones-and-missiles-out-of-705-launched.html
- NewsGram: https://www.newsgram.com/world-news/nato-jets-scramble-amid-mass-russian-attack-on-ukraine
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive), at least one credible media report (from outlets such as Reuters, AP, BBC, AFP, or official statements from NATO or a NATO member state's military/government) confirms that a Russian-origin drone, missile, or military aircraft entered the sovereign airspace of any NATO member state without authorization. This includes both confirmed Russian military objects (drones launched as part of strikes on Ukraine that strayed into NATO airspace, or deliberate Russian aircraft incursions) and objects officially attributed to Russia by the affected NATO member state's government. Unidentified drones near airports that are NOT officially attributed to Russia by a government or NATO authority do not count. The airspace violation must involve the object physically crossing into the internationally recognized airspace of a NATO member state. Resolution sources include official statements from NATO (https://www.nato.int/), the Polish Armed Forces General Command (https://www.wojsko-polskie.pl/), the Estonian Ministry of Defence (https://www.kaitseministeerium.ee/en), the Romanian Ministry of National Defence (https://www.mapn.ro/), or credible international news agencies (Reuters, AP, BBC, AFP). If no such report is published by December 5, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Russian airspace incursions into NATO territory are the most direct precursor to an actual strike on NATO soil. The ultimate question asks whether a Russian drone or missile will impact the ground of a NATO member state. For such an impact to occur, the object must first enter NATO airspace. The frequency and nature of airspace violations is a strong leading indicator: more frequent violations, especially involving drones from active strike campaigns against Ukraine, increase the probability that one will fail to be intercepted and impact NATO territory. If airspace incursions continue or intensify in November 2025, forecasters should update upward on the probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes. Conversely, if Russia reduces strike intensity or NATO airspace violations cease, this would suggest lower risk. This subquestion differs from the ultimate question because an airspace incursion does not require ground impact—it is an earlier, more frequent event in the escalation chain.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between October 31 and November 30, 2025, a Russian-origin drone, missile, or military aircraft must have physically entered the sovereign airspace of any NATO member state without authorization, confirmed by credible media or official statements from NATO/government authorities with the object officially attributed to Russia. Key entities: Romania (NATO member), Russian military drones launched as part of strikes on Ukraine. Threshold: At least one credible official attribution to Russia.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Russian drone missile NATO airspace violation November 2025' - to find any NATO airspace violations; 2) 'Russian drone enters Poland Romania Estonia Latvia Lithuania airspace 2025' - to find specific country incursions; 3) 'Romania Russian drone airspace breach November 25 2025 official statement' - to find major confirmed event; 4) 'Romania drone incursion November 2025 defense ministry Mosteanu NATO fighter jets' - to confirm official attribution; 5) 'Romania drone fragments airspace November 4 2025 Galati Russian official' - to check for earlier events; 6) 'Romania drone airspace violation November 11 2025 fragments officially attributed Russia' - to confirm first occurrence in window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) November 10-11, 2025: Russian drone crashed ~5km inside Romania (Grindu/Tulcea County) during Russian strikes on Ukrainian Danube ports. Romania's Ministry of Defense confirmed fragments matched Russian military drones; Romania's Foreign Minister Oana Toiu explicitly attributed to Russia's 'war of aggression.' AFP filed an official report. (2) November 25, 2025: Two Russian drones breached Romanian airspace — the deepest-ever incursion (100+ km inland into Vrancea County). Romania's Defence Minister Ionut Mosteanu officially called it a 'Russian provocation.' NATO fighter jets (German Eurofighters and Romanian F-16s) scrambled. Drone crashed on Romanian soil at Puiesti. Fragment evidence recovered. Zelensky confirmed Russian drones entered Romania. Multiple Tier-1 sources: AFP, AP, Newsweek, Firstpost, Deutsche Welle, The Straits Times, The Independent, RFERL. Belgian drone incidents (Nov 1-5): Unidentified drones, NOT officially attributed to Russia by Belgian government → rejected per resolution criteria. DW article notes a 'drone attack on November 4 near Galati' but the AFP Romania incursion report is the first confirmed official attribution within window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: November 11, 2025 event EXACTLY satisfies all criteria: (1) NATO member state: Romania [AP](https://apnews.com/article/romania-drone-fragments-russia-ukraine-daa57cb972d1c6f7eb7b8cb7fb3fa93a); (2) Russian origin officially attributed: Romania's Ministry of National Defense 'confirmed the fragments originated from drones used in attacks on Ukrainian ports' and 'drone samples collected match those used by the Russian military' [AP]; Romania's Foreign Minister Oana Toiu stated 'Russia's ongoing war of aggression' as responsible; (3) Physical entry into sovereign airspace: drone fragments recovered 5km inside Romania's border [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/83N44CQ); (4) Credible official sources: AFP and AP both confirm based on Romanian Ministry of Defense statements; (5) Within window: overnight November 10-11, 2025. November 25, 2025 event also satisfies criteria as reinforcing/additional evidence [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/863F963), [AP](https://apnews.com/article/romania-drone-fragments-russia-ukraine-daa57cb972d1c6f7eb7b8cb7fb3fa93a), [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/russian-drones-breach-nato-airspace-in-long-range-strikes-ukraine-romania-11103426), [Firstpost](https://www.firstpost.com/world/romania-scrambles-nato-jets-after-deepest-ever-drone-incursion-calls-it-russian-provocation-13954019.html), [Deutsche Welle](https://www.dw.com/en/russian-drones-fly-undeterred-over-moldova-and-romania/a-74944321), [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/nato-scrambles-jets-after-deepest-drone-breach-yet-into-romania).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: November 11 event: Romania's Defense Ministry stated radar detected drone groups 'just after midnight on November 11, 2025' — approximately 2025-11-10T22:00:00Z to 2025-11-11T00:00:00Z UTC (Romania is UTC+2). AFP filed on 2025-11-11. Earliest exact timestamp: 2025-11-11T00:00:00Z (just after midnight Romania time). November 25 event: First drone detected at 6:28 a.m. local time Romania (UTC+2) = 2025-11-25T04:28:00Z per News18 report.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The November 11, 2025 event appears to be the first qualifying event within the window (October 31 - November 30, 2025). DW article mentions 'a drone explosion on November 4 near Galati' but no official NATO attribution was confirmed for that exact event in the sources reviewed. The November 11 AFP/AP reports are the earliest explicitly confirmed events with full official Romanian attribution within the window. No earlier qualifying event found within the window with official attribution.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources confirm: AFP (wire service, Tier-1), AP (Tier-1 wire service), Euronews, Yahoo News, Business Standard, Newsweek, Deutsche Welle, The Independent, RFERL all confirm the November 11 and November 25 events. Romania's own officials (Defense Ministry for November 11; Defence Minister Mosteanu explicitly calling it 'Russian provocation' for November 25) provide official attribution. Romanian Foreign Minister Toiu explicitly links the drone fragments to Russia's 'war of aggression' for Nov 11. NATO Secretary General Rutte previously acknowledged 'Russia's airspace violations' (Nov 13 Anadolu statement). No contradictory evidence disputing Romanian attribution. The only potential nuance is that Romanian President Dan described some incidents as 'accidental' — but this refers to unintentional straying into Romanian airspace, not disputing Russian origin, and accidental straying still qualifies per resolution criteria ('drones launched as part of strikes on Ukraine that strayed into NATO airspace').
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is YES. Multiple qualifying events occurred within the window: (1) November 10-11, 2025: A Russian drone (fragments confirmed by Romanian military to match Russian military drones) entered Romanian airspace ~5km inside the border, officially attributed to Russia by Romania's Defense Ministry and Foreign Minister. Reported by AFP and AP. (2) November 25, 2025: Two Russian drones breached Romanian airspace (deepest-ever penetration, 100+ km inland), officially labeled a 'Russian provocation' by Romania's Defence Minister Mosteanu. Drone crashed on Romanian soil. Reported by AFP, AP, Newsweek, Firstpost, multiple sources. The first qualifying occurrence in the window is the November 11 event, with the timestamp of just after midnight Romania time (approximately 2025-11-11T00:00:00Z).

question: Will Russia capture Drobysheve by February 28?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the intersection between Derzhavna Vulytsya and Slobozhanska Vulytsya located in Drobysheve, Donetsk Oblast,(49°02'31.4"N 37°43'54.7"E) by February 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.

The intersection will be considered captured if any part of the intersection is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by the specified date, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. “Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine” will not qualify.

question: Will BTS release any tracks in 2025?
description:

The track must be publicly released through major music platforms (e.g., Spotify, Apple Music, or YouTube) and must be announced via official BTS or BigHit Music channels. The release must include new musical content; re-releases, remasters, or compilations of previously released songs do not count unless they contain newly recorded material.

Tracks released by individual members, sub-units, or under any designation other than "BTS" as a group will not count toward resolution.

The resolution source will be any official BTS streaming or download site, e.g. Apple Music or Spotify.

subquestions.question: Will BigHit Music or BTS's official channels announce a specific release date for a BTS group track or album before December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

All reporting consistently points to a spring 2026 release timeline, not a 2025 release. However, there remains a possibility that BigHit Music could announce a surprise single, pre-release track, or move the album timeline forward into late December 2025. K-pop groups sometimes release pre-release singles or holiday tracks ahead of their main album comeback. If BigHit officially announces a specific release date for any BTS group track falling within 2025, that would be a strong signal that the ultimate question resolves Yes. Conversely, if no such announcement is made by late December, it becomes very likely the group will not release a track until 2026.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), BigHit Music or any official BTS channel (including the official BTS Twitter/X account @baborateam/@BIGHIT_MUSIC, BTS Weverse, or HYBE Labels YouTube) publicly announces a specific calendar date for the release of a new music track credited to 'BTS' as a group. Re-releases, remasters, compilations of previously released songs, or solo/sub-unit releases do not count. The announcement must clearly specify a date (not just a vague timeframe like 'spring 2026'). Resolution will be based on posts from verified official BTS or BigHit Music social media accounts (Twitter/X: @BIGHIT_MUSIC, @baborateam; Weverse; official YouTube channel HYBE LABELS) or official press releases reported by major outlets such as Soompi (https://www.soompi.com), AllKPop (https://www.allkpop.com), or Billboard (https://www.billboard.com).

All current reporting indicates a spring 2026 release, but a surprise pre-release single or accelerated timeline is not impossible in K-pop. An official announcement of a specific release date for a BTS group track would be the strongest leading indicator that a 2025 release is actually happening. If no such announcement occurs by late December, it becomes nearly certain the group will not release new music until 2026, effectively resolving the ultimate question as No. This subquestion captures a genuinely different observable event (the announcement) rather than just asking the ultimate question earlier.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: BigHit Music or official BTS channels (Twitter @BIGHIT_MUSIC/@baborateam, BTS Weverse, HYBE LABELS YouTube) publish a post between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 announcing a specific calendar date for a new BTS group track or album release. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout the entire window Nov 30 – Dec 29, 2025, there is overwhelming, consistent evidence from multiple major outlets that no specific release date was officially announced by BigHit Music or HYBE for a BTS group track or album. Vague references to 'spring 2026' or 'March 2026' from members in livestreams do not constitute a specific calendar date announcement from official BigHit/HYBE channels. The window closed on Dec 29, 2025 with no qualifying announcement.

Finishing in the top two means a loss in Week 1 would still give them a second chance via the semi-finals, but a Week 1 win would send them straight to the preliminary final and demonstrate the form needed to win the premiership.

The Raiders' home record in 2025 has been exceptional, winning eight of their last nine home games, and they have been confirmed as eligible to host a preliminary final at GIO Stadium if they finish top two. Their second-half dominance at home has been a key feature, having shut out opponents in the second half in three of their last four home games. However, questions remain about whether this young squad can sustain their form through the pressure of finals football, with analysts noting that the Raiders were originally tipped to finish last.

The 2025 NRL Finals Series is scheduled to begin on September 12, with Week 1 featuring two qualifying finals (1st vs 4th, 2nd vs 3rd) and two elimination finals (5th vs 8th, 6th vs 7th). The NRL Grand Final is scheduled for October 5, 2025.

question: Trump Crypto Pardon Parlay

subquestions.question: Will the Trump White House publicly announce or confirm that a presidential pardon for Changpeng Zhao (CZ) is under active formal review by November 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Changpeng Zhao (CZ), the founder of Binance, pleaded guilty in November 2023 to failing to maintain an anti-money laundering program at Binance and served four months in federal prison in 2024. He confirmed in May 2025 that he had formally filed a pardon application with the Trump administration. His initial pardon request was reportedly denied in March 2025, according to The Wall Street Journal. However, as of October 2025, multiple credible reports — including from Fox Business Senior Correspondent Charles Gasparino — indicate that renewed discussions at the White House are underway, with Trump insiders reportedly believing the felony case was disproportionate. Internal debate within the administration persists over the optics of granting such a pardon, given the Trump family's financial ties to the crypto industry through World Liberty Financial and a $2 billion deal involving Binance and Emirati firm MGX. Democratic senators, including Elizabeth Warren, have raised conflict-of-interest concerns. The ultimate question requires both CZ and Roger Ver to receive pardons by December 31, 2025. A public White House signal regarding the CZ pardon moving to formal review would be a strong leading indicator that the pardon is likely to be granted within the remaining timeline.

- Fox Business report on CZ pardon discussions: https://www.coinfomania.com/trump-pardon-for-cz-could-end-crypto-crackdown/
- Crowdfund Insider on White House deliberations: https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/10/trump-administration-might-be-considering-pardon-for-binance-founder-changpeng-zhao-report/

'Active formal review' means more than speculation or anonymous sourcing — it requires an on-the-record statement from an official government spokesperson or filing. Resolution sources include: the White House official website (https://www.whitehouse.gov), the Department of Justice pardon announcements (https://www.justice.gov/pardon), or transcripts of official White House press briefings. If no such official confirmation is made by 2025-11-17, the question resolves No. Credible mainstream reporting (e.g., Reuters, AP, NYT, WSJ, Fox Business) citing named administration officials would also suffice if no formal government press release is issued.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question requires both CZ and Roger Ver to receive pardons from Trump by December 31, 2025. Roger Ver's situation appears to be moving toward a DOJ settlement rather than a pardon, making CZ's pardon the more uncertain and pivotal component. As of mid-October 2025, reports suggest White House discussions are ongoing but no formal decision has been announced, and CZ was previously denied in March 2025. Whether the White House publicly moves CZ's pardon into formal review within the next month is a strong early indicator: if no official signal emerges by mid-November, the likelihood of completing both pardons by year-end drops substantially. This subquestion captures the pace and seriousness of the pardon deliberation process, which is the key bottleneck for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: An official, on-the-record statement from a named White House/DOJ/senior Trump administration official confirming that CZ's pardon is under active formal review OR has been approved/granted, between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17. evidence.step8_final_decision: The pardon for Changpeng Zhao was officially granted (signed October 22, 2025) and publicly confirmed by White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt on October 23, 2025 — both dates within the October 18 – November 17, 2025 resolution window. Available evidence shows: [Notebookcheck Nov 3](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Apple-signals-major-announcement-brewing-on-November-12-amid-rumours-of-AirTag-2-HomePod-mini-and-Apple-TV-4K-refreshes.1153913.0.html) — 'Apple is not replenishing stock for the Apple TV 4K... in the U.S.' [Notebookcheck Nov 1](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Apple-s-2025-26-launch-timeline-reportedly-leaks-new-Apple-TV-4K-HomePod-mini-2-AirTag-2-and-M5-Pro-Max-MacBook-Pros.1152894.0.html) — 'stock of the current Apple TV 4K has diminished across multiple regions.' [MacRumors Nov 12](https://www.macrumors.com/2025/11/12/where-are-new-homepod-mini-apple-tv-airtag/) — 'low HomePod mini inventory at Apple retail stores and complete stockouts at some resellers.' [heise online Nov 5](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Apple-TV-4K-and-HomePod-mini-New-models-still-in-November-11053947.html) — 'inventory levels have reportedly decreased in the US, though they remain in stock in German Apple Stores.' These reports indicate significant depletion/not replenishing but do NOT explicitly state the Apple TV 4K is 'out of stock' at Apple.com, showing '2+ week shipping delays,' or 'removed from sale.' 'Not replenishing' and 'diminished' describe depletion trends, not confirmed OOS status. 'Complete stockouts at some resellers' from MacRumors Nov 12 is ambiguous — context suggests it refers primarily to HomePod mini, and 'some resellers' ≠ Apple's own store. The criteria requires at least one of the three specific conditions, not just 'inventory shortages.' Criteria match is partial/ambiguous — 'not replenishing stock' is the closest match to 'removed from sale' but does not equal it. PARTIAL MATCH at best.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest explicit 'not replenishing stock' report is from 9to5Mac Nov 2, 2025 (citing Gurman's Power On newsletter), and Notebookcheck Nov 1, 2025. No exact timestamp beyond date-level is available. These are within the window (Oct 17–Nov 15).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence (pre-Oct 17) found in searches. The reports of inventory depletion begin in early November 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: (1) Apple TV 4K was available at Costco on sale at its lowest price ever Oct 28-31, 2025 — suggesting normal availability; (2) heise Nov 5 explicitly notes devices 'remain in stock in German Apple Stores'; (3) No new Apple TV was released on Nov 12 (confirmed by MacRumors, The Verge) — Apple did a holiday decoration refresh instead, suggesting the old model remained on sale; (4) MacRumors Nov 12 article's headline 'Where Are They?' implies the new model had NOT launched and the old one had NOT been removed from sale; (5) tvOS 26.2 MacRumors Nov 14 article discusses compatibility with 'all Apple TV HD and Apple TV 4K models from 2015 onward' with no mention of the current model being OOS. The balance of evidence suggests the Apple TV 4K had low/diminishing inventory and Apple was not actively replenishing it, but it had NOT been formally removed from sale, taken off Apple.com, or shown 2+ week shipping delays through Nov 15.
evidence.step8_final_decision: While there are multiple credible sources reporting 'inventory shortages,' 'diminished stock,' and Apple 'not replenishing stock' for the Apple TV 4K (Notebookcheck x2, heise, MacRumors, 9to5Mac, iGeeksBlog), none explicitly state the device is 'out of stock' at Apple's own online/retail store, showing '2+ week extended shipping delays,' or has been 'removed from sale.' The resolution criteria requires these specific, concrete conditions. 'Not replenishing stock' is directionally similar to 'removed from sale' but is qualitatively different — it's a supply-chain behavior rather than a confirmed consumer-facing unavailability status. The device was confirmed available at Costco as late as Oct 31, remained in stock in some markets per heise Nov 5, and no new Apple TV was released to replace it by Nov 15. The November 12 overnight refresh resulted only in holiday decorations, not product replacement. Given the strict resolution rules requiring explicit evidence and no inference, and given that the criteria match is ambiguous/partial rather than explicit, this resolves No.

subquestions.question: Will a federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida return an indictment or sealed indictment against John Brennan between November 27, 2025 and December 27, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late November 2025, the Department of Justice, under U.S. Attorney Jason Reding Quiñones in the Southern District of Florida, has issued grand jury subpoenas to former CIA Director John Brennan and numerous other officials connected to the 2016-2017 Russia investigation. The probe focuses on allegations that Brennan made false statements to Congress about the CIA's use of the Steele dossier in the 2017 Intelligence Community Assessment (ICA). House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan referred Brennan for criminal prosecution, accusing him of 'willfully and intentionally false statements.' As of November 11, 2025, at least 30 subpoenas had been issued to various figures including James Clapper, Peter Strzok, and Lisa Page. A grand jury order dated January 12, 2026 was filed in South Florida. Former FBI Director James Comey has already been indicted on similar charges and is set for trial in January 2026. Legal experts cited in reporting estimated roughly a 60-40 chance of a Brennan indictment. The grand jury process is actively underway, and the timeline from subpoena issuance to potential indictment could be weeks to months.

Sources:
- Townhall, "Report: DOJ to Issue Multiple Grand Jury Subpoenas As Part of John Brennan Investigation" (Nov 6, 2025): https://townhall.com
- Fox News, "Grand jury subpoenas Brennan, Strzok, Page in Trump-Russia probe" (Nov 7, 2025): https://www.foxnews.com/politics/grand-jury-subpoenas-brennan-strzok-page-trump-russia-probe
- The Independent, "Top prosecutor fires off subpoenas for 'conspiracy' case against Trump's enemies" (Nov 11, 2025): https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-subpoenas-brennan-strzok-page-conspiracy-b2655000.html
- Washington Examiner, "John Brennan and other officials subpoenaed over Trump-Russia inquiry" (Nov 8, 2025): https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/justice/3241000/john-brennan-officials-subpoenaed-trump-russia-inquiry/
- FrankNez Media, "DOJ Now Issues Subpoena to Former CIA Director John Brennan" (Nov 7, 2025): https://franknez.com/doj-now-issues-subpoena-to-former-cia-director-john-brennan/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between November 27, 2025 and December 27, 2025 (inclusive), credible reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., Fox News, AP, Reuters, Washington Post, New York Times, CNN, Wall Street Journal) or official U.S. government court filings confirm that a federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida (or any other federal district) has returned an indictment — whether sealed or unsealed — against John Owen Brennan (born September 22, 1955), former Director of the CIA. The indictment must be a formal criminal charge returned by a grand jury; a mere criminal referral, subpoena, or target letter does not count. If the indictment is sealed and its existence is confirmed by credible reporting citing law enforcement or court sources, that still counts. If no such indictment is confirmed by December 27, 2025, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- PACER federal court records: https://pacer.uscourts.gov/
- Fox News legal/politics coverage: https://www.foxnews.com/category/politics
- AP News: https://apnews.com/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Brennan will be federally charged by December 31, 2025. A grand jury indictment is the most direct precursor to federal charges. Given that subpoenas were issued in early November 2025 and a grand jury is actively convened, tracking whether an indictment is returned by December 27 provides a strong near-term indicator. If an indictment is returned by December 27, the ultimate question almost certainly resolves Yes. If no indictment materializes by then, only 4 days remain, making a Yes resolution on the ultimate question much less likely. This subquestion is slightly different from the ultimate question because it focuses specifically on the grand jury's action (indictment) rather than the broader concept of 'federal charges or criminal indictment announcement,' and its earlier deadline provides meaningful lead time for updating forecasts on the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition for Yes: A federal grand jury must have formally RETURNED an indictment (sealed or unsealed) against John Owen Brennan (former CIA Director, born September 22, 1955) between November 27, 2025 and December 27, 2025. Observable evidence: credible reporting from at least two major news outlets (or PACER court filings) confirming a grand jury indictment was returned — not merely a subpoena, criminal referral, or target designation. Key distinction: being a 'target' of an investigation is not an indictment.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'John Brennan indictment federal grand jury 2025' — to find any formal indictment. 2. 'John Brennan CIA director criminal charges indicted' — to find charging events. 3. 'John Brennan indicted formal indictment returned grand jury December 2025' — to narrow to the resolution window. 4. 'John Brennan charged criminal indictment Southern District Florida December 2025' — to find DOJ or court confirmation. 5. 'Brennan indicted arrested charged December 26 27 2025' — to check the final days of the window. 6. 'John Brennan grand jury investigation update status latest news' — to check for late-breaking developments.
evidence.step3_event_detection: All sources consistently report that as of December 22–24, 2025: (a) Brennan's lawyers confirmed he is a 'target' of a federal grand jury investigation in the Southern District of Florida (case NS 1840-020). (b) Brennan was subpoenaed by the grand jury. (c) Brennan's lawyers filed a letter to Chief Judge Cecilia Altonaga alleging 'judge shopping' by DOJ and requesting intervention. (d) There is NO reporting from any source — major or minor — that a grand jury indictment was formally returned against Brennan during the resolution window. Zero Hedge (Dec 19) explicitly noted 'No Arrests' and that the case was not expected to reach a grand jury indictment until early 2026. The freerepublic/Gateway Pundit article characterizes the situation as 'signaling a high likelihood of an imminent indictment' — future tense, not past.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The AP [apnews.com] confirmed Brennan is the 'target' of an investigation, not that he has been indicted. Bloomberg Law [news.bloomberglaw.com] reports on 'judge shopping' allegations in a grand jury proceeding — not a returned indictment. The Epoch Times [theepochtimes.com] confirms a 'grand jury proceeding' exists but no indictment was returned. The resolution criteria require a 'formal criminal charge returned by a grand jury.' Being a 'target' or receiving a 'subpoena' explicitly does not satisfy this criteria. No source from any outlet — including Fox News, AP, Reuters, NYT, WaPo, CNN, WSJ, or any other — reported that Brennan was formally indicted within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The most recent reporting (December 22–24, 2025) describes Brennan as an investigation target and discusses grand jury proceedings without any indictment having been returned. No timestamp of a formal indictment exists because no indictment occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence found. No indictment was returned during the resolution window (November 27 – December 27, 2025).
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checking multiple sources: AP (Dec 22), Bloomberg Law (Dec 22), Epoch Times (Dec 24), ABC News affiliate (Dec 23), WND (Dec 23), Gateway Pundit (Dec 23) — all describe an ongoing investigation and grand jury probe, with Brennan as a 'target,' but none report a returned indictment. Zero Hedge (Dec 19) explicitly noted 'No Arrests!' and that case was not expected to reach grand jury indictment stage until 'early 2026.' Brennan's own lawyers' actions (seeking to block judge assignment) imply the indictment had not yet been returned and they were trying to preemptively address procedural issues. No contradictory evidence (claiming an indictment was returned) exists.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence unanimously shows that Brennan was a 'target' of a federal grand jury investigation in the Southern District of Florida during the resolution window, had received subpoenas, and that his lawyers were fighting procedural matters — but no formal indictment was returned by a grand jury during November 27 – December 27, 2025. The resolution criteria explicitly state that 'a mere criminal referral, subpoena, or target letter does not count.' The condition for Yes was not met. The window closed on December 27, 2025, with no indictment confirmed.

Hunter has been emphatic that he wants to play both ways and would consider quitting football if forced to play only one position (Bleacher Report, Apr 15, 2025; ESPN, Apr 15, 2025). subquestions.question: Will Attorney General Pam Bondi publicly release or declassify previously sealed Jeffrey Epstein investigation files between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Attorney General Pam Bondi has faced pressure from both conservative activists and congressional Republicans to release Jeffrey Epstein investigation files held by the Department of Justice. As of October 2025, Bondi has refused to release these files despite demands. During her October 7, 2025 Senate Judiciary Committee testimony, the handling of Epstein investigation files was raised as a topic of discussion (https://www.dailybulletin.com/2025/10/07/watch-live-attorney-general-bondi-faces-senate-questions-over-political-pressure-on-justice-department/). The Trump administration has shown a pattern of using the DOJ to pursue politically motivated investigations, including indictments of James Comey and Letitia James (https://www.yahoo.com/news/trump-demands-prosecutions-doj-now-obeys-2025.html). Trump previously promised during his 2024 campaign to release the Epstein files, but as of late October 2025, no major release has occurred. Whether the DOJ takes concrete action on the Epstein files — such as a public release or declassification — could signal whether the administration is building toward a special prosecutor appointment or instead handling the matter through existing DOJ channels.

Sources:
- Daily Bulletin, October 7, 2025: https://www.dailybulletin.com/2025/10/07/watch-live-attorney-general-bondi-faces-senate-questions-over-political-pressure-on-justice-department/
- Yahoo News, October 10, 2025: https://www.yahoo.com/news/trump-demands-prosecutions-doj-now-obeys-2025.html
- MSNBC, October 19, 2025: https://www.msnbc.com/opinion/trump-network-acting-prosecutors-2025.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of Justice, Attorney General Pam Bondi, or the Trump White House announces a public release, declassification, or unsealing of previously non-public Jeffrey Epstein investigation files (including but not limited to grand jury materials, witness interview records, or internal DOJ memoranda related to the Epstein case). The release must consist of substantive investigative documents, not merely a press statement or summary. Resolution will be based on official DOJ announcements, White House statements, or a consensus of at least two credible major news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, NYT, Washington Post, CNN, Fox News) reporting on such a release. If no such release or declassification is announced within this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The release of Epstein files is a meaningful leading indicator for whether the Trump administration will appoint a special prosecutor. If Bondi releases the files, it could indicate the administration is moving toward more aggressive action on the Epstein case, potentially including a special prosecutor appointment. Conversely, continued refusal to release files suggests the administration is unlikely to escalate to a special prosecutor appointment. This is a different observable event from the ultimate question — it tracks DOJ engagement with the Epstein matter rather than directly asking about a prosecutor appointment — and would update forecasters' beliefs about the likelihood of a special prosecutor being named by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose:
The question requires: (1) Between Oct 31 and Nov 30, 2025 (inclusive), (2) The U.S. DOJ, AG Pam Bondi, or the Trump White House (3) announced a PUBLIC RELEASE, DECLASSIFICATION, or UNSEALING of previously non-public Jeffrey Epstein investigation files, (4) The release must consist of SUBSTANTIVE INVESTIGATIVE DOCUMENTS (not merely a press statement or summary), (5) Must be confirmed by official DOJ announcements, White House statements, or at least two credible major news outlets.

Key distinguishing factor: The resolution criteria requires an ACTUAL release of substantive investigative documents within the window — not merely legislation passing, a court motion being filed, or a promise to release documents within a future deadline.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Pam Bondi Epstein files release declassify 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find direct releases; 2. 'Jeffrey Epstein investigation documents unsealed DOJ November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find unsealed documents; 3. 'Epstein files actually released public documents November 2025' — to find confirmed releases; 4. 'House Oversight Committee Epstein documents released November 2025' — to find committee releases; 5. 'DOJ Bondi Epstein files substantive documents released published website November 2025' — to find published documents; 6. 'DOJ 33000 Epstein documents released February 2025 earlier release' — to check earlier releases; 7. 'DOJ Epstein files release December 19 deadline compliance published' — to check post-signing releases; 8. 'Epstein grand jury transcripts unsealed released court November 2025' — to check court-ordered releases.
evidence.step3_event_detection:
Several important events were identified:

1. HOUSE OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE released 33,295 pages of documents on September 2-3, 2025 — but this was BEFORE the question window (before Oct 31, 2025).

2. HOUSE OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE released ~20,000 new documents from Epstein's estate on November 12-14, 2025 — this IS within the window, but these were released by CONGRESS (the House Oversight Committee), NOT by the DOJ/AG Bondi/Trump White House. The resolution criteria specifically requires the 'U.S. Department of Justice, Attorney General Pam Bondi, or the Trump White House' to announce such a release.

3. The EPSTEIN FILES TRANSPARENCY ACT was signed by Trump on November 19-20, 2025 — this is a law mandating future releases within 30 days (by December 19, 2025), NOT an actual release of substantive documents.

4. DOJ filed MOTIONS in courts (Nov 21-25, 2025) to unseal grand jury transcripts in Florida and NY — these are COURT MOTIONS seeking permission to release, not actual releases. Courts had not yet ordered the release; Judge Engelmayer invited responses through December 3 and promised to rule 'promptly thereafter.'

5. Bondi stated 33,000+ documents 'had already been released' — but evidence indicates these were the September 2025 House Oversight Committee releases (provided by DOJ to Congress in response to subpoena), not a new direct public release within the Oct 31–Nov 30 window.

6. No evidence of a new, substantive, direct DOJ/Bondi/White House public release of investigative documents (posted online in searchable format) was found within the Oct 31–Nov 30 window.

Rejected as qualifying events:
- Congress's own document releases (not DOJ/Bondi/White House)
- The signing of legislation (mandates future action, not itself a release)
- DOJ court motions to unseal (not actual unsealing/release)
- Bondi's press conference statements (press statements, not document releases)
evidence.step4_criteria_matching:
The resolution criteria requires: 'announces a public release, declassification, or unsealing of previously non-public Jeffrey Epstein investigation files... The release must consist of substantive investigative documents, not merely a press statement or summary.'

Key evidence:
- [Trump Signs Epstein Documents Bill](https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5614523-donald-trump-jeffrey-epstein-files-bill-signed/) (The Hill, Nov 20): Trump signed a bill giving DOJ 30 days (until ~Dec 19) to release files.
- [DOJ Renews Bid to Unseal](https://www.business-standard.com/world-news/us-doj-renews-attempt-to-unseal-jeffrey-epstein-grand-jury-materials-125112500031_1.html) (Business Standard, Nov 25): DOJ filed motions in court to seek permission to unseal — courts have not yet ordered the release.
- [Pam Bondi 'Shaken'](https://www.inquisitr.com/pam-bondi-appeared-shaken-as-epstein-files-questioning-intensified) (Inquisitr, Nov 23): Bondi stated 33,000+ documents had already been released (via the Sept 2025 congressional release in response to subpoena), promised compliance but 'avoided confirming that all documents would be made public within the deadline.'
- [ABC News on FBI/DOJ](https://abcnews.go.com/US/fbi-working-doj-produce-epstein-files/story?id=127862663) (Nov 25): FBI working to 'see if they can produce anything more' — indicating no release yet occurred.
- [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexamer.com/news/white-house/3893265/trump-signs-epstein-files-bill-timeline-release/) (Nov 20): 'The DOJ has not yet specified how or when the documents will be released.'
- [Kash Patel](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/kash-patel-casts-doubt-full-183114623.html) (Yahoo, Nov 25): Casts doubt on full release by December 19 deadline.

No evidence was found that AG Bondi or DOJ formally published/released substantive investigative documents to the public (e.g., posted in searchable format online) within the Oct 31–Nov 30 window. The legislation mandated action by Dec 19, 2025, and the DOJ was still seeking court permission and assessing what could be released as of Nov 25-27, 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp exists for a qualifying event (an actual substantive DOJ/Bondi/White House release of Epstein investigative files) within the Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025 window. All evidence shows: (a) a law was signed Nov 19-20 mandating future releases; (b) court motions were filed Nov 21-25 seeking permission to unseal; (c) Bondi stated documents were already released (referring to the September 2025 releases); (d) the actual compliance deadline is December 19, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (actual public release by DOJ/Bondi/White House of substantive investigative documents) was found within the Oct 31–Nov 30 window. The September 2025 releases were before the window. The December 19, 2025 deadline is after the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Alternative interpretation considered: Could the Bondi/DOJ releases claimed in September 2025 (33,295 pages via House Oversight Committee) count? The committee released documents provided by DOJ via subpoena. However, these were: (a) released by Congress, not by DOJ directly as a public release; (b) occurred in September 2025, before the Oct 31 start date; (c) were reportedly ~97% already public material. The resolution criteria specifies 'the U.S. Department of Justice, Attorney General Pam Bondi, or the Trump White House announces a public release' — congressional committee releases do not satisfy this. Could the Trump bill-signing on Nov 19-20 constitute an 'announcement of public release'? No — the law gives DOJ 30 days to release; it is forward-looking legislation, not an immediate release. Bondi herself 'avoided confirming that all documents would be made public within the deadline' (Inquisitr, Nov 23). No contradictory evidence found that would establish an actual substantive document release by DOJ/Bondi/White House within the Oct 31–Nov 30 window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The window of Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025 closed without AG Pam Bondi, the DOJ, or the Trump White House releasing substantive Epstein investigative documents directly to the public. As of mid-2025, sponsors discussed attaching the bill to a continuing resolution or other must-pass legislation to accelerate passage (https://medium.com/@nickylee_82870/the-us-congress-has-made-a-major-move-a-bill-to-sanction-russia-may-pass-within-the-month-0ec9e65f2a23). Senate Majority Leader John Thune expressed hope for a floor vote before the August 2025 recess, but that deadline passed without action (https://www.forbes.com/sites/tylerroush/2025/07/15/us-senate-weighs-sanctions-bill-as-russia-stalls-peace-talks/). As of October 2025, the bill has not received a Senate floor vote. For the bill to be signed into law by December 31, 2025, it would need to clear both chambers and reach the President's desk — making a Senate floor vote in the coming weeks an essential precursor.

subquestions.question: Will the Atlas browser appear as a separately listed browser on StatCounter's global daily browser market share data with at least 0.5% share on any single day between October 24 and November 22, 2025?

For Atlas to reach 5% global share by December 31, 2025, it would need to surpass Edge and Firefox, which have taken years to build their current user bases. A key early indicator is whether Atlas even registers as a separately tracked browser on StatCounter within its first month, and at what level. OpenAI claims over 800 million weekly ChatGPT users, but converting those users to active Atlas browser users — especially when the browser is currently macOS-only — is a significant challenge. subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, on any single day between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive), 'Atlas' (or 'ChatGPT Atlas') appears as a separately listed browser entry on StatCounter Global Stats (https://gs.statcounter.com/browser-market-share#daily-20251024-20251122) with a daily global market share of at least 0.5%, using the following settings: Statistic: Browser; Checked: Desktop, Mobile, Tablet, Console; Region: Worldwide; Period: Daily. Only the first released data for each day will be considered; later revisions will not be used. If StatCounter data for this period is not available by December 1, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For Atlas to reach 5% global market share by December 31, 2025, it would need to show rapid early adoption. If it does reach 0.5% quickly, that signals extraordinary adoption momentum that could potentially scale further with Windows and mobile launches. evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Atlas (or ChatGPT Atlas) must appear as a SEPARATELY listed browser entry on StatCounter Global Stats with at least 0.5% global daily browser market share on any day between Oct 24 - Nov 22, 2025. Key entities: StatCounter, Atlas/ChatGPT Atlas, 0.5% threshold, daily global market share.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Atlas browser market share StatCounter 2025' — to find direct StatCounter data mentions; 2) 'ChatGPT Atlas browser launch release 2025' — to understand scope/scale; 3) 'Atlas browser StatCounter market share percentage 2025' — looking for explicit percentage data; 4) 'ChatGPT Atlas browser adoption users downloads growth November 2025' — to find usage data; 5) 'Atlas browser macOS only Windows launch date market share percentage'; 6) 'StatCounter browser market share new browser listed 2025'; 7) 'Atlas browser market share percentage global ranking browser wars November 2025'; 8) 'ChatGPT Atlas StatCounter listed browser share data'
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events found confirming Atlas appearing on StatCounter as a separately listed browser with ≥0.5% share. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found matching the resolution criteria. No news article or data report states that Atlas appeared as a separately listed browser on StatCounter global stats with ≥0.5% daily share during Oct 24 - Nov 22, 2025. The browser was macOS-only throughout the window [Android Police](https://www.androidpolice.com/chatgpt-atlas-browser-makes-its-debut/), [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/openai-s-chatgpt-atlas-ai-browser-new-features-macos-125112000763_1.html), [adworld.ie](https://www.adworld.ie/2025/11/21/opinion-get-ready-to-target-the-robots/). (2) Could Atlas be Chromium-based and still show as 'Atlas'? — Possible if the user-agent string identifies as 'Atlas', but no news article mentions this occurring. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout the entire resolution window (Oct 24 - Nov 22, 2025), Atlas/ChatGPT Atlas was: (1) macOS-only, severely limiting its potential global market share across all devices; (2) a newly launched browser that even optimistic analysts said would struggle to gain significant share quickly; (3) never mentioned in any StatCounter data report as a separately listed browser with measurable market share; (4) a Chromium-based browser that StatCounter may classify differently. The window closed on Nov 22, 2025 without a qualifying event.

subquestions.question: Will credible media report that Marc-André ter Stegen has been cleared for full training (without restrictions) by Barcelona's medical staff by January 3, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Marc-André ter Stegen suffered a serious knee injury (patellar tendon rupture) in September 2024 during a La Liga match against Villarreal, which ruled him out for the remainder of the 2024-25 season. His recovery timeline was estimated at approximately 7-10 months. As of late 2025, ter Stegen has been working through rehabilitation. According to an October 2025 Sports Illustrated article, Barcelona were reportedly willing to loan ter Stegen out in January, suggesting that at that time there was an expectation he might be fit enough to play but possibly surplus to Barcelona's immediate plans. Whether ter Stegen has been fully cleared for training is a crucial indicator of whether he could realistically complete a transfer during the winter window — a player who is not yet medically cleared is far less likely to pass a medical and sign with a new club.

- Sports Illustrated, "Transfer Rumors: Man Utd's €120 Million Double Swoop; Real Madrid Propose Caicedo Swap" (2025-10-24): https://www.si.com/
- BBC Sport coverage of ter Stegen's injury (September 2024): https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cd7dl12r4p1o

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 (inclusive), at least two credible sports media sources (e.g., ESPN, BBC Sport, Marca, Sport, Mundo Deportivo, The Athletic, Sky Sports, or official FC Barcelona communications) report that Marc-André ter Stegen has been cleared for full, unrestricted first-team training by Barcelona's medical staff. Reports of partial training, individual training, or training with restrictions do not count. If no such reports appear by 2026-01-03, or if reports are ambiguous or contradictory, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A player's fitness status is a critical prerequisite for any transfer. If ter Stegen has not been cleared for full training by early January 2026, it is extremely unlikely he could pass a medical examination at a new club and complete a transfer before the January window closes. Conversely, if he is fully fit, this dramatically increases the probability that one of the reportedly interested clubs (Chelsea, Manchester United, Newcastle, Tottenham, West Ham per the October 2025 reports) could finalize a deal. This subquestion captures a different observable event — medical clearance — rather than simply asking about the transfer itself with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: At least two credible sports media sources (ESPN, BBC, Marca, Sport, Mundo Deportivo, The Athletic, Sky Sports, or official FC Barcelona communications) must explicitly report that ter Stegen was cleared for full, unrestricted first-team training by Barcelona's medical staff between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03. Reports of partial, individual, or restricted training do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'ter Stegen cleared full training Barcelona medical staff 2025' - to find direct clearance reports; 2) 'Marc-André ter Stegen injury recovery update December 2025' - to find recovery timeline; 3) 'ter Stegen full training unrestricted Barcelona cleared December 2025' - for specific language match; 4) 'ter Stegen medical clearance Barcelona squad return first team December 2025' - for squad clearance reports; 5) 'ter Stegen fully fit training restrictions Barcelona medical staff 2025' - to check for restrictions still in place.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key candidate events: (1) Dec 4: Mundo Deportivo/Yahoo Sports Canada reports ter Stegen 'participated in several training sessions, including group work' and medical clearance expected 'next week' - prospective, not yet cleared. (2) Dec 7: Mundo Deportivo via Yahoo Sports reports he 'has now resumed full training, with a medical clearance expected' - still prospective. (3) Dec 9: Multiple sources report 'After training with the team for a week and receiving medical clearance, ter Stegen is back in the squad' - medical clearance confirmed. (4) Dec 13: Sources confirm 'previously received medical clearance for the midweek game against Eintracht Frankfurt.' (5) Dec 14: Mundo Deportivo states he is 'nearing full fitness' - suggests not yet fully cleared as of Dec 14. (6) Dec 17-18: AS/Yahoo Sports report Flick's decision was to 'publicly confirm ter Stegen's full recovery'; Yahoo Sports Canada article says ter Stegen 'showed full recovery.' evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require 'cleared for full, unrestricted first-team training by Barcelona's medical staff.' The Dec 9 [Yahoo Sports Canada](https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/official-barcelona-squad-list-face-121500450.html) article states 'After training with the team for a week and receiving medical clearance, ter Stegen is back in the squad' — this implies group first-team training and medical clearance, reported by multiple sources including [Yahoo Sports](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/barcelona-name-squad-face-eintracht-142000608.html) and [Sports Illustrated](https://www.si.com/soccer/hansi-flick-marc-andre-ter-stegen-saga-goalkeeper-recovery). The Dec 17-18 articles from [Yahoo Sports](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/hansi-flick-strategy-behind-handing-120700891.html) and [Yahoo Sports Canada](https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/barcelona-board-left-astonished-hansi-213000653.html) state his 'full recovery' was confirmed. However, none use the exact phrase 'cleared for full, unrestricted first-team training without restrictions.' The reports use 'medical clearance' for squad inclusion, 'full recovery,' and demonstrate his actual competitive match participation (Copa del Rey start Dec 17). The key ambiguity is whether 'medical clearance' for squad/match inclusion equals 'cleared for full, unrestricted first-team training.' The Dec 14 article still says 'nearing full fitness,' creating some contradiction. However, by Dec 9 (confirmed squad), and most clearly by Dec 17 (competitive start), full training clearance is functionally confirmed by multiple sources.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest evidence of medical clearance enabling full group training and squad inclusion: December 9, 2025 (multiple sources published on 2025-12-09 confirm medical clearance and squad inclusion following one week of group training).
