Kupiansk is ~15-20km from Borova (49.37°N, 37.62°E), making Kucherivka well within 25km radius. However, the critical requirement is ISW MAP shading, and ISW was notably skeptical of Russian claims in this area. Novoplatonivka (Dec 16): [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2059419) reported as captured; [Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/international/russia-wins-novoplatonovka-zelensky-digs-his-own-grave-as-ukrainian-frontlines-crumbles/videoshow/126033865.cms) noted Russian forces 'advancing toward Borovaya' after Novoplatonivka capture - this directly implicates proximity to Borova. The ISW assessment from December 15 [Charter97](https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/12/16/666815/) confirming Ukrainian counteroffensive with Ukrainian forces 'liberating several settlements' complicates this, as the balance of the ISW map during this period is hard to definitively pin down from news alone. Critically, the ISW noted that by Dec 14-15, Russian forces 'likely do NOT hold Petropavlovka.' But for Kucherivka (east of Kupiansk) and Novoplatonivka (south of Kupyansk, toward Borova), the dynamics were different.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Kucherivka: December 7, 2025 (Russian MoD announcement, confirmed by multiple sources). Novoplatonivka: December 16, 2025 (Russian MoD announcement, TASS). Both fall within the window (2025-11-28 to 2025-12-21). However, the ISW map-specific confirmation is not directly available as we cannot access the ISW ArcGIS story map directly.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest qualifying event within the window appears to be Kucherivka on December 7, 2025. Ukrainian General Staff reports from December 3 mentioned fighting near Petropavlivka, Pishchane, and Nova Kruhliakivka (within 25km of Borova), suggesting combat was ongoing without confirmed captures. No earlier confirmed capture with ISW map reflection was found.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: (1) ISW December 15 said Russian forces 'likely do NOT hold Petropavlovka' - but this is about a different settlement than Kucherivka; (2) Ukrainian counteroffensive was ongoing with Ukraine gaining 90% of Kupiansk by December 17-19; (3) ISW's overall assessment for this period showed skepticism about Russian claims. However: (1) Kucherivka is east of Kupiansk (not the same contested area as northwest settlements); (2) Novoplatonivka was specifically tied to advances 'toward Borova' per Times of India; (3) Multiple non-Russian sources (Anadolu Agency, Reuters/Market Screener) confirmed Kucherivka capture on December 7. The ISW does generally map Russian gains in the Kupyansk direction, and these settlements east/south of Kupiansk were separate from the northwestern area where Ukraine was counterattacking. The ISW's year-end assessment by Belousov noted 'The liberation of Kupyansk is expected to expand security' implying this was considered Russian-held by Russian sources, but ISW's own maps showed a contested situation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence strongly suggests that Russian forces did capture at least one new settlement within 25km of Borova during the window: Kucherivka (~5km east of Kupiansk, within 25km of Borova) was captured December 7, 2025, and Novoplatonivka (described as advancing toward Borovaya/Borova) was captured December 16, 2025. Both are within the resolution window. The Russian Ministry of Defense claims, confirmed by multiple international news outlets (not just Russian state media), and the geographic location (within 25km of Borova per the Kupiansk-axis focus) strongly support a Yes resolution. While we cannot directly access the ISW ArcGIS map to verify the exact shading, the ISW's pattern of reflecting confirmed Russian territorial gains (even when disputed by Ukraine) in their daily assessments, combined with multiple sources noting these captures were real (unlike more disputed claims like Kupiansk city center), supports resolution as Yes. However, the key uncertainty is whether the ISW map specifically reflected these gains or whether the Ukrainian counteroffensive dynamics prevented ISW from shading them. Given the ISW's December 15 report confirming Ukrainian counteroffensives were taking back settlements near Kupiansk (and geolocation contradicting Russian claims about Petropavlovka specifically), but NOT contradicting the Kucherivka capture (which was east of Kupiansk, outside the counteroffensive focus), it appears Kucherivka's capture was reflected on the ISW map. The resolution is Yes, with the earliest qualifying event being Kucherivka on December 7, 2025.

question: Will Ukraine agree to cede territory to Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede any territory under its control at the time of the agreement is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. 

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine and Russia announce the start of formal, direct bilateral peace negotiations (or negotiations mediated by a third party with both sides at the table) between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
For Ukraine to agree to cede territory to Russia by end of 2025, a necessary precursor is that some form of structured negotiations between the two sides must be underway or announced. As of late September 2025, no formal bilateral peace talks have been announced. Diplomatic activity has been intense but indirect: the US has been engaging Russia and Ukraine separately, European allies held a 26-nation meeting in Paris on September 4, 2025, to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine (https://www.telanganatoday.com/russia-has-provided-fresh-evidence-of-its-territorial-ambitions-in-ukraine), and various proposals for territorial arrangements have been floated in the media. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy reversed his earlier openness to ceding Russian-held territory in late September 2025, stating 'We will never recognize these territories that are temporarily occupied by Russia' (https://www.infowars.com/posts/zelensky-flip-flops-will-not-cede-territory-to-russia/). Russia has maintained maximalist demands, insisting Ukraine cede five regions and halt mobilization (https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-which-territorial-concessions-are-being-discussed/a-70507839). The Kremlin has also signaled interest in claiming Odesa and Mykolaiv regions based on a map seen in a briefing by General Staff chief Valery Gerasimov in August 2025 (https://www.telanganatoday.com/russia-has-provided-fresh-evidence-of-its-territorial-ambitions-in-ukraine). Without formal negotiations beginning, a territorial agreement by year-end is essentially impossible.

Sources:
- Telangana Today: https://www.telanganatoday.com/russia-has-provided-fresh-evidence-of-its-territorial-ambitions-in-ukraine
- Deutsche Welle: https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-which-territorial-concessions-are-being-discussed/a-70507839
- InfoWars (Zelensky reversal): https://www.infowars.com/posts/zelensky-flip-flops-will-not-cede-territory-to-russia/
- Investing.com (peace plan): https://za.investing.com/news/world-news/ukraine-may-cede-russianheld-territory-in-peace-plan--telegraph-93CH-3873457
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), Ukraine and Russia publicly announce or confirm that they have agreed to begin formal bilateral peace negotiations (either direct talks or talks mediated by a third party such as the US, Turkey, or another country, where both Ukrainian and Russian delegations participate or are confirmed to participate in the same structured negotiation process). The announcement must come from official Ukrainian and/or Russian government sources, or be confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, AFP). Informal back-channel communications, shuttle diplomacy where a mediator meets each side separately, or unilateral statements of willingness to negotiate do not count. The negotiations need not have actually commenced by October 31 — a confirmed, mutual announcement that formal talks will take place is sufficient. If no such announcement is made by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- AP News: https://apnews.com
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- Official Ukrainian Presidential website: https://www.president.gov.ua/en
- Kremlin official website: http://en.kremlin.ru
subquestions.rationale: Formal bilateral negotiations are a necessary precondition for any territorial agreement by end of 2025. If no structured talks are announced or confirmed in October, it becomes extremely unlikely that Ukraine would agree to cede territory within the remaining two months of the year, given the complexity of such negotiations and the need for constitutional/political processes on the Ukrainian side. Conversely, if formal talks are announced, it would significantly raise the probability of a deal — or at least a framework agreement — by year-end. This subquestion is a strong leading indicator because it tracks a concrete, observable precursor event rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline. Two forecasters who disagree on whether Ukraine will cede territory by year-end are very likely to update their positions based on whether formal negotiations have been announced.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Both Ukraine and Russia publicly announce/confirm agreement to begin formal bilateral peace negotiations (direct or mediated with both delegations at the same table). Not qualifying: shuttle diplomacy (mediator meets each side separately), unilateral willingness statements, back-channel contacts. The announcement must come from official government sources or confirmed by credible international outlets.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Ukraine Russia peace negotiations formal talks October 2025' (to find any formal talks announced); 2) 'Ukraine Russia bilateral peace talks announcement 2025' (broader search); 3) 'Ukraine Russia direct peace talks confirmed agreed October 2025 formal negotiations' (to check for confirmed agreements); 4) 'Trump Putin Budapest summit Ukraine Zelensky peace deal October 2025' (to assess Budapest summit prospects); 5) 'Ukraine Russia formal peace talks confirmed agreed October 2025' (last 10 days of October); 6) 'Trump Putin call Ukraine ceasefire negotiations late October 2025' (late October activities).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Trump-Putin phone call Oct 16, agreeing to a Budapest summit — REJECTED: this was a US-Russia summit, not a Ukraine-Russia formal talks agreement; (2) Trump-Zelensky meeting Oct 17-18 — REJECTED: this was US-Ukraine bilateral, not formal Ukraine-Russia negotiations; (3) Budapest summit planned — REJECTED: the Budapest summit was postponed/cancelled by Oct 21-22 (White House confirmed 'no plans in immediate future'); (4) Kremlin Oct 24 complaining about Ukraine delaying direct talks — REJECTED: this indicates talks are NOT happening; (5) Trump-Putin phone call Oct 28 — REJECTED: Trump called for Ukraine-Russia direct talks but Putin only offered to draft a 'memorandum on a possible future peace agreement,' no mutual agreement reached; (6) Zelensky Oct 27-28 saying Ukraine working on ceasefire plan in 10 days — REJECTED: this is preparatory work, not a confirmed agreement with Russia to negotiate; (7) Istanbul talks mentioned earlier in 2025 (three rounds through August) but described as 'on pause' with no response from Kyiv to Russian proposals.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that matches the criteria: (1) [TASS Oct 16](https://tass.com/world/2031223) notes formal talks between Ukraine and Russia have been 'on pause' with communications channels 'active despite a current pause in formal talks'; (2) [Medium Oct 22](https://medium.com/@rajk100/peace-talks-collapse-new-proposal-to-end-russias-war-2a7580a05951) explicitly states 'As of October 22, 2025, no formal tripartite meeting has been confirmed'; (3) [RT Oct 24](https://www.rt.com/russia/626913-kremlin-direct-talks-ukraine) Kremlin says Ukraine is behind 'unduly long' delay in direct peace negotiations; (4) [AP Oct 23](https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-europe-us-sanctions-f9d98cd011533b6f1c071ea2cef9f2d9) reports EU/US sanctions designed to 'pressure Putin into peace negotiations' — indicating no agreement yet; (5) [tfiglobalnews Oct 26](https://tfiglobalnews.com/2025/10/21/usa-confirms-cancellation-of-second-trump-putin-summit-in-hungary-amid-stalled-ukraine-peace-efforts/) confirms Budapest summit cancelled; (6) [UDN Oct 28](https://city.udn.com/2976/7210328?raid=7287505) Trump-Putin call Oct 28: Trump said negotiations must happen directly, but 'Putin's response was more cautious, indicating only readiness to draft a memorandum on a possible future peace agreement'; (7) [RT Oct 26](https://www.rt.com/russia/626985-kremlin-peskov-trump-ukraine-peace-efforts) Peskov stated 'peace negotiations are currently on hold due to Kyiv and its European allies showing no interest in resuming talks.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. The Budapest summit planned for ~Oct 28-30 was cancelled by Oct 21-22. The Trump-Putin phone call of Oct 28 produced no mutual agreement to start formal Ukraine-Russia talks. Zelensky's ceasefire plan was announced as a 7-10 day development process starting Oct 27-28, with no Russian acceptance. The question window closes Oct 31, 2025, at 23:59 UTC — no qualifying event occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event was found at all within the October 1-31, 2025 window. The prior rounds of direct talks (three rounds through Istanbul/Alaska, last in August 2025) were before the window and were acknowledged to be 'on pause' with no resumption agreed upon during October 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove No resolution: Searched specifically for any formal Ukraine-Russia talks announcement, any confirmed joint participation, any tripartite format confirmation. All evidence consistently shows: (a) talks are 'on pause'; (b) Budapest summit cancelled; (c) Trump-Putin Oct 28 call produced no mutual agreement; (d) Kremlin blaming Ukraine for delays; (e) Zelensky preparing ceasefire plan but Russia not accepting; (f) multiple sources confirm no formal meeting confirmed as of late October. No contradictory evidence found. The evidence uniformly supports a No resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout October 2025: formal Ukraine-Russia peace talks remained on pause from the previous Istanbul rounds (last in August 2025); the Budapest summit (Trump-Putin bilateral) was cancelled/postponed around Oct 21-22; there was no announcement of formal bilateral Ukraine-Russia negotiations (direct or mediated) with both delegations confirmed at the same table; Trump's Oct 28 call with Putin only produced vague commitments; Zelensky's ceasefire plan was in preparation without Russian acceptance. The October 31 deadline passed without the required mutual announcement.

question: Will 2025 be the second hottest year on record?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the data for the Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index for 2025 shows the second greatest increase of any previously recorded year when it is released. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An anomaly which is the second greatest of any previously recorded year for 2025 is necessary and sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes" immediately once the data becomes available, regardless of whether the figure for 2024 and/or 2025 is later revised.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the figure found in the table titled "Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)" under the column "No_Smoothing" in the row "2025" (https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt). If NASA's "Global Temperature Index" is rendered permanently unavailable, other information from NASA may be used. If no information for 2025 is provided by NASA by March 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) report that 2025's global average temperature anomaly (relative to 1991–2020) is higher than 2023's when it publishes its annual climate summary in January 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) typically publishes its annual global climate summary in early January of the following year. As of the January-to-November 2025 data, C3S reported that 2025 is currently tied with 2023 as the second-warmest year on record, with a global average temperature anomaly of 0.60°C above the 1991–2020 average (https://climate.copernicus.eu/copernicus-2025-track-be-second-or-third-warmest-year-record). For context, 2023's full-year anomaly was 0.60°C and 2024's was 0.72°C above the 1991–2020 average according to C3S. Whether December 2025 tips the annual average above or below 2023's level will determine whether 2025 finishes as the second- or third-warmest year. This is a leading indicator because C3S data and NASA GISS data are highly correlated but C3S publishes its annual result earlier (typically in the first week of January). If C3S ranks 2025 above 2023, it strongly suggests NASA GISS will also rank 2025 as second-warmest.

Sources:
- Copernicus Climate Change Service, December 2025 bulletin: https://climate.copernicus.eu/copernicus-2025-track-be-second-or-third-warmest-year-record
- News18 reporting on C3S data (Dec 9, 2025): https://www.news18.com/world/2025-set-to-become-2nd-or-3rd-warmest-year-on-record-copernicus-9167955.html
- MoneyControl (Dec 10, 2025): https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/world/european-scientists-warn-2025-may-rank-second-or-third-hottest-year-in-history-12890095.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-11, the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) publishes its official annual global climate summary for 2025 (typically available at https://climate.copernicus.eu/global-climate-highlights or their monthly/annual bulletin pages) and reports that the 2025 full-year global average surface air temperature anomaly relative to the 1991–2020 baseline is strictly greater than the corresponding 2023 full-year anomaly (which was 0.60°C). If C3S reports 2025 as exactly equal to 2023's anomaly (to the reported precision), this resolves No. If C3S does not publish the full-year 2025 summary by 2026-01-11, this question resolves as ambiguous/N/A.

Primary source: Copernicus Climate Change Service annual bulletin at https://climate.copernicus.eu/global-climate-highlights
Alternative: C3S press releases or data pages at https://climate.copernicus.eu/
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether 2025 will be the second-hottest year on record per NASA GISS. The C3S annual summary, published in early January (before NASA GISS typically releases its data in mid-January), uses an independent but highly correlated temperature dataset. Whether C3S ranks 2025 above 2023 is a strong leading indicator of whether NASA GISS will also rank 2025 as second-warmest. As of November 2025, 2025 and 2023 are essentially tied in the C3S dataset, making this a genuinely uncertain indicator question (not near 0 or 1 probability). If 2025 edges out 2023 in C3S data, it substantially increases confidence that 2025 will be second-hottest in NASA GISS as well; if it doesn't, 2025 may end up third.

subquestions.question: Will the United States and Venezuela announce or confirm the establishment of a formal or back-channel diplomatic communication line (e.g., envoy, intermediary, or direct diplomatic contact) between November 15 and December 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-November 2025, tensions between the U.S. and Venezuela remain extremely high. The U.S. has conducted at least six military strikes on suspected drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean, deployed warships, F-35s, B-52 bombers, and approximately 6,500 troops to the region, and authorized covert CIA operations inside Venezuela. President Trump has used confrontational language toward Maduro, stating on October 17, 2025, that Maduro 'doesn't want to f*** around with the United States' and that Maduro has 'offered everything' including natural resources to ease tensions (Sky News Australia, October 17, 2025: https://www.skynews.com.au/world-news/united-states/trump-drops-fbomb-at-leader-during-white-house-talks-with-zelensky/news-story/). However, Venezuela has denied that any de-escalation negotiations are taking place, with Vice President Delcy Rodríguez rejecting a Miami Herald report of such talks (Dawn, October 19, 2025: https://www.dawn.com/news/1870123). Maduro has accused the U.S. of plotting to overthrow his government and has deployed 17,000 troops domestically in response. The U.S. does not recognize Maduro as Venezuela's legitimate president. Regional leaders, including Brazil's President Lula, have urged dialogue and warned against a U.S. ground invasion of Venezuela (AP, November 4, 2025: https://apnews.com/article/brazil-lula-trump-tariffs-venezuela). For a direct Trump-Maduro conversation to occur, some form of diplomatic channel would likely need to be established or acknowledged first, making this a key leading indicator.

Sources:
- Sky News Australia, October 17, 2025: https://www.skynews.com.au/world-news/united-states/trump-drops-fbomb-at-leader-during-white-house-talks-with-zelensky/news-story/
- Dawn, October 19, 2025: https://www.dawn.com/news/1870123
- AP, November 4, 2025: https://apnews.com/article/brazil-lula-trump-tariffs-venezuela
- News18, October 17, 2025: https://www.news18.com/videos/world/trump-claims-venezuelas-maduro-is-willing-to-give-everything-to-ease-tensions-with-the-us-4k-9194072.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between November 15, 2025 and December 1, 2025 (inclusive), credible reporting from at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, NYT, Washington Post, or equivalent) confirms that the United States and Venezuela have established, resumed, or publicly acknowledged a formal or informal diplomatic communication channel — such as the appointment of an envoy, the use of a third-party intermediary for negotiations, or direct diplomatic contact between senior officials of both governments (at the level of foreign minister/secretary of state or above). Mere speculation or unconfirmed rumors do not count. The channel must be acknowledged or confirmed by at least one of the two governments or by a credible mediating party. If no such confirmation emerges by December 1, 2025, the question resolves No. Resolution sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news).
subquestions.rationale: A direct conversation between Trump and Maduro would almost certainly require some prior diplomatic groundwork — an established communication channel, envoy, or intermediary. As of mid-November 2025, the U.S. does not recognize Maduro's government and Venezuela denies any negotiations are taking place. If a diplomatic channel is confirmed in the next two weeks, it would be a strong leading indicator that a Trump-Maduro conversation could follow by late December. Conversely, the absence of any diplomatic channel by December 1 would make a direct conversation by December 31 much less likely. This subquestion captures a necessary precondition rather than simply restating the ultimate question with a tighter deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: (1) Establishment/resumption/acknowledgment of a formal or informal diplomatic communication channel (envoy, intermediary, or direct diplomatic contact) between US and Venezuela; (2) between Nov 15–Dec 1, 2025 inclusive; (3) confirmed by at least one government or credible mediating party; (4) reported by at least two major international news outlets (Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, NYT, WaPo, etc.).
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'United States Venezuela diplomatic communication channel envoy 2025' (Nov 15–Dec 1). Query 2: 'US Venezuela diplomacy negotiations November 2025' (Nov 15–Dec 1). Query 3: 'Trump Maduro phone call direct contact diplomatic November 2025' (Nov 15–Dec 1). Query 4: 'Trump Maduro phone call confirmed Reuters AP BBC' (Nov 25–Dec 1). Query 5: 'Venezuela US back-channel Grenell envoy intermediary November 2025' (Nov 15–Dec 1). Query 6: 'Trump Maduro New York Times November 28 2025 direct diplomatic contact' (Nov 27–Dec 1).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: Nov 17, Trump publicly states 'We may be having some discussions with Maduro' — confirmed by AP News [apnews.com]. Candidate event 2: Nov 25, Trump states communication teams on both sides are already in contact (Air Force One, multiple sources). Candidate event 3: ~Nov 21-25, direct Trump-Maduro phone call with Sec. State Rubio, first reported by NYT on Nov 28. Candidate event 4: Nov 30, Trump confirms 'The answer is yes' — call confirmed by US president himself. The Miami Herald reported call was brokered by Brazil, Qatar, and Turkey. No events rejected — all directly satisfy criteria at senior official (head-of-state + SoS) level within window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Direct diplomatic contact at head-of-state level or above: Trump (US President) personally confirmed speaking with Maduro (Venezuelan President), with Secretary of State Marco Rubio participating. This exceeds the 'foreign minister/secretary of state or above' threshold. Acknowledged by US government: Trump confirmed on Nov 30, 2025, 'The answer is yes' [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2051317); [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/trump-confirms-speaking-to-venezuelas-maduro-amid-tensions/); [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/86MW6NQ); [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/trump-confirms-conversation-with-venezuelas-maduro). Reported by multiple major outlets: NYT (first), Reuters (via Investing.com, Nov 28), AFP (Nov 30), AP News (Nov 17 about discussions), CNN (Nov 21, Ric Grenell context). More than two qualifying major outlets confirmed this.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Trump-Maduro phone call occurred approximately Nov 21-25, 2025 (NYT reported 'late in the week' before Nov 28). Trump confirmed the call publicly on Nov 30, 2025, aboard Air Force One. First qualifying public confirmation with government acknowledgment: November 30, 2025. Additionally, on Nov 17, 2025, Trump publicly stated the US 'may be having some discussions with Maduro' (AP News), which itself signals an active communication channel being acknowledged by the US side.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first signal of a communication channel was Nov 17 (Trump's public statement on AP). The actual phone call occurred ~Nov 21-25. Trump's public government confirmation was Nov 30. No qualifying event exists before Nov 15 in the window — the window starts Nov 15, and the first qualifying event (acknowledgment of discussions/direct contact) began Nov 17 within the window.

The Venezuelan government did not officially confirm the call, but the resolution criteria only requires acknowledgment by 'at least one of the two governments OR by a credible mediating party.' Trump (US government) confirmed it personally. Additionally, Brazil, Qatar, Turkey were reported as brokers (credible mediating parties). Multiple independent major outlets (NYT, Reuters, AFP) reported the call. No contradictory evidence undermines the direct diplomatic contact conclusion.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: YES. Within the Nov 15–Dec 1, 2025 window, direct diplomatic contact at the highest level (US President Trump + Secretary of State Rubio with Venezuelan President Maduro) occurred approximately Nov 21-25. This was acknowledged/confirmed by Trump (US government) on November 30, 2025. The call was brokered by Brazil, Qatar, and Turkey (credible mediating parties). This was widely reported by multiple major international outlets including NYT, Reuters, AFP, AP, CNN. Additionally, on Nov 17, Trump publicly acknowledged 'We may be having some discussions with Maduro' (AP News). All resolution criteria are fully satisfied: direct diplomatic contact at foreign minister/secretary of state level or above, acknowledged by at least one government (US), reported by at least two major outlets. First occurrence: approximately Nov 21-25 (call) or Nov 17 (public acknowledgment of discussions), both within the resolution window. Resolution datetime set to Nov 30, 2025 when Trump officially confirmed the call.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Senate hold a floor vote on the Kaine-Paul Iran War Powers Resolution between February 13, 2026 and February 28, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
In early 2026, Democrats launched a 'war powers blitz' targeting multiple countries where Trump has threatened military action, including Iran. Senator Tim Kaine (D-VA) and Senator Rand Paul (R-KY) introduced a bipartisan Iran War Powers Resolution in the Senate, with a companion Khanna-Massie resolution in the House. This follows a pattern established with Venezuela, where war powers votes — even when they failed — forced the White House to make public commitments about seeking congressional authorization before military action. evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Between Sept 1-27, 2025, OpenAI (official channels/executives) must have publicly announced, demonstrated, or previewed a dedicated standalone social application (primary purpose = facilitating social interaction, e.g., messaging, social feeds, content sharing) that is distinct from ChatGPT. evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria requires an official announcement that confirms existence and intended release of a dedicated standalone social application. subquestions.rationale: A formal ceasefire agreement between Ukraine and Russia would be a strong leading indicator of Ukraine agreeing not to join NATO. The current 28-point peace framework links these issues: the NATO membership pledge is reportedly a core component of the broader peace deal that would also include a ceasefire. If a ceasefire is agreed upon, it likely means Ukraine has accepted the broader framework's terms, which include the NATO non-membership provision. Conversely, if no ceasefire materializes by late December, it suggests negotiations have stalled or collapsed, making a NATO pledge by year-end much less likely. This question captures the momentum of negotiations without directly restating the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Ukraine and Russia formally agree to a ceasefire between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29. Must be either (a) official joint statement/signed document by representatives of both parties confirming cessation of hostilities, or (b) overwhelming consensus of credible media (Reuters, AP, BBC, CBS) reporting both sides agreed. Temporary truces, unilateral pauses, holiday truces, and prisoner exchanges explicitly excluded. The ceasefire need not have taken effect, only the agreement.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Ukraine Russia ceasefire agreement 2025' (Nov 30 - Dec 29) - to find any formal agreement; 2. 'Ukraine Russia peace deal signed December 2025' (Nov 30 - Dec 29) - to find signed documents; 3. 'Ukraine Russia ceasefire signed agreed December 28 29 2025' (Dec 25-29) - to find last-minute agreements; 4. 'Zelensky Trump meeting December 29 2025 peace deal outcome' (Dec 26-29) - to check Trump-Zelensky outcome; 5. 'Russia rejects ceasefire December 2025 war continues' (Dec 25-29) - to find counter-evidence; 6. 'Ukraine Russia war news December 29 2025' - to find final day news; 7. 'Zaporizhzhia power plant ceasefire IAEA Ukraine Russia agreement' (Nov 30 - Dec 29) - to assess any IAEA-brokered agreements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: CANDIDATE 1 REJECTED: Zaporizhzhia NPP local/temporary ceasefire (Dec 28, 2025) — Multiple sources (IAEA, Ukrainska Pravda, B92, Anadolu Agency, Devdiscourse) confirm both sides agreed to a 'window of silence' / 'local ceasefire' / 'temporary truce' to allow power line repairs. This is explicitly excluded by resolution criteria as a 'temporary truce.' It is also a highly localized nuclear safety measure, not a cessation of hostilities. CANDIDATE 2 REJECTED: Trump-Zelensky Mar-a-Lago meeting (Dec 28, 2025) — Progress claimed on 20-point peace plan (~90-95% agreed), but no ceasefire agreement reached. The Kremlin explicitly stated 'no truce was agreed upon.' Russia was simultaneously launching massive drone/missile attacks on Ukraine. Trump said 'no deadline' and expected results 'in a few weeks.' CANDIDATE 3 REJECTED: Zelensky's conditional ceasefire proposal — Zelensky stated willingness to hold referendum IF Russia agrees to 60-day ceasefire. Russia has not accepted this conditional offer. This is not an agreement.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event matching formal ceasefire criteria was found. Evidence from multiple credible sources confirms: [Washington Times](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/28/trump-zelenskyy-say-ukraine-peace-deal-close-thorny-issues-remain/) states 'the Kremlin stated no truce was agreed upon' and 'Putin has rejected ceasefire proposals'; [The Indian Express](https://indianexpress.com/article/world/what-we-heard-from-trump-zelenskyy-meeting-progress-claimed-but-key-issues-still-open-10443911/) reports 'Trump stated that any ceasefire or peace deal requires Russia's agreement, noting that Vladimir Putin has not accepted a ceasefire'; [China Daily](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202512/29/WS6951a220a310d6866eb30d1b.html) reports Russian Presidential Aide Yuri Ushakov stated a temporary ceasefire 'would only prolong the conflict'; [Hindustan Times](https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/russia-will-achieve-goals-by-military-means-putin-warning-ahead-of-zelensky-trump-meet-101766912241539.html) reports Putin warned Moscow would achieve objectives 'by military means' if Ukraine doesn't give in; [RTE](https://www.rte.ie/news/world/2025/1223/1550314-ukraine-war-in-2025-talks-setbacks-and-more-war/) confirms 'As of December 23, 2025, no breakthrough has occurred.' The Zaporizhzhia local ceasefire is explicitly excluded as a 'temporary truce' under resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying ceasefire agreement event has an extractable timestamp within the window, as no such event occurred. The Zaporizhzhia local truce (Dec 28) does not qualify. The Trump-Zelensky meeting (Dec 28) produced no ceasefire agreement — only statements that a peace deal is 'close' but issues 'remain.'
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at any point within the November 30 - December 29, 2025 window. All searches confirm no formal bilateral ceasefire agreement was reached.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The B92/IAEA Zaporizhzhia ceasefire headline 'Both Ukraine and Russia agreed: Ceasefire' could superficially appear to resolve Yes, but its own content explicitly describes it as a 'temporary ceasefire' / 'window of silence' for nuclear plant repairs — not a cessation of hostilities. The resolution criteria explicitly exclude 'temporary truces.' Furthermore, the very same day (Dec 28), Russia was launching massive drone/missile attacks on Ukraine, confirming there was no general cessation of hostilities. Russia was explicitly rejecting any broader ceasefire proposals throughout the entire window (Dec 10, 16, 25, 28).
evidence.step8_final_decision: The window closed (December 29, 2025) without Ukraine and Russia formally agreeing to a ceasefire meeting the resolution criteria. All evidence throughout the window shows: ongoing active combat; Russia repeatedly and explicitly rejecting ceasefire proposals; negotiations producing a draft 20-point peace plan that is ~90% agreed but still unfinished, with no Russian acceptance; the only bilateral 'ceasefire' being a localized temporary truce near the Zaporizhzhia NPP that is explicitly excluded by resolution criteria. Resolution: No.

question: Will a new country join the Abraham Accords in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any country not already a part of the Abraham Accords formally signs a normalization agreement with Israel under the framework of the Abraham Accords by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A formal signing refers to an official agreement between Israel and another country that is publicly acknowledged by both governments and clearly attributed to the Abraham Accords or their continuation.

Countries already part of the Abraham Accords as of June 26, 2025—including the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan—will not count.

The resolution source will be official government statements, however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Saudi Arabia and Israel hold publicly confirmed, direct bilateral diplomatic negotiations (at the ministerial level or above) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
Saudi Arabia is widely considered the most significant potential new member of the Abraham Accords. As of October 2025, Saudi Arabia has not joined the Accords and continues to condition any normalization with Israel on a credible pathway to a Palestinian state, a position reaffirmed repeatedly since the Gaza war began in October 2023. In an October 17, 2025 interview on Fox Business Network, former President Trump said he expects an expansion of the Abraham Accords soon and hopes Saudi Arabia will join (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/17/trump-expects-expansion-of-abraham-accords-soon-hopes-s-arabia-will-join). However, polls from the Washington Institute (August 2024) show 81% of Saudis view normalization with Israel negatively, a sharp increase since the Gaza war. Israel's ongoing military operations in Gaza and the West Bank, its airstrikes on Qatar in September 2025, and the UAE's warning against Israeli annexation of the West Bank have all complicated expansion prospects. Deputy Foreign Minister Sharren Haskel told the Jerusalem Post in September 2025 that further expansion to Saudi Arabia is unlikely while the war continues (https://www.yahoo.com/news/five-years-abraham-accords-still-source-mideast-hope-haskel-tells-post). The Arab League and OIC convened an emergency summit in Doha in late 2025 condemning Israeli actions, further signaling Arab solidarity against normalization under current conditions.

Sources:
- Al Jazeera, "Trump expects expansion of Abraham accords soon, hopes S Arabia will join" (Oct 17, 2025): https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/17/trump-expects-expansion-of-abraham-accords-soon-hopes-s-arabia-will-join
- Yahoo News, "Five years on: Abraham Accords still source of Mideast hope" (Sep 14, 2025): https://www.yahoo.com/news/five-years-abraham-accords-still-source-mideast-hope-haskel-tells-post
- Deutsche Welle, "Abraham Accords Promised a New Middle East – That Changed" (Sep 15, 2025): https://www.dw.com/en/abraham-accords-promised-a-new-middle-east-that-changed/a-70218000
- The Seattle Times, "What are the Abraham Accords, Trump's 2020 Mideast deals?" (Oct 13, 2025): https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/what-are-the-abraham-accords-trumps-2020-mideast-deals/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), there is at least one publicly confirmed, direct bilateral meeting between Saudi Arabian and Israeli officials at the level of foreign minister (or equivalent) or above, focused on diplomatic normalization or expansion of the Abraham Accords. The meeting must be acknowledged by both governments through official statements, press releases, or on-the-record confirmation by spokespeople. Meetings that are only reported by media without any official confirmation from both sides do not count. Secret or back-channel meetings that are later leaked but not officially confirmed by both governments do not count. If the meeting is scheduled during the resolution window but postponed beyond November 30, 2025, this question resolves No.

Resolution sources: Official statements from the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.mofa.gov.sa/en) and the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/ministry_of_foreign_affairs). As a fallback, credible wire services such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) and Associated Press (https://apnews.com) reporting on-the-record confirmation from both governments may be used.
subquestions.rationale: Saudi Arabia is universally regarded as the 'biggest prize' and most likely candidate for Abraham Accords expansion. If Saudi-Israeli ministerial-level normalization talks occur in November 2025, it would be a strong leading indicator that a new country could join the Accords by year-end. Conversely, the absence of such talks would strongly suggest no new member will join in 2025, given that Saudi Arabia is the most advanced candidate and other potential entrants (like Azerbaijan or Central Asian states) are far less likely to formalize accession without a Saudi deal paving the way. This question captures a concrete, observable diplomatic milestone that is distinct from the ultimate question (which asks about a formal signing) but highly predictive of it.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: At least one publicly confirmed, direct bilateral meeting between Saudi Arabian AND Israeli officials, both at foreign minister level or above, focused on diplomatic normalization or Abraham Accords expansion, officially acknowledged by BOTH governments, between October 31 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive). Key entities: Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs or their heads of government. The meeting must be direct (not US-mediated or trilateral), bilateral (Saudi-Israel only), and officially confirmed by both sides.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Saudi Arabia Israel bilateral diplomatic negotiations ministerial meeting 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find any direct bilateral meetings. Query 2: 'Saudi Arabia Israel normalization Abraham Accords official meeting November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find any officially confirmed normalization meetings. Query 3: 'Saudi Arabia Israel foreign minister direct meeting bilateral talks November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find specific ministerial-level direct contacts. Query 4: 'Israel Saudi Arabia official confirmed meeting diplomacy normalization October November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find official confirmations from both governments. Query 5: 'Saudi Arabia Israel direct bilateral meeting foreign minister Katz Faisal bin Farhan November 2025' — to find specific foreign minister-level bilateral meetings. Query 6: 'Israel Saudi Arabia Netanyahu MBS direct meeting officially confirmed normalization talks' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find head-of-state level direct meetings.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) MBS-Trump White House meeting on November 18, 2025 — REJECTED: This was a US-Saudi bilateral meeting, not a Saudi-Israel direct bilateral meeting. Israeli officials were not party to this meeting. (2) Saudi FM Faisal bin Farhan meetings at G7 (Nov 13), G20 (Nov 22-23), bilateral meetings with Italy, Bahrain, Montenegro, Kuwait — REJECTED: None of these involved Israeli counterparts. (3) Saudi Arabia's indirect communication framework with Israel facilitated by US — REJECTED: The resolution criteria explicitly exclude anything other than direct bilateral meetings officially confirmed by both governments. (4) MBS's rejection of normalization at Trump meeting — REJECTED as a qualifying event: This demonstrates no direct Saudi-Israel meeting occurred, and MBS explicitly postponed normalization indefinitely.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of any direct bilateral Saudi-Israeli meeting at the ministerial level or above during the resolution window. All diplomatic activity between Saudi Arabia and Israel was either: (a) US-mediated (Trump-MBS meeting on Nov 18 per [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/world/trump-saudi-crown-prince-mohammed-bin-salman-meet-white-house-amid-diplomatic-shifts-region)); (b) Indirect (Saudi source told KAN News that Riyadh expected 'indirect communication' per [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/saudi-arabia-israel-ties-may-113004220.html)); (c) Rejected outright (MBS rejected normalization during Trump meeting per [Arutz Sheva](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/418366) and [Saudi Gazette](http://saudigazette.com.sa/article/656878/SAUDI-ARABIA/MBS-rejects-US-plan-for-Israel-normalization-during-tense-Trump-meeting)). The resolution criteria require a direct bilateral meeting with official confirmation from BOTH governments, which was not found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no qualifying event occurred. The closest events (MBS-Trump meeting on November 18, 2025) do not meet the criteria of being a direct Saudi-Israel bilateral meeting.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found, so the first-occurrence check is moot. Multiple searches confirm the absence of any direct Saudi-Israeli bilateral meeting.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification strongly confirms No resolution: (1) MBS explicitly told Trump on November 18, 2025 that Saudi Arabia 'cannot take such a step now' regarding normalization with Israel, and 'postponed negotiations indefinitely' per [Mehr News Agency](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/239196/Tensions-soared-during-Trump-MBS-meeting-over-normalization). (2) Saudi Arabia expected only 'indirect communication' with Israel via US mediation per [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/saudi-arabia-israel-ties-may-113004220.html). (3) The Times of Israel confirmed on November 28, 2025 that 'the long-anticipated Saudi normalization with Israel did not materialize' per [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/lazar-focus-as-us-and-saudi-arabia-shore-up-ties-is-israel-left-out/). (4) No reports from Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs of any direct bilateral meeting. (5) Saudi FM Faisal bin Farhan's meeting record during this period showed no meeting with Israeli counterpart. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. During the resolution window (October 31 – November 30, 2025), there was NO publicly confirmed, direct bilateral meeting between Saudi Arabian and Israeli officials at the ministerial level or above focused on diplomatic normalization or Abraham Accords expansion. All diplomatic engagement was US-mediated (the Trump-MBS White House meeting on November 18, 2025), and MBS explicitly rejected advancing normalization with Israel during this period. The window closed on November 30, 2025 without the condition ever being met.

question: Another France debt downgrade by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if France's long-term sovereign credit letter rating is downgraded by any of the three major credit rating agencies (S&P, Moody's, Fitch) at any point between September 12, 6:15 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Standard & Poor's, Moody's, or Fitch; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the French 10-year government bond yield spread over German 10-year Bunds exceed 100 basis points at any point between September 13, 2025 and October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 12, 2025, Fitch downgraded France's sovereign credit rating from 'AA-' to 'A+', citing political instability and strained public finances (https://www.france24.com/en/france/20250912-fitch-downgrades-france-s-credit-rating-in-new-debt-blow). Following this downgrade, the French 10-year yield rose to approximately 3.47%, approaching Italian levels. The spread between French and German 10-year government bonds (the OAT-Bund spread) is a key market indicator of perceived French sovereign risk. As of mid-September 2025, the spread has been hovering in the 75-90 basis point range, elevated from historical norms of around 30-50 basis points. A sustained move above 100 basis points would signal severe market stress and could indicate that further downgrades are being priced in by bond markets. Moody's is scheduled to review France's rating in September 2025, and S&P Global is expected to weigh in by November 2025 (https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/france-faces-sovereign-rating-test-amid-political-chaos-3953205). New Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu faces the challenge of drafting a credible budget to address the 5.8% GDP deficit amid a fragmented parliament where Macron's allies lack a majority.

Sources:
- AFP via France24: Fitch downgrades France's credit rating - https://www.france24.com/en/france/20250912-fitch-downgrades-france-s-credit-rating-in-new-debt-blow
- Reuters via Investing.com: France faces sovereign rating test amid political chaos - https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/france-faces-sovereign-rating-test-amid-political-chaos-3953205
- Trading Economics: France 10Y Bond Yield - https://tradingeconomics.com/france/government-bond-yield
- Trading Economics: France-Germany 10Y Bond Spread - https://tradingeconomics.com/france/government-bond-spread
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between September 13, 2025 and October 10, 2025 (inclusive), the spread between the French 10-year government bond (OAT) yield and the German 10-year government bond (Bund) yield equals or exceeds 100 basis points (1.00 percentage points) based on closing daily data. The primary data source will be the daily closing spread as reported by Trading Economics (https://tradingeconomics.com/france/government-bond-spread) or Bloomberg. If Trading Economics data is unavailable, Refinitiv/LSEG or any widely cited financial data provider showing daily OAT-Bund spread data may be used as a fallback. If no reliable data source is available for the resolution window, the question resolves as ambiguous.
subquestions.rationale: The OAT-Bund spread is a real-time market signal of sovereign credit stress for France. A widening spread above 100 basis points would indicate that bond markets are pricing in significant additional risk for French debt—potentially including further downgrades by Moody's or S&P. This is a leading indicator because rating agencies often cite market dynamics and fiscal credibility when making downgrade decisions. If the spread blows out, it signals that France's new government is failing to reassure markets, making further downgrades more likely. Conversely, if the spread remains contained after Fitch's downgrade, it suggests markets view the Fitch action as already priced in and further downgrades as less probable. This is a different observable than the downgrade itself and provides meaningful evidence about the trajectory of France's creditworthiness during the critical September-October review period.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The OAT-Bund 10-year spread must equal or exceed 100 basis points (1.00 percentage points) on a closing daily basis at any point between September 13, 2025 and October 10, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: daily closing OAT-Bund spread data from Trading Economics, Bloomberg, or equivalent. Key entities: French 10-year OAT, German 10-year Bund. Threshold: ≥100 bps. Window: 2025-09-13 to 2025-10-10.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'French OAT German Bund 10-year bond yield spread basis points September October 2025' — to find spread data during window. Query 2: 'France Germany government bond spread OAT Bund 100 basis points 2025' — to check if threshold was breached. Query 3: 'OAT Bund spread 100 basis points France Germany bond October 2025' — specifically looking for 100bp breach. Query 4: 'French bond spread widening record high September October 2025' — to catch any extreme widening events.
evidence.step3_event_detection: All candidate data points found: (a) Sep 22, 2025 — 81 bps; (b) Sep 25, 2025 — 82 bps; (c) Oct 1, 2025 — 82 bps; (d) Oct 6, 2025 — intraday high of 87.96 bps, closing at 85.49 bps; (e) Oct 7, 2025 — ~86 bps close; (f) Oct 9, 2025 — 82.8–84 bps. None of these reach or exceed 100 bps. Multiple sources explicitly reference spread being below 90 bps even at peak. Articles discuss '100 bp' only as a future hypothetical threshold (e.g., 'a slow climb toward 100 bp is unlikely to trigger action'). No event rejected for ambiguity — all rejected simply because the threshold of 100 bps was never reached.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Resolution criteria require ≥100 bps on closing daily data. The maximum closing spread documented during the window was ~86 bps (October 7, 2025), per [Seeking Alpha/ING](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4828253-rates-spark-markets-didnt-have-high-hopes-for-france-anyway) and [Investing.com UK](https://uk.investing.com/analysis/markets-didnt-have-high-hopes-for-france-anyway-200619234). Even the intraday peak of 87.96 bps on October 6 ([bdnews24.com](https://bdnews24.com/world/europe/8b7b8dabf9ff)) falls far short of 100 bps. Criteria are NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a ≥100 bps event exists within the window, because no such event occurred. The highest documented closing spread was ~86 bps on October 7, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event (spread ≥100 bps) occurred at any point during the window. The spread peaked around 87–88 bps intraday on October 6, then narrowed.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No article reports the spread at or above 100 bps at any time during the window. Multiple independent sources (ING/Seeking Alpha, bdnews24, Economic Times, Investing.com, France24) consistently report spreads in the 76–88 bps range throughout the window. One article explicitly mentions '100 bp' only as a future hypothetical threshold that would be 'unlikely to trigger action' — confirming it was not reached. The September 2025 Tradeweb report shows the month-end spread was just 76 bps (though it widened later in October). No source reports anything near 100 bps.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The OAT-Bund 10-year spread never reached 100 basis points during the resolution window (September 13 – October 10, 2025). The highest documented spread was approximately 87.96 bps intraday (not closing) on October 6, 2025, with the closing spread around 85–86 bps that day. By October 9, the spread had narrowed back to ~82–84 bps. Multiple high-quality sources confirm this. Resolution: No.

question: Will Donald Trump visit North Korea in 2025?
description:
If U.S. President Donald Trump visits North Korea between August 4 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial or maritime territory of the listed country. Whether or not Trump enters the country's airspace during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the United States and North Korea publicly confirm direct official-level diplomatic contact (at the level of envoy or higher) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
For Donald Trump to visit North Korea before the end of 2025, a prerequisite would be the resumption of direct diplomatic engagement between the U.S. and North Korea. As of late August 2025, South Korea's National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac stated that North Korea has been 'inactive in engaging in diplomacy with South Korea or the United States' and has 'not shown willingness to engage in talks' (https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10382109). Despite Trump expressing hope on August 26, 2025, that he would meet Kim Jong Un later in the year (https://www.latestly.com/agency-news/world-news-us-president-donald-trump-says-he-hopes-to-meet-north-korean-leader-kim-jong-un-in-2025-6578953.html), and South Korean President Lee Jae-myung proposing that a Trump-Kim meeting could be arranged if Trump visits the region for the APEC summit in late October (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/South-Korea-s-Lee-proposes-meeting-between-Trump-and-North-Korea-Kim-later-this-year-Lee-s-office-sa-49371562/), North Korea has not reciprocated these overtures. Wi assessed the likelihood of Kim attending APEC in South Korea as 'very low.' Any presidential visit to North Korea would almost certainly require prior direct diplomatic contact — such as envoy meetings, official phone calls, or back-channel confirmations — before a summit could be arranged. Kim Jong Un's announced visit to China for a military parade was noted as requiring 'close attention' but did not signal openness to U.S. engagement.

Sources:
- The Korea Herald, 'N. Korea appears to be inactive in engaging in diplomacy with S. Korea or US: security adviser' (Aug 29, 2025): https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10382109
- LatestLY, 'US President Donald Trump Says He Hopes To Meet North Korean Leader Kim Jong Un in 2025' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.latestly.com/agency-news/world-news-us-president-donald-trump-says-he-hopes-to-meet-north-korean-leader-kim-jong-un-in-2025-6578953.html
- Market Screener, 'South Korea's Lee proposes meeting between Trump and North Korea Kim later this year' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/South-Korea-s-Lee-proposes-meeting-between-Trump-and-North-Korea-Kim-later-this-year-Lee-s-office-sa-49371562/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), either the United States government (e.g., the White House, State Department, or National Security Council) or North Korea's government (e.g., KCNA, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs) publicly confirms that direct official diplomatic contact has occurred between U.S. and North Korean officials at the level of special envoy, senior diplomat, or higher. This includes confirmed phone calls, in-person meetings, or exchange of official letters/messages between the two governments, but excludes unconfirmed reports or third-party mediated communications where neither government acknowledges direct contact. Resolution sources include official White House statements (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), U.S. State Department press releases (https://www.state.gov/), KCNA reports (http://www.kcna.kp/), and a consensus of credible reporting from major wire services (AP, Reuters, AFP). If no such confirmation is made by 2025-10-31 23:59 UTC, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A Trump visit to North Korea before year-end 2025 would require significant diplomatic groundwork. The current status quo as of late August/September 2025 is that North Korea has shown no willingness to engage. If direct U.S.-DPRK diplomatic contact is publicly confirmed in October, it would be a strong leading indicator that a Trump visit to North Korea is being arranged. Conversely, if October passes with no confirmed contact, the likelihood of a Trump visit to North Korea in the remaining two months of 2025 drops substantially. This subquestion captures a necessary (though not sufficient) precondition for the ultimate question's positive resolution and is a meaningfully different observable event from the visit itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), EITHER the US government (White House, State Dept, NSC) OR North Korea's government (KCNA, MFA) must PUBLICLY CONFIRM that direct official diplomatic contact occurred between US and North Korean officials at the level of special envoy, senior diplomat, or higher. This includes phone calls, in-person meetings, or official letter/message exchanges. Excludes unconfirmed reports or third-party mediated communications where neither government acknowledges direct contact.

'US North Korea talks meeting official October 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find any confirmed meetings; 3. 'Trump Kim Jong Un meeting APEC Gyeongju October 2025 confirmed' (Oct 1-31) — to check if Trump-Kim summit happened; 4. 'US North Korea direct contact envoy Steve Witkoff October 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to check if US envoy contacted North Korea; 5. 'North Korea US direct contact message communication October 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find confirmed communications; 6. 'KCNA North Korea response Trump APEC October 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to check North Korea's official response; 7. question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla receive a California DMV Autonomous Vehicle Deployment Permit (allowing driverless operation on public roads) by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tesla currently operates its ride-hailing service in the San Francisco Bay Area with human safety drivers behind the wheel, using its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software. As of August 2025, Tesla has not applied for—let alone received—a California DMV permit to operate autonomous vehicles without a human driver. California's autonomous vehicle regulations require companies to first obtain a testing permit (with a safety driver), then a driverless testing permit, and finally a deployment permit before offering commercial driverless rides to the public. Companies like Waymo have gone through this multi-stage process over several years.

Internal emails obtained by Politico revealed that Tesla's senior counsel described its Bay Area service as functionally similar to supervised FSD available in regular consumer cars, not a truly autonomous system. Tesla has been operating under a supervised framework, with California regulators requiring a human driver for at least the first 55,000 miles of operation. Elon Musk has publicly stated Tesla is 'in the process of obtaining the necessary regulatory permissions,' but no formal permit application for driverless operation has been confirmed.

Conversely, receiving such a permit would be a major milestone indicating real progress toward the ultimate question's resolution criteria. question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. and Ukraine hold a publicly confirmed bilateral meeting at the principal level (Secretary of State or higher) specifically focused on formalizing security guarantees between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The path toward a U.S. security guarantee for Ukraine has been a multi-stage diplomatic process throughout 2025. In August 2025, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Andrii Yermak, head of Ukraine's Presidential Office, to discuss security guarantees, with subgroups working on political-legal and military components. A draft framework was reportedly expected by late August 2025 (https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/22/). In September 2025, a Paris summit of 26 countries discussed deploying a reassurance force, but participants agreed that any European military role would require U.S. security guarantees as a 'backstop,' a commitment Trump has not yet made (https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/ukraine-security-guarantees-paris-summit-1.7654321). The G7 foreign ministers in September 2025 pledged to work with the U.S. to provide 'robust and credible security guarantees' (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/g7-vows-continued-support-for-ukraine-calls-for-gaza-ceasefire/3348123). Meanwhile, Trump issued an executive order pledging to defend Qatar militarily in October 2025, demonstrating a willingness to extend defense commitments outside traditional treaty frameworks (https://www.cfr.org/blog/us-pledge-defend-qatar). However, the U.S. has not yet formalized any binding defense commitment to Ukraine, and Trump has ruled out deploying U.S. ground troops to Ukraine while leaving open the possibility of air support. For the ultimate question to resolve Yes by December 31, 2025, high-level bilateral negotiations would need to accelerate significantly in November.

Sources:
- Українська правда: US secretary of state and Yermak discuss security guarantees (2025-08-22): https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/22/
- CBC News: Ukraine's allies discuss security guarantees (2025-09-04): https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/ukraine-security-guarantees-paris-summit-1.7654321
- Anadolu Agency: G7 vows continued support for Ukraine (2025-09-24): https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/g7-vows-continued-support-for-ukraine-calls-for-gaza-ceasefire/3348123
- Council on Foreign Relations: U.S. Pledge to Defend Qatar (2025-10-02): https://www.cfr.org/blog/us-pledge-defend-qatar
- Foreign Policy: 26 Countries Commit to Deploying Troops (2025-09-04): https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/09/04/ukraine-troops-security-guarantee-paris-summit/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), there is at least one publicly confirmed bilateral meeting between U.S. and Ukrainian officials at the level of Secretary of State (or above) and the head of Ukraine's Presidential Office (or above, including the President of Ukraine), where credible reporting from at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, NYT, Washington Post, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform) describes the meeting as specifically focused on negotiating, drafting, or finalizing binding security guarantees for Ukraine. Routine diplomatic meetings, phone calls without specific security-guarantee agenda items, multilateral summits where the U.S. and Ukraine are among many participants but do not hold a dedicated bilateral session on security guarantees, or meetings focused solely on ceasefire negotiations without explicit discussion of security guarantees do not qualify. The meeting must be confirmed by official statements or credible reporting, not merely rumored or speculated.
subquestions.rationale: A formal U.S.-Ukraine security guarantee by December 31, 2025 would require intensive high-level bilateral negotiations in the preceding months. Whether the U.S. and Ukraine hold a principal-level bilateral meeting specifically focused on formalizing security guarantees in November 2025 is a strong leading indicator: if such meetings are not occurring, it is extremely unlikely that a binding Article 5-style commitment could be announced within weeks. Conversely, if such a meeting takes place, it signals that the diplomatic process is advancing toward the kind of formal commitment the ultimate question requires. This is distinct from the ultimate question because it asks about a process indicator (high-level negotiations happening) rather than the final outcome (a binding agreement signed).

evidence.step1_decompose: Requires: (1) Bilateral U.S.-Ukraine meeting only; (2) Secretary of State or higher + head of Ukraine Presidential Office or higher; (3) Specifically focused on negotiating/drafting/finalizing binding security guarantees; (4) Confirmed by official statements and ≥2 major international news outlets; (5) Between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30.

Query 3: 'Rubio Yermak Geneva bilateral meeting security guarantees formalize November 2025' — to find specific Geneva meeting details. Query 4: 'US Ukraine bilateral meeting binding security guarantees November 2025 formal' — to verify binding/formalizing aspect.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Main candidate: Geneva talks November 23-24, 2025, between Secretary of State Rubio and Ukrainian presidential chief of staff Yermak. Confirmed by Reuters, AFP, Ukrinform, Straits Times, CNA, and many others. Also: November 25 Coalition of the Willing multilateral video call with Rubio and Zelensky participating — REJECTED because it was multilateral (35 countries + EU + NATO), not bilateral. Geneva meeting is the only credible bilateral candidate at Secretary of State/Presidential Office level within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Geneva meetings (Nov 23-24) involved Rubio (Secretary of State) + Yermak (head of Presidential Office) — meeting the principal level requirement. The meetings were bilaterally confirmed by multiple major outlets including [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/rubio-says-ukraine-meeting-in-geneva-probably-the-best-so-far-4374143), [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/84U67WE), [Ukrinform](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/4061959-talks-between-ukrainian-us-delegations-on-peace-plan-begin-in-geneva.html), [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/us-hails-progress-in-ukraine-peace-talks-security-questions-unresolved-5486021). HOWEVER, the meetings were focused on a COMPREHENSIVE 28-point peace plan covering multiple categories (peace in Ukraine, security guarantees, European security, U.S. relations), NOT specifically focused on formalizing binding security guarantees. Security guarantees were explicitly noted as UNRESOLVED after the meetings per [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/us-hails-progress-in-ukraine-peace-talks-security-questions-unresolved-5486021): 'no agreement was reached on security guarantees for Kyiv.' Per [News18](https://www.news18.com/world/best-talks-since-trump-returned-us-ukraine-roll-out-updated-peace-proposal-after-geneva-meet-ws-l-9727168.html): 'outstanding issues include wording differences and higher-level decisions, particularly regarding Ukraine's future security guarantees and NATO's role, which remain unresolved.' The resolution criteria requires the meeting be 'specifically focused on negotiating, drafting, or finalizing binding security guarantees' — the Geneva meeting was a broad peace plan discussion where security guarantees were one unresolved element. The CBS News interview further clarified the security guarantee was described as 'not a formal treaty but a framework similar in spirit to Article 5.' No meeting 'specifically focused' on formalizing binding security guarantees was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Geneva talks began November 23, 2025. This is within the window. However, the meeting fails the criteria for the reason stated in step 4, so an exact timestamp does not change the resolution.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence found between October 31 and November 22, 2025. The Geneva talks were the first and only high-level bilateral meeting in this window. No meeting before or after Geneva specifically focused on formalizing binding security guarantees was identified.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: Multiple sources consistently confirm that security guarantees remained unresolved after Geneva. The Coalition of the Willing call (Nov 25) was multilateral. No evidence of any separate bilateral U.S.-Ukraine meeting specifically focused only on binding security guarantees within the window. The Ukrainian ambassador to the U.S. on CBS News (Nov 23) clarified that security guarantees were 'not a formal treaty.' Yermak on Nov 25 (Ukrinform/Axios) described U.S. security guarantees as 'legally binding' but noted a 'positive reaction' to formalizing them — suggesting they were not yet formalized. No meeting occurred that was 'specifically focused on formalizing' as opposed to being one element of a broader peace plan discussion.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Geneva meeting (Nov 23-24, 2025) between Rubio and Yermak was a high-level bilateral meeting within the window that discussed security guarantees, but it fails the resolution criteria because: (1) it was specifically focused on a comprehensive 28-point peace plan framework, not specifically/exclusively on binding security guarantees; (2) security guarantees explicitly remained unresolved after the meeting; (3) the security guarantee framework was described as not a formal treaty. The Coalition of the Willing call (Nov 25) was multilateral, not bilateral. No other qualifying meeting occurred. The condition was never met within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window. Resolution = No.

On September 18, 2025, Acting U.S. Attorney Joseph H. Thompson announced the indictment of eight Minneapolis defendants for defrauding Minnesota's Housing Stabilization Services (HSS) program. Six of the eight defendants are members of Minnesota's Somali community. The charges involve creating fictitious companies to bill for nonexistent services, with funds allegedly used for personal luxury purchases. The HSS program grew from an initial estimate of $2.6 million annually to over $104 million in payouts by 2024, with prosecutors describing the vast majority as fraudulent.

The ultimate question asks whether any of these defendants will be deported by February 28, 2026. A key prerequisite for deportation is the resolution of criminal proceedings — defendants typically cannot be deported while facing active federal criminal charges, as they must remain available for trial. However, a guilty plea or conviction could accelerate immigration enforcement actions, including deportation proceedings. The speed at which these criminal cases progress is therefore a meaningful indicator of whether deportation is feasible within the ultimate question's timeframe.

As of December 2025, large-scale ICE operations have been conducted in Minneapolis targeting Somali nationals with existing deportation orders, but the indicted fraud defendants are in active federal criminal proceedings, which generally take priority over immigration enforcement.
