question: Isar Aerospace successful orbital launch in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any launch attempt of the Spectrum rocket, developed by Isar Aerospace, results in a payload reaching a stable Earth orbit by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

"Reaching stable orbit" is defined as the successful insertion of a payload into a sustained low Earth orbit (LEO) or higher, where the payload completes at least one full revolution around Earth.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Isar Aerospace publicly announce a specific target date or launch window for Spectrum's second flight that falls within calendar year 2025, between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Isar Aerospace conducted the maiden flight of its Spectrum rocket on March 30, 2025, from Andøya Spaceport in Norway. The rocket launched successfully but exploded roughly 30 seconds after liftoff. Despite the failure, the company called the test a 'great success' and noted it did not expect to reach orbit on the first attempt. Following the flight, Isar Aerospace raised €150 million from Eldridge Industries in June 2025 and confirmed that Spectrum launch vehicles 2 and 3 are already in production (https://thenextweb.com/news/isar-aerospace-raises-150mn-strengthen-europes-launch-capabilities). Isar Aerospace was also selected as one of five firms competing for ESA's European Launcher Challenge contracts worth €169 million (https://thenextweb.com/news/5-space-tech-firms-europe-next-launch-provider). ESA's Flight Ticket Initiative confirmed two missions will fly on Spectrum from Andøya Spaceport (https://www.spacedaily.com/reports/First_five_Flight_Ticket_Initiative_missions_confirmed_with_Avio_and_Isar_Aerospace_999.html). As of late October 2025, Isar Aerospace has not publicly announced a firm date for the second Spectrum flight. For Spectrum to achieve orbit by December 31, 2025, the company would need to announce and execute a launch within a very tight timeline. A public announcement of a 2025 launch window in November would be a strong leading indicator that an orbital attempt before year-end is plausible.

Sources:
- The Next Web, Isar Aerospace raises €150mn: https://thenextweb.com/news/isar-aerospace-raises-150mn-strengthen-europes-launch-capabilities
- The Next Web, 5 space tech firms: https://thenextweb.com/news/5-space-tech-firms-europe-next-launch-provider

- NotreTemps, German space startup secures new funding: https://notretemps.com/technologies/german-space-startup-secures-new-funding
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

A vague statement like 'we hope to fly again soon' does not count; the announcement must reference a specific date, week, month, or bounded time window (e.g., 'December 2025,' 'Q4 2025,' 'before year-end 2025') for the second flight. If no such announcement is made by November 30, 2025, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:

- SpaceNews: https://spacenews.com/
- NASASpaceFlight: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/

subquestions.rationale: For Isar Aerospace to achieve a successful orbital launch by December 31, 2025, they would need to attempt a second Spectrum flight in November or December 2025. A necessary precursor is publicly committing to a 2025 launch window. If by the end of November 2025 Isar has not announced any plan to fly Spectrum again before year-end, the probability of a successful orbital launch by December 31 drops dramatically. Conversely, an announced launch window targeting late 2025 would significantly raise the probability. This makes the announcement a high-value-of-information leading indicator — two forecasters disagreeing on whether Isar will reach orbit in 2025 would likely update substantially based on whether a concrete launch timeline is announced in November.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition for Yes: Between October 31 and November 30, 2025, Isar Aerospace (or a credible space news outlet) must publicly announce a specific target date, target month, or bounded launch window (e.g., 'December 2025,' 'Q4 2025,' 'before year-end 2025') for the second Spectrum flight that falls within calendar year 2025 (before January 1, 2026). Vague statements like 'soon' do not qualify. Key entities: Isar Aerospace, Spectrum rocket, second flight. evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Isar Aerospace Spectrum second flight 2025 launch date' (Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025) — to find direct announcements. 2) 'Isar Aerospace Spectrum rocket launch window announcement' (Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025) — to find window announcements. 3) 'Isar Aerospace Spectrum pre-flight testing second flight date 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025) — to find testing-related date references. 4) 'Isar Aerospace Spectrum launch December 2025 Q4' (Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025) — to find specific date references. 5) 'Isar Aerospace Spectrum second launch announcement Norway Andoya 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025) — to find launch site-related announcements. 6) 'Isar Aerospace Spectrum year-end 2025 before January flight' (Oct 1–Nov 30, 2025) — to find year-end references.

question: Will US GDP growth in Q4 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP "Advance Estimate" release for Q4 of 2025, scheduled for January 29, 2026.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the Atlanta Fed GDPNow model estimate for Q4 2025 real GDP growth be below 2.0% as of its last update on or before January 24, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model provides real-time running estimates of current-quarter GDP growth based on incoming economic data. It is widely followed as an early indicator of where official GDP will land. As of late December 2025, the GDPNow model has not yet begun publishing Q4 2025 estimates due to the delayed Q3 GDP data release (the initial Q3 estimate came in at 4.3% annualized on December 23, 2025). Historically, GDPNow estimates converge toward the BEA's advance estimate as more data becomes available throughout the quarter. The Q3 2025 GDP came in at 4.3% annualized, well above expectations, but economists have noted that several factors — including the government shutdown's drag, softer labor market conditions (unemployment rose to 4.6% in November), and potential inventory payback after Q3 buildup — could weigh on Q4 growth. The year-to-date average annualized growth for the first three quarters of 2025 is approximately 2.5%. The GDPNow model was previously estimating Q3 growth at around 3.5% before the official release came in at 4.3%, illustrating that the model can diverge from final readings but generally tracks the direction. A GDPNow estimate below 2.0% for Q4 would suggest that GDP growth is more likely to fall below the 2.0%-2.5% range in the ultimate question, while an estimate at or above 2.0% would keep the 2.0%-2.5% range in play.

Sources:
- Atlanta Fed GDPNow: https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow
- BEA GDP data: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
- Fox Business on Q3 GDP (Dec 23, 2025): https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/us-economy-grew-much-faster-expected-third-quarter-delayed-report-shows
- NBC New York on Q3 GDP (Dec 23, 2025): https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/business/money-report/spending-helped-drive-4-3-economic-growth-in-third-quarter-delayed-gdp-report-shows/6188291/

The estimate should be read from the Atlanta Fed GDPNow page at https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow. If no GDPNow estimate for Q4 2025 has been published by January 24, 2026 (e.g., due to government shutdown or data delays), this question resolves as No. Only the latest GDPNow estimate available on or before January 24, 2026 is considered. The relevant figure is the model's point estimate of real GDP growth (seasonally adjusted, annualized) for Q4 2025.
subquestions.rationale: The Atlanta Fed GDPNow model is one of the most widely tracked real-time GDP nowcasting tools and provides a strong early signal of what the BEA's advance estimate will show. If GDPNow is tracking below 2.0% heading into the advance estimate release on January 29, 2026, it would suggest that the ultimate question (Q4 GDP between 2.0%-2.5%) is less likely to resolve Yes, as growth would more likely fall below that range. Conversely, if GDPNow is at or above 2.0%, the 2.0%-2.5% bracket remains plausible. This is a genuinely different observable than the ultimate question itself — it measures a model's real-time tracking estimate rather than the official BEA release — and resolves before the advance estimate is published.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The Atlanta Fed GDPNow model's last published estimate for Q4 2025 real GDP growth (annualized) must be strictly below 2.0% as of its last update on or before January 24, 2026. No estimate fell below 2.0%. All estimates within the window ranged from 2.7% to 5.4%.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criterion requires the last GDPNow estimate to be strictly below 2.0%. The lowest estimate identified during the window was 2.7% on January 5, 2026 [InstaForex: https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2855315]. The most recent estimate before January 24, 2026, was 5.4% as of January 22, 2026 [Investing.com: https://www.investing.com/analysis/will-us-q4-growth-exceed-q3s-strong-pace-200673778]. None of the estimates satisfy the below-2.0% threshold. The condition is definitively not met.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The Atlanta Fed GDPNow estimate for Q4 2025 real GDP growth was never below 2.0% during the resolution window (Dec 29, 2025 – Jan 24, 2026). question: Foreign intervention in Gaza in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if police officers, security forces, or military personnel belonging to neither Israel nor a Palestinian entity begin an officially acknowledged police, military, peacekeeping, and/or security operation on the ground within Gaza by December 31, 2025 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The foreign personnel must physically enter the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip to qualify. Entering the maritime territory, as occurred during the US’s attempt to construct a floating pier in 2024, or entering the airspace will not qualify. 

Entering Israeli controlled buffer zones will not qualify.  

Egyptian or other forces operating solely along the Egyptian/Gaza border will not qualify regardless of if they cross the border. 

Foreign personnel carrying out individual special operations, diplomatic missions, or solely humanitarian operations will not qualify.

Qualifying deployments must involve active-duty personnel of at least one foreign state or international institution (e.g., the UN or multinational missions) who are officially sent to Gaza for an operational role (e.g., peacekeeping, convoy escort, detention, logistical support). To qualify, the deployment must occur within the specified timeframe; mere announcements will not suffice.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a UN Security Council resolution authorizing or endorsing the deployment of an International Stabilization Force (ISF) or multinational force in Gaza be adopted by November 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Following the Gaza ceasefire that took effect on October 10, 2025, a key component of the Trump administration's peace plan is the deployment of an International Stabilization Force (ISF) to Gaza for border security, peacekeeping, and supporting the transition to civilian governance. However, deploying such a force requires a legal framework, and multiple stakeholders have emphasized the need for a UN Security Council resolution. On October 14, 2025, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul announced that initial talks were underway with Russia and China to secure their support for such a resolution, stressing that a legal framework is 'essential' for deploying the ISF (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/germany-says-talks-underway-for-un-security-council-resolution-on-trumps-gaza-plan/3399012). Egypt has stated it would only contribute to a joint force if it operates under a UN Security Council resolution with a clear mandate (https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20250826-joint-forces-to-govern-gaza-mission-and-repercussions/). Russia and China hold veto power on the Security Council and have historically taken positions sympathetic to Palestinian demands, making their support uncertain. The Trump plan's Phase 2 envisions deploying a multinational force and disarming Hamas, but formal international legal authorization is a prerequisite that could delay or prevent the physical deployment of foreign forces into Gaza.

Sources:
- Anadolu Agency, 'Germany says talks underway for UN Security Council resolution on Trump's Gaza plan' (2025-10-14): https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/germany-says-talks-underway-for-un-security-council-resolution-on-trumps-gaza-plan/3399012
- Middle East Monitor, 'Joint forces to govern Gaza: Mission and repercussions' (2025-08-26): https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20250826-joint-forces-to-govern-gaza-mission-and-repercussions/
- Asia Times, 'The first day after the Gaza war' (2025-10-11): https://asiatimes.com/2025/10/the-first-day-after-the-gaza-war/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15 (inclusive), the UN Security Council adopts a resolution that explicitly authorizes, endorses, or establishes a multinational or international stabilization force for deployment within the Gaza Strip. The resolution must be formally adopted (not merely drafted or discussed) as recorded on the UN Security Council's official resolutions page (https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/content/resolutions). A resolution that only calls for a ceasefire, humanitarian access, or general peace without specifically authorizing or endorsing an international/multinational force for ground operations in Gaza does not qualify. If the UN Security Council website is unavailable, credible reporting from at least two major international news agencies (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP) confirming adoption will suffice.
subquestions.rationale: A UN Security Council resolution authorizing a multinational force is widely viewed as a legal prerequisite for deploying foreign military/security personnel into Gaza. Germany, Egypt, and other potential contributors have explicitly conditioned their participation on such a resolution. If the UNSC adopts such a resolution within this window, it would dramatically increase the probability that foreign forces physically enter Gaza before December 31, 2025. Conversely, failure to pass a resolution — due to Russian or Chinese vetoes or lack of consensus — would be a strong signal that no qualifying foreign intervention will occur within the ultimate question's timeframe. This subquestion tracks a distinct, observable diplomatic milestone rather than simply asking whether troops have entered Gaza earlier.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The UN Security Council must have FORMALLY ADOPTED (not merely drafted or discussed) a resolution explicitly authorizing, endorsing, or establishing a multinational or international stabilization force for deployment in the Gaza Strip, between October 16, 2025 and November 15, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: An official UN Security Council resolution recorded on the official UN resolutions page, or credible reporting from at least two major international news agencies confirming formal adoption within this window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'UN Security Council resolution Gaza multinational force 2025' (Oct 16–Nov 15 window) — to find any adopted resolution. Query 2: 'UN Security Council Gaza International Stabilization Force resolution adopted' (Oct 16–Nov 15) — to find specific ISF-related adoptions. Query 3: 'UN Security Council Resolution 2803 Gaza adopted November 2025' (Nov 1–Nov 20) — to pin down exact date. Query 4: 'UNSC vote Gaza stabilization force resolution November 2025 adopted passed' (Nov 1–Nov 20) — to confirm adoption date. Query 5: 'UN Security Council Resolution 2802 2803 Gaza exact date adopted vote November 17 18 2025' (Nov 15–Nov 20) — to resolve conflicting dates. Query 6: 'Gaza stabilization force UN resolution before November 15 2025 adopted' (Oct 16–Nov 15) — to check for any earlier adoption.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: UN Security Council adopted a resolution (referenced as Resolution 2803 or 2802 in sources) authorizing an International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza, passing with 13 votes in favor and Russia and China abstaining. Multiple sources confirm this vote: AFP (Nov 17), Boston Globe (Nov 17), Irish Times (Nov 17), KTVZ/CNN (Nov 17), TASS (Nov 17/18), The Express Tribune (Nov 17), France Diplomatie (Nov 18), Anadolu Agency (Nov 18), RT (Nov 18), Times of Israel blogs (Nov 18), China Daily (Nov 19). No resolution was adopted BEFORE November 15, 2025 within the window — confirmed by: (1) CNA article published Nov 15 stating vote is set for Monday November 17; (2) The Hindu (Nov 15) stating vote scheduled for November 17; (3) AFP (Nov 14) and multiple sources still urging 'swift adoption' as of Nov 14; (4) The Daily Star (Nov 14) reporting Russia introduced a competing draft. No earlier qualifying adoption found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution adopted on November 17, 2025 meets the substantive criteria — it explicitly authorizes the creation of a temporary International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza, authorizes use of 'all necessary measures,' and establishes a transitional Board of Peace. This resolution exactly matches the type of resolution described in the resolution criteria. HOWEVER, the adoption date of November 17, 2025 falls OUTSIDE the resolution window of October 16 – November 15, 2025 (inclusive). Sources: [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/84BQ7G4), [Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/11/17/world/un-security-council-adopts-us-peace-plan-gaza/), [Irish Times](https://www.irishtimes.com/world/middle-east/2025/11/17/un-security-council-votes-to-adopt-us-resolution-on-trumps-gaza-peace-plan/), [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/trump-gaza-plan-un-security-council-vote-nov-17-5469426), [France Diplomatie](https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/en/french-foreign-policy/france-and-the-united-nations/news-and-events/news/article/united-nations-adoption-of-security-council-resolution-2803-on-the-gaza-peace), [UN News](https://news.un.org/en/story/2025/11/1166391).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The resolution was adopted on November 17, 2025 (New York time), as confirmed by AFP, Boston Globe, Irish Times, KTVZ/CNN, TASS, and UN News. Some sources reporting November 18 likely reflect time zone differences (the vote occurred in the New York evening on Nov 17, which was already November 18 in Europe/Asia). The earliest confirmed adoption date is November 17, 2025. No hour-level timestamp is available, but all credible sources place it as November 17 at minimum — no earlier.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying resolution adoption was found within the window (Oct 16–Nov 15, 2025). As of November 14–15, sources consistently show the resolution was still being negotiated and not yet adopted: a joint statement from the US and Arab states on November 14 called for 'swift adoption,' Russia introduced a competing draft on November 14, and The Hindu and CNA on November 15 reported the vote was scheduled for November 17. There is no evidence of any earlier adoption of an ISF-authorizing resolution within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The Chatham House article states '17 November 2025' as the adoption date, while France Diplomatie says '18 November 2025' — this discrepancy is explained by time zones. The UN News article (un.org) references Resolution 2802, while most other sources say 2803 — this may indicate there were two resolutions voted on sequentially or a numbering discrepancy; regardless, both were adopted on November 17/18, outside the window. No source indicates any earlier formal adoption. The resolution window ends November 15, 2025, and all evidence places formal adoption on November 17 or 18, 2025 — clearly outside the window. The question resolves No.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The UN Security Council formally adopted a resolution (Resolution 2803) authorizing an International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza on November 17, 2025 (New York time). This date is TWO DAYS after the resolution window closed on November 15, 2025. No qualifying resolution was adopted between October 16 and November 15, 2025. The question therefore resolves No, with the resolution window closing on November 15, 2025 without the condition being met.

subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. will formally recognize Russian sovereignty over Crimea by end of 2025. A key precondition for such recognition would be active, high-level U.S.-Russia diplomatic engagement on a Ukraine peace settlement, since recognition of Crimea would most plausibly occur as part of a broader peace deal or grand bargain. As of late October 2025, the Trump administration has signaled interest in ending the Russia-Ukraine war. Trump announced in July 2025 that the U.S. would impose tariffs and other measures on Russia if Moscow did not make progress in ending its war within 10 days (https://www.straitstimes.com/world/while-you-were-sleeping-5-stories-you-might-have-missed-july-30-2025). In August 2025, Trump stated that Crimea 'cannot be returned to Ukraine,' which a Russian expert described as 'de facto' recognition (https://tass.com/world/1823415). Former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo warned in May 2025 against recognizing Russian control over Crimea, calling it 'a mistake of epic proportions' (https://thehill.com/policy/international/4829615-pompeo-warns-against-us-recognizing-russian-control-over-crimea/). Trump met with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and NATO Secretary-General Rutte in October 2025, signaling momentum toward a diplomatic push on the Russia-Ukraine conflict (https://www.foxnews.com/politics/inside-trumps-ultimatum-forced-netanyahu-table-you-cant-fight-world). However, no formal U.S.-Russia summit or bilateral negotiation session specifically on a Ukraine peace framework has been publicly confirmed as of October 31, 2025. Whether such a meeting takes place in November would be a strong indicator of whether the diplomatic conditions exist for a formal Crimea recognition before year-end.

Sources:
- The Straits Times, July 30, 2025: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/while-you-were-sleeping-5-stories-you-might-have-missed-july-30-2025
- TASS, August 19, 2025: https://tass.com/world/1823415
- The Hill, May 31, 2025: https://thehill.com/policy/international/4829615-pompeo-warns-against-us-recognizing-russian-control-over-crimea/
- Fox News, October 23, 2025: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/inside-trumps-ultimatum-forced-netanyahu-table-you-cant-fight-world
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive), there is a publicly confirmed bilateral meeting between senior U.S. officials (President, Vice President, Secretary of State, National Security Advisor, or a formally designated special envoy for Ukraine/Russia) and senior Russian officials (President, Foreign Minister, or a formally designated negotiator) that is specifically described by either government or by a consensus of at least three major credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC, CNN, NYT, Washington Post, Fox News) as focused on negotiating or discussing a peace deal, ceasefire, or diplomatic resolution to the Russia-Ukraine war. Phone calls count only if officially described by at least one side as a substantive negotiation session on a Ukraine peace framework (not merely a brief exchange or congratulatory call). Multilateral meetings (e.g., at the U.N. or G20) count only if they include a confirmed bilateral U.S.-Russia side meeting specifically on Ukraine peace. If no such meeting is publicly confirmed by November 30, 2025, the question resolves No. Resolution sources: official statements from the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov), U.S. State Department (https://www.state.gov), the Kremlin (http://en.kremlin.ru), Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://mid.ru/en/), and major wire services (Reuters, AP, AFP).
subquestions.rationale: Formal U.S. recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea would almost certainly require an active diplomatic track between Washington and Moscow on a Ukraine peace deal. If no high-level bilateral U.S.-Russia meeting on Ukraine peace occurs in November 2025, it would be extremely unlikely that the U.S. would take the dramatic step of recognizing Crimea in the remaining month of 2025. Conversely, if such a meeting does occur, it would signal that the diplomatic groundwork for a deal — potentially including territorial concessions like Crimea recognition — is actively being laid. This makes the occurrence of such a meeting a meaningful leading indicator for the ultimate question, without simply being a restatement of it.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A publicly confirmed bilateral meeting between senior U.S. officials (President, VP, SecState, NSA, or formally designated special envoy for Ukraine/Russia) AND senior Russian officials (President, Foreign Minister, or formally designated negotiator), specifically focused on Ukraine peace/ceasefire, between October 31–November 30, 2025, confirmed by either government or ≥3 major credible outlets.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US Russia bilateral meeting Ukraine peace deal November 2025' — to find qualifying meetings in the window; 2) 'Trump Putin meeting Ukraine negotiations November 2025' — to check for Trump-Putin meeting; 3) 'Dan Driscoll Russia bilateral meeting Abu Dhabi Ukraine peace November 24 25' — to investigate the Abu Dhabi meeting; 4) 'Steve Witkoff Putin Moscow meeting Ukraine peace December 2025' — to check Witkoff-Putin meeting timing; 5) 'Dan Driscoll formally designated special envoy Ukraine Russia negotiations' — to check Driscoll's formal status; 6) 'Kremlin confirmed Abu Dhabi Russia US Driscoll meeting' — to check Russian official confirmation.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: Dan Driscoll (U.S. Army Secretary) meeting with a Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi on November 24-25, 2025 — within the window. Reported by Reuters, AFP, ABC News, CBS News, Financial Times, AP, Straits Times, and others. Candidate event 2: Witkoff-Putin meeting in Moscow on December 2, 2025 — OUTSIDE the resolution window (rejected). Candidate event 3: U.S.-Ukraine-Europe Geneva talks on November 23-24, 2025 — multilateral, not bilateral U.S.-Russia. Rejected as not bilateral U.S.-Russia. Note: The Driscoll Abu Dhabi meeting is the only candidate within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Abu Dhabi meeting (Nov 24-25) raises several criteria issues: (1) Driscoll is U.S. Army Secretary — not President, VP, SecState, or NSA. He was reportedly given 'White House designation as a special representative' per Global News [https://globalnews.ca/news/11544181/trump-united-states-army-secretary-driscoll-russia-ukraine-war/], and called 'newly appointed U.S. special envoy to Ukraine' by DW [https://www.dw.com/en/what-ukraine-can-expect-from-trumps-new-envoy-dan-driscoll/a-74949069], and Charter97 reported 'Trump Appoints New Special Envoy For Ukraine Peace Plan' [https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/11/22/663952/]. However, formal executive designation is ambiguous — he retained his Army Secretary title. (2) The Russian delegation's composition was NOT disclosed — we cannot confirm 'senior Russian officials' (President, Foreign Minister, or formally designated negotiator) participated. The Kremlin did NOT confirm the meeting; Peskov said 'I have nothing to say. We are following the media reports' [AFP, http://doc.afp.com/863P7KE]. (3) Meeting described by ≥3 major outlets as focused on Ukraine peace: Reuters, AFP, ABC News, CBS News, Financial Times, AP, Straits Times — yes, easily 3+. (4) US confirmation: Lt. Col. Jeff Tolbert (Driscoll's spokesman) confirmed talks 'going well'; China Daily cited 'a US Army statement' confirming the meeting [https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202511/26/WS6926c049a310d6866eb2b8ab.html]. (5) The meeting was specifically focused on Ukraine peace/ceasefire — all sources agree on this. KEY ISSUES: Driscoll's formal designation as 'special envoy' is ambiguous (he held Army Secretary title, not formal special envoy appointment by executive order), and the Russian delegation's seniority/identity is unconfirmed, meaning we cannot verify 'senior Russian officials' as defined by the criteria participated.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Abu Dhabi meeting began on Monday evening November 24, 2025 and continued into Tuesday November 25, 2025. Multiple sources cite the start as 'Monday night' (November 24) in Abu Dhabi. The CBS News article and Charter97 article both state November 24 as the start date. This is within the window (Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying bilateral U.S.-Russia meeting specifically on Ukraine peace was found within the window (Oct 31–Nov 30). The Abu Dhabi meeting starting November 24 appears to be the first such candidate event in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: (1) Kremlin spokesperson Peskov did NOT confirm the Abu Dhabi meeting, stating 'I have nothing to tell you. We are following the media reports' — this undermines the 'publicly confirmed by either government' standard on the Russian side. (2) Lavrov confirmed 'permanent channels of communication' but did not specifically confirm Abu Dhabi. (3) The Russian delegation's composition remains classified/undisclosed, preventing verification that 'senior Russian officials (President, Foreign Minister, or formally designated negotiator)' participated — the criteria require one of these specific roles. (4) Driscoll's formal designation: while multiple sources describe him as 'special envoy,' this appears to be informal/media characterization; his formal title remained Army Secretary. No executive order or formal State Department designation as 'special envoy for Ukraine/Russia' was found. The Witkoff-Putin meeting (Dec 2) would clearly satisfy the criteria but falls outside the window. The resolution criteria appear not to be fully satisfied for the Abu Dhabi meeting due to: (a) uncertain formal status of Driscoll as 'formally designated special envoy,' (b) unconfirmed identity/seniority of Russian delegation, (c) Kremlin non-confirmation. However, against this: (a) a US Army spokesperson confirmed the meeting's occurrence and focus; (b) well over 3 major credible outlets (Reuters, AFP, ABC, CBS, AP, Financial Times) specifically described it as focused on Ukraine peace; (c) multiple sources report Trump designated Driscoll as special representative/envoy. The ambiguity on Driscoll's formal designation and Russian delegation seniority is the key issue preventing confident resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Abu Dhabi meeting (Nov 24-25, 2025) between Driscoll and a Russian delegation is the only candidate bilateral U.S.-Russia meeting within the window. However, it fails to clearly satisfy ALL resolution criteria: (1) Driscoll's formal designation as 'special envoy' is ambiguous — he was Army Secretary informally elevated to this role, not formally designated by executive order; (2) The Russian delegation's identity and seniority are undisclosed — we cannot confirm 'President, Foreign Minister, or formally designated negotiator' participated; (3) The Kremlin did NOT confirm the meeting. While ≥3 major outlets described the meeting as Ukraine peace-focused, and a US Army spokesperson confirmed it, the criteria require specific senior officials from each side. Given these unresolved ambiguities about the qualification of the participants — particularly on the Russian side — this question cannot be resolved with certainty. The Witkoff-Putin meeting (December 2) clearly would resolve Yes, but it falls outside the window. Given the ambiguities, resolvable=false is the appropriate call.

question: Will EJ Antoni be confirmed as BLS Commissioner in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if E.J. Antoni is confirmed as Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If Antoni’s nomination is formally withdrawn, or if the Senate rejects their nomination, this market will immediately resolve to “No”.

The Senate must confirm this nominee for this market to resolve to "Yes". Recess appointments without Senate confirmation will not count toward a "Yes" resolution.

The resolution source for this market is information from the U.S. Senate (see: https://www.senate.gov/legislative/NominationsRejectedorWithdrawn.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Senate HELP Committee schedule a confirmation hearing for EJ Antoni's nomination as BLS Commissioner between September 1 and September 28, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
President Trump nominated EJ Antoni, chief economist at the Heritage Foundation, to serve as Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics on approximately August 14, 2025, after firing the previous commissioner Erika McEntarfer. For a nominee to be confirmed by the full Senate, the nomination typically must first be referred to the relevant committee — in this case, the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) — which holds a confirmation hearing and then votes on whether to advance the nomination to the full Senate floor.

As of September 1, 2025, no hearing has been scheduled for Antoni's nomination. Senate Democrats, including Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Sen. Patty Murray (ranking member of the HELP Committee), have strongly opposed the nomination, calling Antoni 'unqualified' and an 'unqualified right-wing extremist' who would politicize economic data (The Hill, August 17, 2025; Colorado Newsline, August 16, 2025). Even some economists who have worked under Republican administrations, such as former BLS Commissioner William Beach, have expressed concerns about the nomination.

The HELP Committee is chaired by Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-LA). The committee has a Republican majority, but scheduling a hearing and advancing the nomination requires committee action. Given the strong opposition and the controversial nature of the nomination, the timeline for a hearing is uncertain. Past BLS Commissioner confirmations have sometimes taken months; for example, Erika McEntarfer was nominated in 2023 and confirmed in early 2024.

Sources:
- The Hill: Trump stuns Wall Street, Washington with controversial BLS nominee (August 17, 2025): https://thehill.com/business/economy/4908678-trump-stuns-wall-street-washington-bls-nominee/
- Colorado Newsline: Trump taps economist from far-right foundation to head agency that tracks jobs numbers (August 16, 2025): https://coloradonewsline.com/2025/08/16/trump-taps-economist-head-agency-tracks-jobs/
- Senate HELP Committee: https://www.help.senate.gov/
- Senate Nominations page: https://www.senate.gov/legislative/nominations.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and September 28, 2025 (inclusive), the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) officially schedules a confirmation hearing for EJ Antoni's nomination as BLS Commissioner. The hearing does not need to have taken place — it only needs to have been formally scheduled (i.e., a date announced) during this window. Evidence of scheduling may come from the official HELP Committee website (https://www.help.senate.gov/), the Senate's nominations page (https://www.senate.gov/legislative/nominations.htm), or a consensus of credible news reporting (e.g., AP, Reuters, The Hill, Politico, major newspapers). If no hearing is scheduled by end of day September 28, 2025, the question resolves No. If the nomination is formally withdrawn before a hearing is scheduled, the question also resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A Senate HELP Committee hearing is a necessary procedural step before full Senate confirmation. If no hearing is even scheduled by late September, it becomes extremely unlikely that Antoni could be confirmed by the full Senate before October 1, 2025 (the ultimate question's end date), since a hearing, committee vote, and floor vote would all need to occur. Conversely, if a hearing is quickly scheduled, it signals that Republican leadership is prioritizing the nomination and that confirmation is plausible within the remaining window. This subquestion tracks a concrete, observable procedural milestone that is highly informative about whether the ultimate confirmation can happen in time.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The Senate HELP Committee must have OFFICIALLY SCHEDULED (announced a date for) a confirmation hearing for EJ Antoni as BLS Commissioner between September 1-28, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: Official HELP Committee announcement, Senate nominations page update, or credible news reporting confirming a specific hearing date was announced. Key entities: Senate HELP Committee, EJ Antoni, BLS Commissioner nomination.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'EJ Antoni BLS Commissioner nomination Senate HELP Committee confirmation hearing' (Sept 1-28, 2025) — to find direct evidence of scheduling. Query 2: 'EJ Antoni Bureau of Labor Statistics Commissioner Senate confirmation 2025' (Jan-Sept 2025) — to find broader context. Query 3: 'Senate HELP Committee EJ Antoni confirmation hearing scheduled date September 2025' — to find specific scheduling announcements. Query 4: 'EJ Antoni BLS hearing September 2025 HELP Committee schedule' — variant search. Query 5: 'EJ Antoni BLS Commissioner withdrawn nomination September 2025' — to check for withdrawal. Query 6: 'Senate HELP Committee nominations hearing October 2025 EJ Antoni' — to check late-September window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Mint/Bloomberg (Sept 5): 'HELP has received the paperwork and will hold a hearing, though the date is not yet set' — does NOT confirm a scheduled hearing. (2) MSNBC (Sept 5): 'a confirmation hearing has not yet been scheduled' — explicitly confirms NO scheduling as of Sept 5. (3) CNN (Sept 5): 'plans to hold a hearing pending paperwork' — no date set. (4) Heritage Foundation (Sept 23): discusses Antoni's nomination without mentioning a scheduled hearing. (5) No article in the entire search window announces a specific confirmed hearing date. All candidate events were rejected as they either confirmed no hearing was scheduled or provided no relevant information about scheduling.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article explicitly confirms that the HELP Committee scheduled a confirmation hearing for Antoni within the September 1-28, 2025 window. The Mint/Bloomberg article [https://www.livemint.com/politics/trumps-pick-to-lead-bls-is-slated-to-face-senate-panel-11757110597125.html] states 'the date is not yet set.' The MSNBC article [https://www.msnbc.com/rachel-maddow-show/maddowblog/ej-antoni-labor-statistics-trump-nominee-bls-rcna229399] explicitly states 'a confirmation hearing has not yet been scheduled' as of September 5. No later articles in the window contradict this or announce a scheduled date.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp exists for a hearing being scheduled, because no hearing was scheduled during the window based on available evidence.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event (hearing scheduled) was found in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: The Mint headline 'Trump's Pick to Lead BLS Is Slated to Face Senate Panel' could be misread as indicating a scheduled hearing, but the article body clarifies 'the date is not yet set.' No other article reports a specific hearing date being announced. The HELP Committee during Sept 2025 held hearings on CDC/RFK Jr. (Sept 17) and confirmed Aronowitz (Sept 19) but no Antoni hearing was mentioned. No evidence of nomination withdrawal was found. Late-September articles (Heritage Foundation Sept 23, TheStreet Sept 23) still discuss Antoni's nomination in future tense without mentioning a scheduled hearing.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The window closed on September 28, 2025 without any evidence of the HELP Committee formally scheduling a confirmation hearing for EJ Antoni. Multiple credible sources explicitly confirmed as of September 5 that no hearing date had been set, and no subsequent articles in the window reported a hearing being scheduled. The condition was never met within the window. Resolution: No.

question: TikTok sale announced in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if ByteDance announces their intention to sell TikTok by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to “No”.

A public announcement of the intention to sell TikTok will qualify even if a sale has not been finalized. This includes any formal declaration made by ByteDance or its authorized representatives regarding their plans to sell or transfer ownership of TikTok.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from ByteDance. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will President Trump publicly reveal the identity of the proposed TikTok buyer(s) before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On June 29, 2025, President Trump announced during a FOX News interview that a 'group of very wealthy people' had agreed to purchase TikTok's US operations and that he would reveal the buyers' identities in 'about two weeks.' As of September 1, 2025, the identities of the buyers have not been conclusively and formally confirmed. The current deadline for ByteDance to divest TikTok's US operations is September 17, 2025, following a third 90-day extension signed by Trump on June 18, 2025. Trump has expressed confidence that Chinese President Xi Jinping would approve the deal, but Beijing's position remains uncertain. ByteDance has not publicly committed to selling TikTok, and the complexity of separating TikTok's algorithm and operations from ByteDance's infrastructure remains a significant obstacle. The identification and public confirmation of a credible buyer group is a critical precondition for any sale announcement by ByteDance.

Sources:
- Trump Announces TikTok Sale: Wealthy Buyers Await Chinese Approval, Devdiscourse (2025-06-29): https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/politics/3288091-trump-announces-tiktok-sale-wealthy-buyers-await-chinese-approval
- Trump grants ByteDance another 90-day extension to sell TikTok, Invezz (2025-06-19): https://invezz.com/news/2025/06/19/trump-grants-bytedance-another-90-day-extension-to-sell-tiktok/
- Trump Says 'Very Wealthy People' Are Ready to Buy TikTok, Gizmodo (2025-06-29): https://gizmodo.com/trump-says-very-wealthy-people-are-ready-to-buy-tiktok-2000613892
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), President Trump, the White House, or credible news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, Wall Street Journal, New York Times) report the specific names of the individual(s), consortium, or company that have agreed or are in advanced negotiations to purchase TikTok's US operations. Vague references to 'wealthy buyers' or unnamed groups do not count — the resolution requires at least one named entity (person or company) publicly identified as the lead buyer or part of the buyer group. If Trump or the White House makes such an announcement, or if credible reporting based on official sources or confirmed leaks identifies the buyer(s), this resolves Yes. If no such identification is made by 2025-10-01, this resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- White House official statements: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com/
subquestions.rationale: The public identification of a specific buyer is a necessary precursor to a formal sale announcement by ByteDance. If Trump reveals the buyer(s) in September, it strongly signals that deal negotiations are progressing and increases the likelihood of ByteDance announcing a sale by year-end. Conversely, if the buyer remains unnamed as the September 17 deadline passes, it suggests the deal is stalled, which would decrease the probability of a sale announcement in 2025. This is a meaningful early indicator because it tracks a concrete, observable milestone in the deal process rather than simply asking whether the ultimate sale announcement happens sooner.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, credible sources (WSJ, Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, NYT) or Trump/White House must name at least one specific entity as the lead buyer or part of the buyer group for TikTok's US operations. Vague references (e.g., 'wealthy buyers') do not count. Observable evidence: named company or individual explicitly identified as buyer in credible reporting.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'TikTok buyer identity named Trump announcement 2025' (Sept 1-Oct 1) — to find named buyer announcements. Query 2: 'TikTok US sale acquisition deal September 2025' (Sept 1-Oct 1) — to find deal news. Query 3: 'Trump names TikTok buyers Oracle Silver Lake Andreessen Horowitz Murdoch Dell Ellison' (Sept 1-Oct 1) — to find specific named entities. Query 5: 'TikTok buyer named first announcement Wall Street Journal September 16 2025' (Sept 15-17) — to pinpoint first occurrence.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) September 16, 2025: Wall Street Journal reports Oracle, Silver Lake, Andreessen Horowitz as buyer consortium — ACCEPTED as credible named source. (2) September 16, 2025: Trump says 'group of very big companies' without naming them — REJECTED as vague. (3) September 20, 2025: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirms Oracle, Andreessen Horowitz, Silver Lake on CNN — ACCEPTED. (4) September 21, 2025: Trump on Fox News names Larry Ellison, Michael Dell, Lachlan Murdoch, Rupert Murdoch — ACCEPTED (Trump himself naming individuals). (5) September 25-26, 2025: Executive order finalized, full consortium confirmed — ACCEPTED but later than first occurrence.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Wall Street Journal — explicitly listed as a qualifying source in resolution criteria — reported on September 16, 2025 that Oracle, Silver Lake, and Andreessen Horowitz were in final talks to acquire TikTok's US operations. [WSJ via Investing.com/Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/oracle-silver-lake-consortium-to-control-80-stake-in-tiktok-in-us-wsj-reports-4241096); [Australian Financial Review](https://www.afr.com/world/north-america/tiktok-buyers-group-to-include-oracle-silver-lake-andreessen-20250917-p5mvmt); [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91405633/tiktok-oracle-andreessen-horowitz-consortium). evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Wall Street Journal first reported on September 16, 2025. Multiple articles cite WSJ as reporting on September 16 (Tuesday). The Mashable article states published September 17 but references WSJ's Tuesday (September 16) reporting. The Australian Financial Review article is dated September 16/17, 2025. The resolution criteria allows for 'credible news sources... based on official sources or confirmed leaks' — the WSJ report meets this standard, and it was subsequently officially confirmed. evidence.step8_final_decision: The Wall Street Journal — a qualifying credible news source per the resolution criteria — explicitly named Oracle, Silver Lake, and Andreessen Horowitz as the buyer consortium for TikTok's US operations on September 16, 2025, within the September 1-October 1, 2025 window. This was subsequently confirmed by the White House (September 20) and by Trump himself (September 21, naming Ellison, Dell, Murdochs). The resolution criteria is satisfied. Resolution: Yes. First occurrence: September 16, 2025 (WSJ reporting).

subquestions.question: Will Trump and Xi Jinping meet in person at the APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, between October 25 and November 2, 2025?

This would be Trump's first in-person encounter with Xi since returning to the White House. The meeting was nearly canceled after Beijing imposed rare-earth export curbs and Trump threatened 100% tariffs, but both sides appear committed to meeting. Trump has stated he hopes to reach a 'deal on everything' with Xi. The APEC summit runs from approximately October 31 to November 1, but bilateral meetings on the sidelines are expected to begin around October 30. Analysts from the Brookings Institution have cautioned that the meeting is unlikely to be a turning point but is an important 'data point.' Trump's broader Asia itinerary includes stops in Malaysia (ASEAN summit), Japan (meeting PM Takaichi), and South Korea.

Sources:
- AFP, 'Trump heads to Asia and high-stakes meeting with Xi' (Oct 24, 2025): https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20251024-trump-heads-to-asia-and-high-stakes-meeting-with-xi

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if credible news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP, CNN, BBC) report that Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met in person between October 25, 2025, and November 2, 2025 (inclusive), at or on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, or at any other location during this window. subquestions.rationale: The Trump-Xi meeting is one of the three required meetings for the ultimate question to resolve Yes. It is the most imminent and most likely of the three, with a specific date already scheduled (October 30). Confirming whether this meeting actually takes place provides a strong early signal: if Trump cannot even complete the most well-planned of the three meetings, the ultimate question is very unlikely to resolve Yes. Conversely, a successful Trump-Xi meeting would confirm one-third of the requirement and signal diplomatic momentum that could facilitate the harder-to-arrange meetings with Putin and Kim.

question: EU sanctions on Israel by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the European Union officially imposes new sanctions of any form against Israel between September 2 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Sanctions could include measures like tariffs, trade restrictions, financial penalties, diplomatic expulsions, travel bans, restrictions on specific individuals, or any other actions that are commonly recognized as sanctions.

Sanctions against Israeli citizens or entities which do not directly target the Israeli state or members of the Israeli government will not qualify.

The passage of an official act authorizing sanctions on Israel within this market's timeframe will count toward a "Yes" resolution, regardless of if/when the sanctions come into effect.

Only the imposition of sanctions on Israel by the EU as an entity will qualify; if individual member states of the EU apply sanctions against Israel (e.g., France imposes novel trade restrictions on Israel unilaterally), it will not be sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes".

The primary resolution source will be official information from the European Union; however, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the EU Foreign Affairs Council formally adopt any sanctions targeting the Israeli government or its members by October 3, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, the EU has been debating a range of punitive measures against Israel over the humanitarian situation in Gaza. EU High Representative Kaja Kallas presented an 'options paper' to member states that includes partial or full suspension of the EU-Israel Association Agreement, targeted sanctions on Israeli government ministers and military officials, trade restrictions, an arms embargo, and suspension of scientific cooperation. However, the EU remains deeply divided: Germany and Hungary have opposed suspending the Association Agreement, and unanimity among all 27 member states is required for most foreign policy sanctions under the EU's Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP). At the informal foreign ministers' meeting in Copenhagen on August 30, 2025, Kallas acknowledged the division, stating 'If you ask personally how that feels, that I'm the face that is to blame, that we don't have a decision, then it's hard.' She noted that the majority favoring action is growing but consensus has not been reached. Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen suggested alternative approaches like heavy tariffs on imports from occupied territories using qualified majority voting. Kallas indicated that concrete measures would be proposed the following week (early September 2025). The next formal EU Foreign Affairs Council meeting is expected in mid-September 2025, which would be the earliest opportunity for a formal decision.

Sources:
- Euronews, 'EU Member States divided over Gaza at their Copenhagen meeting' (2025-08-30): https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/08/30/eu-member-states-divided-over-gaza-at-their-copenhagen-meeting
- Europa press remarks by Kaja Kallas (2025-08-30): https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/informal-meeting-foreign-affairs-ministers-press-remarks-high-representative-kaja-kallas-after_en
- Anadolu Agency, 'EU prepares sanctions options as pressure on Israel grows' (2025-07-05): https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-prepares-sanctions-options-as-pressure-on-israel-grows/3388123
- Euractiv, 'EU to Examine Possible Measures Against Israel Over Gaza Situation' (2025-07-06): https://www.euractiv.com/section/global-europe/news/eu-to-examine-possible-measures-against-israel-over-gaza-situation/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03 (inclusive), the Council of the European Union (Foreign Affairs Council or European Council) formally adopts a legal act imposing sanctions that directly target the Israeli state, Israeli government members, or Israeli military officials. 'Formally adopts' means a Council Decision or Regulation is published in the Official Journal of the European Union or announced via an official EU Council press release. Sanctions targeting only individual settlers or non-governmental entities do not count — the sanctions must target the Israeli government, its members, or Israeli military officials in their official capacity. If no such formal adoption occurs by 2025-10-03, the question resolves No. The primary resolution sources are: (1) the Official Journal of the European Union (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/oj/direct-access.html), (2) the EU Council's press releases page (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/), and (3) a consensus of credible international media reporting.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly tracks whether the EU can overcome its internal divisions and move from discussion to formal adoption of sanctions against Israel within the next month. The key obstacle to the ultimate question resolving Yes is the unanimity requirement for CFSP sanctions and the known opposition from Germany and Hungary. If the EU manages to adopt formal sanctions by early October — just weeks after Kallas promised 'concrete measures' — it would be a very strong indicator that the ultimate question resolves Yes. Conversely, if no formal decision is reached by October 3 despite the momentum from late August, it suggests the divisions are too deep for action by year-end, making the ultimate question more likely to resolve No. This subquestion captures the critical near-term decision point without merely restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, as it focuses specifically on the formal Council adoption process rather than the broader category of any EU sanctions action.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the EU Foreign Affairs Council (or European Council) to FORMALLY ADOPT (via Council Decision or Regulation published in the Official Journal of the EU or announced via official EU Council press release) sanctions that DIRECTLY TARGET the Israeli state, Israeli government members, or Israeli military officials in their official capacity — between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03 (inclusive). Sanctions against only settlers or non-governmental entities do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'EU Foreign Affairs Council sanctions Israel government officials 2025' (Sep 3–Oct 3); 2) 'European Union Council sanctions Israeli military officials formal adoption' (Sep 3–Oct 3); 3) 'EU Council formally adopts sanctions Israel Official Journal decision regulation September October 2025'; 4) 'EU Foreign Affairs Council vote Israel sanctions adopted approved October 2025'; 5) 'EU Council Israel sanctions Ben-Gvir Smotrich formal adoption approved October 1 2 3 2025'; 6) 'EU informal council Copenhagen October 1 2025 Israel sanctions decision'; 7) 'EU Israel sanctions no majority blocked adopted October 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key events identified within the window: (a) September 10, 2025: Von der Leyen announced in her State of the Union address that the Commission would PROPOSE sanctions and suspension of EU-Israel Association Agreement trade provisions. (b) September 16–17, 2025: European Commission formally PROPOSED (not adopted) a package including sanctions against extremist Israeli ministers (Ben-Gvir, Smotrich, others) and suspending trade preferences — but this is a COMMISSION PROPOSAL, not a Council adoption. (c) September 17, 2025: European Commission approved the package, sending it to EU Council for member-state approval. (d) October 1–2, 2025: Informal EU summit in Copenhagen — focused on defense/Ukraine; no binding decisions on Israel expected or announced. Multiple sources confirm the Israel sanctions vote was scheduled for October 20, 2025 (the formal FAC meeting), well outside the window. All sources consistently characterize the measures as proposed/pending — NOT formally adopted. Rejected candidates: Any Belgian/Slovenian/Spanish/Irish individual national measures — these are not EU Council actions. The Commission's own bilateral payment suspension is a Commission act, not a Council Decision/Regulation sanctioning the Israeli government.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution requires a formal Council Decision or Regulation published in the EU Official Journal or announced via official EU Council press release targeting the Israeli state, its government members, or military officials. All evidence found in the window indicates: (1) The European Commission PROPOSED the sanctions package on September 17, 2025 [AP News](https://apnews.com/article/eu-israel-sanctions-tariffs-gaza-war-94aa802ef07e2483b06724800c5c0238); (2) The Council had NOT adopted the measures — multiple sources confirm opposition from Germany, Italy, Hungary, Czech Republic, and others blocking the required majority [Euractiv](https://www.euractiv.com/news/von-der-leyen-still-needs-allies-onside-to-make-good-on-israel-sanctions-pledge/); (3) The formal FAC vote was expected for October 20, 2025, OUTSIDE the window [EJPress](https://ejpress.org/israels-fm-slams-eu-commission-president-for-empowering-a-terrorist-organisation-with-sanctions-against-israel/); (4) EUR-Lex searches found no Council Decisions/Regulations targeting Israel published in the Official Journal during this period; (5) The October 1–2 Copenhagen summit discussed defense and Ukraine — not Israel sanctions [Euractiv](https://www.euractiv.com/news/rapporteur-omnibus-omni-blame/), explicitly noting 'No qualified majority exists to suspend Israel's trade privileges'; (6) The European Parliament's answer to parliamentary question E-002981/25 (published October 2, 2025) describes the Commission's measures as proposals requiring member state approval — confirming no formal adoption had occurred [European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2025-002981-ASW_EN.html).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp exists for a formal Council adoption of Israel sanctions within the window (September 3–October 3, 2025), because no such adoption occurred. The question resolves No at the end of the window: 2025-10-03T23:59:59Z.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event occurred.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (a) Could the Commission's bilateral payment suspension count? No — the resolution criteria specifically require a Council Decision or Regulation targeting the Israeli government/members. The Commission's unilateral suspension of payments does not meet this criteria. (b) Could individual member-state bans (Slovenia, Ireland, Spain) count? No — these are national measures, not EU Council actions. (c) Was there any EUR-Lex entry for an Israel-targeting Council Decision? Only decisions found were for Iran (CFSP 2025/1971), Guinea-Bissau (CFSP 2025/1935), Syria (CFSP 2025/1936), and EESC appointment (2025/1911) — none targeting Israel. (d) Multiple independent sources confirm no qualified majority existed and that the formal vote was scheduled for October 20, 2025. The evidence is highly consistent across sources that formal adoption had not occurred by October 3, 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The EU Foreign Affairs Council did NOT formally adopt any Council Decision or Regulation imposing sanctions targeting the Israeli government, its members, or Israeli military officials in their official capacity between September 3 and October 3, 2025. What occurred was: (1) a Commission PROPOSAL on September 17, 2025, and (2) ongoing political discussions, but no formal Council adoption. The formal vote was expected at the FAC meeting on October 20, 2025, outside the resolution window. No qualifying event occurred within the resolution window. Resolution: No.

question: Trump eliminates capital gains tax on crypto in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to eliminate capital gains tax on any cryptocurrency assets by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If capital gains is eliminated only for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will any member of Congress formally introduce a standalone bill or amendment specifically to eliminate or substantially reduce federal capital gains tax on cryptocurrency between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether Trump will eliminate capital gains tax on crypto by the end of 2025. For this to happen, a bill or amendment would need to be introduced, pass both chambers of Congress, and be signed by the President — or Trump would need to take executive action. As of late 2025, no such legislation has been enacted. The closest legislative effort was a 'Hail Mary' push in late June 2025 to include a crypto tax exemption (specifically a de minimis exemption for small crypto transactions) in Trump's 'One Big Beautiful Bill' (OBBB), but a full elimination of capital gains tax on crypto was not part of that effort (Decrypt, June 30, 2025: https://decrypt.co/news-flash/trumps-big-beautiful-bill-may-get-a-hail-mary-bitcoin-tax-exemption). The GENIUS Act, signed into law on July 18, 2025, regulated stablecoins but did not address capital gains taxation (Invezz, July 18, 2025: https://invezz.com/news/2025/07/18/crypto-wrap-eth-xrp-and-ltc-see-gains-as-trump-signs-genius-act-into-law/). Trump's executive actions so far have focused on regulatory frameworks, strategic crypto reserves, and 401(k) access for crypto — none have addressed capital gains tax elimination (ValueWalk, August 8, 2025: https://www.valuewalk.com/trump-signs-order-to-broaden-access-to-crypto-private-equity-in-401ks/). A de minimis exemption for small crypto transactions has been discussed but is distinct from a full elimination of capital gains tax. For a full elimination to occur by year-end, legislative activity would need to materialize very quickly. Tracking whether any bill or amendment is formally introduced in October is a meaningful leading indicator.

Sources:
- Decrypt (June 30, 2025): https://decrypt.co/news-flash/trumps-big-beautiful-bill-may-get-a-hail-mary-bitcoin-tax-exemption
- Invezz (July 18, 2025): https://invezz.com/news/2025/07/18/crypto-wrap-eth-xrp-and-ltc-see-gains-as-trump-signs-genius-act-into-law/
- ValueWalk (August 8, 2025): https://www.valuewalk.com/trump-signs-order-to-broaden-access-to-crypto-private-equity-in-401ks/
- Crowdfund Insider (July 29, 2025): https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/07/crypto-policy-under-the-trump-administration-could-enhance-adoption-of-digital-assets-analysis/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), at least one member of the U.S. Congress (House or Senate) formally introduces a standalone bill or floor amendment that specifically proposes to eliminate federal capital gains tax on cryptocurrency assets (either all crypto or a defined subset such as Bitcoin), as recorded in the Congressional Record or on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/). A 'de minimis' exemption for small transactions does NOT count unless it effectively eliminates capital gains tax on all crypto transactions regardless of size. The bill or amendment must be formally introduced (i.e., assigned a bill number or recorded as a filed amendment); mere public statements of intent, press releases, or draft proposals without formal introduction do not qualify. If Congress.gov is unavailable, resolution may rely on official records from the House Clerk (https://clerk.house.gov/) or Senate (https://www.senate.gov/) or a consensus of at least three credible news sources (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, Politico, CoinDesk). This question resolves No if no such bill or amendment is formally introduced during the specified window.
subquestions.rationale: For Trump to eliminate capital gains tax on crypto by the end of 2025, either Congress must pass legislation or Trump must take executive action. Executive action to change tax law faces severe legal constraints (the taxing power belongs to Congress), making legislation the most plausible path. If no bill or amendment is even introduced in October 2025, the legislative timeline to pass such a major tax change through both chambers by year-end becomes extremely compressed — making the ultimate question's resolution as 'Yes' very unlikely. Conversely, if a bill is introduced with apparent momentum, it would significantly update the probability upward. This subquestion tracks a necessary precursor to the legislative path without simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: U.S. Congress member formally introduces (bill number assigned or recorded as filed amendment) a standalone bill or floor amendment between Oct 1-31, 2025, proposing to eliminate federal capital gains tax on cryptocurrency (all crypto or defined subset). De minimis exemptions limited to small transactions do NOT qualify. Observable evidence: Congress.gov bill number, Congressional Record entry, or 3+ credible news sources confirming formal introduction.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Congress bill eliminate capital gains tax cryptocurrency 2025' (Oct 1-31); 2) 'cryptocurrency capital gains tax bill amendment Congress October 2025'; 3) 'Lummis Digital Asset Tax Fairness Act new bill October 2025 introduced Congress.gov'; 4) 'Congress bill zero capital gains tax Bitcoin crypto October 2025 introduced'; 5) 'Ohio crypto bill state capital gains tax exemption digital asset fiat currency October 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidates found: (A) Senator Lummis S.2207 - introduced in June/July 2025 (before the Oct 1-31 window), proposes only $300/transaction de minimis exemption with $5,000 annual cap — rejected on two grounds: wrong date range AND fails criteria (de minimis only). (B) Ohio state bills (HB 116, etc.) — state legislature, not U.S. Congress — rejected. (C) Retirement Investment Choice Act (Oct 14) — crypto in 401(k)s, not capital gains elimination — rejected. (D) Various market structure bills, AI chip bills — not related to capital gains tax elimination — rejected. No qualifying candidates remain.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No bill or amendment was found that: (1) was formally introduced during Oct 1-31, 2025, AND (2) specifically proposes to eliminate or substantially reduce federal capital gains tax on crypto in a way that would apply to ALL crypto transactions regardless of size. Senator Lummis's bill [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/jack-dorsey-wants-tax-exemption-092441201.html) was introduced in June/July, not October, and is a limited de minimis exemption. The Coinspeaker article mentions Ohio state lawmakers (not U.S. Congress) introducing a bill [Coinspeaker](https://www.coinspeaker.com/crypto-tax-uk-authorities-more-determined-to-clawback-gain/). No new qualifying federal bill introduced in October 2025 was identified.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp found within Oct 1-31, 2025 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at all within the window, so first occurrence check is moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources confirm that during October 2025: (1) the government was in a shutdown starting Oct 1 [Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/republican-lawmaker-crypto-bills-congress), which slowed legislative activity; (2) Lummis was 'working on' new crypto tax legislation but had not formally introduced any new bill [cryptonews.com](https://cryptonews.com/news/working-on-it-senator-lummis-backs-jack-dorseys-push-for-a-bitcoin-tax-exemption/); (3) Senator Tillis expressed pessimism about advancing any crypto bills [Blockonomi](https://blockonomi.com/republican-senator-warns-time-running-out-to-pass-crucial-crypto-bill/); (4) no news source reports a formally introduced bill eliminating crypto capital gains tax in October 2025. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence consistently shows no qualifying bill was formally introduced in the October 1-31, 2025 window. The most relevant legislation (Lummis S.2207) was introduced before the window and only provides a limited de minimis exemption (not an elimination of capital gains tax). The government shutdown further stalled new legislative introductions. Resolution: No.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by December 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla receive a Texas Department of Motor Vehicles permit to operate autonomous vehicles without a human driver by September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Texas House Bill 4500, signed by Governor Greg Abbott on June 22, 2025, requires autonomous vehicle operators to obtain a permit from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) before operating self-driving vehicles on public streets without a human driver. This law takes effect on September 1, 2025. Tesla currently operates a limited robotaxi trial in Austin, Texas, with 'safety monitors' riding in the front passenger seat — meaning the service does not qualify as fully driverless. For Tesla to launch a truly driverless robotaxi service (as defined by the ultimate question), it would need to operate without a safety driver or monitor actively positioned to control the vehicle. In Texas, this now requires a TxDMV permit under the new law. Whether Tesla applies for and receives this permit in the first week of September is a critical gating factor for any driverless launch in Austin.

Sources:
- CNA: "Texas enacts robotaxi rules on the eve of Tesla's Austin rollout" (2025-06-22) https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/texas-enacts-robotaxi-rules-eve-teslas-austin-rollout-5191171
- The Express Tribune: "Tesla's robotaxi won't be driverless, set to launch with 'human monitors'" (2025-06-21) https://tribune.com.pk/story/2539123/teslas-robotaxi-wont-be-driverless-set-to-launch-with-human-monitors
- TechRadar: "I'm not buying the Tesla robotaxi hype" (2025-06-23) https://www.techradar.com/vehicle-tech/hybrid-electric-vehicles/im-not-buying-the-tesla-robotaxi-hype-heres-why-its-still-miles-behind-waymo
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and September 8, 2025 (inclusive), credible reporting or an official announcement from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles confirms that Tesla has been granted a permit under Texas HB 4500 (or equivalent regulation effective September 1, 2025) to operate autonomous vehicles on public roads without a human driver present or actively controlling the vehicle. The permit must specifically authorize operation without a safety driver in the driver's seat. Sources for resolution include official TxDMV announcements (https://www.txdmv.gov/), Tesla's official communications, or a consensus of credible news reporting from outlets such as Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, or major automotive/technology news sources. If no such permit is confirmed by September 8, 2025, this question resolves No.

Tesla's Austin robotaxi trial has been its most advanced public-facing service, but it currently operates with human safety monitors. For Tesla to launch a truly driverless robotaxi service (as required by the ultimate question), obtaining a Texas permit is a necessary regulatory prerequisite for its Austin operations. If Tesla does not secure this permit in the first week of September, it is extremely unlikely to launch a fully driverless service anywhere by September 11. Conversely, if Tesla does obtain the permit, it signals serious regulatory progress toward a driverless launch. This is a concrete, observable regulatory milestone that serves as a strong early indicator.

Under Texas HB 4500 or equivalent regulation. Must allow fully driverless operation (no safety driver in driver's seat).
