subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), either the White House, the Kremlin, or both officially announce or confirm a specific scheduled date for a second in-person meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin (distinct from the August 15, 2025 Alaska summit). The announcement must include at least a target date (month-level specificity or more precise) for the meeting. Vague statements about willingness to meet again or general references to 'future talks' without a specific date do not count. Resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting from major international news outlets such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), the Associated Press (https://apnews.com), TASS (https://tass.com), or official government statements published on the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov) or the Kremlin website (http://en.kremlin.ru). If no such announcement is made by 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For a second Trump-Putin meeting to occur before December 31, 2025, the diplomatic groundwork — including scheduling — would likely need to begin in the near term. After the Alaska summit ended without a deal but with both sides expressing openness to continued dialogue, whether a follow-up meeting is formally scheduled within the next month is a strong early indicator. If a date is announced by October 1, it significantly raises the probability that a second meeting happens before year-end. If no date is set, it suggests diplomatic momentum has stalled, making a second meeting less likely. This is a different observable event from the ultimate question (the meeting itself) and serves as a meaningful leading indicator.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between September 1-October 1, 2025, White House or Kremlin officially announce a specific scheduled date (at minimum month-level) for a second in-person Trump-Putin meeting, distinct from the August 15, 2025 Alaska summit. Observable evidence: Official press release, statement, or credible reporting citing a specific date. Key entities: Donald Trump (U.S. President), Vladimir Putin (Russian President), White House, Kremlin. Threshold: Must include specific target date; vague willingness does not count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump Putin second meeting scheduled date announcement 2025' (Sep 1-Oct 1) - to find announcement; 2) 'Trump Putin summit meeting announcement September 2025' - broader search; 3) 'White House Kremlin announce second Trump Putin meeting date confirmed' - official announcement focus; 4) 'Trump Putin next summit scheduled confirmed date October November 2025' - forward-looking date; 5) 'Trump Putin Moscow meeting invitation confirmed date' (Sep 20-Oct 1) - late period search; 6) 'Kremlin Peskov Trump Putin bilateral summit date scheduled' (Sep 20-Oct 1) - Kremlin-specific statements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidates identified: (1) Sep 5 Peskov statement - meeting 'could be organized very quickly' - REJECTED: vague, conditional, not a scheduled date. (2) Sep 16-19 Ryabkov statement - aims for talks 'by end of autumn' - REJECTED: vague timeframe, no specific date, not a confirmed meeting. (3) Sep 17 TASS - Peskov explicitly says 'no plans for phone call or face-to-face meeting' - CONFIRMS NO date. (4) Sep 19 uawire.org - 'White House and Kremlin have not officially confirmed... new meeting date and venue' - CONFIRMS NO confirmed date. (5) Sep 28 Peskov - Putin invitation 'still stands,' 'rest depends on Trump' - REJECTED: open invitation only, no date. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that exactly satisfies resolution criteria. The TASS article from September 17 [TASS Sep 17](https://tass.com/politics/2017793) explicitly states 'no plans for a phone call or face-to-face meeting.' The uawire.org article [uawire Sep 19](https://uawire.org/kremlin-aims-for-fall-trump-putin-talks-amid-behind-the-scenes-u-s-russia-consultations) explicitly states 'The White House and the Kremlin have not officially confirmed the reports of a new meeting date and venue.' The RT/TASS September 28 article [TASS Sep 28](https://tass.com/politics/2022437) confirms only that Putin's invitation 'still stands' but no date is set. evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with a timestamp exists. The clearest timestamp of a non-event is September 17, 2025 (Peskov: 'no plans for a meeting') and September 19, 2025 (uawire explicitly confirming no official confirmation of meeting date).

(4) No contradictory evidence found suggesting a specific meeting was announced during the window - all evidence consistently shows no specific date was confirmed.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout the entire September 1-October 1, 2025 window, no official announcement of a specific scheduled date for a second Trump-Putin meeting was made. The Kremlin explicitly stated on September 17 that 'no plans' existed for a meeting. By September 28, the situation remained that Putin's invitation to Moscow was 'still open' but with no date, and Vance claimed Russia had 'refused' meetings. The window closed October 1 without the condition being met.

question: TrumpRX launched by January 31, 2026?
description:
TrumpRx (https://trumprx.gov/) is scheduled to launch in January 2026 and is intended to help consumers access lower-cost medications by directing them to manufacturers’ direct-to-consumer purchasing channels.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if TrumpRx.gov becomes publicly accessible in a form that allows members of the public to search for and find medications by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

To qualify, the site must be publicly accessible and operational in at least a limited capacity, meaning it functions in its intended portal role by allowing users to search for or view medications and be redirected to purchase them. Glitches or minor technical issues will not render the site non-functional, provided the core portal functionality remains available to the public.

Once the qualifying functionality goes live, the market will resolve to "Yes" immediately, regardless of any subsequent reversal, rollback, or withdrawal of access.

This market will resolve to "No" if TrumpRx.gov becomes permanently unavailable.

The primary resolution source for this market will be TrumpRx.gov; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the TrumpRx.gov website display any content beyond a 'Coming Soon' placeholder page before January 29, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
TrumpRx.gov is a government-run portal intended to direct consumers to pharmaceutical manufacturers' direct-to-consumer purchasing channels for discounted medications. As of January 5, 2026, the site displayed only a 'Coming Soon. January 2026' message with a placeholder image of the president (Hattiesburg American, Jan 5, 2026). The Trump administration has announced agreements with 14 pharmaceutical companies including Pfizer, Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, Amgen, Merck, and others, offering discounts on medications for diabetes, obesity, migraines, asthma, and more. Multiple sources confirm the site is scheduled to launch in January 2026, but no specific date within January has been publicly confirmed. The Washington Times reported on January 9, 2026 that the site 'will direct patients to manufacturers' direct-to-consumer programs rather than selling drugs through the TrumpRx.gov website.' This subquestion tracks whether the site transitions from its placeholder state to showing any substantive drug-related content, which would be a necessary precursor to the full portal functionality required by the ultimate question.

Sources:
- Hattiesburg American (Jan 5, 2026): https://www.hattiesburgamerican.com/story/news/health/2026/01/05/trumprx-prescription-drug-discounts/77422091007/
- Washington Times (Jan 9, 2026): https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/jan/9/art-drug-deal-trumprx-website-will-direct-patients/
- ABC17NEWS (Dec 19, 2025): https://abc17news.com/news/national-world/cnn-national/2025/12/19/trump-announces-most-favored-nation-deals-with-nine-drug-companies-aiming-to-lower-prices-for-us-patients/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between 2026-01-13 and 2026-01-29 (inclusive), the website TrumpRx.gov (https://trumprx.gov/) displays substantive content beyond a 'Coming Soon' placeholder page. 'Substantive content' means any of the following: a list of medications or drug names, links to manufacturer purchasing pages, a search function, informational pages about specific drug discounts, or any interactive functionality related to finding or purchasing medications. A simple redesign of the placeholder page (e.g., changing colors, updating the launch date, or adding general promotional text without drug-specific information) does NOT count. Resolution will be based on direct observation of TrumpRx.gov, supplemented by credible news reporting (e.g., from major U.S. news outlets such as AP, Reuters, Washington Post, NYT, Wall Street Journal, Politico, etc.) confirming the site has been updated. If TrumpRx.gov becomes inaccessible (e.g., returns a server error) for the entire resolution window, this question resolves No. Web archive snapshots from the Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org/) may also be used as evidence.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether TrumpRx launches with full portal functionality (search for medications, redirection to purchase) by January 31, 2026. As of January 5, the site was still a placeholder. Whether the site transitions from 'Coming Soon' to displaying any substantive drug content by January 29 is a strong leading indicator: if the site still shows only a placeholder by January 29, it becomes very unlikely that full search/redirect functionality will appear in just 2 more days. Conversely, if substantive content appears, it signals the launch process is underway and full functionality is imminent. This subquestion asks about a different, earlier observable event (any content beyond a placeholder) rather than the full launch criteria of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: TrumpRx.gov displays substantive content (drug lists, manufacturer links, search function, drug-specific info, or interactive functionality) at any point between 2026-01-13 and 2026-01-29. Evidence required: direct observation or credible news reporting confirming site was updated beyond 'Coming Soon'. Key entities: TrumpRx.gov, pharmaceutical companies (Pfizer, Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, AstraZeneca), drug names (Xeljanz, Ozempic, etc.).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'TrumpRx.gov website launch content medications Jan 13-29 2026' - to find news about site launching; 2) 'TrumpRx drug discount website Trump Jan 2026' - to find early reporting; 3) 'TrumpRx.gov launch January 28 website live' - to find specific launch date coverage; 4) 'TrumpRx website Pfizer Eli Lilly Novo Nordisk January 2026' - to find participating companies and drug lists; 5) 'TrumpRx website links manufacturer purchasing medications January 2026' - to find confirmation of substantive content; 6) 'TrumpRx website content drug list search function' - to find direct confirmation of site functionality.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Jan 5, 2026 - site confirmed as 'Coming Soon' (pre-window); (2) Jan 15, 2026 - PBS/Newsday explicitly state 'no drugs were listed on January 15, 2026' (within window, but confirms no substantive content yet); (3) Jan 28, 2026 - GuruFocus reports 'White House is launching TrumpRx, a direct-to-consumer pharmaceutical platform, on Friday, January 28, 2026' with named drugs and discounts (within window, substantive launch). Rejected: Jan 17 article about 'confidential' TrumpRx website - doesn't confirm drug listings. Jan 27 Seeking Alpha article references 'the launch of TrumpRx.gov' without describing site content.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The GuruFocus article (Jan 28, 2026) [https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8560129/trumprx-launch-pfizer-pfe-and-other-pharma-giants-join-new-platform] explicitly states TrumpRx is launching on January 28, 2026 as a direct-to-consumer pharmaceutical platform with specific drug names (Xeljanz at 50-85% discount) and participating companies (Pfizer, Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, AstraZeneca). Washington Times Jan 9 article [https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/jan/9/art-drug-deal-trumprx-website-direct-patients-heavily-discounted/] describes TrumpRx directing patients to manufacturers' direct-to-consumer programs, which constitutes 'links to manufacturer purchasing pages' under resolution criteria. The Jan 28 GuruFocus article suggests a substantive launch occurred on that date.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: GuruFocus article published January 28, 2026 states TrumpRx is launching on 'Friday' (January 28, 2026). This is within the resolution window. No exact time is provided. The Seeking Alpha article (Jan 27, 2026) also references the launch having occurred, suggesting it was already live or imminent. PBS/Newsday (Jan 15) confirm no drugs listed on Jan 15 - so the substantive launch must have occurred between Jan 15 and Jan 28.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Evidence strongly suggests the substantive content first appeared on or around January 28, 2026. Jan 15 articles confirm no drugs listed yet. GuruFocus Jan 28 reports it as launching on that date. No evidence of earlier substantive content between Jan 13-15.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Washington Times (Jan 9) describes TrumpRx directing patients to manufacturers' sites but this was before the resolution window and may describe the planned design. The Jan 15 PBS/Newsday articles confirm no drugs were listed as of Jan 15, 2026 - consistent with the site still being in 'Coming Soon' state then. The Jan 28 GuruFocus article explicitly describes the launch of the platform with drug names and companies, suggesting substantive content appeared on Jan 28. No contradictory evidence found claiming the site remained at 'Coming Soon' after Jan 28. However, the GuruFocus article doesn't directly say it observed the website's content - it reports that the White House is 'launching' the platform, which is somewhat indirect. Still, reporting from multiple sources about drug names and manufacturer participation qualifies as 'credible news reporting confirming the site has been updated' per resolution criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence shows: (1) TrumpRx.gov was a 'Coming Soon' page as of Jan 5 and Jan 15, 2026; (2) GuruFocus reported on Jan 28, 2026 that the White House was launching TrumpRx as a direct-to-consumer pharmaceutical platform with Pfizer, Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, AstraZeneca, and specific drug Xeljanz at 50-85% discounts; (3) Multiple articles describe TrumpRx directing users to manufacturer purchasing pages (links to manufacturer purchasing pages); (4) The launch date falls within the resolution window (Jan 13-29, 2026). Based on this evidence, TrumpRx.gov displayed substantive content on January 28, 2026, meeting the resolution criteria for Yes.

question: US bank failure by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any US bank fails between November 11 2025, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET (according to FDIC's "Failed Bank List"). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

For this market to resolve to "Yes", the bank's closing date as listed by the FDIC must be within the listed date range. If there is a potential bank failure within this market's date range and FDIC "Failed Bank List" has not been updated yet, this market may remain open to allow for the list to be updated.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), specifically the "Failed Bank List" available here: https://www.fdic.gov/resources/resolutions/bank-failures/failed-bank-list/; however, other official statements from the FDIC and government entities will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will the FDIC add any new bank to its Problem Bank List (or will the number of FDIC-insured problem institutions increase) between Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 as reported in the FDIC's Quarterly Banking Profile?
subquestions.background_information:
The FDIC publishes a Quarterly Banking Profile (QBP) that includes the number of banks on the 'Problem Bank List'—institutions with CAMELS composite ratings of 4 or 5, indicating significant financial, operational, or managerial weaknesses. An increase in problem banks is a leading indicator of potential bank failures, as banks typically appear on this list before they fail. As of Q2 2025, the FDIC reported 66 problem banks with $87.3 billion in total assets, up from 63 in Q1 2025. The Q3 2025 QBP was published on November 20, 2025, and reported 68 problem banks with $83.4 billion in total assets. The Q4 2025 QBP is typically released in late February or early March 2026, but preliminary data or updates from the FDIC Board meetings and press releases often emerge in January. However, since the Q4 QBP may not be available before January 12, 2026, this question focuses on whether the FDIC issues any formal enforcement action (cease and desist order, consent order, or prompt corrective action directive) against a US bank between December 13, 2025 and January 12, 2026, which would signal deteriorating bank health and elevated failure risk.

Actually, to make this more tractable, this question will focus on whether the FDIC issues a new formal enforcement action (cease and desist order or consent order) against any FDIC-insured depository institution between December 13, 2025 and January 12, 2026. The FDIC publishes enforcement actions on its website. In 2025, the FDIC has been issuing enforcement actions at a moderate pace. A new enforcement action against a bank would be an indicator of financial stress that could precede a failure.

Sources:
- FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile: https://www.fdic.gov/analysis/quarterly-banking-profile
- FDIC Enforcement Actions: https://orders.fdic.gov/s/

question: Will ChatGPT reach 1b monthly active users in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ChatGPT reaches 1 billion monthly active users (MAUs) during by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PMET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The primary resolution source will be official information from OpenAI, however a consensus of reputable sources including, major analytics firms (e.g. Similarweb, Sensor Tower), investor or regulatory disclosures, or reputable media may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI or a credible analytics source report that ChatGPT has reached 800 million or more weekly active users by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
ChatGPT's weekly active user (WAU) growth has been extraordinary in 2025. In December 2024, ChatGPT had approximately 300 million WAU. By March 2025, it had surpassed 500 million WAU. In early August 2025, OpenAI VP Nick Turley announced ChatGPT was on track to reach 700 million WAU that week, representing a fourfold increase from the prior year (https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/04/openai-says-chatgpt-is-on-track-to-reach-700m-weekly-users/). Key growth drivers have included the upgraded GPT-4-powered image generation feature launched in March 2025, the release of GPT-5 in August 2025, and the expansion of agentic capabilities. ChatGPT's paid business users grew from 3 million in June to 5 million by early August 2025. Sensor Tower data shows users average 16 minutes daily on the app and access it over 12 days per month (https://www.techrepublic.com/article/chatgpt-700m-weekly-users/). The relationship between WAU and MAU is important: with 700 million WAU and high engagement frequency, the monthly active user count is likely significantly higher than the weekly figure, though OpenAI has not consistently disclosed MAU numbers. The trajectory from 500M WAU in March to 700M WAU in August suggests roughly 40% growth over 5 months. Reaching 800M WAU by end of September would require approximately a 14% increase over roughly 2 months from the 700M baseline, which is consistent with (though slightly below) the recent growth trend.

Sources:
- TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/04/openai-says-chatgpt-is-on-track-to-reach-700m-weekly-users/
- TechRepublic: https://www.techrepublic.com/article/chatgpt-700m-weekly-users/
- Decrypt (Similarweb data): https://decrypt.co/resources/chatgpt-is-eating-the-internet-openai-commands-80-of-ai-market
- Gizchina: https://www.gizchina.com/2025/07/22/chatgpt-hits-2-5-billion-daily-requests/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive), OpenAI (via official announcements, executive statements, blog posts, or regulatory/investor filings) or a reputable third-party analytics firm (such as Similarweb, Sensor Tower, or data.ai) reports that ChatGPT has reached at least 800 million weekly active users (WAU) at any point during this window. The report must be published or the data must reference a measurement period falling within 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-30. Acceptable sources include: OpenAI's official blog (https://openai.com/blog), public posts by OpenAI executives on social media platforms (e.g., X/Twitter), Similarweb's public reports (https://www.similarweb.com/), Sensor Tower reports (https://sensortower.com/), or credible major news outlets (e.g., TechCrunch, Reuters, Bloomberg) citing such data. If no such report or disclosure is made by 2025-09-30, this question resolves No. If a report states a range (e.g., 'approaching 800 million'), it resolves Yes only if the stated figure is explicitly 800 million or above.
subquestions.rationale: The path from 700M weekly active users to 1 billion monthly active users is the key trajectory to track. WAU and MAU are closely related but distinct metrics; however, WAU growth is the most frequently reported metric for ChatGPT. If ChatGPT reaches 800M WAU by late September, it signals continued strong growth momentum that would make 1 billion MAU by year-end plausible — since MAU typically exceeds WAU for high-engagement apps (users who use the product weekly likely use it multiple weeks per month, plus there are additional less-frequent monthly users). Conversely, if ChatGPT's WAU growth stalls below 800M, it would suggest the growth rate is decelerating, making 1B MAU by December less likely. This is a genuine crux: forecasters who believe ChatGPT will hit 1B MAU likely expect WAU to continue its ~8-10% monthly growth, while skeptics likely expect growth to plateau.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: An explicit report from OpenAI or a credible analytics firm (Similarweb, Sensor Tower, data.ai) published between Sept 1–30, 2025 stating ChatGPT reached ≥800 million weekly active users (WAU), with the data referencing a measurement period within that window. The threshold is 800 million WAU exactly — 'approaching 800 million' does not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'ChatGPT weekly active users 800 million 2025' (Sept window) — to find direct reports of the threshold. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require an explicit figure of ≥800 million WAU. [PCMag](https://uk.pcmag.com/ai/160079/openai-women-make-up-more-than-half-of-chatgpt-users) states '700 million users — about 10% of the global adult population.' [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91406385/openai-wants-to-transform-business-many-of-its-users-just-want-life-hacks) states '700 million weekly active users worldwide.' No source states 800 million or more. The 700 million figure does not meet the ≥800 million threshold. Criteria not met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The most recent and authoritative OpenAI data point was published on approximately September 15, 2025 (OpenAI's NBER working paper), citing July 2025 data of ~700 million WAU. This is within the resolution window but does not meet the threshold.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (≥800 million WAU) was found at any point, either within or before the September 2025 window. The highest figure reported is 'over 700 million.'
evidence.step7_verification: Verified through 9+ sources all citing the same 700 million figure from the OpenAI NBER working paper released in September 2025. evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition (≥800 million WAU explicitly reported within September 2025) was not met. The highest figure reported during the window by OpenAI and credible news outlets is 700 million WAU. The window closed on September 30, 2025 without the threshold being reached. Resolution: No.

subquestions.question: Will Turkey and Israel announce or confirm the establishment of a formal military deconfliction mechanism for Syrian airspace by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Since the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, both Israel and Turkey have significantly increased their military operations in Syria — Israel through air strikes and Turkey through troop deployments and support for the transitional government. This has led to near-encounters between Israeli and Turkish fighter jets over Syrian airspace. In April–May 2025, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan warned that encounters between Turkish and Israeli jets were inevitable and called for a deconfliction mechanism. Senior Israeli and Turkish defense officials held indirect talks in Baku, Azerbaijan, to establish such a mechanism, with Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz thanking Azerbaijan for mediating (https://www.turkishminute.com/2025/05/19/israeli-defense-minister-katz-thanks-azerbaijan-for-mediating-with-turkey-over-syria/). Analysts at Forbes noted the risk of 'mock dogfights' between the two air forces over Syria, with experts believing the U.S. would work hard to prevent actual hostilities (https://www.forbes.com/sites/pauliddon/2025/05/12/the-risk-of-israeli-turkish-mock-dogfights-over-syria/). As of September 2025, no formal deconfliction agreement has been publicly confirmed, though talks have been ongoing. The existence or absence of such a mechanism is a key factor in whether an accidental or intentional military clash could occur.

Sources:
- Turkish Minute: Israeli Defense Minister Katz thanks Azerbaijan for mediating with Turkey over Syria — https://www.turkishminute.com/2025/05/19/israeli-defense-minister-katz-thanks-azerbaijan-for-mediating-with-turkey-over-syria/
- Forbes: The Risk Of Israeli-Turkish Mock Dogfights Over Syria — https://www.forbes.com/sites/pauliddon/2025/05/12/the-risk-of-israeli-turkish-mock-dogfights-over-syria/

The confirmation must come from official government communications, press conferences, or credible international media outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, Hürriyet Daily News). Mere reports of ongoing talks or informal communication channels do not qualify — there must be an explicit statement that a mechanism or agreement is in place. If no such announcement is made by 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The presence or absence of a formal deconfliction mechanism between Israel and Turkey is a critical leading indicator for whether an actual military clash will occur in 2025. If a formal mechanism is established, the probability of an accidental escalation from near-encounters in Syrian airspace drops significantly, making a military clash less likely. Conversely, the continued absence of such an agreement raises the risk of miscalculation. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question would likely update their views significantly based on whether this mechanism is confirmed, as it directly addresses the most plausible pathway to a clash — contested operations in Syrian airspace.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official statement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) from Israeli government, Turkish government, or credible mediator (Azerbaijan, US) confirming that a formal military deconfliction mechanism for Syrian airspace/ground operations has been established or formally agreed upon between Turkey and Israel. Mere reports of ongoing talks do not qualify — must be an explicit statement that a mechanism or agreement is in place.

Their previous pre-summit engagement occurred ahead of the August 2025 Alaska meeting, where Rubio and Lavrov were both present (https://tass.com/politics/1900385).
